**Files**

  `audience: players`. The in-world rumor (sightings, boiling water, no confirmed body).

  reality: an entity forced through the Drowned Maw from the Elemental Plane of Water
  after the Pearl of Souls shifted the breach; Auralis reads it as a parasitic invader.

**Why it's flagged:** both share the slug `leviathan`, so `[[leviathan]]` is ambiguous
(duplicate-slug). They are the *same entity* but deliberately split by audience, so a
plain merge would leak DM-only truth into a published page.

**Signal:** nearly every inbound `[[leviathan]]` link means the **DM-truth** entity
(campaign-timeline, pearl-of-souls incursion, the-drowned-maw, vestra, auralis, the
other Plane-of-Water elementals). The truth is the primary referent; the legend is the
secondary, in-world version.

**Recommendation (DM to confirm):** keep the DM-truth page as the canonical `leviathan`
(it's what the graph points at) and rename the published legend to `leviathan-legend`
(or `leviathan-rumor`), keeping it `publish: true`. Do **not** fold the truth into the
published page. Alternatively, if section-level visibility is ever supported, one page
with a DM-only callout.

**Status:** OPEN — awaiting DM decision. Until then both pages stand; `[[leviathan]]`
resolves arbitrarily.

**Files**

Empirical combat data from sessions 03–04. Party punches above weight through coordination — bardic inspiration is the force multiplier.
After each combat; when encounter difficulty patterns become clear

# Combat Analytics — Shattered Sea

## Design Adjustments (Active Flags)

- Bardic inspiration is the party's force multiplier. Perrin's d6 repeatedly turned misses into hits and failed saves into passes. Design encounters where the inspiration economy matters — multiple saves per round, contested checks, AC breakpoints at +3–5 above average rolls.
- Crissdalynn's grapple is a dominant opener. Enemies with high contested Athletics/Acrobatics or Freedom of Movement effects counter this; enemies without it get locked down.
- Gloom Stalker in darkness is near-invisible ambush. Any encounter in darkness where enemies rely on darkvision gives Jean-Claude effective surprise. Counter: tremorsense, blindsight, or lit environments.

## Encounter Log

| Session | Encounter | CR/Difficulty | Rounds | PC Downs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 03 | Whip shark (open water) | ~CR 5 | 3 | 0 (JC badly wounded) | Crissdalynn lifted 60ft shark from water (shark nat 1 contest). JC arrow through anus. Party coordination strong. |
| 04 | Kyzil spar (non-lethal) | CR 14 | 3 | 0 (Delmar to 2 HP) | Designed as 4v1 survival test. Stat block held. Crissdalynn grappled R1 (Kyzil nat 1). Bardic inspiration saved two key moments. Delmar landed sneak attack through Empty Wing Parry via inspiration. |
| 04 | Grung sewer ambush | ~CR 2 total | 1 (ambush) | 0 | Jean-Claude instant-killed first Grung from ceiling (24 damage: Dread Strike). Crissdalynn clotheslined second. Ship destroyed by fire arrow to powder. Purple Grung captured via kingfisher dive. Entirely one-sided — party had surprise, darkness, and aerial advantage. |

## Patterns Observed

- **Party coordination is their biggest asset.** Bardic inspiration, flanking for sneak attack, grapple-to-advantage — they chain abilities across turns. Solo monsters without legendary actions get locked down fast.
- **Crissdalynn dominates physical contests.** Grapple, aerial pursuit (45ft fly), deflect attacks. She controls positioning. Enemies need ways to break grapple or deny flight.
- **Perrin is a combat multiplier, not a damage dealer.** Healing word, bardic inspiration, cutting words — all from behind cover while drumming. Targeting him is the smart tactical play. Kyzil identified this: "that drum is troubling."
- **Delmar is feast-or-famine.** High damage when sneak attack lands (17 damage through Empty Wing Parry), but misses often against high AC even with advantage. Luck points are a limited resource he burns fast.
- **Jean-Claude in darkness is lethal.** Gloom Stalker invisibility + ceiling movement + Dread Strike = ambush kills. In lit environments he loses his biggest advantage.
- **The party burns resources unevenly.** Perrin's spell slots and inspiration go fast. Delmar's luck points are gone by round 2. Crissdalynn's focus points and deflects are steady. Jean-Claude is resource-light.

## Calibration Notes

- CR 14 four-on-one held for exactly 3 rounds before the party would have trivialized it. For boss fights: CR 12–14 with legendary actions is the sweet spot for a tense 3–4 round encounter.
- Mook-tier enemies (CR 1/2 to CR 1) are ambush fodder. Don't run them straight — use terrain, numbers (6+), or environmental hazards to create challenge.
- The party lacks AoE damage. Clustered enemies are a valid pressure — they can't clear groups efficiently.

Agent quick reference for spotlighting and fairly pressuring Jean-Claude's darkness kit, Grung mobility, concentration, and moral triggers.

# Jean-Claude Primer

> Agent use: Read before building scenes or encounters that involve Jean-Claude darkness play, Grung instincts, slavery triggers, or poison constraints.

## Fast Read

- **Table role:** stealthy ranged controller who spikes in dim light/darkness.
- **Spotlight with:** dim light, water, vertical terrain, tight spaces, clustered enemies.
- **Pressure with:** bright magical light, blindsight/tremorsense, poison immunity, concentration breaks.
- **Avoid:** Restrained + bright light at the same time.

## Encounter Levers

- **Give them:** shadows, climb lines, water, Small-size routes, and clustered targets.
- **If struggling:** add dim light or an already blinded/restrained target.
- **If dominating:** spread enemies, add blindsight/tremorsense, use Daylight-equivalent light, or target concentration.
- **Avoid:** stacking hard shutdowns; choose one pressure axis at a time.

## Roleplay Levers

- **Escalates:** slavers, torture, active abuse, and Grung caste cruelty.
- **Uneasy around:** fast or threatening birds; use as texture, not a hard phobia.
- **Dramatic lever:** force a tactical choice between staying disciplined and stopping visible abuse.

## Power Spikes

| Level | Feature | Table Impact |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Extra Attack | Roughly doubles sustained ranged damage. |
| 5 | Tongue Lash combos | Adds positional control to attack turns. |
| 5 | Toxic Secretion | Passive contact poison becomes relevant. |

## Key Mechanics

| Ability / Factor | Use | Watch |
|---|---|---|
| Umbral Sight | Darkness can make him functionally unseen. | Full darkness hurts other PCs, especially Crissdalynn. |
| Entangle / concentration | Area control against clustered enemies. | INT/CHA saves and damage can break his plan. |
| Flask of Endless Water | Geyser: 30-ft line, STR DC 13, 1d4 + prone. | Useful for terrain and ledges; not his main DPR plan. |
| Prone targets | Helps melee allies. | Hurts his ranged attacks beyond 5 ft. |

Agent quick reference for spotlighting and fairly pressuring Perrin's ranged play, water mobility, avoidance, and family/patron hooks.

# Perrin Primer

> Agent use: Read before building scenes or encounters that involve Perrin ranged lanes, water mobility, avoidance, family pressure, or patron fallout.

## Fast Read

- **Table role:** evasive ranged caster with water mobility and avoidance instincts.
- **Spotlight with:** ranged lanes, water, tight spaces, social trickery, and escape routes.
- **Pressure with:** one STR grapple threat, concentration disruption, divided damage, strong WIS saves.
- **Avoid:** Frightened + Restrained stacks.

## Encounter Levers

- **Give them:** lanes to shoot, water where the cloak matters, and corridors that reward Boneless movement.
- **If struggling:** add prone targets, fragile allies to protect with Vicious Mockery, or a clean escape line.
- **If dominating:** disrupt concentration, split incoming damage, or use enemies with WIS +4 or better.
- **Avoid:** locking both movement and nerve at once.

## Roleplay Levers

- **Escalates:** threats to family standing, the Tangle, or his ability to keep moving.
- **Destabilizes:** [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] can trigger prey-response cowering.
- **Dramatic lever:** make him choose between running the con and telling the truth to his own people.

## Key Mechanics

| Factor | Use | Watch |
|---|---|---|
| Cloak water speed | Makes water scenes feel personal. | Do not make every water scene only about escape. |
| Boneless movement | Rewards tight corridors and awkward spaces. | Grapples still create real pressure. |
| Vicious Mockery | Protects fragile allies. | High-WIS enemies blunt the trick. |

## Related

- [[party-combat-primer|Party Combat Primer]]

# Player Interests — Shattered Sea

## Content Priority Queue

1. **Grung bombing plot / Jean-Claude's Simone connection** — highest engagement from JC's player, personal stakes, active deadline
2. **Umberlee / Pearl of Souls** — Delmar's player drove the entire confession and shrine scene with long-form RP
3. **Kyzil / pilgrimage thread** — Crissdalynn's player eager for martial identity content; spar was a highlight
4. **Festival (Il Gioco delle Beffe)** — party signed up; provides tonal relief and cover for the Grung plot
5. **Perrin's abyss / patron thread** — quieter this session but still active; the "Grow" thread hasn't advanced

## Per-Player Tracking

### Kaden — Perrin Black-Jaw

- **Engaged with:** supporting the party tactically (healing, inspiration, scouting), Nona/Passage relationship, species-aware social dynamics (avoided bringing owl to Rattkin venue), comic relief
- **Cold to:** nothing clearly cold yet; Perrin's own threads (abyss vision, patron) didn't advance this session but the player didn't resist them
- **Notes:** Perrin's player shows restraint and emotional intelligence — the "I know your pain" moment with Delmar was deliberately understated. Plays support in both combat and RP. Watch for his threads falling behind as JC and Delmar dominate.

### Sam — Delmar Fisk

- **Engaged with:** backstory vulnerability (confession scene was entirely player-driven monologue), negotiating with Umberlee (stood his ground against a god), slice-of-life tavern RP, tactical combat (sneak attack through bardic inspiration was a peak moment)
- **Cold to:** nothing observed
- **Notes:** Delmar's player drives social scenes and character vulnerability. Session 04 was his strongest RP session — the confession, the Umberlee negotiation, and the Crissdalynn reaction. Now abstaining from alcohol in-character. High investment in the Pearl plotline. "I see why you guys like rogues" — discovering combat identity.

### Jean-Claude's Player

- **Engaged with:** gear acquisition and optimization (drove shopping for 12+ minutes), the Grung investigation as a personal-stakes mission, tactical precision in the sewers, complex emotions around executing the purple Grung, the defector revelation (genuinely surprised), Kyzil tension (the "no threat" dismissal landed)
- **Cold to:** nothing observed — this player engages with everything
- **Notes:** Jean-Claude's player took full investigative lead on the Grung plot — directing marching order, reading signs, testing witnesses with physical evidence. The execution scene showed genuine character conflict between Grung identity and opposition to Simone. The defector concept opens a new personal arc. Festival joke: "I can poison someone and then go, ha ha ha."

### Crissdalynn's Player

- **Engaged with:** martial identity (eager for spar, spun staff when challenged), master-apprentice dynamic with Kyzil, combat dominance (the kingfisher dive was a table-wide celebration moment), protective instinct toward Delmar (leg sweep for going to Umberlee alone)
- **Cold to:** nothing clearly cold; quieter in investigation/social scenes
- **Notes:** Crissdalynn's player peaks in physical moments — the grapple, the kingfisher dive, the leg sweep. DM acknowledged "this fucking character." Perrin's player compared her to Goku. Combat is her spotlight; investigation is JC's.

## Recent Signals

### Session 04

- **JC drove shopping + Grung investigation.** Highest sustained engagement across two distinct activity types. The Grung plot is personal-stakes content and it shows.
- **Delmar drove confession + Umberlee negotiation.** Two of the session's biggest RP scenes were entirely Delmar-initiated. The abstinence flag is new character texture.
- **Crissdalynn dominated combat.** Grappled Kyzil (nat 1), kingfishered the purple Grung at 45ft fly speed. "Peak moments" player — design combat that gives her one signature move per fight.
- **Perrin played support + comic relief.** Bardic inspiration was the session's mechanical MVP. Healing kept the party alive through the spar. The taunting ("you'll have to catch me, see?") is his combat voice.
- **Kyzil/JC tension is real.** The "no threat" comment and dagger pin bothered JC's player at the character level. This is an interpersonal thread worth developing.
- **Boots of flying retcon** — Perrin's "I have little rat feet and I need to feel the ground" was a character-first mechanical decision. Players are prioritizing character identity over optimization.

### Session 03

- Perrin/abyss vision was high engagement — Kaden leaned in hard
- Delmar's water moment flagged but brief
- Crissdalynn/Kyzil reunion was emotional peak
- Nona meeting was strong for Perrin's player

# Alys Kuiper

![[Alys-Kuiper.webp|Alys Kuiper calmly inventorying the HCS Surety surgeon's cabinet]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Ship's Surgeon |
| **Wage** | 8 gp/week (surgeon rate) |

## Overview

Calm, slight, and currently in the medic's cabinet doing inventory. She finds this calming. Before any of this started, she reorganized the cabinet after a loose shelf tried to make itself her problem, then returned to dinner without mentioning it.

She discusses triage and recovery with clinical warmth — as if everyone in the room shares her comfort with medical detail. They do not, but she has never quite registered this.

She kept the Murrat casualties alive. She is precise about the limits of her own work: *"They pulled through because of him. I'll say that plainly."* She means [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]]. She does not know what that credit means, and she is not wrong to give it.

## Background

She served on a Crown frigate before the Surety. She says so when the topic comes up, then stops mid-sentence and moves to something else. She has not been pressed on it.

## Aboard Ship

She will announce, without particular inflection, that healer's kit supply is adequate for two more field engagements and that the surgical instruments are well-maintained except for one probe that needs replacing. She is not asking to stay. She is not asking to leave. She is performing the inventory because someone has to and she is the most qualified.

## Recruitment

She wants that fact acknowledged — that she is the most qualified, that this is a real post, that the Surgeon's Berth is a real facility and not a cabinet someone stocked once. Formally name the role — **Surgeon**, ship's medical officer, something that constitutes an actual position — and she stays.

If the party mentions they intend to keep the Surgeon's Berth staffed and stocked, she looks at the cabinet the way Holst looked at the hull: assessing what it could be.

> [!dm]
> She is the only trained surgeon in this crew. Without her, Beaumont's comment that "the cabinet is stocked but Alys has been handling things" becomes "nobody is handling things." She also fills the Surgeon's Berth bastion facility requirement the moment she's formally hired. The recruitment bar is low: just call it a real job.

## Connections

- [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]]
- [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]]
- [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]]

# Geoffrey Draves

![[portraits/Geoffrey-Draves.webp|Geoffrey Draves, a nineteen-year-old lean Dravosi deckhand and ship's carpenter]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human (Dravosi) |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Seaman |
| **Crew Role** | Carpenter |
| **Wage** | 6 gp/week (carpenter rate, no boarding duties) |

## Overview

He doesn't look like a turncoat.

Geoffrey Draves stands easy on deck, loose-limbed, not quite at rest, fidgeting with a length of rope that probably doesn't need doing. He's young, lean for a sailor, and his expression is the carefully neutral kind that takes practice to maintain.

During the boarding of the [[saltwright|Saltwright]], when the fight turned and the men around him went down faster than he could make sense of it, he dropped his sword.

[[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]]'s voice cut across the deck: *"I'll shoot you myself for that, turncoat."*

[[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] looked at him. "Would you rather fight for men who'll threaten to shoot you, or men who'll protect you?"

*"I'll do whatever keeps me alive today."* Delmar handed him his sword back. He was the party's first crew member — before they had a ship to put him on.

## Before the Sea

Geoffrey didn't choose the water. His father chose it for him. He was good at it, in the resigned way capable people are good at things they never wanted.

His father's connections produced a berth on the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] — not an officer's post, a carpenter's posting, plus marine duties on boarding operations for a supplement. Seven and a half gold a week, which sounded like progress. He has not yet done the full arithmetic. A rated marine earns fourteen gold weekly, plus the carpenter rate on top. [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] knew. Crew costs are operational line items. The arrangement was not an accident.

At night, below deck, in the gaps between watches, he danced. Contemporary movement, nimble and precise, the kind of dancing that has no place on a naval vessel. He was certain no one had ever seen him. On shore leave, someone did.

A young woman — [[verity-hollowell|Verity Hollowell]] — caught him mid-movement and didn't laugh. They spent that night dancing under open sky. They came close to a first kiss. Then the ship's bell called him back.

He returned to that same spot every time his ship made port. For years, she wasn't there. Then one evening, her father, [[cedric-hollowell|Cedric Hollowell]], was. The terms were simple: Geoffrey was not a man of means. Until he could provide for a wife and family for the rest of their days, he was not to see her again.

Geoffrey agreed. He didn't see another choice.

## The Vow

That conversation changed something in him. He stopped drifting and started calculating. The plan hardened into a single shape: earn enough as a sailor, become a professional dancer in the Grand Opera Halls, marry the woman he'd spent years trying to find again. The end would justify any means. He was prepared to sail with vagabonds if that was what it took.

It's been just shy of a year since he made that vow.

## His Carpentry

He can read a hull the way a good medic reads a patient: which seams need attention now, which can wait a week, which look fine but won't hold through the crossing being planned. If the party acquires a ship, Geoffrey can run actual maintenance — not patch-and-pray, but a real assessment of what the vessel needs and in what order, mostly done himself given materials and time.

With the party, his terms are carpenter only, six gold a week, no boarding duties.

# Noor

![[Noor.webp|Noor reading a sailing manual while working in the HCS Surety galley]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Ship's Cook (learning) |
| **Crew Role** | Cook |
| **Wage** | 4 gp/week (cook rate) |

## Overview

Fifteen, maybe. Was behind the water barrels the whole fight and has now emerged with the energy of someone who has been waiting to be useful. They had a sailing manual open and were reading it while standing up.

They know every sailing manual by heart. They have sailed on almost none of them. This gap between theory and experience is the thing they are most actively trying to close, and any ship going somewhere new is a better classroom than Port Tidefall.

[[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] referred to them obliquely as *"our guest below is useful in a galley"* — which is true. They learned from watching, which is how they learn everything.

## Aboard Ship

They are the easiest crew member to direct and the most likely to ask follow-up questions. They manage provisions, keep the galley running on voyages over three days, and do whatever else needs doing with genuine enthusiasm. They will check the manual for any situation they haven't encountered yet. If the situation isn't in the manual, they find this a point in its favor.

## Recruitment

They haven't decided where they're going and they want, more than anything, to be on a ship that goes somewhere interesting. Name any destination that isn't immediately familiar and they check the manual. If it's not in the manual, they look thoughtful in a way that means yes.

There is no bar to clear. They are already staying if anyone asks.

> [!dm]
> Noor is the most low-maintenance recruit in this crew. The only scenario where they leave is if the party explicitly names a destination so boring that even Noor's enthusiasm can't find a foothold — somewhere like "back to Port Tidefall, permanently." Any forward motion keeps them. They are not complicated. They are fifteen and they want to go somewhere.

- [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]]
- [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]]

# Old Faas

![[Old-Faas.webp|Old Faas calmly assessing the HCS Surety rigging from above deck]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Rated Bosun |
| **Crew Role** | Bosun / Rigger |
| **Wage** | 8 gp/week (bosun rate) |

## Overview

Old Faas is a rigger of uncertain age who has outlasted several captains, a number of ships, and at least two situations that should have killed him outright. He answers questions with short, accurate sentences. He does not raise his voice. Very little surprises him, and the things that do surprise him do not seem to bother him either.

He was the one who told the party about Murrat, flatly, between courses: *"He took us to Murrat. Wanted a live one. Went ashore with six crew. Four came back needing the surgeon."* He reported it the way you report a weather event you survived.

He returned from shore leave in [[calveno|Calveno]] with two peg legs.

## The Head

When Faas was seven years old, he fell from a hay loft and landed on his head on the stone floor of a barn. He was unconscious for three days. When he woke up, something was gone.

He does not experience fear. Not suppressed fear, not managed fear — simply absent, the way a man born without a sense of smell does not smell things. He will tell you this if you ask. He does not think it is interesting.

> [!dm]
> This is not a death wish. He is not trying to die; he simply cannot feel the thing that would stop him from doing dangerous things. No anxiety about heights, no dread when outnumbered, no instinct to flinch. He is not brave. Bravery requires something to overcome. He just goes ahead and does it.
>
> He has never mentioned this to a captain. It has never come up.

## The Legs

He returned from shore leave in [[calveno|Calveno]] with two well-fitted peg legs — good timber, brass ferrules, proper socket work. He is slightly shorter than he was. Slightly less stable standing still on a flat surface. He is faster on the rigging.

When asked about the legs, he has given three accounts:

**Account One:** *"The bull. Part of the festival. They were running it through the Mercatura and it got loose near the Bridge. The right leg. I stopped it. Eventually."*

**Account Two:** *"The scaffolding on the south side of the Bridge. The view from the top was better for watching the Beffa in Le Paludi. I could see it was not stable before I climbed. The left leg. I was correct about the view."*

**Account Three:** *"Both legs, actually. The canal under the Mercatura dock. I misjudged the depth. Current took me under the moorings and pinned me between the hull and the stone. Both legs. That was Tuesday."*

He has offered all three accounts to different people with identical conviction.

> [!dm]
> The party will never learn which story is real, if any. If directly confronted with all three stories at once, he will listen carefully, nod, and say: *"Ja. It was a busy week."*
>
> The peg legs do not slow him on the rigging. Do not explain it.

## Aboard Ship

He manages rigging, sails, and on-deck crew. He is the kind of bosun who doesn't raise his voice because the crew learned early that quiet from Faas means worse things than loud. He knows every line on this ship, what it should feel like under tension, and how long it has left.

He will go aloft in any weather. He has no strong opinion about staying or leaving. He is a sailor. There is a ship. That is sufficient.

## Session History

**Session 03 (transit):** Showed [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] the ropes during the five-day crossing to Calveno. Told stories about running cargo with [[barnaby-rook|Rook]] in his old days — an asset, given Rook's history of unusual cargo and contacts.

**Session 03 (dinner):** Told the party about the Murrat expedition flatly, between courses. Six crew went ashore with Rook to capture a live [[moucheron|Moucheron]]. Four came back needing the surgeon. Faas was not among those four. He offered this without prompting and did not elaborate.

**Shore Leave — Calveno:** Returned to the ship with two peg legs. Gave three contradictory accounts of how he lost them over the course of one week. Went back up the rigging approximately forty minutes after returning aboard.

Lean shipwright who catalogues damage without being asked and stays if someone demonstrates they understand the difference between a caulked seam and a packed one.
The shipwright who sees hull damage the way a doctor sees symptoms — as information, not drama — and whose professional opinions are always correct and sometimes annoying.

# Sem Holst

![[Sem-Holst.webp|Sem Holst inspecting a hull seam in the HCS Surety lower deck]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Carpenter's Mate |
| **Crew Role** | Carpenter's Mate (assists [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]]) |
| **Wage** | 4 gp/week |

## Overview

Lean, weathered, sawdust still in his hair. He takes in the party the way he'd take in a cracked frame: assessing damage, not people. He fixes things without being asked and has opinions about how they should have been built in the first place.

He is already cataloguing damage [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] didn't mention. He will tell you exactly what's wrong with this hull and exactly how long it will take to fix, and he will not soften either number.

## Aboard Ship

He works alongside [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] and does not resent the reporting line. He is more specialized — hull structure and planking — and he knows it. If the ship takes significant hull damage and both are working, repairs go faster and come out better.

He does not make small talk. He makes assessments. If you ask him how the ship is, he will tell you, in structural terms, with time estimates.

## Recruitment

He wants to know if the party is serious about maintaining the vessel — not what it can do, but the ship itself. If a PC demonstrates they know the difference between a caulked seam and a packed one, or asks a question about the hull that isn't about speed or cargo, he reconsiders.

*"Not many privateers bother learning that."* He says it the way you admit something surprised you. That's the moment. He's in.

> [!dm]
> Any PC with proficiency in carpenter's tools, navigator's tools, or a relevant background (sailor, marine) can make this approach credibly. Asking a specific question about the Surety's current hull condition — and listening to the answer — clears the bar. He doesn't need expertise. He needs evidence of interest.

## Session History

**Session 03 (transit):** Worked hull repairs alongside [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] during the five-day crossing to Calveno. JC cast Mending; Sem quietly fixed what JC missed without commenting on it.

**Shore Leave — Calveno:** First morning ashore he was at the dry dock where the *Uncertainty* is being repainted. Found a problem in the forward keel joint — a fatigued timber hiding under fresh caulk, the kind the repaint covered without addressing. Fixable before departure, but needs hardwood stock and at least a day of dry dock access. He documented it in his own notes. Nobody asked him to. He has not mentioned it to the party yet and will not until someone asks him about the ship.

Former Crown Shipyards blacksmith turned naval gunner — the best man at a cannon the party is likely to meet, who will not tell them that unless someone asks. Holds a master's degree in chemistry that he has never mentioned because it has not come up.

# Thunk

![[Thunk.webp|Thunk, a warm orc gunner with scarred smith hands, standing beside a cannon aboard the HCS Surety]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Orc |
| **Post** | Formerly [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]], under [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] |
| **Rank** | Rated Gunner |
| **Crew Role** | Gunner |
| **Wage** | 8 gp/week (gunner rate) |

## Overview

He is the largest man on the ship and also the most pleased to see you.

Thunk stands at the stern gun with the ease of someone who has been in this spot a long time and found it agreeable. His hands are the tell: huge, knuckled, cross-hatched with scars from knowing exactly where a hot surface is and touching it slightly wrong a predictable number of times. He keeps them clean. He cares about his tools.

When the party finds him: *"Ah. You are the new crew, ja?"* He nods. *"Very good fight. I heard it from here. The explosions — very nice."*

He is complimenting them sincerely. He found the explosions impressive. He is not concerned that this is the primary thing he noticed.

## Before the Sea

> [!dm]
> Thunk holds a master's degree in chemistry from his homeland. His homeland has a recognizable academic tradition; it is simply not recognized in the Shattered Sea, and he has not volunteered the information because it has not come up.
>
> He talks the way he talks because everyone from home talks that way. It is not a register of intelligence. The party has clocked the accent and the size and the warmth and concluded something about him. They are wrong.

He worked the Crown Shipyards at Port Tidefall for eleven years — cannon casting first, then fitting, then repairs on pieces that had come back bent in interesting ways. He was the one they called when a breach looked like a metallurgy problem rather than an operator problem. He received a commendation from the Crown Ordnance Office in his sixth year, which he kept in a tin.

*"The sea,"* he will explain to anyone who asks, *"she is very loud. I cannot sleep sometimes."* This is literal. He found it pleasant. Eventually he decided that indicated something.

## His Gunnery

He counts as two crew when manning a ship weapon. He runs the loading cycle at a pace that assumes a second loader who consistently isn't there. He compensates. He has always compensated.

He also has opinions about powder. He smells a charge and says it is wrong, or right, or almost. He is correct more often than anyone who can explain their reasoning. He will share his opinions if asked and will be unable to justify any of them beyond *"I don't know — she just smells like that."*

Then, in the same breath, without registering the shift, he will tell you that black powder is made from saltpeter, nitrogen, and carbon — dense carbon chains — that it is a flammable explosive and not shock-sensitive, meaning friction and impact will not set it off; it requires fire, always fire. He offers this the way another man might mention the weather.

> [!dm]
> When Thunk mans a cannon or ship weapon, he counts as two crew for the purpose of determining how many weapons can be manned simultaneously.
>
> He is proficient with smith's tools and can operate a Smithy facility without additional staff. He will have views on how it should be organized. He will be correct about all of them.
>
> **The gimmick:** Thunk reads as a one-note joke — enormous, warm, slightly dim, very good at cannons. Drop the depth whenever it feels natural: a correct physics observation, an unexpected metallurgy note, a precise stoichiometry comment. He never signals that it's remarkable. The reveal, if the party ever gets there, is not that he's secretly smart — it's that he was always this, and they misread him from the start.

## Session History

**Session 03 (transit):** Taught [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] the guns. The lesson was thorough — correct breakdown of black powder composition, ignition principle, non-shock-sensitive mechanics. Jean-Claude left gun-proficient.

**Shore Leave — Calveno:** Went to a Mercatura tavern with [[sem-holst|Sem Holst]] and Jean-Claude, paid for the drinks. The next morning went to the Arsenal district alone. Stood at the quay gates long enough to identify a bad mounting bracket on a Crown ordnance barge — wrong casting angle on the pivot collar, will crack on the third or fourth sustained firing. Told a dock hand. The dock hand wrote nothing down. Thunk left. He is not certain anyone will fix it before it matters. He feels fine about this.

Gnome naturalist and author of Clyde's Bestiary of Oceanic Creatures — four feet of impeccable dress and documented contempt for every creature he's spent his life studying.
Werner Herzog doing the job of David Attenborough — rigorous, meticulous, accurate; his contempt is the fuel, not the product.

# Algernon Reginald Clyde

![[Clyde.webp|Argibald Reginald Clyde, an elderly gnome scholar, standing on wet docks with a book and walking stick]]

---

|                |                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Species**    | Gnome                                                        |
| **Role**       | Naturalist, author                                           |
| **Known For**  | *[[clydes-bestiary-of-oceanic-creatures|Clyde's Bestiary of Oceanic Creatures]]* |
| **Currently**  | Book tour — Port Tidefall, [[kalowe|Kalowe]], [[calveno|Calveno]] |
| **Status**     | Not yet encountered                                          |

---

## Overview

A.R. Clyde is a gnome naturalist in his late sixties and the author of *[[clydes-bestiary-of-oceanic-creatures|Clyde's Bestiary of Oceanic Creatures]]*, a multi-volume survey of oceanic fauna that has become the standard reference text for maritime creature identification across the Scatter. The work is meticulous, accurate, and suffused throughout with a contempt for its subject matter that readers have broadly agreed improves it.

He is currently on book tour promoting Volume II. He did not want to do the tour. He is doing it because his publisher correctly identified that a gnome who visibly despises every creature he has spent his life documenting is, commercially speaking, an asset, and Clyde could not produce a compelling counter-argument.

He is not on tour. He is conducting field outreach to an at-risk population. The distinction matters to him enormously.

## Appearance & Manner

Four feet nothing in good boots. Impeccably dressed — jacket brushed, collar straight — in a way that reads less as vanity and more as a decision made long ago that the field would not have him looking like he belongs there. His complexion is pale, wind-reddened across the nose and cheeks from decades of maritime exposure he resents on a cellular level. Silver hair kept short and precisely parted.

He carries a leather satchel at all times: notebooks, a portable inkwell, a quill wrapped in oilcloth against the humidity. Ink has worked itself permanently into the knuckles of his right hand. His left has a small crescent scar along the thumb. He changed the subject when asked about it.

## The Bestiary

The project began as a commission in his early thirties — a financial gap he has never specified, three months of coastal documentation, standard rates. He finished it. His publisher wanted more. He said yes, and then yes again, and somewhere in the writing of the second volume he understood that what he was building was not a reference text. It was a record.

His prose makes his position clear. He treats evolutionary features as moral failures. He describes the ocean's indifference to its own creatures not as neutral fact but as the only good thing about it. Sailors are his primary intended audience — the people most likely to benefit from accurate identification of things that will destroy their ships — and they have received the work accordingly. Volume I sold. Volume II is selling.

He hates frogs most of all.

## What He's Documented

- **[[sawek|Sawek]]** — documented personally at [[kalowe|Kalowe]]; measured a dead specimen pulled from a blue hole by seven divers; found the experience professionally satisfying and personally grim
- **[[whip-shark|Whip Shark]]** — documented from hull damage and survivor accounts; has never seen a live specimen; considers this an acceptable outcome
- **[[leviathan|Leviathan]]** — Ch. 13, Volume II; the one entry that gave him genuine difficulty, not from contempt but from uncertainty; he finds this more unsettling than the creature itself
- **[[ridgeback|Ridgeback]]** — Ch. 9, Volume II; documented entirely from survivor accounts; the only entry he has concluded with practical advice, which he resents
- **[[krakling|Krakling]]** — Ch. 10, Volume II; documented from Kalowe dock reports and two days of survivor interviews he describes as the low point of the project

## On Tour

Seventeen copies sold in three days across Port Tidefall. He has had the same argument at every port — the Scatter's relationship with its marine life, the naming traditions, the evident fondness — and he finds it professionally baffling and personally exhausting.

He is easy to find at the docks. He is usually the one in an argument about someone's pet.

# Bala Tane

|               |                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Species**   | Orc                            |
| **Pronouns**  | she/her                        |
| **Location**  | [[the-mud-pits|The Mud Pits]], [[kalowe|Kalowe]] |
| **Role**      | Pit boss                       |

---

An orc woman in her mid-forties, built like she has been absorbing impacts for a long time and found it agreeable. She does not fight anymore — she makes matches. The distinction matters to her and she will explain it to you once if you imply otherwise.

She announces each match the way you would announce a coronation: full name, island of origin if she knows it, and a one-sentence description of the fighter's most notable quality, which is always accurate and occasionally unkind. Then she goes completely still. She does not cheer. She does not react. She watches the way a chart clerk watches a ledger — tracking, not feeling. When a fighter is down and staying down, she says "done" in the same voice she uses for everything else, and the crowd knows it is over.

Her read on a matchup is flawless. She does not make fair fights. She makes interesting ones.

## Role

Pit boss of [[the-mud-pits|The Mud Pits]] on Kalowe's third island. Controls entry, makes the matchups, manages the betting runners, and decides when a fight is over. Her rulings are final and have never been seriously contested, which is not a coincidence. She has run it for fifteen years; the harbour bosses treat her as a peer.

Bisou is a small capuchin monkey who has ridden [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]]'s left shoulder for the full eleven years he has run the Midchain route. She is not a pet in any passive sense. She moves with precision and purpose, makes decisions quickly, and has zero hesitation about stealing the pipe from the corner of Beaumont's mouth. He corrects this with the weary patience of a man who has lost this argument many times.

Her tail stays looped once around his neck when she is settled. She goes where he goes.

## Appearance & Manner

Small, dark-furred, with bright amber eyes that are more expressive than most animals allow themselves to be. Quick movements and quick decisions. She tilts her head at things that interest her. When something interests her, you will know.

She is not decorative. She watches. She steals with absolute confidence — the pipe most often, but she is not selective. When Beaumont needs her to be still, she is still. The shift is immediate and complete.

She has an opinion about coin tricks. The results depend on how good the trick is.

## Combat Maneuvers

Bisou is an extension of Beaumont's tactics, not a passenger:

- **The Kalowe Maneuver** — Beaumont tosses her alongside a healing potion to a downed ally; she uncorks and administers it.
- **The Calveno Maneuver** — She carries an alchemical item to a target point, triggers it, and clears the blast radius.
- **The Tidefall Maneuver** — Beaumont tosses her toward a target; she uses 20 ft. of movement to locate and soak any exposed black powder, rendering powder weapons inoperable before the next shot.

## Session History

**Session 01:** Beaumont threw Bisou through a gun port on the HCS Surety to neutralize the cannons. She pissed in the powder. The cannons did not fire.

**Session 02:** Systematically removed 15 gp of shinies from the Surety's inventory before Beaumont called her back. Showed no remorse. He treated it as fair business. The party did not dispute it.

# Cap'n Gorgeous

![[portraits/Capn-Gorgeous-Archer.webp|Cap'n Gorgeous, a striking golden-haired Dravosi enforcer in a dark naval coat, holding a heavy crossbow in the HCS Surety's hold]]

*Real name unknown. It didn't come up.*

|                 |                                                |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **Species**     | Human (Dravosi)                                |
| **Role**        | Enforcer, HCS Surety; hold inspection detail   |
| **Status**      | Deceased — Session 01, Phase 1                 |

---

He was the Dravosi enforcer [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] sent down the ladder first. Heavy crossbow, tight hold, five strangers in the dark — standard inspection procedure. He'd probably done it a hundred times.

The party put him down before he realized he stepped into the trap. One poison-tipped arrow through his shoulder, one musket blast to the chest at point blank range, and his shattered kneecap. Simultaneous. He never acted. He never shouted. He hit the deck.

His crewmates had taken to calling him Cap'n Gorgeous. They shouted it when he went down.

## Appearance

The nickname wasn't ironic. Athletic build that made the hold feel smaller when he walked into it, long golden hair that moved like he was perpetually in a sea breeze, a jawline that belonged on a coin, pale blue eyes sharp enough that you noticed them even in poor light.

He looked like the kind of man who wins fights just by showing up.

## House Knighton

He wore a House Knighton crest on his coat. [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] recognized it immediately; his crewmates probably had no idea what that meant.

House Knighton has served the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] since its founding and has accrued corresponding leverage. [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]] will hear that his son died aboard a Crown patrol vessel now missing from Tidefall. He will send people — not the Crown navy, his own — to find out what happened and to whom.

The party does not know his real name. It will surface eventually.

Crown-licensed import factor in Port Tidefall and Verity's father — set the financial terms that sent Geoffrey away, has a ledger problem he may or may not know about, and keeps making introductions his daughter keeps not concluding.

# Cedric Hollowell

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human (Dravosi) |
| **Role** | Crown-licensed import factor |
| **Location** | [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] |

## Overview

Cedric Hollowell runs a mid-tier import agency out of offices near the Tidefall inspection pier. Thirty years in Crown commercial licensing has made him fluent in the language of fees, delays, and expedited resolution. He is not corrupt in any dramatic sense — he is simply a man who has spent his career understanding that every transaction has a price and every relationship has a use, and who applies this logic to his family with the same unsentimental efficiency he applies to cargo.

When a sailor kept returning to a dock near his property, he made inquiries, assessed the situation, and set terms. He was not wrong that Geoffrey Draves had no money and no prospects. The terms were calibrated to seem fair while being practically unachievable on patrol cutter wages. He does not think about this distinction.

His daughter [[verity-hollowell|Verity]] runs his secondary accounts better than anyone he has hired. He considers this settled. What is not settled is her refusal to conclude any of the introductions he arranges, which is becoming a logistical problem as much as a personal one.

## Terms & Manner

He speaks the way someone speaks when they have been negotiating with Crown inspectors for thirty years: precise, patient, and never the first to name what something is actually worth. He does not raise his voice. He restates his position more clearly when challenged rather than backing down.

He is not hostile to the party by default — he is a factor, and factors are useful to people moving cargo through Tidefall. He will help if there is a reason to help and a reasonable accounting for it.

> *"My daughter is an excellent account manager. I'm sure whatever brought you here can be addressed through the appropriate channel."*

> *"The terms I set were reasonable. A man who cannot meet them in three years cannot meet them in ten. That is arithmetic, not cruelty."*

> [!dm]
> **The ledger problem:** [[verity-hollowell|Verity]] has found a gap in his primary accounts — bonded cargo moved through Hollowell licensing without a manifest entry. Whether he placed it there or someone exploited his credentials is unresolved. If the party knows before he does, that is leverage. If he is managing it quietly, he is in a worse position than he appears.

## Relationships

- [[verity-hollowell|Verity Hollowell]] — daughter; runs his secondary accounts
- [[aldous-draves|Aldous Draves]] — knows him; set Geoffrey's berth terms in coordination

## Pressure Points

- Geoffrey's claim on Verity tests Cedric's terms and his sense of standing.
- The missing manifest entry can turn him from gatekeeper into liability.

Beautiful siren-like elf. Her voice stops people mid-conversation. It was already in her — she learned to weaponize it. Joins after the first arc.

## Personality

Wants an audience. Wants to be listened to, to matter, to not have the world ignore her. What she actually wants: to go home safely, acceptance, apologies, her music recognized. Fairly immature (young for an elf). Doesn't know the history of her salvaged trident. Treats beggars, servants, and children with respect.

**Red line:** Will not mess with dolphins or other marine mammals.
**Red button:** Her animal friends in danger, AND being talked over simultaneously. Take both at once and she stops thinking.

## Faith

Raised to follow Deep Sashelas. Admires Umberlee for her absolute control and authority over her domain — wants that kind of certainty.

## Mechanics

Sorcerer/Bard multiclass. Innate magical gift weaponized through training. Produces music and magical effects beyond what her voice alone could explain (the full scope of this is a secret). Trident salvaged from a downed ship (origin unknown to her).

## Active Situations

- **Self-exile from Halythion** — left before the evaluation could force a conclusion; a Council hearing presumably still waits. She has not gone back.
- **Incomplete Aoidos title** — the title and its obligations are unresolved; carries it by default
- **The hermit crab** — she owes it a good shell; still looking
- **Flappers** — out chasing mackerel; does not know where Coralyra is

## What She's Carrying

- A trident salvaged from a downed ship she never knew the name of (magical, origin unknown to her)
- Her voice (the weapon and the wound)
- The hermit crab debt

## Backstory

Raised in [[halythion|Halythion]]. Liked, comfortable, normal. Told her music was disturbing people and she needed evaluation — she left before that happened. Worst thing: got inked by a [[sawek|Sawek]]. Worst thing she's done: accidentally made a hermit crab homeless.

## Key Relationships

- [[flappers-the-seal|Flappers the Seal]] — closest relationship; whose opinion matters most; currently chasing mackerel
- Sea turtles — the creatures she'd trust with her life

## Connections

- [[halythion|Halythion]] — home she left
- [[flappers-the-seal|Flappers the Seal]]
- [[sawek|Sawek]] — marked her
- [[umberlee|Umberlee]] — admired (not worshipped)

Midchain first mate, sole survivor of the Cormorant wreck; drinking at The Flat Water in Kalowe, looking for divers to recover the captain's strongbox.

# Davu Kamu

Mixed Midchain heritage, late thirties, former first mate of the *Cormorant*. The sloop went down three months ago on the reef shelf southwest of Kalowe — he survived; the captain didn't.

He drinks steadily rather than heavily and talks in the careful way of someone who knows he is leaving things out. He's been at [[the-flat-water|The Flat Water]] for two months, savings spent, offering 30% of whatever is recovered from the wreck. He has the captain's strongbox key. He has not mentioned that the captain's widow in Tidefall has a legal claim to the contents.

If confronted about the rubies' real value (he's underselling them): *"I needed someone to say yes."*

See [[kalowe-merrows-prize|Kalowe — The Merrow's Prize]] for full situation mechanics.

## Overview

Barely twenty, uniform almost still correct, quill already out before he's fully through the door. He had the boarding manifests sorted by date before anyone asked him to. He hadn't noticed doing it yet.

He served the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] — Crown-trained navigator, chart work, reef avoidance, Maw crossings. Competent without being exceptional. He had nowhere particular to go when the ship made port and was quietly aware of it.

## Aboard Ship

He gravitated to the chart table. This is where he was useful and he knew it. He would produce organized, legible logs, update manifests, and flag navigation problems before they became navigation crises — in a tone of mild apology, as if the reef was his fault.

Under pressure he did paperwork. This was not a coping mechanism — it was simply how his mind organized chaos. The paperwork was always correct.

Black jaguar tabaxi bodyguard for Nona Black-Jaw. Impeccable suit, polished claws, lit cigar. The most dangerous person in the room who will not be the first one to speak.

# Enzo

|               |                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Species**   | Tabaxi (Jaguar)                                         |
| **Pronouns**  | he/him                                                  |
| **Location**  | [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]], [[warren|The Warren]]          |
| **Role**      | Bodyguard, [[the-passage|The Passage]] / Black-Jaw Run  |

---

Enzo does not threaten. He holds doors, pulls chairs, and keeps a lit cigar balanced in two fingers for the duration of any meal [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] is hosting. The cigar is a timer — it burns whether the conversation is going well or not. When it has burned down far enough and Nona is still waiting for an answer, he sets it on the edge of the table and unsheathes one claw. That is generally all it takes.

His sentence, delivered with complete politeness: *"Nona asked you a question."*

## Appearance & Manner

Medium-built black jaguar tabaxi — obsidian fur with rosette patterning visible when light catches it, broken by a long pale scar across the left side of his jaw. Dark tailored suit, collar buttoned tight, shoes mirror-polished. Claws maintained to a shine.

He does not raise his voice. He does not hurry. He stands slightly behind and to Nona's right, weight on his back foot, one hand always free.

At the table, he reads guests faster than [[ruk|Ruk]] does and communicates his read through small signals — a tap of the cigar, a shift of weight, a glance at Nona. If he moves between a guest and Nona, the conversation is over.

He is comfortable with people. He is more comfortable with violence.

## Session Events

- **Session 03:** Present in Nona's kitchen in Le Paludi when Perrin arrived. Leaned against the far wall. After Nona met with the party, she sent Enzo to arrange consolation for the Vestra's surviving crew and to call off the attacks she'd set in motion against [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]].
- **Session 04:** Opened the door at Nona's safe house, growled at the party before letting them in. Nona dispatched him with reinforcements after receiving the Grung bombing intel via sending stone.

Enzo does not threaten. He holds doors, pulls chairs, and keeps a lit cigar balanced in two fingers for the duration of any meal Nona is hosting. The cigar is a timer — it burns whether the conversation is going well or not. When it has burned down far enough and Nona is still waiting for an answer, he sets it on the edge of the table and unsheathes one claw. That is generally all it takes.

His sentence, delivered with complete politeness: “Nona asked you a question.”

Appearance & Manner

Medium-built black jaguar tabaxi — obsidian fur with rosette patterning visible when light catches it, broken by a long pale scar across the left side of his jaw. Dark tailored suit, collar buttoned tight, shoes mirror-polished. Claws maintained to a shine.

He does not raise his voice. He does not hurry. He stands slightly behind and to Nona’s right, weight on his back foot, one hand always free.

At the table, he reads guests faster than Ruk does and communicates his read through small signals — a tap of the cigar, a shift of weight, a glance at Nona. If he moves between a guest and Nona, the conversation is over.

He is comfortable with people. He is more comfortable with violence.

Session Events

  • Session 03: Present in Nona’s kitchen in Le Paludi when Perrin arrived. Leaned against the far wall. After Nona met with the party, she sent Enzo to arrange consolation for the Vestra’s surviving crew and to call off the attacks she’d set in motion against Perrin.
  • Session 04: Opened the door at Nona’s safe house, growled at the party before letting them in. Nona dispatched him with reinforcements after receiving the Grung bombing intel via sending stone.

Heavyset, grey, and possessed of the deeply settled quality of a man who has not moved quickly in fifteen years and sees no reason to start. He runs the [[hook-and-ledger|Hook & Ledger]] with the mild authority of someone who has outlasted seven garrison commanders and three harbourmasters and expects to outlast several more.

He has opinions on the current state of the Strait, on proper manifest procedure, on the declining quality of the cask wine, and on whoever sat at the corner table last Tuesday and left without paying. He will share all of these opinions in sequence if you give him half an opening. He considers this hospitality.

If a Crown officer asks him something he does not want to answer, he answers a different question with great thoroughness.

Margaret "Maggie" Porcelain Pots is a dragonborn potter whose family has fired ceramics on their home island for three generations. She uses her fire breath to feed the kilns. Her work is exclusive, beautiful, and extraordinarily durable. She is an absolute sweetheart to everyone she meets and takes no shit from anyone, and there is no contradiction there.

She is [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]]'s first love. They were together for a couple of years before his wanderlust ended it badly — with an argument she punctuated by leaving him with a shiner that lasted a week. He has avoided his home island ever since. The shiner is locally famous. She has never felt the need to explain it.

## Appearance & Manner

Dragonborn, peach-and-cream scales and vibrant pink eyes. She usually has clay somewhere on her — on her hands, at her wrist, occasionally somewhere less explicable. She wipes her hands before a handshake whether or not they're dirty.

## Her Work

Three generations of her family have fired pottery on this island. Maggie is the latest, and she is very good at it. The pieces are not cheap and are not meant to be — they last. She uses her fire breath to feed the kilns directly. She is currently expanding the operation and scouting locations on other islands. Her work travels further than she does, but that is beginning to change.

> [!dm]
> If she appears: the reunion would feel like both gift and threat for Delmar. She'd dislike his musket-wife on instinct — but once she hears the shiner story, she'd befriend her quickly.

A large man, round and red-faced, who takes up a chair the way water takes up a glass — completely, without apology. The former Dravosi uniform is long gone; he wears a merchant's coat, good quality, the buttons straining at the middle. He laughs often and loudly, a half-second before the punchline, like his body can't wait.

He ran the Midchain patrol route for over a decade and knew every merchant captain on it by name and preference. His method was effective: a meal, a drink, a good story, and a willingness to find that the manifest was in order. He was removed from the route shortly before Session 01 — officially retired, no ceremony. He did not ask too many questions about why. He knows the answer. He now keeps a table at a dockside tavern in Port Tidefall and eats well and talks often and never mentions the route.

The arrangement he ran was corrupt and known — but it was predictable, human-scaled, and survivable. What replaced him is none of those things.

# Pell

> *A gnome who died trying to be free.*

| | |

| **Species** | Gnome |

| **Status** | Deceased |

## Overview

Pell was a labour slave on [[sorn|Sorn]] and the person who made [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] understand that the Grung caste order was not the only possible shape of the world.

## Appearance & Manner

Slight even for a gnome. Deep-brown skin, a tight braid kept behind one ear, calloused hands. Small in the way of someone who had spent years making herself smaller than she was — but the eyes gave her away. Too steady, too still.

## Who She Was

Pell talked to Jean-Claude as if he were a person — not an authority, not a threat, not a caste above her. In fragments of conversation stolen between her work and his guard duty, she told him things he had never heard said aloud: that she had come from somewhere else, that the world outside the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] was full of peoples who had built differently.

She never told him what to think. She just described what she had seen, and waited to see what he did with it.

The night before everything went wrong, she told him that every race has something the others lack, and that the only way to grow is to reach across that gap. He has been trying to prove her right ever since.

## The Plan and Its End

Jean-Claude proposed faking her death and smuggling her west. She said yes.

He walked to his parents' hut on what felt like the best day of his life. He walked in and found his parents, his sister [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]], and Pell already in chains. Simone had told them everything.

**Thirty-one days.** Pell died in a cell beneath [[sorn|Sorn]] while Jean-Claude was already in open water, already free. She died not knowing whether he had made it.

> [!dm]
> Dead before the campaign began. No appearance possible unless flashback, memory, or supernatural contact. His weight is carried entirely by Jean-Claude. The count of thirty-one days is the number JC carries.

- [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]] — his closest friend; JC carries his death
- [[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]] — Simone's betrayal put her in chains
- [[sorn|Sorn]] — where she died
- [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]]

Lizardfolk bodyguard for Nona Black-Jaw. Massive, scarred, incapable of pretending not to notice things. He understands Nona because he understands hatchlings.

# Ruk

|               |                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Species**   | Lizardfolk                                              |
| **Pronouns**  | he/him                                                  |
| **Location**  | [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]], [[warren|The Warren]]          |

---

Ruk understands four things: territory, loyalty, feeding rituals, and the defense of hatchlings. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] touches all four. He does not need to understand the politics to understand who she is, and he has decided she is worth protecting with his body.

He cannot pretend not to notice things. This is not a skill gap — it is a philosophical position. If someone is lying, he says so. If something smells wrong, he names it. Nona has found this useful for twenty years and has learned to manage the timing.

> *"He is lying. I can smell the fear-sweat. Also, he looked left before answering."*
>
> *"Ruk, darling, we accuse guests after dessert."*

## Appearance & Manner

Large for a lizardfolk — broad through the chest, scarred across both forearms and the left side of his neck where the scales have grown back lighter and rough. Dark olive-green with darker banding. He sits with his back to the wall, hands on the table, and watches every door.

He is not unfriendly. He is literal. He is more likely to offer someone food than to threaten them — but the threat is clearly available if the food is declined badly.

At the table, [[enzo|Enzo]] manages social reads; Ruk manages physical ones. Ruk's job is presence — he is the reason nobody tries anything.

If combat starts, he moves to put himself between Nona and whatever is moving toward her.

RoleBodyguard, Black-Jaw Run

Ruk understands four things: territory, loyalty, feeding rituals, and the defense of hatchlings. Nona touches all four. He does not need to understand the politics to understand who she is, and he has decided she is worth protecting with his body.

He cannot pretend not to notice things. This is not a skill gap — it is a philosophical position. If someone is lying, he says so. If something smells wrong, he names it. Nona has found this useful for twenty years and has learned to manage the timing.

“He is lying. I can smell the fear-sweat. Also, he looked left before answering.”

“Ruk, darling, we accuse guests after dessert.”

Appearance & Manner

Large for a lizardfolk — broad through the chest, scarred across both forearms and the left side of his neck where the scales have grown back lighter and rough. Dark olive-green with darker banding. He sits with his back to the wall, hands on the table, and watches every door.

He is not unfriendly. He is literal. He is more likely to offer someone food than to threaten them — but the threat is clearly available if the food is declined badly.

At the table, Enzo manages social reads; Ruk manages physical ones. Ruk’s job is presence — he is the reason nobody tries anything.

If combat starts, he moves to put himself between Nona and whatever is moving toward her.

# Sera Maddock

Old privateer. Compact and wheezing, very still. Seventy-one years old. Three days from dead by Ilaria Grimaldi's estimate — lung sickness, treatable in Tidefall, not in Kalowe. She makes eye contact the way someone does who has spent a career reading strangers fast.

She ran Dravosi-licensed privateer work forty years ago. Her crew buried a cache on [[orak|Orak]] from one of those runs and she is the last one alive who knows where. Half the chart is tattooed on her left forearm. She burned the other half when the man she was going to share it with tried to sell her to the Crown.

She is not sentimental about the money. She would rather someone get it than it rot under a rock. Her one requirement is leaving Kalowe.

**Deal:** 200 gp and passage out (not to Tidefall — she wants a healer city with the right herbalist). The forearm tattoo is worth the price.

**Location:** [[grimaldis-dispensary|Grimaldi's Dispensary]], back room — see [[kalowe-captains-map|Kalowe — The Captain's Map]].

A tiger tabaxi fighter, shrine guardian, and former passenger aboard the [[saltwright|Saltwright]]. His tribe watched the sea go wrong and sent their strongest hunter west to find the cause.

He is not subtle. He's not a diplomat. Where most sailors deal with problems by talking their way around them, Stripes looks built to stand in the middle and not move.

## Backstory

Stripes comes from [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]], one of five small islands around the Blue Hole at the heart of the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]]. His tribe has guarded a primal shrine of [[umberlee|Umberlee]] for generations. When the sea around the Blue Hole started going wrong, the elders sent their strongest hunter west.

He bartered passage aboard the [[saltwright|Saltwright]] with [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] and has not been home since.

The Keth-Naar accent — clipped consonants, a slight Germanic lilt — marks him immediately as someone from somewhere else.

## Character

Stripes is a showoff. Spends voyages performing for the crew — climbing rigging, demonstrating shots, showing off the [[bracers-of-archery|bracers]], narrating his own maneuvers with obvious satisfaction.

Fifties, broad even for an orc, efficient. Suryo has spent thirty years watching captains make bad supply decisions and has made peace with offering the right answer once. He works fast and talks at the same speed — no flourish, no softening. He knows exactly how long a given crew complement can run on a given number of stores and will say so directly if an order is short, in terms that are precise rather than unkind. He extends credit to captains he has dealt with three times or more — handshake terms, no ledger, specific memory.

Sixties, grey-green scaled, unhurried. Taufa wears his authority lightly and his accounting precisely. He has survived two generations in Kalowe's port trade by being useful to people on both sides of the ledger and forgettable to all of them. Lizardfolk flat affect works in his favour here: he asks no unnecessary questions and registers no personal reaction to the answers.

He knows every ship that has bought rope from him and what they used it for in general terms; he does not keep a book on specifics and will say so plainly if asked. If he doesn't stock something, he'll name who might — once, no elaboration.

## Role

Proprietor of [[taufa-fifita-and-sons|Taufa Fifita & Sons]], Kalowe's primary chandlery. Two adult sons work the back storeroom; they are not introduced by name. The family also runs [[fifitas-slip|Fifita's Slip]] on the lagoon side — his son [[noa-fifita|Noa]] operates it — which Taufa does not discuss from behind the counter.

# Aldo Riva

> *"Allora — you want to know about this fish? She came in this morning. I can tell by the gills. Sit down, I'll explain."*

## Overview

Aldo Riva runs the kitchen at [[al-fondale|Al Fondale]] and has been doing so for twenty-two years, since he and [[bice-riva|Bice]] bought the place from the previous owner. He is stocky, white-haired, and has flour on his forearms from the morning until the kitchen closes. He cooks everything on the menu and has opinions about all of it.

He comes out of the kitchen to talk. [[bice-riva|Bice]] manages the room; Aldo fills it with noise. Together they have run Al Fondale long enough that the division of labour no longer requires discussion.

## Toy Chest

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Primary Goal** | Cook food people remember and tell everyone in Le Paludi everything he knows about Le Paludi |
| **Consistent Method** | Begins every answer with context nobody asked for. Cannot be interrupted — not rudely, he simply doesn't notice and continues. |
| **Active Problem** | Two nights ago he came down for a bottle of wine around midnight and heard the cellar panel mechanism click. He went back upstairs and has said nothing to Bice because he does not want her to worry. He has not been sleeping well. |
| **Performance Hook** | Cliff Clavin (Cheers) if he were a 70-year-old Italian cook — a fact or story about Le Paludi for every situation, delivered at the same unhurried pace |
| **Link of Relevance** | Any PC willing to listen — Aldo will inadvertently surface useful information mid-story; Perrin specifically, via Le Paludi canal history and Nona's prior visits |

## Appearance & Voice

> [!appearance]
> Dwarf, white-bearded, broad across the shoulders in the way of someone who has been lifting things for two centuries. Slow-moving in the way of a man who decided a long time ago there was no point rushing. Wears a cook's apron in the kitchen and switches to a slightly cleaner one when he comes out to talk. Flour on his forearms until the kitchen closes; after that, oil. Large hands. Unhurried gestures.

**Voice & Delivery:** Starts sentences with *allora*. Calls people *amico*. Cannot give a short answer — every answer has a prior context that must be established first, and that context has its own prior context. Delivers all of this at the same warm, unhurried pace regardless of urgency.

*"Allora — this building, you know, before they rerouted the south channel — the second rerouting, not the one everyone talks about — this whole side was open water. My wife says I've told her this. I have. It's still true."*

*"My wife says I talk too much. I say: someone has to remember these things."*

## Lore Sheet

Aldo was born in Le Paludi and has left it for a total of approximately three years across his entire life. He knows the building histories, the old families, the families before those families, and the general shape of everyone's business going back further than anyone else in the district can verify. He does not process this as intelligence — it is simply what he knows, and he shares it freely to anyone who sits still long enough.

He is not a member of the Passage and does not know the details of the cellar arrangement. Bice told him there was something in the cellar she had agreed to with "the Rattkin woman from the Warren" and that he should not go looking. He has not gone looking. He is, however, a light sleeper.

> [!dm]
> Aldo is not a liability — he doesn't know enough to be one. The midnight panel event is the active pressure. He heard it, he knows what it was, and he is holding it alone because he doesn't want to concern Bice.
>
> If a PC has any extended conversation with him — especially wandering into canal history, the building, or "anything unusual lately" — this comes out in the middle of something else: *"— and then the canal commission rerouted the north channel, which is why the water flows the way it does now, which reminds me, two nights ago I heard something in the cellar. Probably nothing. Allora, where was I —"*
>
> He hasn't told Bice. If they are both present when this surfaces, Bice goes still in a way Aldo doesn't notice.

## Hooks

- Any patient listener gets two centuries of Le Paludi history and, embedded somewhere in the middle, whatever Aldo has been turning over quietly.
- If asked about recent visitors, he will describe the watch officer at the corner table with complete accuracy and zero alarm.
- He can name every family that has owned property in Le Paludi for as long as records exist.

Minor Dravosi gentleman and Crown-licensed factor — Geoffrey Draves's father, who arranged his son's berth on the Surety using a wage contract he knew was not what Geoffrey believed it was.

# Aldous Draves

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human (Dravosi) |
| **Role** | Crown-licensed import factor; Geoffrey's father |
| **Location** | [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] |

## Overview

Aldous Draves is a Crown-licensed import factor operating out of [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] — which means he has spent thirty years reading shipping manifests, filing inspection appeals, attending maritime court proceedings, and learning the names of every clerk worth knowing. He is not a naval man. He is a man who has spent his life adjacent to the naval world, which is a different thing, and which he has never fully admitted is not the same thing.

He arranged his son's berth on the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] through patient cultivation of the right connections. A patrol cutter posting is not a commission. It was what those connections could produce, and Aldous presented it to [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] as the opening move in a plan rather than the ceiling of his reach.

His son has been somewhere on the eastern patrol routes and has not written in some time. He has filed formal inquiries with the Harbourmaster's Office. He is waiting.

## Appearance & Manner

When you meet him, the first thing you notice is the clothes. The cut is correct; the insignia accurate to Crown administrative rank; the whole presentation reads as respectable Dravosi gentleman from a distance. Up close, the cut is a decade out of date.

He is formal the way people are formal who were taught that informality is how family names become forgettable. He uses titles correctly and consistently. He does not smile easily, and when he does, it looks like a decision he made after weighing the alternatives.

## Wants

To close the gap. The Draves family has Crown access and the right connections, but the line between *access* and *inside* has never been crossed. His son becoming a man whose name reaches the ears of important Crown officers without being attached to a problem: that would be something. He does not say this plainly.

## Voice

Formal, economical, precise. Refers to Geoffrey as "Geoffrey" in every context — no warmth or distance attached to it, just designation.

> *"Geoffrey is a capable young man. Whether capable becomes something more is a question of whether he applies it in the right direction."*
>
> *"The berth on the Surety was not a small thing to arrange. The Crown does not distribute patrol postings casually. I want to be clear about that."*

## The Wage Situation

He has been a licensed factor for thirty years. Crown privateer marine ratings and their baseline wage schedule are standard knowledge in the Port Tidefall commercial tier. He knows that a rated marine earns considerably more than a carpenter-plus-supplement for the same boarding work. Whether he explained the difference to [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] is the question to hold. If pressed directly, he will cite the contract language. The contract is accurate. He knows this. He is counting on it.

## The Knighton Question

If Geoffrey's activities reach [[rupert-knighton|Knighton's]] desk — a defecting Crown sailor working for foreign privateers — whether Aldous distances himself or frames the whole sequence as bold initiative will depend entirely on how things land. He is not a disloyal man. He is a careful one.

## If Geoffrey Returns

**Successful, with money and connections:** He arranged the berth. He always believed the sea was the right path.

**Disgraced, wanted by the Crown:** He has no record of the arrangement. The connections he used were informal. Informal connections leave no paper trail.

**Dead:** He will have the Harbourmaster's inquiry letter framed and kept. He has already drafted it in his head.

## Hooks

- Geoffrey returning with money, a warrant, or proof of desertion forces Aldous to choose which version of the story he will claim.
- A formal inquiry into the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] gives him a reason to enter play before Geoffrey is ready.
