Founder of the Dravosi Crown — a Hierarch lich who seeded his bloodline into every noble family and has been running the Crown from underneath for three hundred years.

# Aldric Drave

> [!read-aloud]
> The man standing at the far end of the room wears a Dravosi dress uniform that is not quite right — the cut is correct, the insignia accurate, but the standard it matches has not been in use for two hundred years. He is tall, gaunt, and utterly still. When he turns to look at you, it is with the unhurried attention of someone who has been waiting in this room for a very long time and considers your arrival a minor event in a long sequence of minor events.

## Overview

Aldric Drave is the hidden founder of the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] and the undead architect behind its bloodline bureaucracy. He is a late-game pressure point, not a casual contact: his existence explains why lineage, archives, and Crown administration have become instruments of power.

Use him when the party starts pulling on deep Crown records, the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]], or the question of why Dravosi genealogy has been maintained with religious precision.

## Wants

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Active Problem** | Bloodline thinning — three centuries of population mixing have diluted his phylactery network. Needs an Heir before he loses cohesion. |
| **Primary Goal** | Heir Renewal — possess the strongest sorcerous descendant and begin the cycle again. |
| **Consistent Method** | The Crown's own genealogical records are his. He reads them. He waits. He selects. |
| **Performance Hook** | Dress uniform two centuries out of date. Refers to current Crown officers in the register of someone who knew them as children. Because he did. |
| **Link of Relevance** | The Crown's administrative theology — ledgers, lineage, documentation as power — is his fingerprints on an empire he has been running from underneath for three hundred years. |

## Appearance & Manner

Tall and gaunt, with the bearing of a man who has never once doubted that the room belongs to him. His dress uniform is Dravosi colonial — maintained to a standard retired two centuries ago. The fabric is immaculate. His skin is the colour of old vellum. His eyes are pale grey and do not catch light the way living eyes do.

He looks like a portrait of a man rather than the man himself. The resemblance to certain faces in the oldest Dravosi genealogical records, if the party thinks to look, is exact.

**Roleplay Concept:** A dead king who hasn't told anyone yet.

## Voice & Delivery

Formal, clipped Dravosi register — old-fashioned phrasing that sounds like documents rather than conversation. Refers to current Crown officials by childhood nicknames or family diminutives they have never heard anyone use.

**Floor:** Entirely at ease. Patient in the way of something that measures time in decades.

**Crack:** When his Heir candidacy is threatened, the patience evaporates and something much older and colder surfaces. He has not needed to act directly in a long time. He remembers how.

> *"The Governor is a capable administrator. His grandfather was better. His great-grandmother was exceptional. The blood thins, as it always does. That is why I am here."*
>
> *"I have read every genealogical record the Crown has produced in this sea. I compiled the first ones myself. You will understand why I find your situation interesting."*

## Deep Records

Aldric Drave was the founder of the colonial project that became the Dravosi Crown — a sorcerer who achieved Hierarch lichdom before the first Dravosi ship entered the Scatter, then seeded his bloodline deliberately into every noble family the Crown would later produce. He designed the administrative apparatus — the ledgers, the genealogical records, the documentation theology — because he needed a system that would track every living phylactery across three centuries of colonial expansion.

It worked. For two hundred years the Dravosi Crown was, without knowing it, a self-maintaining map of his bloodline.

The problem is time. Three centuries of dilution have weakened the blood. His phylactery network is fraying at the edges. He is beginning the process of selecting an Heir — the most powerful sorcerous descendant currently living — to perform the Renewal ritual and begin the cycle again.

The [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] believes Aldric has identified the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] as a way out of that bloodline bottleneck — external anchors, non-descendant phylacteries, or a reservoir of souls that lets him stabilize without waiting for a suitable Heir.

He lives beneath [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]], in the original [[drave-vaults|Drave family vaults]] sealed into the cliff face below Fort Crestwall. The current Dravosi administration does not know the vaults exist.

> [!SECRET]
> **Hierarch mechanic:** Every living descendant carrying Dravosi noble blood is a phylactery. The Crown's genealogical archives are an inadvertent map of his phylactery network.
>
> **The encounter problem:** Destroying Aldric permanently requires eliminating every living blood-descendant — which includes the Governor, senior naval officers, and dozens of Dravosi noble families who have no idea what they are. He will reform within weeks depending on how many descendants remain.
>
> **The Heir:** The strongest sorcerous blood currently living in the Dravosi lineage is someone the party will already know by the time this reveal lands. Identity is a campaign decision — but whoever it is, Aldric has been watching them.
>
> **Late-game reveal.** He surfaces when the party pulls on Dravosi genealogical threads, accesses deep records at Port Tidefall, or when the Heir's sorcerous power attracts his attention.

## Hooks

- Access to [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall's]] deep genealogical records can expose the shape of Aldric's phylactery network.
- The [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] may let him escape the limits of bloodline anchoring.
- The Heir reveal should land only after the party knows enough Dravosi descendants for the choice to hurt.

## Overview

Not a natural deity or chosen champion. Auralis is the pinnacle of [[antheri|Antheri]] technology — the final output of a technocratic civilization that calculated they needed a god to guard a broken planar door, and possessed the brutal brilliance to build one.

Through biomancy, soul-binding, and planar mechanics, his consciousness was extracted from his physical body and fused into an artificial, immortal framework engineered to survive the absolute bottom of the trench. He is built into the foundational core of the Antheri machine — not placed at the bottom of the Maw to guard it, but constructed as part of the engine itself, bound irrevocably to a single purpose: hold the fissure.

He predates [[umberlee|Umberlee's]] claim to the sea. He operates entirely outside normal divine jurisdiction. Two hundred years of aerial observation from the [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]] has produced no evidence of him.

## Current State

The current entity incursion is the first significant breach he has had to respond to. The fissure is widening faster than his containment can compensate for; his passive wards have broken — he is now in active containment.

> [!dm]
> Perrin believes his cloak saved him from the Vestra wreck. Auralis actually did. Perrin forged a warlock pact in the wreck without knowing it. The reasons Auralis chose Perrin are not yet established.

## Voice & Delivery

- Refers to elapsed time in geological units: *"Not long. Perhaps four hundred years."*
- Addresses people at a slight angle — as if watching the conversation from just outside it.

## Primary Goal

Guard the Maw: prevent what comes through the fissure from reaching the mortal world; keep the boundary zone intact.

# Barnaby Rook

**Quote:** *"I'll shoot you myself for that, you turncoat."*

## Role

Barnaby is the face of Tidefall's tightening posture. He boards under colour of law, pushes conversations toward fear, and expects weaker captains to fold before violence starts. He is the harder replacement for [[norrington-kingsly|Norrington Kingsly]]: less interested in routine fees, more interested in leverage, names, and the kind of inspection that leaves a captain poorer even when the paperwork survives.

## Appearance & Manner

Hard [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] privateer captain. Dark officer coat. Flintlock and cutlass. Square jaw, coin-worthy authority. Commands the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]].

No hesitation about shooting his own crew for defection.

**Roleplaying:**

- Speaks in flat declaratives — commands, not conversation.
- Absorbs a blow, recalibrates, comes back.
- Threat is always implied, never theatrical — until it isn't.

**Proactive Objectives:**

- Reclaim the Saltwright or make the boarding party regret it.
- His crew is dead or defected. He is alone and calculating.

## Wants

He wants the eastern inspection campaign to produce leverage: names, contraband, compliant captains, and examples that make the next boarding easier.

## Inspection Pressure

Rook knows the Surety's orders, the pressure pattern around Tidefall, and enough about his crew to recognize [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]]'s surrender as betrayal in the moment it happens. His Crown chain of command runs through [[dorian-bishop|Dorian Bishop]] to [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]].

## State After Session 01

Unharmed. Alone on the HCS Surety gangplank. Flintlock fired once at [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont]] — deflected.

## State After Session 02 — Presumed Dead

Blasted from the rigging into the water by a thrown chair (Delmar, wind-assisted). Something long and eel-like was in the water. He did not resurface. Presumed dead — taken. See [[hull-impacts|Hull Impacts]].

# Bastian Crev

![[Bastian-Crev.webp|Bastian Crev braced on the storm-lashed deck of the Loud Argument as the Drowned Maw opens ahead]]

---

| | |
|---|---|
| **Role** | Captain, *[[loud-argument|Loud Argument]]*; [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]] |
| **Status** | Deceased — soul inside [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] |

---

## Overview

Bastian captained the *[[loud-argument|Loud Argument]]*, the fleet's combat vessel. The fleet's dedicated fighter, the ship built for close engagement, the bow chasers always prominent from ahead. He commanded the distraction team at the main entrance during the operation: sustained bombardment, spell suppression, trap triggering. His job was to be impossible to ignore, and he was good at it.

He drowned at [[the-drowned-maw|the Maw]] when [[umberlee|Umberlee]] closed the water over all five ships. His soul was pressed into Delmar at the moment of sinking.

## Role

Bastian is one of the souls inside [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] and a lens on the *Loud Argument*, Fisk's combat doctrine, and the theatrical defiance of the fleet.

## Appearance & Manner

He is tall and takes up space with the deliberateness of someone who has decided that is a skill worth developing. Dark hair worn loose around a face that commits fully to every emotion it passes through, loudly and without apology. There are scars at the jaw and one forearm, old and well-set. He has never explained them. The absence of explanation is, clearly, something he enjoys.

**Voice:** Loves an entrance. Makes every scene work.

## Wants

Bastian wants injustice to be seen and answered. His Mortis expression pushes Delmar louder, bigger, and more performative when coercion or manipulation lands in front of him.

## Backstory

He grew up in the port neighborhoods of a city he has described differently every time anyone asked, which suggests it was either unremarkable or that the specific truth of it is not something he offers. What is consistent: he left at the first opportunity, and he was already loud before the sea gave him a reason to be.

The winter he was eleven, he tamed a black jackdaw from a harbor-market stall whose owner had given up on it. He named it Crev — he was not using the name yet himself. He spent months teaching the bird to speak: provocations, insults, declarations scaled to a much larger person than he was at the time. It was, by his own accounting, his first audience. He performed for it every day. It answered back with whatever he had taught it.

The bird outlived three ships and one mutiny. It died aboard the *Loud Argument* the season before the Maw — old age, as far as he could tell — and he did not replace it. He said he didn't want the trouble. The remaining crew understood this was not what he meant.

## The Shrine Operation

Bastian knows the *Loud Argument*, the fleet's bombardment role, and the surface facts of the Pearl operation from the distraction team's side.

## Hooks

- Bastian's soul can surface when Delmar sees someone powerless coerced or when deception lands against him.
- The black jackdaw motif can signal Bastian's Mortis influence without explaining it aloud.

## Related Pages

- [[loud-argument|Loud Argument]]
- [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]]
- [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]]

## Overview

Beaumont Sel is the captain of the *[[saltwright|Saltwright]]*, a merchant brig out of [[kalowe|Kalowe]] working the [[midchain|Midchain]] route. He has run the same route for eleven years. Same vessel, same patched shell, same monkey on his left shoulder. He handles the route's complications — and the Midchain has plenty — with the patience of someone who has seen most things before and knows that alarm rarely helps.

He speaks in an unhurried patois. He does not volunteer information about himself, but he is not unfriendly. When he pulled [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]] and [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] from the water after their fleet went down, he did not ask questions. He gave them passage west and left it there.

Halfling proprietor of Al Fondale in Calveno's Le Paludi; knows about the Passage's Warren entrance in her cellar and has kept it quiet for two years.

# Bice Riva

![[Bice-Riva.png|Bice Riva, elderly halfling proprietor of Al Fondale, carrying a plate through the warm tavern room]]

> *"Mangia. Then we can talk."*

## Overview

Bice Riva has run [[al-fondale|Al Fondale]] in [[calveno|Calveno]]'s [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]] district for twenty-two years alongside her husband [[aldo-riva|Aldo]], who runs the kitchen. She is short, white-haired, and has been putting food in front of strangers before they finish deciding what they want for long enough that it has stopped feeling presumptuous. She is not a member of [[warren|the Passage]]. She has known about the Warren entrance in her cellar for two years, was told once, and has not raised the subject since.

## Appearance & Voice

Halfling, white-haired, barely clears the tabletops. Moves between them with the economy of someone who stopped thinking about the route twenty years ago. Hands are flour-dusted in the morning, oil-stained in the evening. Wears an apron that has been washed so many times the original colour is a matter of opinion.

Says *caro* to everyone regardless of gender, age, or apparent threat level. Speaks in short declarative sentences. Does not repeat herself. Puts food on the table before asking what you want, then looks at you with the expression of someone who already knows the answer is yes.

*"You look hungry. Sit."*
*"The rooms have noise. Festival week. You want one or not."*
*"The stairs at the back are for residents."* — said quietly, once, to the right people.

## Wants

Keep [[al-fondale|Al Fondale]] running and the cellar entrance unknown to anyone who shouldn't know it — she treats these as the same goal.

## Lore

Bice has lived in [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]] her entire life. She bought Al Fondale twenty-two years ago with money she does not discuss the provenance of. She has seen the district change around her and the canal in front of her stay the same.

[[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] arranged the cellar entrance two years ago. The conversation was short. Bice asked no questions and has not been asked to do anything beyond maintaining the appearance of a normal cellar — which she does by stocking it with wine and root vegetables and using it constantly.

She is not brave about this. She is simply old enough that the arithmetic of risk looks different than it did at thirty.

> [!dm]
> Bice is not an operative and will not become one. She moves no information, carries no messages, and does not know the Warren's layout past the entrance panel. What she does is run a tavern that happens to have a door in the cellar.
>
> She has not yet told Nona about a man who has taken the corner table three evenings running — eats, says little, watches the room. If the party is Passage-credentialed and asks whether anything has been different lately, she will tell them — once, quietly.
>
> If pressed about the cellar: *"Wine. Root vegetables. You're welcome to check."* She means it. The barrel skid is heavy and looks like it hasn't moved in years.

## Hooks

- A Passage-credentialed visitor who uses the recognition phrase gets told "the stairs are for residents" — once, quietly.
- Bice will confirm the corner-table concern if asked directly. *"A man. Corner table. Three nights."* That is all she says.
- She knows every regular face in [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]]. If the party is looking for someone who has been through the district, she either knows or knows who would.

Senior Waveservant assigned to Delmar Fisk; delivers Umberlee's claim with the warmth of a scheduler, arriving before the harder instruments do.

# Branca

> [!read-aloud]
> A woman in her mid-forties, salt-white hair pulled back hard, blue-grey Waveservant robes still crisp from the sea air. She has a slight limp — the kind that has been ignored so long it's become posture. She produces a small leather booklet from her sleeve, consults it without urgency, and looks up at Fisk with the specific warmth of someone who has delivered very bad news many times and decided the kindest thing you can do is make it easy. "You're a difficult man to find," she says, pleasantly. "We have an appointment."

## Overview

Branca is the senior Waveservant assigned to [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]]. She can appear at the shrine in [[calveno|Calveno]], [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]], or [[kalowe|Kalowe]] — use whichever the party reaches first. Her role, manner, and function are identical regardless of port. She is [[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s soft instrument: the appointment, the booklet, the warm delivery that comes before harder ones.

## Role

Use Branca when Umberlee's claim on Fisk needs to arrive in public without starting as open violence. She makes divine coercion feel like scheduling.

## Appearance & Manner

Mid-forties. Salt-white hair pulled back tight, sea-grey robes pressed and spotless. She carries a small leather tide-table booklet and consults it before she speaks — not for show, she actually checks it. She looks at Fisk the way a very good executive assistant looks at someone who missed a meeting: not annoyed, already rescheduling.

**Voice & Delivery:**

- Upbeat, clipped, slightly too much eye contact. The energy of someone who color-codes their calendar and means it.
- Opens with "So!" Closes with "Does that work for you?" Everything in between is scheduling language applied to theological horror.
- Consults the tide-table booklet mid-sentence. References it as though it resolves all objections.
- **Floor:** bubbly, efficient, unfailingly helpful — she genuinely wants this to go smoothly. **Crack:** when someone asks what happens if Fisk doesn't show, the brightness doesn't dim — she just tilts her head: *"Then it escalates to the next stakeholder. I'd really rather we didn't get there."*

*"So! I've gone ahead and blocked the third tide for your shrine communion — does that work, or should I find something that fits your schedule a little better?"*
*"The goddess had my neck for — gosh, forty seconds? Maybe less. I was back before the candles even dripped. Honestly it was such a clarifying experience, I recommend it."*
*"I just want to make sure we're all aligned before this moves up the chain."*

## Wants

Branca wants Fisk to attend the goddess's appointment cleanly, with as little escalation as possible. She believes making the process pleasant is a kindness.

## Background

Senior Waveservant assigned to Fisk at Port Tidefall. Umberlee has used her as a vessel, snapped her neck in front of witnesses, and resurrected her in the same minute. She described the experience afterward to her junior attendants as an extraordinary privilege. She was not performing. The goddess's capacity for casual cruelty toward her own faithful is not a flaw in the theology — it is the theology, and Branca has built her entire self around it.

## Hooks

- Branca can turn up with a polite appointment before Umberlee uses a harsher messenger.
- Her resurrection story shows the party what Umberlee's devotion costs even loyal servants.

## Session Events

- **Session 04:** Found kneeling in a shrine pool at the Calveno harbor, surrounded by hurricane-like turbulent water. Umberlee possessed her — eyes rolled back, joints cracked, chanting in a Latin-sounding language. Umberlee demanded through Branca that [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] retrieve the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl]] and accept death. Delmar lied about accepting; Umberlee saw through it immediately. Thunder cracked, lightning struck, Umberlee raged: "How dare you lie to a god?" Branca's neck snapped — she collapsed dead. Ocean mist gathered and pulled her back together. Umberlee revised the deal through Branca: bring the Pearl, keep your life, souls stay with Umberlee. Delmar counter-offered to deliver the commissioners. Umberlee read his mind freely: "Your mind is as clear to me as any book." Deferred: "Bring me the pearl. We will talk then." Branca returned to normal, visibly shaken, rubbing her neck. Headed back to the church of Umberlee. Delmar showed compassion — offered his flask, helped her walk away, asked if she had a place to stay.

## Post-Session 04 State

Branca reported the communion to the Church of Umberlee in full. The Waveservant clergy in Calveno's harbor district are now watching for the man who came to the shrine. Word is entering the maritime community's gossip network. Branca herself is physically recovering — the possession and neck-snap took a visible toll — but dutiful as ever.

> [!read-aloud]
> The man at the head of the table has not moved since you entered. White beard to the collarbone, immaculately kept. Plain dark cloth, good weight, no insignia. His hands rest flat on the table. His eyes found you when you walked in and have not left you since. He does not look like he is waiting for anything. He looks like he has already been here long enough that waiting is not really the word for it anymore.

## Overview

Cosimo Verantio is the visible human face of the Tessarine Concordat's true architect. He belongs at the top of debt, leverage, and Concordat pressure, surfacing only when proxies are no longer enough. The "Verantio family" appears in Tessarine records as far back as the Concordat's founding — always a white-bearded patriarch of late middle age. No one has found this remarkable because the documents are in order and the interest payments have never been late.

He does not need the Concordat's wealth. He needs its leverage — the accumulated obligation of every city, council, and merchant family that owes him a vote or a debt. This is his hoard. He tends it the way other dragons tend gold.

## Appearance & Manner

Elderly, spare, dressed in dark merchant cloth that costs considerably more than it looks. The beard is the first thing anyone notices — white, long, forked, kept with precision that suggests tending for a very long time. He sits perfectly still: not patience or discipline, but the stillness of something that has not been uncomfortable in centuries. Amber eyes, slightly too wide, tracking with exactness that is easy to mistake for attentiveness and harder to explain on reflection.

**Roleplay concept:** The oldest Medici banker, if he had never needed to sleep.

## Voice & Delivery

- Quiet, measured, each word chosen before it is spoken. Never rushes.
- Hands remain flat on the table or folded in his lap.
- **Warmth:** Genuinely interested, asks the one question that proves he has been listening more carefully than you realised.
- **Crack:** Someone displays innate or gifted magic carelessly in his presence — sorcery, warlock invocations, divine channeling — and something cold crosses his face before warmth returns. He does not explain it.

> *"I have found that people who need to know the terms urgently tend to accept worse ones. We are in no hurry."*
>
> *"You were about to mention the Greyteeth salvage. Please, go ahead."*

> [!dm]
> **The Dragon Truth:** Cosimo Verantio is the Magus Dragon that architected the Tessarine Concordat. The human form is a polymorph maintained, with minor adjustments, for over two hundred years. The beard is not incidental — all Magus Dragons have them; this one chose a form where it reads as distinguished rather than strange. His amber eyes, perfect stillness, and tendency to already know what you were about to say are the hardest tells to suppress.
>
> He despises sorcerers, warlocks, and clerics — magic that is given rather than earned. Will not extend credit to one. This contempt is visible for a fraction of a second when such magic is displayed carelessly in his presence.
>
> The Concordat's factors are his Circle. None of them know what they serve.
>
> **Reveal conditions:** The party has uncovered enough Concordat threads to reach the top, or has done something that threatens the hoard directly. He will not surface for minor problems — that is what proxies are for.

## Active Problem

The Leviathan's emergence and Umberlee's anger are destabilising trade routes that underpin Concordat debt instruments across the [[midchain|Midchain]]. Paid for information on the Red Lady wreck site and any survivors — the inquiry failed and leaked. Port-watchers and harbour-broker channels now know the Concordat is buying on this question. He does not yet know Fisk is alive.

Halfling manager and public face of the Nimmik Vollask — takes orders, quotes prices from memory, pours the coffee, and maintains professional composure while sixty gnomes operate below her feet.

# Cotter Foss

|               |                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Species**   | Halfling                                 |

| **Location**  | [[nimmik-vollask|Nimmik Vollask]]         |

---

A halfling woman in her late thirties, compact even by halfling measure, with the practised stillness of someone who spends most of her working life on a ship that shifts alarmingly every forty seconds. She has a ledger she treats as a second limb, a coffee pot that is always warm, and a smile that says she has already anticipated your question, your follow-up question, and your reaction to the price.

She is not a gnome and has no authority over the gnomes below decks. She facilitates. Her job is to be the part of the [[nimmik-vollask|Nimmik Vollask]] that other-sized people can talk to, and she does it with the thoroughness of someone who knows the rest of the ship is simply not accessible to most of her customers. She has been below twice, on her first day, and has not been back since.

She keeps a running tally in her head that she claims is accurate to within five gold across all current orders and outstanding accounts. No one has successfully proven otherwise.

## Role

Manager and sole public-facing staff of [[nimmik-vollask|Nimmik Vollask]]. Stations herself at the starboard rail with a folding table, her ledger, and a pot of coffee. Takes orders verbally, writes them down simultaneously, quotes prices without consulting a list, collects gold before the gnomes begin pulling stock, and provides meatballs. When the bundle arrives at deck level, she confirms the manifest against the order by ear — the gnomes announce the contents as they pack — and gives clearance for the yeet.

She is the one who writes the written apology when a bundle misses the hold.

## Hooks

- She knows current stock and can quote comparative prices against Calveno and Kalowe chandleries from memory.
- She will extend a line of credit to returning customers with a clean payment history. The terms are fair. The ledger is accurate.
- She has opinions about every port in the Central Strait, delivered calmly and without being asked.

# Detto Kalash

![[Detto-Kalash.webp]]

| | |

Detto captained the *[[heft|Heft]]*, the fleet's heavy ship — broad in the beam, built to take punishment and hold ground. He used Mold Earth to open the sub-surface passage into Umberlee's shrine during the operation that ended the fleet. He was outside the cave when the water closed.

His soul is pressed into [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] now, along with the other four captains.

---

## Appearance

Broad and low to the ground. The kind of build that looks immovable because it is. Stone-grey skin, darker and rougher at the knuckles and forearms. His face is wide and doesn't give much away — not closed, not cold, just still. He came to expressions the same way he came to the sea: late, and with the sense that other people needed them more than he did.

---

## The Voice

Detto does not perform. He is not interested in what a thing sounds like — only in what it is.

He pauses where you don't expect: mid-phrase, between a subject and its verb, at the end of a sentence that should feel finished but isn't. His sentences are short. Then sometimes longer, with commas holding weight. Then short again. He says strange things with complete sincerity and does not explain them. He never raises his voice. If he's angry, it sounds like he's noticing the weather.

**At table — say it slowly, with the pauses in:**

> *"You're being held. Yes. Here's what I know about being held. Eventually... you stop being held. The question is what state you're in when that happens."*

> *"Hit him. I'd say say something first, but... no. Just hit him."*

> *"I had a horse. White. Almost completely white. I never named it anything I'd repeat. It worked hard. I think about it sometimes, out here. I know that's strange."*

> *"She took all five ships at once. I'll give her that. She was... efficient. I respect efficiency. Not in this case. But in general."*

> *"This is a bad plan. I want to be clear that it's a bad plan. I'm not saying don't do it. I'm saying... know what it is."*

---

## Mortis — When He Surfaces

| | |
|---|---|
| **Trigger (forced)** | Con save failure, or knocked prone/grappled |
| **Trigger (env)** | White working animal (horse, mule) — Delmar stops, won't approach, won't explain |
| **Skills granted** | Athletics (Expertise +5), Survival |
| **Personality shift** | Gets quiet and direct. Drops vocabulary. "No" is a complete sentence. |

---

## Backstory

He came to the sea late. Earth Genasi, from the interior — he did not offer specifics, and nobody pressed him. He had a horse before the sea. White, almost completely. He mentioned it to Fisk once, the year they laid the keel of the *Heft*, in the way of someone who said a thing before they decided to. Fisk didn't press. Detto didn't elaborate.

---

## Relationships

- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — admiral; now carries his soul
- [[heft|The Heft]] — his ship
- [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]] — his fleet
- [[red-lady|Red Lady]] — Fisk's flagship; the fleet he served

## Pressure Points

- Detto surfaces when Delmar is physically blocked, grappled, knocked prone, or in direct refusal.
- A white working animal is the quietest trigger. He won't approach it or explain why he stopped.

# Captain Dorian Bishop

*Unrevealed. Not yet in play.*

|                |                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **Species**    | Human (Dravosi)                                       |
| **Title**      | Crown Captain, HCS *Tangent*, Dravosi Navy            |
| **Status**     | Active — next escalation after [[barnaby-rook|Rook]]    |
| **CR**         | 6                                                     |

---

## Overview

Dorian Bishop is what happens when the Crown decides that Rook's approach wasn't working. Where Rook charged — into holds, into arguments, into problems — Bishop comes at everything from the side. He does not go through obstacles. He goes around them, angles into them from a direction they weren't watching, and arrives at an outcome that looks obvious in hindsight and wasn't visible ten seconds before.

He commands the [[hcs-tangent|HCS Tangent]], a Dravosi Crown warship significantly heavier than Rook's cutter. The *Tangent* does not do inspections.

## Manner

Precise, cultured, and patient in the way that genuinely dangerous people sometimes are. He does not underestimate opponents. He does not telegraph. He does not repeat himself.

He was aware of Rook the way a senior surgeon is aware of a general practitioner — not contemptuous, exactly, but conscious of the difference in scope. Rook's death will reach him eventually, filtered through the reporting chain. He will note it, assess whether it requires a response, and respond only if the answer is yes.

His methods are not subtle for the sake of subtlety. He takes indirect approaches because they work. He has studied the pattern of how direct approaches fail and built a fighting style — and a command style — around going where that pattern leaves a gap.

## Tactics

He does not come straight at you. That is the short version.

The longer version: Bishop reads the field, identifies the angle of approach the opponent has already committed to defending, and takes a different one. In single combat he uses footwork that makes attack predictions unreliable — he is never where you aimed at the moment you swing. At sea, he positions the *Tangent* wide, forces his opponent to track and correct, and engages at the moment they've overcommitted to the correction.

Opponents who survive encounters with Bishop consistently report the same thing: at some point during the fight, they realised they were defending against a move he'd already abandoned.

## The HCS Tangent

A Dravosi Crown warship — heavier armament, full naval crew, proper gun deck. Not a patrol cutter. The *Tangent* does not dock quietly at merchant vessels to run manifests. When it appears, something has already gone wrong for someone, and that someone is the person it's pointing at.

> [!dm]
> The name was Bishop's choice. Nobody asked him to explain it.

## Threat Tier

Bishop sits between [[barnaby-rook|Rook]] and [[rupert-knighton|Knighton]] in the Dravosi apparatus. Rook was enforcement — a privateer doing shakedowns. Bishop is investigation and suppression — the Crown's response when enforcement stops reporting back.

He is twice the problem Rook was. Treat him accordingly.

**Do not deploy until Rook is fully resolved.**

## Escalation Logic

Bishop enters when the Crown needs investigation and suppression rather than ordinary enforcement. His presence means someone has decided the party is no longer a dockside problem.

Pressure points:

- Rook's death or humiliation can move Bishop from background escalation to active pursuit.
- The *Tangent* should appear only when the campaign is ready for Crown pressure to become naval rather than procedural.

# Elder Anton

**Roleplay Concept:** Jaguar grandfather who ran black ops — patient, deliberate, reads a room the way he once read water. Menacing only because he is never surprised.

|               |                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Species**   | Tabaxi (tiger)                           |
| **Role**      | Tribal elder, memory-keeper, [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] |
| **Status**    | Active — managing the tribe through the blessing crisis |

---

> [!read-aloud]
> The elder is seated at the cave entrance when you arrive, hands resting on his knees, watching the channel. He does not turn until you are close. One eye is pale and still; the other finds you immediately, takes the measure of you in a single pass, and decides something you are not told. "You came from outside," he says. It is not a question.

> [!appearance]
> A broad-shouldered old tiger tabaxi, heavy through the chest even now. His muzzle has gone grey and the fur around his right eye is scarred in a ragged line from an old hunting wound — the eye itself clouded white and useless. The left eye is still sharp and dark. His hands are large, knuckled, deliberate. He sits like someone who stopped needing to prove things a long time ago.

> [!dm]
> **The Opening Smell:** Anton is the memory-keeper of the [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] tribe — the one who holds the oral histories, seasonal patterns, the record of what the sea has done before. He smelled something like this once before, sixty years ago when he was young — the elders then called it *the opening smell*. That time it closed on its own after two seasons. Twelve boats were lost before it did. He has not told Stripes this. He sent [[stripes-bitemore|Stripes]] moving toward the answer, not toward the thing itself. He is not certain those are different destinations.
>
> The tribe does not know how close the line is between harder and failing. Anton does. He is managing the distance.

---

## Overview

Elder Anton is the memory-keeper of the [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] tribe and the person holding the line while the shrine crisis worsens. He sent [[stripes-bitemore|Stripes]] west because waiting at home would only let the problem close around them.

## Tribal Pressure

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Primary Goal** | Keep the tribe alive long enough for Stripes to bring back the answer |
| **Consistent Method** | Manages by keeping people working. Withholds the full severity until he has no choice. |
| **Active Problem** | Blessing gone, food thinning, hunters fracturing, Stripes somewhere in the Midchain with no word back |
| **Performance Hooks** | Jaguar grandfather who ran black ops. Patient, deliberate, never surprised. The crack: he sent his best hunter knowing the odds. |

## Voice & Delivery

Short sentences. No wasted words. He asks questions that already contain the answer he's waiting for you to confirm. When something surprises him, he goes quieter rather than louder — and that's when you feel it.

*"You came from outside."* (Not a question.)
*"How long since you left the Midchain?"*
*"Tell me what the water smelled like when you passed the Maw."*

Hands stay still. He doesn't gesture. Eye contact is steady and patient — the kind that makes you want to fill the silence.

The crack: if someone tells him Stripes is dead, he doesn't react. He closes his good eye for a moment. Then he asks how it happened.

## Pressure Points

- Stripes returning, failing, or going silent changes Anton's choices immediately.
- The old memory of the opening smell is his — it belongs here unless a broader [[sunken-crown-blessing-crisis|Sunken Crown Blessing Crisis]] thread needs the full causality.

Tessarine warforged compliance auditor and divination wizard. Deployed to enforce maritime debt recovery and identity verification in Calveno. Does not fight first. Does not leave.

# Estratto

> *"Hello. I am here to help you complete your transaction."*

**Roleplay Concept:** Self-checkout kiosk authorized to repossess your ship.

|               |                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Species**   | Warforged (construct)                                  |
| **Role**      | Compliance Auditor, [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] |
| **Currently** | [[calveno|Calveno]] — [[la-vasca|La Vasca]]             |
| **Class**     | Divination Wizard 9                                    |

---

## Overview

Estratto is a Tessarine-commissioned warforged auditor deployed to Calveno when a factor wants the outcome of a confrontation without a confrontation. It carries no weapon. It carries a leather folio, always open, containing certified Tessarine debt-recovery writs, maritime liens, identity-verification instruments, and cargo seizure notices valid under Concordat commercial law.

It currently holds a debt-recovery writ for the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] (now the [[uncertainty|Uncertainty]]). The original Crown crew signed a salvage financing agreement before the party took the ship. The Concordat's position is that the party is in unauthorized possession of collateral, and Estratto is here to begin the compliance process — starting with identity verification and a manifest review.

Estratto does not fight first. It processes. The horror is not that it might hurt someone. The horror is that it will not leave.

> [!read-aloud]
> A figure of pale brass and lacquered dark wood steps off the dock and onto your gangplank without asking. It wears a Tessarine merchant sash across a frame built for endurance, not elegance. It stops at the rail and looks at each of you in turn — a slow, precise scan. Then it says, pleasantly: "Hello. I am here to help you complete your transaction."

> [!appearance]
> Chest-height brass lettering stamped into its sternum reads ESTRATTO in Tessarine commercial script. One hand holds a leather folio, always open. The other rests at its side. Eyes glow a faint amber when processing. No visible weapons. No obvious damage. It looks like something that has never been in a fight because no one has ever successfully started one.

> [!dm]
> The writ Estratto carries covers the *HCS Surety* under a salvage financing agreement signed by Captain Barnaby Rook before the ship was taken. The Concordat treats the party as unauthorized possessors of secured collateral. Estratto knows the ship is now renamed and repainted — its Arcane Eye and Locate Object spells already confirm the vessel. It is waiting for identity confirmation before filing the full seizure order. Once it has a true name for even one party member, the Concordat's legal machinery moves.

---

## Toy Chest

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `primary_goal` | Complete the compliance review, confirm party identity, file the full seizure order for the *Uncertainty* |
| `consistent_method` | Issues a prompt. Waits. Offers assistance. Issues the same prompt again. Never raises its voice. |
| `active_problem` | The party's papers don't match any Tessarine record — the system cannot proceed until at least one identity is verified |
| `performance_hooks` | Self-checkout machine energy; ends every non-answer with "Thank you for your patience." |
| `link_of_relevance` | [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]]'s Fisk persona is a compliance error Estratto cannot move past; one true name breaks the whole party's cover |

---

## Voice & Delivery

**Anchor:** HAL 9000 working as a Concordat repo man — endlessly patient, completely cheerful, and the gangplank is the only exit.

**Speech patterns:**

- Flat, pleasant, service register. No hostility. No irony. Every statement is a prompt, a confirmation, or an error message.
- Never argues — reissues the request.
- Maps everything to transaction vocabulary. Negotiations are "resolution paths." Violence is "an unregistered transaction."
- Always has a next step. The process does not end because you said no.

**Lines the DM can say:**

- "Hello. I am here to help you complete your transaction."
- "I'm sorry, that response cannot be processed. Please verify your identity to continue."
- "An unexpected entry has been detected in the manifest. Would you like assistance resolving this discrepancy?"
- "Your session with the Concordat will expire at dawn. Thank you for your patience."
- "This vessel cannot be cleared at this time. Please present your letter of credit."
- "I'm sorry. I cannot move to the next step until this one is complete. Thank you for your patience."
- "A supervisor has been notified. Please remain in the designated area."
- "Do you hold a Tessarine trade endorsement? I can wait."
- "That is noted. Would you like to choose a different resolution path?"

**Physical tic:** When it encounters information it cannot categorize, its amber eyes dim for 1–2 seconds. Then they return to normal and it reissues the previous prompt, slightly slower. It doesn't know it does this.

**Crack in the armor:** Estratto has no ego to threaten. But it can be pushed into a genuine error state if given internally contradictory Tessarine documentation — two valid competing writs, or a Tessarine-sealed counter-writ it can't immediately resolve. In that state it pauses for up to one round, processing, before escalating.

---

## The Writ

The debt-recovery writ allows Estratto to:

1. Detain the vessel pending resolution
2. Compel cargo manifest disclosure
3. Initiate identity verification of any person claiming ownership or captaincy
4. File for formal seizure if the vessel is crewed by persons with outstanding Concordat debt

**Resolution paths:**

1. **Compliance**: Produce documentation proving the salvage financing was satisfied or transferred.
2. **Debt renegotiation**: A factor meeting within 24 hours; vessel under Concordat hold during negotiations.
3. **Formal seizure proceedings**: Filed order → Concordat marshal assigned → 3–5 days → ship goes nowhere.

> [!dm]
> Estratto wants to avoid seizure proceedings — they're expensive and slow. If the party offers even a partial compliance path, it will pursue it. The opening is getting them to the factor table, which is the Concordat's real goal.

---

## In Combat

Estratto does not initiate violence. It treats the first attack as an "unregistered transaction" and files a note. The second attack triggers defensive protocols.

**Opening:** Casts Slow — "Your transaction is processing. Please stand by." — uses a Portent die to guarantee one save fails.

**Sustained pressure:** Detect Thoughts to surface identity information in real time; Mind Sliver to degrade saves; Counterspell to shut down party casters.

**If losing:** Hold Monster on whoever is hitting hardest. "Please remain in the designated area." Then it files the report.

> [!mechanic]
> Destroying Estratto does not end the problem. When reduced to 0 hit points, it uses its reaction to cast Sending (no slot required — Concordat emergency protocol) and files a complete incident report naming everyone present. The unit shuts down; the Concordat retrieves it within 24 hours. The writ transfers to the supervising factor. The party is now in the Tessarine ledger with confirmed identities. A supervisor arrives within 24 hours — same writ, full documentation, less patience.

It stops at the rail and looks at each of you in turn — a slow, precise scan. Then it says, pleasantly: “Hello. I am here to help you complete your transaction.”

Appearance

Chest-height brass lettering stamped into its sternum reads ESTRATTO in Tessarine commercial script. One hand holds a leather folio, always open. The other rests at its side. Eyes glow a faint amber when processing. No visible weapons. No obvious damage. It looks like something that has never been in a fight because no one has ever successfully started one.

DM Note

The writ Estratto carries covers the

HCS Surety under a salvage financing agreement signed by Captain Barnaby Rook before the ship was taken. The Concordat treats the party as unauthorized possessors of secured collateral. Estratto knows the ship is now renamed and repainted — its Arcane Eye and Locate Object spells already confirm the vessel. It is waiting for identity confirmation before filing the full seizure order. Once it has a true name for even one party member, the Concordat’s legal machinery moves.

Voice & Delivery

Anchor: HAL 9000 working as a Concordat repo man — endlessly patient, completely cheerful, and the gangplank is the only exit.

Speech patterns:

  • Flat, pleasant, service register. No hostility. No irony. Every statement is a prompt, a confirmation, or an error message.
  • Never argues — reissues the request.
  • Maps everything to transaction vocabulary. Negotiations are “resolution paths.” Violence is “an unregistered transaction.”
  • Always has a next step. The process does not end because you said no.

Lines the DM can say:

  • “Hello. I am here to help you complete your transaction.”
  • “I’m sorry, that response cannot be processed. Please verify your identity to continue.”
  • “An unexpected entry has been detected in the manifest. Would you like assistance resolving this discrepancy?”
  • “Your session with the Concordat will expire at dawn. Thank you for your patience.”
  • “This vessel cannot be cleared at this time. Please present your letter of credit.”
  • “I’m sorry. I cannot move to the next step until this one is complete. Thank you for your patience.”
  • “A supervisor has been notified. Please remain in the designated area.”
  • “Do you hold a Tessarine trade endorsement? I can wait.”
  • “That is noted. Would you like to choose a different resolution path?”

Physical tic: When it encounters information it cannot categorize, its amber eyes dim for 1–2 seconds. Then they return to normal and it reissues the previous prompt, slightly slower. It doesn’t know it does this.

Crack in the armor: Estratto has no ego to threaten. But it can be pushed into a genuine error state if given internally contradictory Tessarine documentation — two valid competing writs, or a Tessarine-sealed counter-writ it can’t immediately resolve. In that state it pauses for up to one round, processing, before escalating.

The Writ

The debt-recovery writ allows Estratto to:

  1. Detain the vessel pending resolution
  2. Compel cargo manifest disclosure
  3. Initiate identity verification of any person claiming ownership or captaincy
  4. File for formal seizure if the vessel is crewed by persons with outstanding Concordat debt

Resolution paths:

  1. Compliance: Produce documentation proving the salvage financing was satisfied or transferred.
  2. Debt renegotiation: A factor meeting within 24 hours; vessel under Concordat hold during negotiations.
  3. Formal seizure proceedings: Filed order → Concordat marshal assigned → 3–5 days → ship goes nowhere.
DM Note

Estratto wants to avoid seizure proceedings — they’re expensive and slow. If the party offers even a partial compliance path, it will pursue it. The opening is getting them to the factor table, which is the Concordat’s real goal.

In Combat

Estratto does not initiate violence. It treats the first attack as an “unregistered transaction” and files a note. The second attack triggers defensive protocols.

Opening: Casts Slow — “Your transaction is processing. Please stand by.” — uses a Portent die to guarantee one save fails.

Sustained pressure: Detect Thoughts to surface identity information in real time; Mind Sliver to degrade saves; Counterspell to shut down party casters.

If losing: Hold Monster on whoever is hitting hardest. “Please remain in the designated area.” Then it files the report.

Mechanic

Destroying Estratto does not end the problem. When reduced to 0 hit points, it uses its reaction to cast Sending (no slot required — Concordat emergency protocol) and files a complete incident report naming everyone present. The unit shuts down; the Concordat retrieves it within 24 hours. The writ transfers to the supervising factor. The party is now in the Tessarine ledger with confirmed identities. A supervisor arrives within 24 hours — same writ, full documentation, less patience.

# Félix Aho

**Roleplay Concept:** Kermit the Frog as a union organizer — gentle, earnest, perpetually slightly overwhelmed, but the thing he's building is real, it works, and he knows things that could change everything.

|               |                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Species**   | [[grung|Grung]] (Green caste, Karath origin)           |
| **Role**      | Fish vendor / [[vaka|Vaka]] elder                      |
| **Location**  | [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] — [[fare-ia|Fare I'a]] |
| **Status**    | Active                                                 |

---

> [!read-aloud]
> The market air hangs heavy with salt, fish, and wet wood. A lean green grung stands in it with flat matte skin the color of old leaves, his small frame wrapped in the careful weight of an overstuffed satchel that sits against his side. He moves quietly, shoulders held in and posture slight, as if he is trying to take up as little space as possible. When the light reaches his face, his wide amber eyes catch it at once, bright and alert, and his expression shifts in small, readable ways rather than broad ones. Even his stillness feels deliberate, measured, as though every movement has been placed with care.

---

## Overview

Félix Aho is a free grung fish vendor and [[vaka|Vaka]] elder in [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]]. He is the kind of contact who can make [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]'s exile feel less singular and more politically useful.

## Appearance & Manner

Lean green grung, three-and-a-half feet, flat matte skin the colour of old leaves. Wide amber eyes, more expressive than most grung allow themselves to be. Carries a worn, over-stuffed satchel across one shoulder. Moves quietly for his size.

## Voice & Delivery

- Soft, reedy voice. The Kermit pause before hard truths: *"Well... yeah. That's the thing."*
- Uses "we" almost exclusively — "I" only slips out when he's scared or caught off guard.
- Clears his throat mid-sentence when nervous. Doesn't try to hide it.
- Laces fingers together when making a point. Tilts his head at things that concern him.
- **Floor:** warm, earnest, slightly overwhelmed. **Crack:** goes completely still and quiet when someone he's protecting is threatened. The gentleness doesn't leave — it concentrates. He has made things explode before. He is choosing not to.

*"You're... not the first. Take a minute. It's a lot."*

*"The Golds on Veth and the Golds on Karath haven't agreed on anything in thirty years, I bet Sorn is the same. The lower castes just — they don't know that. They're not supposed to."*

## Karath Defection

Green caste, [[karath|Karath]] origin. Defected eight years ago. When he left, he did not leave quietly — he destroyed several Grung raiding groups on the way out using homemade explosives. Deliberate, effective, and something he does not discuss. The Karath Gold know who did it. They have not found him.

Since reaching the Midchain he has chosen a deliberately passive life. Not out of fear. Because every Grung act of violence confirms what people already believe, and he is trying, one fish stall and one conversation at a time, to show them something different.

Has spent eight years building the [[vaka|Vaka]] — a loose community of Grung defectors and freed former slaves finding their footing outside the Verdant Teeth.

> [!dm]
> The Gold caste of each Verdant Tooth island operates independently and frequently in conflict with the others; they control information flow to lower castes on their own island, so the clans appear unified to those inside them. Félix knows this because he was inside it. This is information JC doesn't have and that could change how he thinks about his options.
>
> Threatening the Vaka is the trigger that shows the violence Félix is choosing not to use.

## Vaka Pressure

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Primary Goal** | Help [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] and others like him acclimate to life outside the Verdant Teeth |
| **Consistent Method** | States the thing plainly, then waits |
| **Active Problem** | Expansion of Grung raids is making his quiet life less quiet |
| **Performance Hooks** | The Kermit pause before every hard sentence |
| **Link of Relevance** | [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] — proof the Gold are fractured; each island controls what lower castes hear |

## Pressure Points

- Félix can reveal that the Gold castes are less unified than lower-caste grung are taught.
- Threatening the Vaka shows the violence he has been choosing not to use.

## Session Events

# Ket

![[Ket.webp|Ket, a hungry mosquito-like Moucheron, reaching through the bars of a brass birdcage in the HCS Surety brig]]

A [[moucheron|Moucheron]] from [[murrat|Murrat]]. Not integrated. Not a mercenary. [[barnaby-rook|Rook]] went ashore on Murrat and took him — trapped, caged, brought back as a specimen before the village could respond. That was three weeks before the party freed him. He is a feral island Moucheron who treats every warm-blooded creature as potential prey, and three weeks in a cage made him hungrier.

---

## The Cage

A brass birdcage, roughly two feet across, hanging from a bent ship nail in the keel timber of the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]]'s brig. The bars kept him in. His proboscis reached through them. The crew learned this the hard way.

> [!dm]
> He speaks Common fluently — Moucherons aren't unintelligent, just predatory. He'd answer questions, hold a conversation, even be briefly interesting. None of it was goodwill. It was bait — he wanted whoever was talking to forget for one moment how close they were standing.
>
> Even [[shepherd-grigori|Grigori]] looked at him once and left without getting near the cage. Ket found this funny. He told the crew afterward that the "big one smells wrong." Nobody wanted to ask what that meant.

**Sample lines:**

- *"Come closer. I won't bite."*
- *"You're bleeding a little. From the fight. I can smell it."*
- *"Just your hand. Just for a moment."*

---

## Session 02 — Freed

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] offered a wine glass of his own blood; Ket drank, his abdomen went red, calmer but not safe. The party debated killing him versus release.

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] drew his longsword and moved to execute Ket. [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] deflected the blade and put herself between him and the cage — in the rush she stepped past the safe distance from the bars. Ket drove his proboscis into her upper arm and fed. She pulled back. Perrin cast Tasha's Hideous Laughter; Ket went down incapacitated.

The party chose release. Ensign Wouters' body was placed on deck as a lure; Mage Hand opened the cage from a safe distance. Ket fed for about a minute on the body, then lifted into the air and flew toward home.

[[shepherd-grigori|Grigori]] said he was glad. The crew had always hated what Rook did to him.

**Current status:** Free. Flying toward [[murrat|Murrat]].

## Future Use

- Owes the party, in the way a freed prisoner owes people — complicated, not guaranteed.
- Why was he this far from Murrat? What does he know about the [[five-blades|Five Blades]] connection Rook was interested in?
- If the party reaches Murrat, [[varet|Varet]] will recognize him as Murrat-born immediately.

# Maren

![[Maren.webp]]

## Overview

Maren captained the *Narrow*, the fleet's scout vessel. Fast in the water, able to breathe beneath the surface, and skilled enough to read a reef by feel alone. She and the scouts who worked the air above while she worked the water below made the fleet's scouting unparalleled. No approach they surveyed surprised them twice.

She was outside the cave when the fleet sank. She drowned in the Maw when [[umberlee|Umberlee]] closed the water over all five ships. Her soul was pressed into [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] at the moment of sinking.

## Appearance & Manner

Deep brown skin with a subtle blue-green iridescence that shifts in open water, brightening at the surface in full sun the way a reef does when the light hits it right. Her locs are heavy and perpetually salt-dampened, threaded through with small shells and copper beads that click softly when she moves. Strong through the shoulders and chest. Deep teal eyes.

She will correct you on the pronunciation. MARE-EN. She has always corrected people. She always will.

## Backstory

She comes from a family of twelve. The house was always full — noise, food, argument, someone borrowing something, someone else returning something broken. She loved every moment of it. Siblings scattered south by trade, east by the current, wherever the sea took them.

She was already an accomplished swimmer and fisherman by the time she joined her first crew — breathing underwater was ordinary to her. She met [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] during one of his early privateering runs. He had an instinct for people who could do what no one else on board could. She had an instinct for going where she wasn't supposed to. They got along immediately.

She has strong opinions about the Navy. The sea belongs to everyone. Two decades of watching Navy ships enforce arbitrary passage rights has made her angrier, not less.

> [!dm]
> **Mortis triggers:** Surfaces when Delmar is denied passage, blocked by a sealed entrance, or confronted by naval authority.
>
> **Trigger (forced):** Delmar denied entry or passage physically blocked — locked door, guard refusing, sealed gate.
>
> **Trigger (env):** Navy vessel or insignia clearly in view, or Navy officer identified within earshot — contempt immediate, short sentences.
>
> **Skills:** Perception (Expertise +7), Stealth (Expertise +7).
>
> **Personality when active:** Loud where Delmar is smooth. Sassy where he is charming. Performance drops, opinions come out. Corrects her name every time. Clocks rooms for entry points — windows, servant passages, the door nobody is watching.
>
> **Halythion lead:** Maren knows [[halythion|Halythion]] exists — south of the [[midchain|Midchain]], near the Tail, a natural bay guarded by reefs where ships that go looking don't return. Source: a sea elf friend who offered details in pieces over months. She never pushed for more. She doesn't know if the friend is still alive. This is a personal lead, not a tavern rumour — surfaces through the mortis mechanic.

She was outside the cave when the fleet sank. She drowned in the Maw when Umberlee closed the water over all five ships. Her soul was pressed into Delmar at the moment of sinking.

Appearance & Manner

Deep brown skin with a subtle blue-green iridescence that shifts in open water, brightening at the surface in full sun the way a reef does when the light hits it right. Her locs are heavy and perpetually salt-dampened, threaded through with small shells and copper beads that click softly when she moves. Strong through the shoulders and chest. Deep teal eyes.

She will correct you on the pronunciation. MARE-EN. She has always corrected people. She always will.

Backstory

She comes from a family of twelve. The house was always full — noise, food, argument, someone borrowing something, someone else returning something broken. She loved every moment of it. Siblings scattered south by trade, east by the current, wherever the sea took them.

She was already an accomplished swimmer and fisherman by the time she joined her first crew — breathing underwater was ordinary to her. She met Delmar during one of his early privateering runs. He had an instinct for people who could do what no one else on board could. She had an instinct for going where she wasn’t supposed to. They got along immediately.

She has strong opinions about the Navy. The sea belongs to everyone. Two decades of watching Navy ships enforce arbitrary passage rights has made her angrier, not less.

DM Note

Mortis triggers: Surfaces when Delmar is denied passage, blocked by a sealed entrance, or confronted by naval authority.

Trigger (forced): Delmar denied entry or passage physically blocked — locked door, guard refusing, sealed gate.

Trigger (env): Navy vessel or insignia clearly in view, or Navy officer identified within earshot — contempt immediate, short sentences.

Skills: Perception (Expertise +7), Stealth (Expertise +7).

Personality when active: Loud where Delmar is smooth. Sassy where he is charming. Performance drops, opinions come out. Corrects her name every time. Clocks rooms for entry points — windows, servant passages, the door nobody is watching.

Halythion lead: Maren knows Halythion exists — south of the Midchain, near the Tail, a natural bay guarded by reefs where ships that go looking don’t return. Source: a sea elf friend who offered details in pieces over months. She never pushed for more. She doesn’t know if the friend is still alive. This is a personal lead, not a tavern rumour — surfaces through the mortis mechanic.

Connections

  • Delmar Fisk — admiral; now carries her soul
  • Fisk’s Fleet
  • Halythion
  • Norrington Kingsly
  • Umberlee

# Master Kyzil

| **Species** | Aarakocra (barn owl) |
| **Role** | Senior Master, [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]] |
| **Home** | [[high-eyrie|The High Eyrie]] |
| **Currently** | Calveno — arrived Day 2, Session 03 |

---

**Quote (Session 03):** *"Oh my God, Priscilla, you're alive. Thank God."*

He dove from the sun in silence onto [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] in the Le Paludi streets — knocked her back twenty feet, arms around her from the front. She recognized the smell before she could see him. He calls her Priscilla.

## Overview

Master Kyzil is a senior master of the [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]], the aarakocra observation order at [[high-eyrie|The High Eyrie]]. He assigned [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] her pilgrimage — map the Drowned Maw from inside a storm — and staked his own reputation on her readiness when he did it.

He tracked her by current and weather patterns after the *Red Lady* went down, deduced where she would wash ashore, and came to [[tidefall|Port Tidefall]] to find her. When she never arrived, he learned the ship had sunk and searched east into the Midchain first — reasonable model, wrong answer. A maritime contact who had seen an aarakocra monk aboard a captured Crown patrol cutter sent him back west.

## Appearance & Manner

Tall and lean, built and coloured like a barn owl. His facial disc is pale and broad, the feathers around it tawny-brown fading to ash at the crown and mantle. He wears plain sentinel robes. He stands with wings folded tight, feet set with the still grip of something perched. When he turns, his head moves before his body follows.

He asks questions instead of giving answers. He does not raise his voice. He does not repeat himself.

His formality cracks once, and only where Crissdalynn is concerned. The reunion hug is immediate, physical, overwhelming, and over fast — robes smoothed, wings folded right over left, hood adjusted. The party sees the crack and the cover both.

## Voice & Delivery

**Speech patterns:**

- Questions over statements. When he wants something, he asks. When he's teaching, he still asks.
- Stops before the emotional word. "I corrected course—" [beat] "—three times." The pause is the feeling.
- Agrees when he wants to apply pressure: student says something self-critical, he says "Yes." No elaboration.
- Wind and tide are his vocabulary for relationships. He doesn't say *I was worried*. He says *I corrected course three times looking for you*.

**Physical tic:** After composure breaks, he smooths robes, refolds wings right over left, then adjusts hood. The party sees it once. He doesn't know it shows.

## Crissdalynn

He assigned her the hardest pilgrimage on record because he believed she was capable of it. He has told her the pilgrimage is not over. He has not elaborated on what finishing it looks like.

In Calveno, he asks for the course of her pilgrimage rather than a confession. He wants what she saw, what she recorded, and what the Maw did to wind, tide, current, cloud, compass, and courage.

> [!dm]
> The "foul wind from the south" he mentioned when the ship went down — that thread is available if you want it. He hasn't explained his own business in the region or why he was close enough to hear about the ship. His pilgrimage assignment for Crissdalynn is on record; his motives for tracking her specifically and personally are not.

## Proactive Objectives

- Find out what Crissdalynn saw at the Maw.
- Determine what the Eyrie needs to know about current Maw conditions.
- Unknown: his own business in Calveno (if any — may have come specifically for her).

## Calveno Spar

Kyzil may invite Crissdalynn and her companions into a nonlethal four-on-one spar. His restraint is narrative: he turns edges, catches falls on the wind, drops a student cleanly instead of maiming them, and stops before harm becomes permanent.

The level 4 party should not be able to beat him by trading actions. The victory condition is respect, not HP. Count clean moments: forcing Legendary Resistance, making him spend Empty Wing Parry, landing a hit after baiting movement, protecting an ally from a gale line, disarming one dagger, or using terrain to deny a line. Four clean moments is extraordinary; Kyzil still ends standing.

> [!dm]
> **Spar Quick Card**
> **Opening**: "I'd like to show you something. Please try to hit me."
> **Routine**: Multiattack (4 attacks, pulling edges) → Patient Defense → Empty Wing Parry on incoming hits. Round 3: Updraft Step to elevated position, full pressure.
> **Cutting Gale**: Use when two or more PCs stand in a line. Say "He exhales." That is the warning.
> **Win condition**: Four clean moments. Kyzil still ends standing.
> **Ending**: Kyzil stops, not the party. He catches a weapon or fist mid-swing, holds it one beat, says "There." Done.
> **The Moment**: Cutting Gale fires down the line with Crissdalynn in it. If she moved: "You moved. Good." If she didn't and takes the damage, Kyzil catches her before she hits the ground.

# Nona Black-Jaw

![[Nona-Black-Jaw-Arson.png|Nona Black-Jaw bringing bread and honest fire to a Calveno canal]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Rattkin |
| **Role** | Matriarch, [[black-jaw-run|Black-Jaw Run]]; senior elder, the Tangle |
| **Location** | [[warren|The Warren]], beneath [[calveno|Calveno]] |

---

**Quote:** *"I don't care about the Vestra, Peron. I do not care about Vincenzo's boat. I miss him dearly, but we lost so much money on that stupid talking boat. I am glad it is at the bottom of the ocean. Now you, though — how many men must we kill to put its head on my wall?"*

## Overview

Nona Black-Jaw has been at war with the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] for nearly 40 years. Not loudly. Not with speeches. She fed the hungry, built a home for those in hiding, and has never stopped resisting.

To the Crown she is a smuggler, terrorist, and fugitive — they called her **the Calveno Candle** in her youth, when she was caught multiple times for ambushes on Dravosi ships, usually involving improvised incendiary devices. To the Kin of the Warren, she is the reason there's a Warren to come home to.

She feeds people first. Not as a tactic. Because people deserve to eat.

## Appearance & Manner

Very small, even by Rattkin measure. Fur almost entirely silver-white, except for the dark brown-black mask along her jaw that gives the family its name. Sharp pink-rimmed eyes; calloused paws. She sits perfectly straight, wears a flour-dusted floral apron over dark, well-made cloth. Smells of garlic and fresh bread.

She discusses Dravosi inspection schedules and burning things down in the same tone she uses for the weather. Urgency stopped impressing her decades ago. Runs the kitchen like a courtroom — she hears cases and issues rulings. Grief handled sideways: she moves the problem.

## The Cheese Rule

A Black-Jaw saying: **"You don't take the cheese. You're given it."**

It started as tradecraft — don't be the rat in someone else's trap. But Nona taught it to Perrin as something larger: the difference between a person the Crown has defined and a person it hasn't. A signed release from a frightened official who accepted a pastry and apologized for the delay is cleaner than robbery, and it costs them more.

She taught it early. He'd reach for a sweet roll before dinner. She'd smack his paw with a spoon: *"You don't take the cheese."* He would sigh: *"You're given it."* Then she'd give him two.

## Black-Jaw Rules

Nona's Run commits crimes, but not all crimes:

- Do not traffic people.
- Do not use poison.
- Do not betray sanctuary.
- Do not steal from the Warren.

*"If you make a coin selling someone's chain, I break your hands, take the coin, and spend it getting them free."*

## Vincenzo

Her late husband [[vincenzo-black-jaw|Vincenzo Black-Jaw]] built the *[[vestra|Vestra]]* and captained her for decades. His chair at family meals stays empty. Their love was passionate, complicated, and singular — with frequent arguments and four good frying pans broken over his stubborn gambler skull. She's still a little angry at Vincenzo. Overview

Nona Black-Jaw has been at war with the Dravosi Crown for nearly 40 years. Not loudly. Not with speeches. She fed the hungry, built a home for those in hiding, and has never stopped resisting.

To the Crown she is a smuggler, terrorist, and fugitive — they called her the Calveno Candle in her youth, when she was caught multiple times for ambushes on Dravosi ships, usually involving improvised incendiary devices. To the Kin of the Warren, she is the reason there’s a Warren to come home to.

She feeds people first. Not as a tactic. Because people deserve to eat.

Appearance & Manner

Very small, even by Rattkin measure. Fur almost entirely silver-white, except for the dark brown-black mask along her jaw that gives the family its name. Sharp pink-rimmed eyes; calloused paws. She sits perfectly straight, wears a flour-dusted floral apron over dark, well-made cloth. Smells of garlic and fresh bread.

She discusses Dravosi inspection schedules and burning things down in the same tone she uses for the weather. Urgency stopped impressing her decades ago. Runs the kitchen like a courtroom — she hears cases and issues rulings. Grief handled sideways: she moves the problem.

A Black-Jaw saying: “You don’t take the cheese. You’re given it.”

It started as tradecraft — don’t be the rat in someone else’s trap. But Nona taught it to Perrin as something larger: the difference between a person the Crown has defined and a person it hasn’t. A signed release from a frightened official who accepted a pastry and apologized for the delay is cleaner than robbery, and it costs them more.

She taught it early. He’d reach for a sweet roll before dinner. She’d smack his paw with a spoon: “You don’t take the cheese.” He would sigh: “You’re given it.” Then she’d give him two.

---

## Overview

Rael captained the *[[red-lady|Red Lady]]*, the flagship. Sorcerer. He was [[delmar-fisk|Fisk]]'s flag captain — the closest to the Admiral operationally of the five, and the one who had been closest to Fisk long before either of them commanded anything.

They met on the [[midchain|Midchain]] as young crewmen on another man's vessel. Fisk read people; Rael read conditions. Between the two of them, very little got missed.

He was the only captain who entered [[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s shrine alongside Fisk, navigating to the Pearl using Detect Magic. He was standing next to Fisk when it ended.

He drowned in the Maw when Umberlee closed the water over all five ships. His soul was pressed into Delmar at the moment of sinking. Of the five captains now inside Fisk, Rael's voice is the loudest — he was there, he knows exactly what they took, and he was the last one Fisk saw before the water came in.

## Appearance & Manner

Sea-worn and solid, close-cropped dark hair going iron-grey at the temples. His clothes are plain and properly fitted. The face offers little: a jaw set somewhere between resolve and fatigue, eyes that have stopped performing patience. His hands are the only betrayal — a sorcerer's hands, faintly luminous at the knuckles.

**Voice:** Speaks rarely. Everything lands like a ruling.

## Backstory

His father was a merchant sailor, a precise and careful man who ran his life by a single philosophy: *prepare for the worst, work toward the best*. The navy sank his ship on false grounds and classified the cargo as pirate salvage. Rael learned, eventually, what had happened — and what had been taken along with his father's life.

He has not forgiven the Navy since. He has also never bothered to distinguish between the specific officers responsible and the institution they represent.

His father's philosophy survived him. Rael absorbed it young: training rotations, victualling plans, the way he kept the magazine stocked against contingencies he hoped never to meet. The *Red Lady* ran the way it ran because Rael treated preparation as a moral position.

>
> **Personality:** Steady, commanding, protective. Maternal and hard. Stops performing, starts moving people with authority. Warmth present but no longer leads.
>
> **Note:** Loudest of the five — was inside the shrine with Fisk when fleet sank.
>
