# Commodore Rupert Knighton

*Background pressure only — do not escalate until [[dorian-bishop|Bishop]] is resolved. One Knight is now in motion in the Central Strait corridor.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human (Dravosi) |
| **Title** | Commodore, Knight Squadron, Dravosi Crown Navy |
| **Status** | Active — distant threat |
| **Relation** | Uncle of [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] (blood only) |

## Overview

Rupert Knighton commands a fleet. Not patrol cutters and manifest stamps — a fleet, Crown naval vessels, the kind that doesn't arrive for inspections. When his ships appear on the horizon, someone has already made a serious mistake.

He is not a privateer. He is not enforcement. He is the thing enforcement reports to when enforcement fails.

Within the Dravosi Crown apparatus, [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] was a working piece on the board, not a peer. Rook's death alone might not reach him. [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]] was his son — or close enough to House Knighton to amount to the same. The party killed him in Session 01. Knighton doesn't know yet. When he hears, his response will not go through Crown channels.

---

## The Knights

Knighton refers to every ship under his command as one of his Knights — not by their registered hull names, which are administrative. His fleet is his chessboard. How many ships that is, exactly, is not public knowledge. Enough that a port captain who hears "the Knights are coming" doesn't ask follow-up questions.

---

## Manner

Posh in the old way — the kind that doesn't need to announce itself. He doesn't shout. He doesn't threaten. He gives orders, and the orders happen. His reputation is built on outcomes, not style. He is fearsome precisely because he is not theatrical about it.

> *"He doesn't threaten. He replaces."* — Crown officers who've seen him work.

## Tactics

Every commander in the Dravosi Navy charges. Every commander flanks. Knighton does both, in sequence, in ways that make the enemy feel stupid afterward.

His signature is commitment: he commits his vanguard hard — harder than makes sense, harder than anyone believes is intentional — and the opposing line compresses to meet it. Then the flank arrives. Not a feint. Not a probe. The real weight, from a direction that was open thirty seconds ago and somehow isn't anymore.

Other fleet commanders study his engagements and come away with notes they can't use. The moves are not complicated. They simply require a level of coordinated nerve that most officers can't sustain under fire. He doesn't win every battle. He wins the ones he chooses to fight.

---

## Connection to Geoffrey

[[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] is his nephew by blood. Knighton almost certainly does not think about this. Geoffrey has never met him. The Draves branch is not the Knighton branch — it's the branch that didn't go anywhere in particular.

Whether Knighton would extend consideration to a nephew who has defected to work for a foreign crew is a question that hasn't come up yet.

> [!dm]
> **Threat Tier:** Late-campaign problem. Placed here to explain why Geoffrey's family has Crown access but Geoffrey himself ran cargo inspections for Rook. The gap between them is not just rank — it's the distance between someone the Crown uses and someone the Crown answers to.
>
> **Do not escalate until [[dorian-bishop|Bishop]] is resolved.**
>
> **Cap'n Gorgeous:** When Knighton learns of his son's death, the response bypasses Crown procedure entirely. His people, his timeline, no paperwork requirements.

## Relationships

- [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] — nephew (blood; no relationship)
- [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] — commands within; answers to Admiralty
- [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] — subordinate; dead
- [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]] — effectively his son; dead; unreported to him yet
- [[dorian-bishop|Dorian Bishop]] — subordinate; next escalation before Knighton moves

## Pressure Points

- Cap'n Gorgeous's death gives Knighton a personal channel outside Crown procedure.
- Geoffrey's defection makes the family connection useful once the party becomes visible enough.

Aasimar fortune-teller and wanderer, Delmar Fisk's wife — drawn to specific places by precognitive pull, currently somewhere in the Scatter.

# Serafina Windfall Fisk

![[Serafina-Windfall-Fisk.webp|Serafina Windfall Fisk looking over a stormy harbor with red cloth whipping in the wind]]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Aasimar |
| **Role** | Fortune-teller, compelled wanderer |
| **Location** | Unknown — somewhere in the Scatter |

## Overview

Serafina Windfall Fisk is an Aasimar fortune-teller who moves through the Scatter on compulsion — drawn to specific places and people at specific times by a precognitive pull she has stopped trying to explain or fight. She goes where she is needed. She does not always know why until she arrives.

She is [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk's]] wife. They married knowing their work would keep them apart more often than not. She was not aboard the *Red Lady* when the fleet went down. Fisk named [[the-duchess|his musket]] after her.

## Appearance & Manner

Tall, dark-skinned, with long curly reddish-brown hair kept bundled in a headscarf. Reads as human at a glance and rarely corrects the assumption. Long multicolored skirt, and a well-kept leather tarot case she produces before she sits down.

## The Gift

Her fortune-telling is genuinely accurate — not infallible, she would say that herself — but reliable enough that people who have seen it once tend not to bet against it a second time. She does not perform. She tells you what she read, does not elaborate on method, and does not chase you down if you choose not to hear it.

She goes where the pull leads. Some meetings she knows are coming weeks in advance. Others she understands only after. Either way, she is where she is supposed to be.

## Relationships

- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — husband
- [[the-duchess|The Duchess]] — Delmar's musket; named for her
- [[red-lady|Red Lady]] — the ship she was not aboard when it went down

## Pressure Points

- Her pull can bring her into a scene before anyone understands why she needs to be there.
- Her absence from the *Red Lady* disaster makes her one of the few pieces of Delmar's old life not swallowed by the Maw.

She goes where the pull leads. Some meetings she knows are coming weeks in advance. Others she understands only after. Either way, she is where she is supposed to be.

Relationships

  • Delmar Fisk — husband
  • The Duchess — Delmar’s musket; named for her
  • Red Lady — the ship she was not aboard when it went down

Pressure Points

  • Her pull can bring her into a scene before anyone understands why she needs to be there.
  • Her absence from the Red Lady disaster makes her one of the few pieces of Delmar’s old life not swallowed by the Maw.

# Shepherd Grigori

| | |
|---|---|
| **Role** | Wandering holy man; miracle worker to the desperate nobility |
| **Location** | Currently ashore in [[calveno|Calveno]]; no fixed port |

> *"Anyone who wants off at the next port walks free."*

## Overview

Shepherd Grigori is a miracle worker — the story is consistent across the noble courts of the Crown Islands. A holy man who appeared from nowhere and started curing noble heirs of things that shouldn't be curable. Red and gold coat, glass of wine, always a guest on someone else's ship.

He is said to be impossible to kill. Poison. Drowning. Worse. He survives. The nobility who have benefited from his cures don't tend to ask how.

## Appearance & Manner

Rugged, imposing frame. Dark flowing hair, untamed beard, unnerving hypnotic gaze. Opulent red and gold coats. Usually seen with a glass of fine wine.

His presence fills a room. Warm, deliberate, genuinely curious about people. He asks good questions and listens to the answers. Calm and practical — runs a galley the way a diplomat runs a meeting.

## Session History

### Session 02 — Aboard the Surety

The party found Grigori in the galley with the table already set. He had made something real out of the galley's stores. He asked what kind of pirates they were. No trafficking, no cannibalism — near enough.

The crew filed out from behind a locked door after he gave the signal. [[old-faas|Old Faas]] explained why they stayed loyal to Grigori despite the fear: Rook had taken six crew ashore at [[murrat|Murrat]] to retrieve a "specimen." Four came back needing the surgeon. [[alys-kuiper|Alys]] kept them alive as long as she could. Grigori sat with them through the night. *"They pulled through because of him. I'll say that plainly."* The crew does not know what that credit means.

He told them about [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]] and [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]] — specifically that Knighton would send ships in response to Gorgeous's death. His condition for the surviving crew: anyone who wants off at the next port walks free. He said he was glad [[ket|Ket]] was freed.

He has business in Calveno — a young heir whose physicians have given up on them.

### Session 03 — Calveno Departure

After the whip shark fight, Grigori came up to the weather deck carrying tins of a pale healing liquid for the crew. He healed [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]'s wounds silently — a red, viscous, gaseous light flowed from his wrist and knit the flesh. No components, no words, no incantation. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]]'s Arcana roll (18) confirmed: the magic just flowed.

He mentioned "Impuni" — someone he needs to reach in Calveno in time.

At [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] he said his goodbyes, thanked the party for the voyage, and left alone. His handshake with [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] was icy cold — not normal warmth, like touching a dead body.

He expects his Calveno business concluded in a week or two.

## Table Tells

Three specific details for crew-time scenes or any moment a PC pays close attention:

- **Never sleeps.** If it's late and someone checks, he's awake. He does not explain this.
- **Hands always cold.** Every handshake. Not cool — cold, like pressing flesh that has been outside too long. He does not react to it.
- **Prays at 3am in a language that isn't Common.** If someone catches him, he finishes, folds his hands, and turns to face them. He is not rattled if asked.

> [!dm]
> Do not explain any of these. If a player asks about one, ask back: *"What do you do?"* He will give a warm, partial non-answer. Move on.

## Current State

Ashore in [[calveno|Calveno]]. Business of his own; 1–2 week timeline. His magic type is unidentified. His knowledge of Crown operations on the *Uncertainty* has not been fully tapped.

> [!dm]
> **DM Truth:** Grigori is an undead sorcerer and shepherd of the [[khlysty|Khlysty]] — a secret mystical flock threaded through Dravosi and Tessarine noble courts. He heals dying heirs and binds them as unwitting phylactery threads. The cold handshake and unidentifiable magic are the player-facing mystery. Develop his Calveno business (Impuni) before the party crosses his path again. The Khlysty truth should surface in layers, not exposition.

## Relationships

- [[calveno|Calveno]] — current destination
- [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]] — warned the party about him
- [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]] — gave Knighton intelligence about
- [[ket|Ket]] — was glad to see him freed

# Sienne Orre

![[Sienne-Orre.webp]]

| | |
|---|---|

| **Status** | Deceased — soul inside [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] |

Sienne captained the *[[fernen|Fernen]]*, the fleet's fourth vessel. Druid, capable of wildshaping into aquatic forms. She ran the second underwater scout team alongside [[maren|Maren]] during the perimeter survey of Umberlee's shrine island. She was outside the cave when the fleet sank.

Her soul was pressed into [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] at the moment of sinking, along with the other four captains.

---

## Appearance & Manner

Silver-streaked hair cut close, older than her role implied she needed to be. She carries that without embarrassment. Unhurried — she moves like someone who has learned that rushing produces worse information. Wherever she goes, she is writing something down.

## The Voice

Meticulous report delivered after three drafts. Worn by how rarely other people come as prepared as she does.

**At table:**
> *"We have the perimeter, we have the chart, and we have one piece that isn't matching. I need five minutes."*
> *"I know it's not what you wanted to hear. I wrote down what I saw."*

---

## Mortis — When She Surfaces

| | |
|---|---|
| **Trigger (forced)** | Targeted by 2nd+ level spell, or fails Int save |
| **Trigger (env)** | Green mermaid sign/figurehead/carving — wistfulness, asks how long it's been there |
| **Skills granted** | Arcana, Investigation |
| **Personality shift** | Methodical, careful. Slows down, wants more info before committing. |
| **Cue** | Asks questions instead of answering. Charm quiets. Almost professorial. |

---

## Backstory

She kept a room at the Green Mermaid — a harborside tavern in Kettermoor — where she stored fourteen years of research notes. Tide charts, druidic correspondences, migration patterns, contracts annotated in the margins. She had been meaning to organize them properly. She did not get to.

She went to sea because the sea had a set of systems she didn't yet understand, and she was constitutionally incapable of leaving a system unexplained.

---

- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — admiral; now carries her soul
- [[fernen|The Fernen]] — her ship
- [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]] — her fleet
- [[maren|Maren]] — ran the second scout team with her

## Pressure Points

- She surfaces when magic targets Delmar directly — investigation replaces action.
- The Green Mermaid sign or figurehead is the quietest trigger: wistfulness, a question about how long it's been there.

# Simone Tabarnack

| | |

| **Species** | Grung (Purple Caste) |

| **Location** | [[sorn|Sorn]], [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] |

## Overview

Simone Tabarnack is [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude's]] younger sister. She is purple-caste — skilled, disciplined, and fully committed to the Botukuri clan and its caste order. She was a garrison soldier on [[sorn|Sorn]] when Jean-Claude left.

She is the one who told their parents about [[pell|Pell]].

Jean-Claude walked into that hut expecting the best day of his life. He found Simone already there, Pell already in chains, and every part of the plan already known. What followed was a month of torture. By the time he ran, he understood exactly what she had done and why. She had done it because she believed in the clan. She still does.

## Appearance & Manner

Purple Grung, compact and precise. Fitted armor, spear in hand. She carries herself like someone used to giving orders from a position of caste authority — still when things around her are moving, watching before committing. Reads as a soldier first and a person second.

## What Jean-Claude Knows

She was younger than him and always more certain. Where he questioned the system quietly, she moved through it with the confidence of someone who has never seen a reason to doubt it. Reporting him wasn't a betrayal in her frame. It was the correct action. That is the part that stays with him: not that she did it, but that she thought she was right to.

## Session 01 — The Canister

During the Session 01 boarding of the [[saltwright|Saltwright]], a Dravosi Alchemist threw a gas canister into the fight. [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] was caught in the cloud. He placed the compound immediately — standard Grung hunting toxin, cheap bulk stock. What stopped him was the preparation method. He knew that hand. He and Simone had brewed versions of it together before he left.

His sister is supplying the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]].

She sold them something disposable — cheap enough to pass Crown intake as "amphibian alkaloid derivative," generic enough to disappear from any supply ledger. Jean-Claude said nothing. The party doesn't know yet.

> [!dm]
> **Open questions:** Does she know Jean-Claude is operating in the Shattered Sea? Is the Crown arrangement voluntary, coerced, or commercially arms-length? What does the Crown want from Grung toxin specifically? Her toxin supply to the Crown is the thread that connects Jean-Claude's desertion to current party events. See [[the-canister|The Canister]] situation.

## Relationships

- [[pell|Pell]] — her betrayal put him in chains
- [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] — supplies with Grung toxin
- [[sorn|Sorn]] — garrison base

Red-caste Grung warlock and Simone's ritual specialist — operates the Otar summoning circle beneath the Mercatura. Pact-bound chaos caster with Counterspell and Hold Person.

# Solange Barret

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Grung (Red Caste) |
| **Role** | Ritual specialist, warlock; direct subordinate of [[simone-tabarnack\|Simone Tabarnack]] |
| **Location** | [[calveno-sewers-grung-magazines\|Primary detonation chamber]], Mercatura collector system |

## Overview

Solange Barret is the reason [[otar-the-foul|Otar the Foul]] can be summoned at all. She is the only member of Simone's operation with the arcane training to operate the summoning circle beneath the Mercatura — a circle built with techniques the Grung did not develop themselves. Solange learned the binding geometry from her patron, an entity she does not name and refers to only as *le courant* (the current).

She is red caste — the highest operational rank below Simone herself. Where Simone designs operations, Solange executes the parts that require precision no warrior can provide. She has been with Simone since Sorn, and she is the only subordinate Simone trusts with the circle's activation sequence.

## Appearance & Manner

Red-skinned Grung, small even for her kind. Wears no armor — a sleeveless leather harness over bare skin, tools and chalk sticks in belt loops. Her hands are always stained with circle-inscription residue: powdered limestone, charcoal, something iridescent that does not wash off. She works with the focused stillness of someone who knows that one misdrawn line ends the operation. Does not speak unless spoken to. When she does, her voice is flat and certain.

## Roleplay Concept

Seminary dropout meets demolitions engineer. She has real arcane training in a society that does not value it, and she treats the summoning circle with the reverence of someone who understands exactly what she is calling through. Not fanatical — professional. The circle is her craft. Otar is her work product.

> *"The circle is not a weapon. It is an invitation. What arrives does not care about your objections."*

## Proactive Objective

When the party encounters Solange, she is working. Final inscriptions on the summoning circle — calibrating the resonance channels that key the activation to the blackpowder detonation above. She has been at this for hours. She is close to finished. Her attention is split between the circle and the four [[grung-elite-warrior|Elite Warriors]] guarding the chamber. She does not expect intruders at the primary site — it is compartmentalized above green-caste clearance, and the secondary sites should absorb any interference.

## Tactical Behavior

**Opening:** Mirror Image is already active (pre-cast, 3 duplicates — soaks 3 attacks before real damage lands). Hex on Crissdalynn (disadvantage on STR checks — shuts down grapple dominance, the party's strongest opener). Eldritch Blast from behind the Elite Warrior line. Stays within 10 ft of the circle (Circle Ward: AC 15, advantage on concentration saves). The circle sheds bright light in a 10-ft radius — Jean-Claude's Umbral Sight does not function here.

**Escalation:** If a spellcaster attempts to disrupt the circle or target the Elite Warriors with control spells, Solange Counterspells. She has two 3rd-level slots — one Counterspell burns half her resources. Force her to choose between maintaining Hex and countering party magic. If Crissdalynn breaks Hex through damage or distance, Solange re-Hexes on the next grapple threat.

**Crisis:** If the chamber is clearly lost (3+ Elite Warriors dead, circle being physically disrupted), Solange uses Misty Step to break line of sight, then Dimension Door on her next turn to escape entirely. She will not die for the circle — she is too important to Simone's future operations.

**Morale:** Retreats when the fight is clearly lost. Does not surrender. If captured, she says nothing about Simone. She gives her name and caste. That is all.

## If She Escapes

Solange reports to Simone: the primary site is compromised, the party includes a Grung defector who identified caste notation (Jean-Claude), and the operation's centrepiece is lost. This confirmation — that Jean-Claude is actively working against the clan — is a major escalation of Simone's awareness. It is also the first intelligence Simone receives about exactly who is interfering.

Tactical Behavior

Opening: Mirror Image is already active (pre-cast, 3 duplicates — soaks 3 attacks before real damage lands). Hex on Crissdalynn (disadvantage on STR checks — shuts down grapple dominance, the party’s strongest opener). Eldritch Blast from behind the Elite Warrior line. Stays within 10 ft of the circle (Circle Ward: AC 15, advantage on concentration saves). The circle sheds bright light in a 10-ft radius — Jean-Claude’s Umbral Sight does not function here.

Escalation: If a spellcaster attempts to disrupt the circle or target the Elite Warriors with control spells, Solange Counterspells. She has two 3rd-level slots — one Counterspell burns half her resources. Force her to choose between maintaining Hex and countering party magic. If Crissdalynn breaks Hex through damage or distance, Solange re-Hexes on the next grapple threat.

Crisis: If the chamber is clearly lost (3+ Elite Warriors dead, circle being physically disrupted), Solange uses Misty Step to break line of sight, then Dimension Door on her next turn to escape entirely. She will not die for the circle — she is too important to Simone’s future operations.

Morale: Retreats when the fight is clearly lost. Does not surrender. If captured, she says nothing about Simone. She gives her name and caste. That is all.

If She Escapes

Solange reports to Simone: the primary site is compromised, the party includes a Grung defector who identified caste notation (Jean-Claude), and the operation’s centrepiece is lost. This confirmation — that Jean-Claude is actively working against the clan — is a major escalation of Simone’s awareness. It is also the first intelligence Simone receives about exactly who is interfering.

  • Calveno — Beffa Grung Raid — the operation Solange’s ritual anchors
  • Jean-Claude Tabarnack — if Solange escapes, she identifies him to Simone

Port Tidefall factor's daughter who can read a cargo manifest faster than most Crown inspectors — searching records for Geoffrey Draves, sitting on a ledger anomaly that implicates her family's license.

# Verity Hollowell

| | |
|---|---|
| **Species** | Human (Dravosi) |
| **Role** | Secondary account manager, Hollowell Import Agency |
| **Location** | [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] |

## Overview

Verity Hollowell is the older daughter of [[cedric-hollowell|Cedric Hollowell]], whose import agency operates near the Tidefall inspection pier. She came into the ledger work sideways — she caught errors faster than the men paid to catch them, and eventually her father stopped pretending the arrangement was temporary.

She met a sailor once on a shore leave dock, years ago. They spent several hours moving together in the dark, no conversation that needed words, just movement and the sound of the water under the dock. Then a ship's bell called him back and he went. She returned to that dock on subsequent evenings for a long time. He was not there.

Then her father went instead, one evening, and waited.

She does not speak about what was said. She has continued her ledger work. She is careful now about what she brings home.

## Role

If the party arrives in Port Tidefall and [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey's]] name surfaces, she already knows it is him. She does not volunteer this. She answers what is asked.

She is more useful than her father in most practical conversations — she has the same Tidefall access and considerably better judgment about when to use it.

## Manner

Twenty-four. Dark hair kept pinned under a practical hat when working. A particular stillness people mistake for disinterest until they notice she has already catalogued everything in the room. Level tone. Complete sentences. Does not reach for warmth or frost on strangers.

> *"The secondary accounts are mine. The primary ones are my father's. If you need access to pier scheduling, that runs through my desk."*

> [!dm]
> **The ledger problem:** Sitting on a gap in her father's primary accounts — bonded cargo moved through Hollowell licensing without a formal manifest entry. Whether her father placed it or someone exploited his credentials is unresolved. She has reported nothing. The gap implicates her family's license and her father's standing.

## Relationships

- [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] — the sailor she met; currently serving on the party's ship
- [[cedric-hollowell|Cedric Hollowell]] — her father; she manages his secondary accounts
- [[aldous-draves|Aldous Draves]] — Geoffrey's father; connected through Tidefall commerce

Fourteen-year-old crow aarakocra monk (Kensei 4). Sole survivor of the Red Lady with Delmar Fisk; was mapping the Drowned Maw when it sank. Kyzil's student; cast out of the High Eyrie at 14 — the monastery banishment is the wound that makes everything else matter.

# Crissdalynn Khinriss

Fourteen. Blue-black iridescent feathers. Geometric leatherwork armor. Chart satchel. Talons. Flies.

Irreverent and light until the fight starts. First three seconds of combat: friends, exit, weak point — in that order, without thinking.

> [!dm]
> Whose opinion matters: [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]]. He is the fixed point. If someone threatens him, everything stops. She pulled him from the crow's nest as the Maw closed and flew them both through thirty feet of solid water.

## Backstory

Was mapping the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] for [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]] when the [[red-lady|Red Lady]] went down. The task was consequence and calling both — she'd been goofing off at the [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]] and was cast out at 14, not for malice but for not taking her craft seriously. The mapping was the assigned price.

The timeline source states her banishment is permanent until the Drowned Maw task is complete. She served aboard the Red Lady for one year and ten months before the fleet sank.

The mapping is incomplete. She knows it.

**The wound:** The monastery banishment. It's why the wreck matters more than it otherwise would. Not the direct cause — but the context that makes it load-bearing.

## What She Wants

- **Says:** Kyzil's approval. Finish the Maw mapping. Kinship with the monastery that cast her out.
- **Actually:** To be let back in. The banishment is still open.
- **Core belief:** Shiny things are valuable regardless of what they actually are. She has said this aloud.
- **Red line:** Will not turn her back on those she is loyal to.

## Gear

- Crystal dreidel from Kyzil — casts rainbows in sunlight; in her pocket
- Satchel of charts

## Mechanics

**Class:** Monk (Kensei) 4 | **Background:** Acolyte / Cartographer

**Species:** [[aarakocra|Aarakocra]]

**Tactical note:** No darkvision. Jean-Claude's darkness features (invisibility, advantage) are a liability for her — she is blinded and at disadvantage in magical darkness. Party coordination required when managing light.

**Gods:** [[remnis|Remnis]] (primary). [[syranita|Syranita]] and [[aerdrie-faenya|Aerdrie Faenya]] in the margins. Wears it lightly; prays from habit, not theology.

**Read the Current (Kensei technique, taught by Kyzil):** Once on her turn when she hits a creature with an unarmed strike or Kensei weapon, she can spend 1 ki/focus point to read the target through the contact. Cannot combine with Stunning Strike or Deft Strike on the same hit. Choose one question; DM answers truthfully using combat-observable information:

- **Guard:** What is this creature relying on most for defense right now — armor, agility, toughness, will, magic, distance, or terrain?
- **Opening:** Which saving throw appears easiest to pressure — STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, or CHA?
- **Pattern:** What is one combat habit the creature is relying on right now — counterattacks, reach, mobility, guarding an ally, protecting an object, concentration, brute force, or escape?

No exact numbers, full statblocks, secret identity, hidden lore, or motives. Repeating on the same creature should reveal a different category or deeper version, not the same fact again.

## Relationships

- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — fixed point; sole co-survivor of the Red Lady; his opinion is the one that matters
- [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]] — mentor; approval-chase; gifted her the crystal dreidel
- [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] — party

## Session Events

- **Session 01** — Dragged Cap'n Gorgeous through Perrin's Minor Illusion to conceal the engagement; breached the weather deck when Delmar launched her through the hatch; redirected Grung toxin gas with Gust.
- **Session 02** — Deflected Rook's flintlock shot; blocked Perrin before he killed Ket; let Ket feed on Rook's men.
- **Session 03** — Caught Perrin and JC in their rigging fall from the crow's nest. Flew out over the water and lifted a 60-ft whip shark clean out of the sea (contested strength; shark nat 1). Dug through Rook's chart archive — found he broke Imperial rules about the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] twice and kept no record of what he found. Tried to scout Calveno from above; too many people, gave up. Reunited with [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]] in Le Paludi streets — he dove from the sun. Broke down.
- **Session 04** — Sparred [[master-kyzil|Kyzil]] on the [[ponte-bassa|Ponte Bassa]] rooftop. Grappled him R1 (Kyzil rolled nat 1 on contested check); Kyzil acknowledged her growth. Activated tattoo for 15ft reach. Deflected 13 damage and redirected it (Kyzil saved). Fell off the roof from Kyzil's Downburst — Kyzil panicked and flew down to catch her. Vouched for [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] to Kyzil. Kyzil told her the pilgrimage was the hardest in Eyrie history. Clotheslined the second patrol Grung in the sewers. Kingfishered the fleeing purple Grung at 45ft fly speed — dove from altitude, grappled with talons, shrugged off the spear hit and poison (Hero's Feast immunity). Delivered the captive to the party. Leg-swept [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] the next morning for going to [[umberlee|Umberlee]] without her: "My burden was to carry you out of that stupid water." Flew ~100ft over Calveno looking for Kyzil — couldn't spot him.

41-year-old human Swashbuckler Rogue 4. Self-appointed Admiral; carries five captains' souls pressed into him by Umberlee when his fleet sank. His crime triggered the sinking. He hasn't told anyone.

# Delmar Atticus Fisk

Sandy red hair in a messy topknot. Thick beard and curled moustache going grey at the edges. The smile reaches his eyes. Built by the sea, held together by charm.

The scarlet admiral coat is in the captain's chest ashore. He doesn't put it on unless he has to.

> [!dm]
> Self-appointed Admiral — youngest in living memory, bought the title with charm before anyone official handed it to him. Five captains' voices live in his head. He is never alone in his own head.

## The Wound

[[umberlee|Umberlee]] pressed five captains' souls into him when his fleet sank — the five who stayed loyal through every rank, the five he could have saved. They surface as personalities. Duration is limited: running too long shifts his cadence, his diction, his names for people.

The fleet had stolen the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] from Umberlee's Blue Shrine on [[vel-orn|Vel Orn]]. The Red Lady was the flagship; [[the-narrow|The Narrow]], [[heft|Heft]], [[fernen|Fernen]], and [[loud-argument|Loud Argument]] went down with it.

The five captains were [[rael-corven|Rael Corven]], [[maren|Maren]], [[detto-kalash|Detto Kalash]], [[sienne-orre|Sienne Orre]], and [[bastian-crev|Bastian Crev]]. See [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]].

**The secret:** The crime that triggered the sinking was his. He made the call. He didn't intend what happened, but five people paid with their souls.

**What he wants:** Resurrect the five captains. If impossible, release them so they can find their afterlives. Full resurrection is where his guardrails come off.

**What he wants to become:** Stable. Forgiven — though he knows that has to be earned.

## Mechanics

**Class:** Swashbuckler Rogue 4 | **Background:** Sailor

**Mortis:** Five captains as personalities. Each brings skill proficiencies and borrowed mastery. Duration limited — running too long causes drift (hair, cadence, names). See Session 03: called Crissdalynn "Crystalline."

**Return trigger:** A brass flagon. Tied to the night after the mutiny — stranded with nothing, five people who stayed, one flagon passed around. The moment the fleet was born. Anchors him to himself before the captains take hold.

**Phobia:** Ferrets. Abject terror. Not weasels — ferrets specifically. Learned as a boy. Clear on his face when triggered.

## Gear

- [[the-duchess|The Duchess]] — musket; his wife
- [[the-baroness|The Baroness]] — rapier
- Scarlet admiral coat / [[delmars-cloak-of-the-manta-ray|Cloak of the Manta Ray]] — locked in captain's chest ashore in Calveno
- Pocket watch with mother's picture inside — his father's only relic; his mother pickpocketed it for him

## Personality

**Core belief:** Everyone has value regardless of station; everyone has use even if they don't see it. Extended generosity as default. Developed an eye for reading people as self-protection.

**Red line:** Loyalty to found family is absolute. Do not call his crew backstabbers — the smile stays but the eyes don't. Violence is on the table.

**Crisis response:** Group assessment, self-assessment, then choice: fight, escape, or in what order. Prefers talking his way out — better coin in it.

## Backstory

As a kid: shipwreck during a pirate attack. Stranded on an island with a disgruntled, dangerous group of survivors. Built a raft with help from one kind crew member; escaped. Returned years later with a proper boat to rescue the remaining survivors. Found only corpses. Hardened something in him. He kept the smile.

## Key Relationships

**[[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]]** — The fixed point. Sole co-survivor of the [[red-lady|Red Lady]]. She grabbed him from the crow's nest as the Maw closed. Her opinion is the one that matters.

**[[margaret-porcelain-pots|Margaret "Maggie" Porcelain Pots]]** — First love. Dragonborn, glittering peach-and-cream scales, vibrant pink eyes. Ended in an argument — she punched him hard enough to leave a shiner for a week. He has avoided her on every return to his home island. A reunion would hit hard on both sides.

## Session Events

- **Session 01** — Fired the opening musket shot in the hold; took temporary hearing loss from the blast; knelt as a launch platform for Crissdalynn's deck breach; talked Geoffrey Draves into defecting.
- **Session 02** — Fired through the HCS Surety gun port and hit Ensign Wouters. Picked up a chair, called for wind, threw it — Rook went into the water a second time and didn't come back. Told Beaumont he had a friend in [[admiral-fisk|Admiral Fisk]].
- **Session 03** — Fired both swivels and the broadside at the whip shark in one coordinated shot. Dove in manta ray form to retrieve the whip shark barb. Delmar Atticus Fisk

Sandy red hair in a messy topknot. Thick beard and curled moustache going grey at the edges. The smile reaches his eyes. Built by the sea, held together by charm.

The scarlet admiral coat is in the captain’s chest ashore. He doesn’t put it on unless he has to.

DM Note

Self-appointed Admiral — youngest in living memory, bought the title with charm before anyone official handed it to him. Five captains’ voices live in his head. He is never alone in his own head.

The Wound

Umberlee pressed five captains’ souls into him when his fleet sank — the five who stayed loyal through every rank, the five he could have saved. They surface as personalities. Duration is limited: running too long shifts his cadence, his diction, his names for people.

The fleet had stolen the Pearl of Souls from Umberlee’s Blue Shrine on Vel Orn. The Red Lady was the flagship; The Narrow, Heft, Fernen, and Loud Argument went down with it.

The five captains were Rael Corven, Maren, Detto Kalash, Sienne Orre, and Bastian Crev. See Fisk’s Fleet.

The secret: The crime that triggered the sinking was his. He made the call. He didn’t intend what happened, but five people paid with their souls.

What he wants: Resurrect the five captains. If impossible, release them so they can find their afterlives. Full resurrection is where his guardrails come off.

What he wants to become: Stable. Forgiven — though he knows that has to be earned.

Mechanics

Class: Swashbuckler Rogue 4 | Background: Sailor

Mortis: Five captains as personalities. Each brings skill proficiencies and borrowed mastery. Duration limited — running too long causes drift (hair, cadence, names). See Session 03: called Crissdalynn “Crystalline.”

Return trigger: A brass flagon. Tied to the night after the mutiny — stranded with nothing, five people who stayed, one flagon passed around. The moment the fleet was born. Anchors him to himself before the captains take hold.

Phobia: Ferrets. Abject terror. Not weasels — ferrets specifically. Learned as a boy. Clear on his face when triggered.

Gear

  • The Duchess — musket; his wife
  • The Baroness — rapier
  • Scarlet admiral coat / Cloak of the Manta Ray — locked in captain’s chest ashore in Calveno
  • Pocket watch with mother’s picture inside — his father’s only relic; his mother pickpocketed it for him

Personality

Core belief: Everyone has value regardless of station; everyone has use even if they don’t see it. Extended generosity as default. Developed an eye for reading people as self-protection.

Red line: Loyalty to found family is absolute. Do not call his crew backstabbers — the smile stays but the eyes don’t. Violence is on the table.

Crisis response: Group assessment, self-assessment, then choice: fight, escape, or in what order. Prefers talking his way out — better coin in it.

Backstory

As a kid: shipwreck during a pirate attack. Stranded on an island with a disgruntled, dangerous group of survivors. Built a raft with help from one kind crew member; escaped. Returned years later with a proper boat to rescue the remaining survivors. Found only corpses. Hardened something in him. He kept the smile.

12-year-old blue Grung Gloomstalker Ranger 4. Cannot lie or mask himself (Mortis). Carries guilt for a gnome's death and for the slave raids he ran before his conscience woke. Simone is his sister and she betrayed him.

# Jean-Claude Tabarnack

Three feet tall. Electric-blue slick skin with large black underside patches and geometric black bands across arms, legs, shoulders, and face. Visible scars worn proudly. Hard escaped-hunter stare.

Red beret. False black moustache. Worn ranger harness. [[corto-di-velo|Corto di Velo]].

> [!dm]
> Cannot lie or mask his intentions — permanent disadvantage on Persuasion/Deception (Mortis). What you see is what he is. Advantage on Perception/Survival in exchange. He is genuinely uncertain whether this is a flaw or just how he is.

## The Wounds

**[[pell|Pell]]:** His gnome friend. Tortured to death over a month as a lesson in hardness. When JC freed slaves and fled, they were slaughtered behind him — their screams covered his exit. He ran into the dark. He hasn't processed any of it. Just moving.

**The last ordinary day:** He had a plan — petition his parents to make Pell his personal slave, take him hunting to establish companionship, then fake Pell's death and let him go free. He walked to his parents' hut and found his sister, his parents, and Pell already in chains. [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]] had betrayed them. The moment his plan would have worked was already gone.

After Pell's death and the slave escape, he fled east through the [[midchain|Midchain]], living rough for months to avoid leaving a trail — keeping ahead of Simone's garrison at [[sorn|Sorn]]. Her hunter unit followed one island behind.

**The secret:** Before his conscience woke, he was a slave-raider. Scout years: identified settlements, acquired slaves, developed ambush tactics, and made the Grung a more effective threat. Did it chasing glory. Was good at it. No one knows.

## What He Wants

- **Now:** See the world. Find a society not built on slavery.
- **Long-term:** Return to the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] with enough power and evidence to show the [[grung-clans|Grung clans]] a better way.
- **The pipe dream:** Be the one who changes Grung society forever. Pell taught him that every species has unique strengths and working together is the only way to grow. He's living for both of them now.

**Who he trusts:** No one yet. Hopefully someone, eventually.

**What he hasn't processed:** The suffering of the slaves — the gnome and the ones who died escaping. He ran. Their screams covered his exit. He has not dealt with it. Just moving.

**One thing he'd compromise for:** Freedom. For anyone. He would do questionable things to deliver it, and he knows it.

## Mechanics

**Class:** Gloomstalker Ranger 4 | **Background:** Hermit

**Species:** [[grung|Grung]] (blue caste) | **Clan:** Botukuri *(BOH-too-KOO-ree)*

**Mortis:** Permanent disadvantage Persuasion/Deception; advantage Perception/Survival. Cannot mask intentions.

**Darkness:** Umbral Sight — invisible to darkvision creatures in dim light/darkness. Hard counters: magical daylight, Blindsight/Tremorsense enemies. Extra Attack at level 5 will nearly double sustained damage output.

**Combat terrain:** Vertical (climb speed), water (amphibious), tight spaces (Small). Prone enemies give him disadvantage on ranged attacks >5 ft — melee allies should signal before dropping targets prone.

## Personality

**Crisis response:** He thinks first. Reads the situation. Then acts. Unless someone is being hurt — then thought doesn't enter into it.

**Red line:** Slavery is absolute. Will break formation and attack without thought if he witnesses active abuse or torture.

**Phobia:** Genetic terror of birds. Avian creatures make him deeply uneasy; fast-moving or threatening birds trigger visible fear.

> [!dm]
> [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] is a crow aarakocra. JC has a genetic terror of birds. This tension exists and the table may not have fully surfaced it — available as a pressure point or a trust-building moment.

**Belief:** Any intentional non-combat skin-to-skin contact is the beginning of a mating ritual. Watching the party hug or shake hands perplexes him. He does not understand.

**Disguise logic:** Grung distinguish caste by color, so humanoids must distinguish individuals by facial hair and accessories. Red beret, false moustache. The disguise has worked. He does not find this remarkable.

**Nicknames in the wild:** "Jumpy Don't Touch," "Sticky Tongue Death Skin," "Hopstradamus."

**On those who can't fight back:** Treats them with compassion and pity — unless they're committing evil. He was not raised this way. He had to find it himself.

**On Umberlee:** Respects her — not for goodness, but because the sea doesn't care about caste or species. *"Equally a bitch to everyone. There's something almost fair in that."*

**When scared:** Tries to master his fear by becoming something to be feared.

**Transparent by nature:** He cannot mask himself, his intentions, or what he is. This reads as mechanical Mortis and social behavior: he is genuinely unsure whether he is bad at talking to people or if something deeper is happening.

## Party

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]], [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]], [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]].

## Simone

His younger sister. She betrayed Pell and him to their parents. A reunion would be a threat and a grief in equal measure. He has twenty vials of her tincture in the cargo and has said nothing to the party. See [[the-canister|The Canister]].

## Session Events

- **Session 01** — Opened gangplank engagement with [[flask-of-endless-water|Flask of Endless Water]] geyser, blasting Rook off the plank; identified the Grung toxin canister as Simone's work; said nothing.
- **Session 02** — Used the [[truth-stone|Truth Stone]] Beaumont gave him; confirmed three truths: former kinsmen hunted him, he stowed away to survive, nobody sent him. Found twenty vials of Simone's tincture in the HCS Surety cargo; said nothing. Seasick in the storm.
- **Session 03** — Fell from rigging with [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] (nat 1); Crissdalynn caught both. Arrowed the whip shark; chest torn open by tail swipe; held on. Shot arrow through shark's anus — killed it. Healed by Grigori (wordless, red viscous light). Recovered 3 fertilized whip shark eggs. Worked hull with Sem Holst for 4 days; Sem quietly fixed what he missed. Changed color green as city disguise; visited [[casa-lupo|Casa Lupo]], then [[studio-orsini|Studio Orsini]] re: eggs. See [[whip-shark-eggs|Whip Shark Eggs]].
- **Session 04** — Sold 3 whip shark eggs for 300gp (30pt) to a Le Paludi merchant. Bought a +1 [[silent-shortbow|silent shortbow]] (50gp) and [[boots-of-flying|boots of flying]] (125gp) from [[casa-lupo|Casa Lupo]]; gave the boots to the party (went to [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] after [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] realized he doesn't wear shoes). Met [[master-kyzil|Kyzil]] — dismissed as "no threat"; Kyzil pinned his shirt with a returning dagger during the spar as a dominance display. JC pulled it free, killed his cigarette, stared Kyzil down. Led the Grung sewer investigation at [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]]'s request — scouted from the ceiling via Gloom Stalker, found Grung directional markers, ambushed two patrol Grung from above (24 damage instant kill via Dread Strike). Fired a fire arrow into 8 barrels of black powder, destroying the ship. Executed the purple Grung captive after it called him a traitor and confirmed [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]]'s involvement: "I wish you could see the error of your ways." Took the fake handlebar mustache. Learned Grung defectors exist as a recognized kill-on-sight category — he is one. Wants to keep [[felix-aho|Felix Aho]] alive to learn about defectors.

Ten-year-old fancy-rat Rattkin Bard 3 / Warlock 1. Built the Vestra to support his family; lost it to something massive from below; now carries vengeance, silence, and Nona's favor.

# Perrin Black-Jaw

Three feet tall. Ten-year-old lean fancy-rat Rattkin: black head, white body, long pink tail, olive-drab hooded cloak, cream shirt, bodhran drum at hip, oversized longsword that looks too big for him. Shortest person in the party by a significant margin; compensates with volume, charm, and nerve.

Used **Minor Illusion** to conceal the doorway in the Saltwright hold during the ambush.

## Foundation

**Class:** Bard 3 (College of Lore) / Warlock 1 (Pact of the Blade) | **Background:** Custom | **Player:** Kaden

**Species:** [[rattkin|Rattkin]] (fancy rat) | **Languages:** Common, Dwarvish, Gnomish

**Mortis:** "The Small" — disadvantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Charisma. His frame makes him unsuitable for hard ship labor, so he leads by reading currents, people, exits, and leverage.

**Core drive:** Vengeance against the thing that destroyed the [[vestra|Vestra]]. He also genuinely misses fishing, wants to support his family, and wants to become an elder of the Tangle who teaches young Rattkin how to move through the Dry without getting killed.

**What he does not see:** The chase has become the point. The version of him that survives it may not fit the Run hierarchy anymore, and he may put his family in the path of vengeance to get there.

## Beliefs And Limits

- Loyal to his Run specifically, not Rattkin broadly. Proud, not supremacist.
- Will not traffic people. Manipulation, bribery, and blackmail remain available tools.
- Does not mistreat people who cannot fight back. He also stops paying attention to them.
- Sees people as useful or not useful, and accepts this about himself.

## Current Pressure

His family knows he is alive. They do not know the full scale of the [[vestra|Vestra]]'s loss or that the ship is gone. He has gone quiet on them and knows it.

The Vestra was built and captained by Nona Black-Jaw's late husband, Perrin's grandfather. Losing it is not just a financial blow; it was the last thing his grandfather left.

Recently, something large and otherworldly spoke to him from the abyss. He was not a believer before. Now a patron-level power has decided he matters, and he does not know what that means.

The timeline source says the [[leviathan|Leviathan]] destroyed the Vestra and that Perrin believes his old cloak saved him. It was actually [[auralis|Auralis]]. Perrin forged a warlock pact in the wreck without knowing it. The [[perrins-cloak-of-the-manta-ray|Cloak of the Manta Ray]] is no longer with him.

## What He Carries

- Cloak of Protection (attuned) — current; the Manta Ray cloak is gone
- [[miras-blade|Mira's Blade]]
- [[sending-stone-nona|Nona's sending stone]]
- Longsword, bodhran drum, Clyde's Bestiary of Oceanic Creatures
- Guilt about crew members he thinks died

## Party

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]], [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]], [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]]. [[cobb|Cobb]] is an old contact met at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] on the Calveno arrival.

## Unresolved Threads

- A surviving Vestra crew member could walk through a door; relief would arrive wrapped in guilt.
- Family does not know about the ship.
- Perrin does not know what destroyed the Vestra, only that it was massive and came from deep below.
- Dravosi bounties on Rattkin are a background pressure: real, rarely enforced, always present.

## Combat Notes

**Strengths:** Reading people and situations, social pressure, charm, bribery, escape routes, Bard/Warlock magic.

**Weaknesses:** Prey response when genuinely scared; physical weakness from Mortis; limited trust for dry-landers; [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]]'s avian shape sits directly against his instinctive fear response.

**Crisis response:** Finds the nearest exit first. Not necessarily to run, but to know it is there.

## Session Events

- **Session 01** — Laid Minor Illusion over the hold doorway; emerged from a deck gap at a second angle during the breach; resisted Grung toxin gas.
- **Session 02** — Received [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont]]'s message: Nona Black-Jaw is searching for him; Anzolo may already be at sea. Drew his longsword to kill [[ket|Ket]] before Crissdalynn intervened; cast Tasha's Hideous Laughter to drop Ket safely. Received [[miras-blade|Mira's Blade]] from the cargo. Named himself as a Black-Jaw to the assembled crew. See [[nona-and-anzolo|Nona and Anzolo]].
- **Session 03** — Experienced the [[abyss-vision|abyss vision]] on watch: worked stone floor, bioluminescent entities, inhabited a 60-ft creature's body, witnessed something longer than two ships below, heard *"Grow."* Gave bardic inspiration to all three party members and drummed through the whip shark fight. Navigated the alternate approach into Calveno. Renamed ship to *Uncertainty* on approach. Met [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] in Le Paludi — told her about the Vestra, attacks called off, promised a favor without conditions. Received [[sending-stone-nona|Nona's sending stone]]. Spotted the bioluminescent whale on day 2 at sea and recognized it. Met [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]]; emerged from a barrel to shake his finger.
- **Session 04** — Led the party to the [[ponte-bassa|Ponte Bassa]] as their Calveno base — chose it to avoid bringing two avian predators into a Rattkin establishment. Won the boots of flying roll but passed them to [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] — doesn't wear shoes ("I have little rat feet and I need to feel the ground"). Supported the [[master-kyzil|Kyzil]] spar: healing word on Delmar (7 HP) and Crissdalynn (8 HP), bardic inspiration saved Crissdalynn's grapple (Downburst save 15+d6=20), attempted cutting words on Kyzil's attack vs himself (insufficient). Drummed from behind cover; Kyzil identified the drum as a tactical threat. Went invisible in the sewers alongside [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]], used Rattkin keen senses (5ft detection) and nose to track black powder scent. Swam underwater to scout the Grung boat — returned with intel on 3 Grung and 8 barrels. Sent urgent [[sending-stone-nona|sending stone]] message to [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] about the operation. Shared a silent knowing look with Delmar during the confession — hinted at his own undisclosed loss without revealing it.

  • Will not traffic people. Manipulation, bribery, and blackmail remain available tools.
  • Does not mistreat people who cannot fight back. He also stops paying attention to them.
  • Sees people as useful or not useful, and accepts this about himself.

Current Pressure

His family knows he is alive. They do not know the full scale of the Vestra‘s loss or that the ship is gone. He has gone quiet on them and knows it.

The Vestra was built and captained by Nona Black-Jaw’s late husband, Perrin’s grandfather. Losing it is not just a financial blow; it was the last thing his grandfather left.

Recently, something large and otherworldly spoke to him from the abyss. He was not a believer before. Now a patron-level power has decided he matters, and he does not know what that means.

The timeline source says the Leviathan destroyed the Vestra and that Perrin believes his old cloak saved him. It was actually Auralis. Perrin forged a warlock pact in the wreck without knowing it. The Cloak of the Manta Ray is no longer with him.

What He Carries

  • Cloak of Protection (attuned) — current; the Manta Ray cloak is gone
  • Mira’s Blade
  • Nona’s sending stone
  • Longsword, bodhran drum, Clyde’s Bestiary of Oceanic Creatures
  • Guilt about crew members he thinks died

Party

Jean-Claude Tabarnack, Delmar Fisk, Crissdalynn Khinriss. Cobb is an old contact met at La Vasca on the Calveno arrival.

Unresolved Threads

  • A surviving Vestra crew member could walk through a door; relief would arrive wrapped in guilt.
  • Family does not know about the ship.
  • Perrin does not know what destroyed the Vestra, only that it was massive and came from deep below.
  • Dravosi bounties on Rattkin are a background pressure: real, rarely enforced, always present.

Combat Notes

Strengths: Reading people and situations, social pressure, charm, bribery, escape routes, Bard/Warlock magic.

Weaknesses: Prey response when genuinely scared; physical weakness from Mortis; limited trust for dry-landers; Crissdalynn‘s avian shape sits directly against his instinctive fear response.

Crisis response: Finds the nearest exit first. Not necessarily to run, but to know it is there.

  • Session 01 — Laid Minor Illusion over the hold doorway; emerged from a deck gap at a second angle during the breach; resisted Grung toxin gas.
  • Session 02 — Received Beaumont‘s message: Nona Black-Jaw is searching for him; Anzolo may already be at sea. Drew his longsword to kill Ket before Crissdalynn intervened; cast Tasha’s Hideous Laughter to drop Ket safely. Received Mira’s Blade from the cargo. Named himself as a Black-Jaw to the assembled crew. See Nona and Anzolo.
  • Session 03 — Experienced the abyss vision on watch: worked stone floor, bioluminescent entities, inhabited a 60-ft creature’s body, witnessed something longer than two ships below, heard “Grow.” Gave bardic inspiration to all three party members and drummed through the whip shark fight. Navigated the alternate approach into Calveno. Renamed ship to Uncertainty on approach. Met Nona in Le Paludi — told her about the Vestra, attacks called off, promised a favor without conditions. Received Nona’s sending stone. Spotted the bioluminescent whale on day 2 at sea and recognized it. Met Master Kyzil; emerged from a barrel to shake his finger.
  • Session 04 — Led the party to the Ponte Bassa as their Calveno base — chose it to avoid bringing two avian predators into a Rattkin establishment. Won the boots of flying roll but passed them to Delmar — doesn’t wear shoes (“I have little rat feet and I need to feel the ground”). ## In the Shattered Sea

The [[doldrums|Doldrums]] are the right habitat. Still water, no wind, mangrove shallows, the accumulated rot of anything that blooms or dies in flat heat with nowhere to go. A black dragon laired in the Doldrums' deeper mangrove channels has everything it needs: cover, patience, and prey that cannot run.

A becalmed ship is close to ideal hunting. The crew cannot sail. Towing with boats means people in the water. The Doldrums silence carries the acid breath line clean across a deck with nothing to scatter it. The dragon is amphibious — it can strike from below, surface for one clean pass, and go back under before a crossbow is drawn. Crews that survive describe the attack in very similar terms: something long and dark alongside the hull that they mistook for shadow, then a burning line across the deck that smelled wrong, then a wing-shape dropping back into water that barely registered the impact. ^[inferred]

The account that made it into [[midchain|Midchain]] pilot circles came from a brig becalmed for three days south of the Midchain's edge. On the second night, a deckhand checking the stern in the pre-dawn saw a shadow beneath the keel that blotted out the bottom. Nothing else. By morning, one of the stern planks had a seam that hadn't been there at departure — dissolved rather than split. The captain towed out at first light and ran the oars for six hours until the wind found them. His repair log described weather damage. The hull carpenter's private notes said something else. ^[inferred]

## In the Shattered Sea

Blue dragons are territorial rather than predatory in the way that matters to shipping. They don't hunt vessels. They tax them.

The [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] dragon is laired in the limestone cliffs of the Greyteeth, the notoriously contradictory reef system that has defeated three generations of Crown charts. The burrowing ability is part of why the lair has never been located precisely — it digs into coastal limestone above the waterline, hunts from elevation, and uses the Greyteeth's reputation for wreck-producing reefs as cover for a second category of loss. Ships that disappear in the Greyteeth are logged as reef casualties. Some of them are. ^[inferred]

The arrangement that currently exists is not officially acknowledged by the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]], but it is functional. Captains who fly certain colours and keep a designated chest on the aft deck, unsealed, come through the northern Greyteeth passage without incident. Captains who don't know about the arrangement, or who know and decline it, take their chances with what Crown harbourmasters file as navigational error. A merchant who survived a lightning strike near the northern reef returned to port with fused iron fittings, a split boom, and three dead crew. The harbormaster's report noted challenging weather conditions. ^[inferred]

Blue dragons are lawful enough to keep agreements. The Crown is pragmatic enough to make them. Neither side has confirmed the arrangement exists. Neither side has broken it. ^[inferred]

## In the Shattered Sea

[[Galewall|Galewall]] crews have a name for it: the Stormwarden. Not a fixed name — the figure appears differently each generation, always in humanoid form, always in a small boat that has no business being where it is. A battered cutter in the middle of the storm belt. A one-mast smack running alongside a failing ship without apparent difficulty. An old woman in oilskins who comes aboard a dismasted brig in conditions that shouldn't allow boarding, sets the crew to tasks they don't understand until the ship is through, and is gone by the time anyone thinks to ask her name.

What's consistent across the accounts is the result. The ships that follow the Stormwarden's instructions reach the [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall]] lee. The ships that don't are logged as lost to weather. [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall]] crews treat the legend as navigational fact: if something appears during the worst of a crossing and offers guidance, you follow it and you ask questions afterward. ^[inferred]

The shapechange ability is the reason the legend has no single face. Bronze dragons are patient observers who take humanoid form to move among people, gather information, and intervene where they judge it necessary. The Galewall is a crossing that produces exactly the kind of military courage, desperate seamanship, and genuine stakes the dragon finds worth watching. [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall]] pilot family logs have entries predating their grandparents' time, all describing the same category of intervention in different hands. ^[inferred]

## In the Shattered Sea

The oldest [[midchain|Midchain]] pilots know that [[aruhe|Aruhe]] is not avoided because of the [[grung-clans|Grung]]. The Grung don't go there either.

The public story — patrol boats, territorial pressure, a settlement that never held — is true as far as it goes. The settlement failed because people started disappearing. Not all at once. One a season, then two, then the kind of rate that makes a community decide it has misread the island and leave while there are still enough of them to sail. The Grung patrol boats came after, and they are a sufficient reason to stay away, which is convenient because the real reason is harder to say out loud.

The water around [[aruhe|Aruhe]]'s eastern tip runs a faint brown-gold at low tide. Not silt. Not algae. Old Midchain pilots who have passed close enough know the smell — the same sharp-mineral bite as a hull plank dissolved by acid seep. Something in the flooded interior drains into the sea, and what drains out of something that old, in something that large, in an island it has had to itself for long enough to shape the drainage — that is not weather. The terraces didn't fall from neglect. They dissolved from the base up, slowly. ^[inferred]

The [[sorn|Sorn]] intermediaries who know enough of the Grung language to trade have described their name for Aruhe as something like *the island that is already eaten*. Nobody from outside has verified this. Nobody from outside has had a reason to get close enough to try. ^[inferred]

## In the Shattered Sea

The Redwind Isles are described on pilot charts as hot, arid, and barely inhabited. The barely is doing significant work.

The Isles sit in the southeastern [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]], named for the seasonal dust that blows in from the south and leaves red grit on every surface. The geology is old sandstone and dry limestone, fractured by the same ancient seismic activity that formed the Maw's trench. Good burrowing ground. Almost no fresh water. Almost nothing worth the voyage — which is the same thing colonial cartographers have written about these islands for two centuries without asking what made them that way. ^[inferred]

The Isles were not always barely inhabited. Old charts from before the colonial era mark permanent settlements on two of the larger islands and seasonal anchorages on three more. Those marks stopped appearing within a generation of each other, without explanation. Something moved in, or something that had always been there finally made its presence felt, and the people on those islands made a reasonable decision. ^[inferred]

The few vessels that have anchored in the Redwind harbours and returned describe a stillness that doesn't match the wind — an absence of birds, a quality of silence that has intent in it, and, in one account from a pilgrim ship that cut its visit very short, a shape moving through overcast above the southern cliffs that was too deliberate for weather and too large for anything else. ^[inferred]

## In the Shattered Sea

The [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] have rules every experienced salvager knows. There is a less-discussed one that veteran crews hold without advertising: do not touch the sealed rooms on the lower northwest hall.

Nobody has posted a sign. Nobody has been told directly. The rule exists because three separate crews who broke it — across different seasons, without knowing about each other — all reported the same thing: a current that wasn't there before, cold water arriving from no clear source, and their lines going taut in a direction that had nothing to do with the drift. Two of the three surfaced without the pieces they went down for. The third surfaced without two of its divers. The current behavior in those incidents matches what the ancient's Control Water ability would produce if something very large and very deliberate decided a particular area was closed. ^[inferred]

The [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] has been watched from above by the [[high-eyrie|Sentinels of the High Eyrie]] for two centuries. Their records note, without editorial comment, that a Gargantuan creature has been observed moving through the western shelf waters at irregular intervals since the records began. It does not attack vessels. It is present more often when the [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] or [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] increase extraction operations, and less often when they don't. ^[inferred]

An ancient bronze dragon old enough to have watched the [[antheri-ruins|Antheri Ruins]] since before the current colonial era would have opinions about how they are being used. It is Lawful Good. It has not destroyed the Shelfworks. What it has done is establish, through current and cold water and the occasional very direct repositioning of a dive line, that there are parts of the ruins it considers outside the scope of the salvage gold rush. ^[inferred]

In the Shattered Sea

The Shelfworks have rules every experienced salvager knows. There is a less-discussed one that veteran crews hold without advertising: do not touch the sealed rooms on the lower northwest hall.

Nobody has posted a sign. Nobody has been told directly. The rule exists because three separate crews who broke it — across different seasons, without knowing about each other — all reported the same thing: a current that wasn’t there before, cold water arriving from no clear source, and their lines going taut in a direction that had nothing to do with the drift. Two of the three surfaced without the pieces they went down for. The third surfaced without two of its divers. The current behavior in those incidents matches what the ancient’s Control Water ability would produce if something very large and very deliberate decided a particular area was closed. ^[inferred]

The Drowned Maw has been watched from above by the Sentinels of the High Eyrie for two centuries. Their records note, without editorial comment, that a Gargantuan creature has been observed moving through the western shelf waters at irregular intervals since the records began. It does not attack vessels. It is present more often when the Tessarine Concordat or Dravosi Crown increase extraction operations, and less often when they don’t. ^[inferred]

An ancient bronze dragon old enough to have watched the Antheri Ruins since before the current colonial era would have opinions about how they are being used. It is Lawful Good. It has not destroyed the Shelfworks. What it has done is establish, through current and cold water and the occasional very direct repositioning of a dive line, that there are parts of the ruins it considers outside the scope of the salvage gold rush. ^[inferred]

## In The Shattered Sea

Ancient dragon turtles belong in the parts of the Sea where the chart stops being useful: the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]], the open water beyond it, and the deep indigo edge around the Keth-Naar Blue Hole. Sailors do not usually identify them cleanly. They report heat first: warm brine, softened pitch, fog lying low on water that had been still a moment before.

The most useful public account is indirect. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] survived the destruction of the *Vestra* near the Maw and later washed ashore at Keth-Naar. His account describes boiling water, a burned rail, and a deliberate strike from below. That evidence is not enough to prove an ancient dragon turtle rather than the older [[leviathan|Leviathan]] rumor — but it is enough that experienced sailors now treat the Maw-to-Sunken-Crown run as dragon-turtle water.

Ancient sea serpents belong to cold, deep movement: the open water beyond the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]], the long currents of the Outer Reach, and the shelf-edge approaches where the Tail sends longline crews out after night fish. They are easier to mistake for current than for island. Warning signs: cold water where the current should be warm, birds lifting from the surface all at once, fish lines going slack together, and a moving wake with no sail above it.

## Lore

A cleric who achieved undeath through the belief of a religious following. The Apotheosis positions itself as the sole conduit to a god, builds a devoted cult, then ritually sacrifices itself — the cult's collective belief in its immortality becomes the phylactery. As long as members convene to affirm the Apotheosis's deathlessness, it reforms.

The mechanism requires active maintenance: a cult that stops believing, or is destroyed, severs the anchor.

## In The Shattered Sea

Arclight phoenixes belong to the western edge where volcanic stone meets permanent weather: the black spires of the [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]] and the [[galewall|Galewall]] that begins just past them. They are born inside Ashwall volcanoes — the sign is lateral lightning inside the ash plume. An eruption with lateral lightning in the ash is a hatching, and the bird that emerges will be in the storm within hours.

Ashwall crews hold a belief the colonial weather-offices dismiss: that the Galewall is not the environment the arclight phoenix inhabits — it is what the arclight phoenix makes. The permanent weather belt may be the accumulated output of something alive.

Player index for beasts, swarms, and natural predators of the Shattered Sea.

# Beasts

Natural predators, swarms, and wildlife of the Scatter's islands and waters.

## Large Predators

- [[giant-crocodile|Giant Crocodile]] — Apex ambush predator of the tidal rivers and mangrove channels of the [[midchain|Midchain]]
- [[giant-constrictor-snake|Giant Constrictor Snake]] — Found in rainforest interiors of the [[midchain|Midchain]] and [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]]; large enough to pin and suffocate a horse
- [[giant-ape|Giant Ape]] — Territorial apex predator of dense rainforest interiors; sightings at [[sorn|Sorn]] suggest at least one family controls the highland canopy
- [[giant-boar|Giant Boar]] — Charges without warning from undergrowth of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]; big enough to stave in a ship's boat
- [[giant-shark|Giant Shark]] — Follows cold upwellings and blood trails; a serious threat near [[galewall|Galewall]]'s wreckage and along [[tail|the Tail]]'s longline grounds
- [[giant-squid|Giant Squid]] — Deep-water ambush predator that rises from the drop-off at night; a hazard for divers at the [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]]
- [[panther|Panther]] — Silent apex predator of the dense canopy of the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]]; a party may be stalked for hours before it commits
- [[tiger|Tiger]] — Forest and grassland predator; fast, powerful, and rarely seen before the first strike
- [[owlbear|Owlbear]] — Ambush predator of the dense interior forests of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]; the screech is usually the last thing heard before contact
- [[primeval-owlbear|Primeval Owlbear]] — A massive prehistoric variant, CR 7; significantly stronger and more durable than its common cousin
- [[giant-axe-beak|Giant Axe Beak]] — Aggressive flightless predator on the clifftop scrublands of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] and exposed ridgelines; fast enough to run down a horse

## Birds

- [[giant-eagle|Giant Eagle]] — Nests in the clifftop aeries of the High Eyrie; large enough to carry a grown sailor
- [[giant-vulture|Giant Vulture]] — Carrion bird found wherever the sea deposits its dead; circles the clifftops of the High Eyrie and the [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]]
- [[giant-owl|Giant Owl]] — Nocturnal forest hunter of the old-growth interiors of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]; near-silent on the wing
- [[pegasus|Pegasus]] — Rumoured to range the updrafts above the High Eyrie; the Sentinels claim sightings but treat the subject as a private matter
- [[unicorn|Unicorn]] — Unconfirmed; a single account from a [[midchain|Midchain]] interior expedition describes a white-maned creature that vanished before anyone else could see it

## Reptiles and Amphibians

- [[giant-lizard|Giant Lizard]] — Rocky-shore and ruin predator of the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]] and [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]]; territorial and fast
- [[giant-toad|Giant Toad]] — Ambush predator of boggy lowlands and freshwater margins of [[karath|Karath]]
- [[giant-frog|Giant Frog]] — Marshland and tidal-flat ambush predator of [[sorn|Sorn]], the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], and [[orak|Orak]]
- [[constrictor-snake|Constrictor Snake]] — Common tree-and-water snake of the [[midchain|Midchain]] lowlands; large enough to take a dog
- [[giant-venomous-snake|Giant Venomous Snake]] — Large ambush serpent of the mid-canopy and river margins in the [[verdant-scatter|Verdant Scatter]] and [[karath|Karath]]
- [[venomous-snake|Venomous Snake]] — Common bite hazard of the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] undergrowth; small enough to go unnoticed until stepped on
- [[giant-seahorse|Giant Seahorse]] — Large enough to serve as a mount; found in sheltered reef waters of the [[central-strait|Central Strait]]

## Arthropods and Arachnids

- [[giant-scorpion|Giant Scorpion]] — Found in dry rocky terrain of the [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]]; hides under flat stone and inside hollow logs
- [[giant-spider|Giant Spider]] — Web-builder of the deep jungle interior; found across the [[verdant-scatter|Verdant Scatter]], [[karath|Karath]], and [[orak|Orak]]
- [[giant-wolf-spider|Giant Wolf Spider]] — Hunting spider of the undergrowth of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] and [[ral-arn|Ral-Arn]]; doesn't web, runs fast
- [[giant-wasp|Giant Wasp]] — Nests in cliff overhangs and hollow shoreline trees around [[doldrums|the Doldrums]] and [[kalowe|Kalowe]]; disturbing one nest sends the whole colony
- [[giant-centipede|Giant Centipede]] — Found under loose stone and damp timber throughout [[sorn|Sorn]]; bites rather than charges
- [[giant-crab|Giant Crab]] — Intertidal heavyweight of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] beaches; large enough to shear rope
- [[giant-octopus|Giant Octopus]] — Reef-dwelling ambush predator in the rocky shallows of the [[central-strait|Central Strait]]

## Small Creatures and Pests

- [[giant-bat|Giant Bat]] — Cave-roosting hunter of the [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]] and [[tail|the Tail]]; emerges at dusk in columns thick enough to blot the stars
- [[giant-rat|Giant Rat]] — Dock-bred pest of [[kalowe|Kalowe]]'s warehouses; larger than a cat and aggressive when cornered
- [[giant-weasel|Giant Weasel]] — Burrow hunter of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] forest floor; occasionally found in cargo holds after a Crown Islands layover
- [[boar|Boar]] — Common feral hog of the scrubland and coastal heath of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]

## Swarms

# Bestiary

Every sailor working the Scatter has a story. The sea that fills the space between islands is not empty — something is always in the water, in the canopy, or waiting in the dark of a sealed ruin. Some of what follows is confirmed. Some of it is rumour. The distinction matters less than you might hope.

## On the Water

- [[sea-life|Sea Life]] — Ocean predators, sharks, krakens, and the things sighted from the rail at night
- [[dragons|Dragons]] — Dragon turtles, sea serpents, and true dragons; encountering one is a survival problem, not a fight

## On Land

- [[beasts|Beasts]] — Natural predators, wildlife, and swarms across the Scatter's islands
- [[fey|Fey]] — Goblin warbands found in the interior forests and hill country
- [[monstrosities|Monstrosities]] — Harpies, rocs, and creatures that don't fit a cleaner category

## In the Deep Places

- [[fiends|Fiends]] — Sahuagin who raid from the shelf walls and outer reef drop-offs
- [[plants|Plants]] — Myconid colonies and fungal hazards of the underdark beneath the Scatter
- [[oozes|Oozes]] — Dissolving predators of the deep underdark; no confirmed surface sightings

## The Undead

- [[undead|Undead]] — Pointy Hat lich variants: Hierarch (bloodline phylactery), Intoner (memory phylactery), Blight (place phylactery)

## Made Things and Outliers

- [[humanoids|Humanoids]] — Pirates, admirals, and the people most likely to try to take your ship
- [[constructs|Constructs]] — Animated objects and magical sentinels left behind in sealed halls and old collections
- [[celestials|Celestials]] — Sacred creatures; encountering one is rarely accidental
- [[elementals|Elementals]] — Elemental-bound creatures, including what the Ashwall pilots believe keeps the [[galewall|Galewall]] burning

Druid lich whose phylactery is a place — the Death Bloom at the heart of the land it died protecting. Stat block is tiered as the Death Bloom is damaged. Active at Aruhe in the Midchain.

# Blight

![[Blight.webp|The Blight grown from the Death Bloom at the heart of Aruhe]]

> Full stat block in the Pointy Hat source. The Blight's stat block is tiered — it degrades in stages as the Death Bloom phylactery is damaged.

## What a Blight Is

A Blight begins as an Archdruid who performed a ritual to fuse their soul and body to a piece of land they were trying to protect — killing themselves in the process. The result is a druid lich whose phylactery is not an object or a living being but **a place**: the Death Bloom, a location at the heart of the protected land.

Unlike other liches, a Blight cannot be destroyed by finding and smashing a phylactery object. The Death Bloom is a location — a dungeon to be cleared, not an item to be stolen.

## Combat Notes

- **Stage 1 (Death Bloom intact):** Full power — high CR, full action economy.
- **Stage 2 (Death Bloom damaged):** Degraded — reduced HP, weakened abilities.
- **Stage 3 (Death Bloom nearly destroyed):** Desperate — erratic, may use environmental hazards.
- **Death Bloom destroyed:** Blight cannot reform; final death.

## In The Shattered Sea

**Aruhe** hosts an active Blight. The abandoned island interior is its dungeon. The Death Bloom is the encounter at the island's interior center. The acid drainage dissolving the old agricultural terraces is the Blight's byproduct working on the soil.

The [[grung-clans|Grung Clans]] patrol the surrounding reefs but refuse to land. Their name for Aruhe translates roughly as "the island that is already eaten." They know what is there.

The Blight is an **optional encounter**. It enters play if the party shelters at Aruhe, follows a drifting wreck there, needs to avoid patrols, or investigates a chart note. It sits in the same Midchain stretch as [[the-drowned-maw|The Drowned Maw]] — useful thematic context if the party is already moving that direction.

*Source: Pointy Hat*
