## Geography

The island is lower than [[harwick|Harwick]] and greener than [[calven|Calven]] — rolling agricultural land, hedgerow-bordered fields, and a central depression that floods with the tides and never fully drains. That depression is the mere: perhaps a mile across at its widest, shallower in summer and deeper in spring, ringed by reed beds and low pasture and old alder stands.

The coast is mostly gentle: short cliffs on the northern face, shelving beaches and tidal flat on the south. The harbour sits on the southwestern side, sheltered by a natural headland. The approaches are straightforward enough that a visiting captain does not strictly need a local pilot, though local pilots will tell you otherwise.

## The Mere

The inland lake is the island's defining feature and its oldest source of protein — freshwater eels, crayfish, and reed-filtered fish, harvested on a seasonal rotation established well before the Crown arrived. The inlet channel is navigable by flat-bottomed boats at high tide, giving the mere a working function as sheltered anchorage for small craft in bad weather.

The deeper sections stay murky year-round. Locals know which channels are safe and which are not, and they do not always explain the difference to visitors.

## The Town

The main settlement runs along the eastern shore of the mere and back up the slope toward the harbour road. Stone houses, low and practical. A market square that doubles as a fish-drying ground in season. A harbourmaster's office that is genuinely just an office — no rating station, no Crown registry desk.

Ships stop here for water, provisions, and occasionally shelter, pay a modest berthing fee, and move on.

## People & Power

The island pays its tithe and is otherwise governed by local habit, fishing families, and practical harbour officials. Crown administration appears as a revenue officer twice a year.

## Trade & Resources

Aldenmere

Overview

Aldenmere is the fourth island of the Crown Islands, one step east of Harwick and one step west of Stenmark. There is no fortress here — no admiralty office, no naval yard, no inspection pier. The Dravosi Crown holds the island on paper and sends a revenue officer twice a year with a ledger and expectations about the fishing tithe. The island pays and the officer leaves.

The name comes from the mere — a broad, still tidal lake in the island’s interior, connected to the sea by a narrow inlet channel. The farms run down to its eastern shore. The fishing fleets work both the mere and the offshore grounds. The town grew where the ground was solid enough for stone, and has not grown much since.

Geography

The island is lower than Harwick and greener than Calven — rolling agricultural land, hedgerow-bordered fields, and a central depression that floods with the tides and never fully drains. That depression is the mere: perhaps a mile across at its widest, shallower in summer and deeper in spring, ringed by reed beds and low pasture and old alder stands.

The coast is mostly gentle: short cliffs on the northern face, shelving beaches and tidal flat on the south. The harbour sits on the southwestern side, sheltered by a natural headland. The approaches are straightforward enough that a visiting captain does not strictly need a local pilot, though local pilots will tell you otherwise.

The Mere

The inland lake is the island’s defining feature and its oldest source of protein — freshwater eels, crayfish, and reed-filtered fish, harvested on a seasonal rotation established well before the Crown arrived. The inlet channel is navigable by flat-bottomed boats at high tide, giving the mere a working function as sheltered anchorage for small craft in bad weather.

The deeper sections stay murky year-round. Locals know which channels are safe and which are not, and they do not always explain the difference to visitors.

The Town

The main settlement runs along the eastern shore of the mere and back up the slope toward the harbour road. Stone houses, low and practical. A market square that doubles as a fish-drying ground in season. A harbourmaster’s office that is genuinely just an office — no rating station, no Crown registry desk.

Ships stop here for water, provisions, and occasionally shelter, pay a modest berthing fee, and move on.

# Calder's Tooth

![[1778025287065~2 2.png]]

Calder's Tooth rises at the western mouth of the [[central-strait|Central Strait]] as a massive, jagged slab of limestone and basalt — its windward face sheer and storm-battered, taking everything the [[galewall|Galewall]] sends without complaint. The eastern side softens into mudflats, mangrove estuaries, and fishing hamlets that face the calmer Strait water. Between the two coasts runs a wet, fog-choked interior ridge riddled with sinkholes, where the roads are more like guidelines. The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] claims the island absolutely. What that claim covers in practice is the fortifications, the harbour mouth, and the ledgers.

[[the-passage|The Passage]] runs cargo through limestone caves beneath the Overland Track, which the Crown has been trying to find for years.

## Geography

**The Western Wall** is a miles-long basalt and limestone cliff face slick with sea spray and battered by Galewall winds. Functionally unscalable from the water without magic.

**The Marrow** is the island's north-south interior ridge — porous limestone riddled with sinkholes, collapsed cenotes, and unstable cave systems. Iron-oak and crown-pine dominate the canopy; the undergrowth is thick with razor-vine and stinging nettles.

**The Eastern Mudflats** slope toward the [[central-strait|Central Strait]] in broad tidal flats and shallow mangrove-like estuaries. Tidal shifts can strand travellers in waist-deep muck, which makes the eastern approach difficult for armored patrols.

---

## Port Tidefall

The western cliffside fortress-port is where the Crown wants incoming Strait traffic to stop first.

- [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] — Dravosi fortress-port carved into the cliff face in three tiers; Dockfront, Shelf, and Crown tiers.
- [[fort-crestwall|Fort Crestwall]] — fortified crown of Tidefall with cannon battery and command post.
- [[inspection-pier|Inspection Pier]] — first contact point for official Tidefall arrivals.
- [[harbourmasters-office|Harbourmaster's Office]] — berths, ratings, charts, writs, and port paperwork.
- [[tidefall-chandlery|Tidefall Chandlery]] — main supply shop for ship goods and nautical gear.
- [[tessarine-trade-house|Tessarine Trade House]] — Concordat office handling licensing, contracts, courier dispatch, and salvage work.
- [[shelf-instrument-dealer|Shelf Instrument Dealer]] — navigational tools, charts, almanacs, sextants, chronometers.
- [[governors-seat|Governor's Seat]] — Tidefall administrative seat and ceremonial Crown authority.
- [[hook-and-ledger|Hook & Ledger]] — Shelf tavern for paperwork-adjacent business and quiet deals.
- [[fare-ia|Fare I'a]] — Grung-style fish jerky counter on the Dockfront.

## South & East Coast

The calmer side of Calder's Tooth is muddier, less formal, and harder for the Crown to police consistently.

- [[south-harbour|South Harbour]] — eastern working harbour, repair sprawl, fishing fleet, and lower-profile cargo point.
- [[south-harbour-impound|South Harbour Impound]] — Crown seizure yard on the east pier.
- [[oshas-slip|Osha's Slip]] — stilt-platform fishing village over the southeastern mudflats.

## Roads & Crossings

- [[overland-track|Overland Track]] — muddy southern switchback road between South Harbour and Port Tidefall.
- [[high-line|High-Line]] — northeastern cliff-face fishing hamlet built around counterweighted winches.

## Outer Points

- [[cape-solitude|Cape Solitude]] — wind-battered northern point with a ruined pre-colonial tower and an abandoned Crown lighthouse project.

## Fauna

Giant bats roost in sinkhole chambers and old sea caves in the limestone — colonies large enough to disturb a trail party on a night crossing and to draw predators that eat bats. Giant boar sign is consistent along wetter ridge sections — torn root beds, wallows, track damage. Giant wolf spiders occupy old cisterns and any structure unused long enough for web architecture to develop; villages on the mudflat side check cisterns before sending children for water. Giant axe beaks on the open switchbacks pace alongside wagons on broad track sections before deciding whether to commit.

## Hazards

Fog, sinkholes, mudflats, Crown inspection, cliff exposure, and interior predators. The island is administered, not tame.

## Current Hooks

- A ship trying to avoid Tidefall inspection may risk the northern reefs or eastern mudflats.
- Interior travel between South Harbour and Port Tidefall can be interrupted by fog, sinkholes, or animal sign.

# Cape Solitude

## Overview

Cape Solitude is the northernmost point of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]], where the island runs out of island and faces open ocean directly. Heavy surf, constant wind off the [[galewall|Galewall]], and no shelter. Local fisherfolk won't anchor within two miles of the cape. They don't explain why if you ask them directly, but the short version is the Dead Light.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Wind-scoured cape and ruined tower landmark |
| Location | [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]], northern point |
| Controlled By | Avoided by locals; failed [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] lighthouse project |
| Access | Dangerous open-ocean approach; locals avoid anchoring within two miles |
| Known For | The Dead Light, vanished lighthouse crews, cliff voices, and aggressive shore fauna |

## Description

Cape Solitude faces open ocean with no shelter: hard surf, constant Galewall wind, boulder fields at the cape base, updrafts along the cliff, and a ruined pre-colonial tower standing on the point.

## Access & Approach

The approach is exposed to open ocean and heavy surf. Local fisherfolk avoid anchoring within two miles. The cape base is a boulder field with aggressive giant crabs, and the clifftop wind makes voices carry in ways locals do not trust.

## People & Power

The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] attempted a lighthouse project here and abandoned it after three successive work crews disappeared without signs of struggle. No bodies, no tools left behind, nothing disturbed. The project was quietly struck from the ledgers.

## Notable Features

**The Dead Light** — A ruined stone tower on the point, pre-colonial construction older than the Crown's claim to the island.

**Abandoned Lighthouse Project** — Three Crown work crews vanished here without signs of struggle.

## Fauna

The surf at the cape base runs hard against a boulder field, which suits giant crabs — the colony here is larger than the ones on Calder's Tooth's eastern mudflats, and more aggressive. Giant vultures use the cape's updrafts daily, circling the point in numbers that suggest they expect something to die here regularly.

The locals' reluctance to anchor near the cape predates the lighthouse project. The fisherfolk say voices carry from the clifftop on windy nights — not wind noise, but voices with phrasing in them. Harpies nest in cliff-face crevices across the northern headland. Whether the three lighthouse crews followed a sound toward the cliff edge is a question nobody has gone back to confirm.

## Hazards

Open-ocean exposure, heavy surf, giant crabs, harpy cliff voices, giant vultures, and the unresolved disappearance of three lighthouse crews.

## Current Hooks

- The tower still stands. Nothing has moved into it that anyone has reported, and no one has gone back to look carefully.
- Whether the vanished lighthouse crews followed a sound toward the cliff edge remains unconfirmed.

# Dath-Mar

> *A hard place kept for hard hours.*

The smallest of the five [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]] islands. Its name preserves the local tabaxi sense of strengthened stone — a place of endurance rather than comfort. A few individuals live there year-round by choice. Most use it only when they need to.

[[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] hunters retreat here when a storm splits boats from home, when someone needs distance from the central settlement, or when a decision is too heavy to bring to the elders without sitting with it first. The island's value is not what it offers — it can hold a person above the water when the rest of the Blue Hole turns against them.

A hard, exposed rock with leeward approaches, a sheltered cut, black stone, higher cracks, and tide-dependent access. Not comfortable. Not meant to be. The current reversals around the Blue Hole have made the approach less predictable — skiffs strand on the wrong side of the rock more often than they used to.

## The Cairns

Cairns mark the leeward approaches and the sheltered cut. They are maintained by whoever last used them. Leaving one worse than you found it is a serious breach — the next arrival may not have the luxury of doing without it.

## People & Power

Dath-Mar is held by [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] custom rather than occupation. The rule is maintenance: leave worse than you found, and the next arrival pays for it.

## Trade & Resources

No trade. Its resource is survival space: a place to wait out weather, separation, or a decision that cannot yet be brought home.

## Fauna

Giant lizards sun against the black stone after storms. Giant bats use the higher cracks when weather grounds them. Giant crabs work the tidal zone at the island's base — the cairn approaches pass through crab territory at low water. [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] hunters harvest selectively, managing the count without eliminating the population.

## Hazards

Exposure, current reversals, tide windows, lizards, bats, crabs, and failing predictability around the Blue Hole.

# Harwick

## Overview

Harwick is the second-largest island in the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] and the military centre of Dravosi power in the Shattered Sea. Where [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]] controls the western entrance to the [[central-strait|Central Strait]] and Calveno handles commercial business, Harwick builds ships and stages fleets. The name is old Dravosi: *hær-wīc*, army place. It has not changed its purpose since.

Two days east of Calder's Tooth, Harwick sits near the middle of the northern arc — accessible from both ends of the Crown Island chain and close enough to open ocean to move the fleet quickly when it has to. The deep-water anchorage on the island's south face is the largest natural harbour in the Scatter that a Ship of the Line can enter, and the Crown has spent considerable money making sure that advantage is fortified rather than merely scenic.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Dravosi naval island and fleet anchorage |

| Primary Economy | Shipbuilding, naval administration, provisions, timber, and sailor services |
| Known For | Harwick Naval Yard, the Bight, Admiralty offices, and Crown warship construction |

## Geography

The island is broader and flatter than the limestone ridges of Calder's Tooth. The interior plateau drops slowly to marsh and tidal channels on the eastern side, and rises toward forested hills in the northwest. The southwestern harbour face is sheltered from the prevailing northeast winds by a curved headland the charts call the Bight. The bay inside it runs deep close to shore, which is why the Naval Yard is there.

The northern coast takes open ocean swell directly. It is uninhabited outside of a signal station and a few fishing hamlets. The eastern marshes drain through a network of channels into a shallow bay used by small craft and anyone who wants to avoid the Yard's official entry points.

## Settlements & Sites

| Place | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Harwick Naval Yard | naval yard | Dry docks, covered slipways, storehouses, and Crown military shipbuilding. |
| The Admiralty | office | Hilltop naval administration and sealed order archive. |
| Harwick Town | town | Civilian settlement serving the Yard, fleet, and market wharf. |

## The Naval Yard

The Harwick Naval Yard occupies the entire western shore of the Bight — dry docks cut into the rock, covered slipways long enough to lay a three-deck hull, storehouses that smell of fresh timber, pitch, and cordage. The Yard produces every class the Crown Admiralty operates. The [[hcs-constancy|HCS *Constancy*]] and the [[hcs-ordinance|HCS *Ordinance*]] were both laid down here, on slipways that have turned out warships for six generations of Dravosi governors.

The Yard is Crown military property. A civilian can observe the outer walls and smell the tar; anything past the gate requires Admiralty permission, which is not freely given.

## The Admiralty

Harwick's Admiralty office sits on the hill above the Naval Yard, overlooking the anchorage. Patrol rotations, commission papers, privateer letters, quarterly chart updates — it all routes through here.

The Admiralty maintains a sealed key protocol for every warship in the fleet. Captains carry orders they are not permitted to open until specified conditions are met. The building is a fortress in the administrative sense — not much to look at from outside, extremely difficult to navigate inside without authorization.

## The Town

The civilian settlement clusters along the eastern edge of the Bight between the Yard wall and the market wharf. It exists because the Naval Yard needs labour, the fleet needs provisions, and sailors on liberty need somewhere to spend their pay. Chandlers, taverns, a ropemakers' district, ships' suppliers, and the usual run of lodging houses.

The naval rating pool that crews Crown ships on rotation lives mostly here, in barracks along the north edge of town. Harwick sailors are not the Scatter's most adventurous. They are, reliably, the Scatter's most sober when they need to be.

## Hazards

Military restriction, shark-filled harbour water, managed but dangerous forests, and Yard security all shape visitor movement.

Overview

Harwick is the second-largest island in the Crown Islands and the military centre of Dravosi power in the Shattered Sea. Where Calder’s Tooth controls the western entrance to the Central Strait and Calveno handles commercial business, Harwick builds ships and stages fleets. The name is old Dravosi: hær-wīc, army place. It has not changed its purpose since.

Two days east of Calder’s Tooth, Harwick sits near the middle of the northern arc — accessible from both ends of the Crown Island chain and close enough to open ocean to move the fleet quickly when it has to. The deep-water anchorage on the island’s south face is the largest natural harbour in the Scatter that a Ship of the Line can enter, and the Crown has spent considerable money making sure that advantage is fortified rather than merely scenic.

Geography

The island is broader and flatter than the limestone ridges of Calder’s Tooth. The interior plateau drops slowly to marsh and tidal channels on the eastern side, and rises toward forested hills in the northwest. The southwestern harbour face is sheltered from the prevailing northeast winds by a curved headland the charts call the Bight. The bay inside it runs deep close to shore, which is why the Naval Yard is there.

The northern coast takes open ocean swell directly. It is uninhabited outside of a signal station and a few fishing hamlets. The eastern marshes drain through a network of channels into a shallow bay used by small craft and anyone who wants to avoid the Yard’s official entry points.

The Naval Yard

The Harwick Naval Yard occupies the entire western shore of the Bight — dry docks cut into the rock, covered slipways long enough to lay a three-deck hull, storehouses that smell of fresh timber, pitch, and cordage. The Yard produces every class the Crown Admiralty operates. The [[hcs-constancy|HCS Constancy]] and the [[hcs-ordinance|HCS Ordinance]] were both laid down here, on slipways that have turned out warships for six generations of Dravosi governors.

The Yard is Crown military property. A civilian can observe the outer walls and smell the tar; anything past the gate requires Admiralty permission, which is not freely given.

The Admiralty

Harwick’s Admiralty office sits on the hill above the Naval Yard, overlooking the anchorage. Patrol rotations, commission papers, privateer letters, quarterly chart updates — it all routes through here.

The Admiralty maintains a sealed key protocol for every warship in the fleet. Captains carry orders they are not permitted to open until specified conditions are met. The building is a fortress in the administrative sense — not much to look at from outside, extremely difficult to navigate inside without authorization.

The Town

The civilian settlement clusters along the eastern edge of the Bight between the Yard wall and the market wharf. It exists because the Naval Yard needs labour, the fleet needs provisions, and sailors on liberty need somewhere to spend their pay. Chandlers, taverns, a ropemakers’ district, ships’ suppliers, and the usual run of lodging houses.

The naval rating pool that crews Crown ships on rotation lives mostly here, in barracks along the north edge of town. Harwick sailors are not the Scatter’s most adventurous. They are, reliably, the Scatter’s most sober when they need to be.

Hazards

Military restriction, shark-filled harbour water, managed but dangerous forests, and Yard security all shape visitor movement.

# Karath

## Overview

Karath looks like the other [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] from the water — low reef approaches, rainforest running close to the shore, no harbour, no smoke, no visible reason to stop. The distinction is what happens when you get close anyway. Outsiders who nose into the reef gaps are met with dart fire, no warning, no gap between the quiet beach and the response. Pilots who know these waters treat Karath specifically as the island you give extra room, not because the others are inviting but because Karath is the one with a reputation for not waiting to see what you were planning.

The [[midchain|Midchain]] coastal settlements have noticed the raids out of this direction are getting worse. The [[chain-council|Chain Council]] has received the complaints.

## Geography

Low reef approaches, rainforest close to shore, wet cuts between ridges, and no harbour, smoke, or visible invitation to land.

## Fauna

The interior makes the beach look welcoming. Giant spiders occupy the older canopy growth. Giant venomous snakes work the root tangles along the wet ridge cuts — they don't announce themselves. Giant toads occupy standing-water pools in the wet cuts between ridges. Outsiders who imagine the beach is the dangerous part of Karath have not thought through the rest of the island.

## Hazards

Dart fire, reef traps, giant spiders, giant venomous snakes, giant toads, wet ridge cuts, and unknown interior patrols.

## Current Hooks

- Raids from the direction of the Teeth are worsening; Karath is the island sailors most fear.
- The Chain Council has received complaints; whether that changes anything is unresolved.

# Keth-Naar

## Overview

Keth-Naar is not one island but twelve promontories of ancient black basalt, clustered close enough that you cross between them at low tide on stepping-stone paths worn smooth by generations of feet. It sits at the edge of the Blue Hole — the vast, dark-indigo circle of deep water at the heart of the Sunken Crown — and from the highest point on the island the boundary between the turquoise shallows and that indigo drop is clean as a cut.

The tribe speaks with a distinct accent — clipped consonants and a precise, slightly stiff cadence. Sailors who have traded around the Sunken Crown recognize it immediately as Keth-Naar speech.

Visitors who arrive carefully may be watched before they are spoken to. This is not unfriendliness. It is the habit of a community that has been here long enough to know what a ship that does not read the water correctly looks like, and what usually follows it.

The catches have been thin lately, and the weather around the Blue Hole has been less predictable than the tribe is used to. The birds are going inland before dark.

## Districts & Landmarks

**Central Stone** — A massive black rock formation at the island's heart, weathered into natural caves and overhangs. Carved symbols mark the entrances.

**Lookout Stone** — A forty-foot eastern platform with sightlines across the Blue Hole and the surrounding islands.

**Tidal Channels** — Lower stone channels guide fish inward on high tide, with skinning racks, drying frames, and nets maintained nearby.

## The Wreck Survivor

Keth-Naar is where [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] came ashore after the *Vestra* was destroyed near the Maw. The useful details were not the name of the monster but the signs before it: still water, heat through the hull, steam where there should have been spray, and a strike from below. Local watchers treat that account as a warning about the deep line between Keth-Naar and [[the-drowned-maw|the Drowned Maw]]. [[stripes-bitemore|Stripes Bitemore]] was also on the island at the time — his tribe had been watching the seas turn wrong for days before the strike. Perrin stowed away aboard the [[saltwright|Saltwright]] in the harbour.

When the Blue Hole goes quiet and the birds leave early, nobody sensible takes a boat over the indigo edge.

## Hazards

Giant lizards warm on black stone after rain, giant bats roost in the higher caves, and giant wolf spiders nest where old paths fall out of use. Local hunters don't make the island safe by denying those things — they make it safe by remembering where they were last seen.

- The catches have been thin; weather around the Blue Hole is less predictable than usual.
- The birds are going inland before dark.

# Meth-Var

The easternmost of the five Sunken Crown islands, facing open Maw waters on an exposed, windswept approach with little shelter for larger vessels. Meth-Var is not inhabited permanently. The people of [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] rotate watchers through it because the island's value is attention — it faces the direction where weather and deep movement can reach the Blue Hole before anyone in the central settlement sees the sign.

Watchers leave marks in paired sets: one for what was seen, one for who must be told. A sighting without a carried warning is considered unfinished work.

Lately, the warning patterns have been arriving wrong.

## At a Glance

| Known For | Paired watcher marks, Maw-facing exposure, and the scalded ropes incident |

## The Scalded Ropes

A Keth-Naar skiff did not return cleanly from the eastern watch run. The next rotation found the landing ropes bleached pale and scalded stiff, the signal stones reset in the emergency pattern, and one watcher alive in the lee crack with burned hands and no boat.

Their account is treated as a warning, not a tale. The water warmed before the attack. Steam moved low over the reef. A dark shell-ridge — too small for the old island-sized stories but large enough to break a skiff — rose from the Blue Hole edge. Whether the wyrmling lairs in the Crown or passed through from the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] is not established; Meth-Var only records that it was close enough to reach the watch route.

## Hazards

Maw weather, exposed landing, giant vultures, giant bats, possible harpy calls, heat events, and dragon turtle wyrmling signs.

## Current Hooks

- Warning patterns have been arriving wrong lately.
- A survivor from the scalded ropes incident may be the clearest witness to the current Blue Hole threat.

# Ral-Arn

> *The island where memory is kept against salt and forgetting.*

The record island of the Sunken Crown — larger than [[dath-mar|Dath-Mar]] or [[meth-var|Meth-Var]], visited when a question must be answered by memory rather than appetite. The oldest family lines maintain carved marks here: tide accounts, storm signs, records of prior seasons. Ral-Arn does not replace oral history. It anchors it. A mark here is only useful if someone living can read the story around it.

Giant lizards bask across the stone paths — the flat, exposed rock holds heat well, and visitors to the record panels routinely wait for an animal to clear a section before working it. Giant wolf spiders have taken the abandoned shelters — any shelter that has gone unvisited for more than a season should be checked before use, and those unvisited for years are checked with a pole. # Stenmark

## Overview

Stenmark is the easternmost island in the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] — the last Dravosi flag before the Drowned Maw. The name is old: *sten-mark*, stone border. Whoever named it was not being poetic. From the eastern cliffs on a clear day, the water changes colour where the Maw begins — the blue-green of the Scatter going flat and dark, a shade that has no bottom in it. The threshold is visible from shore. People who live on Stenmark have looked at that line their entire lives.

The island is stone and cold water and wind from the east. The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] maintains a signal station on the eastern cliff edge, staffed by a small watch rotation. The people here are fishing people and watch people and the occasional salvager using Stenmark as a staging point for work on the [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]].

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Eastern Crown watch island on the Maw edge |
| Region | [[crown-islands|The Crown Islands]] |
| Controlled By | Stenmark settlement + [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] signal station |
| Access | Dangerous eastern shelf; western harbour with costly local pilots |
| Known For | Eastern cliffs, signal station, cold upwelling, and visible Maw waterline |

## Geography

The island runs north to south, long and narrow. The western face is gentler — settlement, harbour, what farmland the shallow soil supports. The eastern face is sheer cliff from end to end, dropping into deep cold water. The Greyteeth reefs are at their worst in the approaches to Stenmark. Local pilots charge more here than anywhere else in the Crown Islands.

## Settlements & Sites

| Place | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The Signal Station | watch station | Crown post logging Maw conditions, fog lines, and unusual sightings. |
| Stenmark Settlement | harbour town | Fishing, watchers, and salvagers; western slope. |
| Eastern Cliffs | cliff line | Sheer deep-water face looking toward the Drowned Maw. |

## The Signal Station

Built low against the wind on the eastern cliff edge. The watch rotation is a three-month posting. The station keeps a daily log: Maw surface colouration, fog line position, compass variance, weather anomalies, unusual sightings. Logs go to Harwick Admiralty monthly. Nobody cross-references them systematically with the Sentinels' records — those who have say it would be instructive.

## The Settlement

Stone houses, low profiles, shutters that actually work. The cold upwelling produces deep-water fish species not caught further west — a modest preserved-fish trade with a reputation for flavour. Residents do not explain too carefully what else shares the water with them.

## Fauna

[[high-eyrie|Harpies]] nest in the eastern cliffs — territorial, consistent, present since before the signal station. Giant vultures ride the eastern thermals after storms. Giant sharks work the eastern shelf. The deeper water below the eastern cliff produces wakes, surface disturbances, and shapes the light catches wrong. Stenmark fishermen use a word for these and change the subject.

## Current Hooks

- The signal logs may reveal patterns nobody at Harwick has cross-referenced.
- The water below the eastern cliff produces wakes and shapes locals do not like naming.

# Umberlee's Shrine — Sunken Crown

## Overview

[[umberlee|Umberlee's]] shrine on [[vel-orn|Vel-Orn]] is cut into black stone in the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]], where five small islands ring the Blue Hole. This is not a bright harbour shrine collecting routine tribute from merchants. It is older, quieter, and pointed more toward the drowned than the living.

The shrine entrance is a mouth in the cliff face, worn smooth by salt spray and years of tide. Kelp wraps the pillars. Candles burn inside where wind should have killed them. The shrine smells of brine, rendered tallow, wet stone, and something older underneath. Sound behaves strangely in the entrance. Footsteps soften.

## Function

The shrine marks debts, keeps drowned names, and preserves the older [[umberlee|Umberlee]] worship of the Blue Hole. Inside, a ledger chamber holds names, tokens, coins, fish bones, carved shells, and bits of ship or sailor preserved as witness. Everything here has weight. Nothing feels decorative.

## Access

Not on colonial charts. Requires prior knowledge, a guide, or difficult navigation. Vel-Orn's approach is sheer, reef-bound, and unfriendly to casual landings.

# The Midchain

## Overview

The Midchain is the southern arc of the Shattered Sea's Verdant Scatter: dozens of low limestone and coral islands packed close, most a half-day's sail from the next. The treeline often appears before the land does. Dense rainforest runs to the water's edge on many coasts; elsewhere, pale limestone cliffs drop straight to reef. The water shifts from turquoise over the shallows to blue-black where the shelf falls away, and the line between them is abrupt.

Fresh water and shelter are rarely far away. Certainty is harder to find.

Charts for the Midchain contradict each other because the Midchain keeps changing the question. Local knowledge is worth more than paper in most of the inner channels. The same back channels that hide a ship also hide teeth. Deep blue holes are avoided unless a pilot knows them by name, because [[sawek|Sawek]] lairs look like useful shelter until something moves below the keel.

Prevailing winds turn more westerly near the Doldrums, creating back channels useful for westbound ships trying to avoid Strait inspection. Dravosi patrol cutters run intercept routes through the more predictable lanes, which is one reason experienced captains prefer the less predictable ones.

The Midchain is also where small piracy becomes geography. A cutter like [[knifes-wake|the Knife's Wake]] can disappear through channels a frigate captain refuses to enter.

Shifting reefs, uncertain channels, Sawek blue holes, [[giant-crocodile|giant crocodiles]] in mangrove water, constrictor snakes along root mats, Grung boundary violations, and piracy that turns local route knowledge into a weapon.

The second of the two eastern [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], sitting close enough to [[dreth|Dreth]] that the channel between them is shadowed and flat. # Osha's Slip

## Overview

A fishing village built on stilt-platforms over the southeastern mudflats of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]]. The villagers trap mud-crabs, spear river-eels, and maintain a rope-and-plank bridge network that shifts with wind and tide. There are no solid roads. Overland approach from Tidefall means crossing the mudflats, which is slow and unpleasant at any tide and impossible in armour at the wrong one.

The village is independent in the way small places far from the fort tend to be. The Crown's authority here is largely theoretical. [[the-passage|The Passage]] uses Osha's Slip as a favored night-landing site for small high-value cargo.

# Ashwall Islands

![[Ashwall-Islands.webp|Dark volcanic islands rising from rough gray water beneath a stormy sky]]

## Overview

The water turns dark before the islands appear — cold, deep blue fading toward black, the warm green smell of the Scatter long gone. Then the spires rise: black volcanic stone, steep-sided, cloud dragging across the upper heights and surf bursting white against the bases. The air carries salt and something mineral beneath it, a thin sulphur bite from the vents in the high stone.

Sailors running the western passage know the Ashwalls as a threshold. Outbound, they are the last solid ground before the [[galewall|Galewall]]. Inbound, they are the first proof of survival. Ashwall crews treat them accordingly — not as a destination, but as a reckoning point. The navigation tradition out here runs on stars and instruments and the kind of careful attention that keeps you alive when there is nothing ahead but open water.

The spires are not empty just because they are hard to land on. Giant bats roost in warm vent caves, giant vultures work the cliffs after wrecks, and high-wind crews still tell harpy stories about voices in the storm gaps. Most pilots file those stories under weather until someone follows the wrong sound inland.

The vent fissures in the high stone also hold giant scorpions. The volcanic heat keeps the crevices warm through cold sea air, and the same crack systems that look like good handholds on the cliff face can run back several feet into occupied dark. A carpenter from a repair crew — name passed around Ashwall crews as Duvane — was attacked in a fissure while assessing a fouled spar: claw across the forearm, sting through the boot, two days down from the poison. He described not seeing it at all before both claws were engaged. Ashwall repair work now typically sends two hands up the stone face, with one watching the rock instead of the job.

## Routes & Access

Sailors running the western passage know the Ashwalls as a threshold. Outbound, they are the last solid ground before the [[galewall|Galewall]]. Inbound, they are the first proof of survival. Ashwall crews treat them accordingly — not as a destination, but as a reckoning point.

## People & Power

The Ashwalls are governed in practice by the crews who can survive and work them: pilots, repair hands, storm readers, and families whose log books preserve practical signs before theory.

## Trade & Resources

The Ashwalls are not a market destination. Their value is navigational and practical: repair lee, storm-edge proof, pilot knowledge, emergency work, and the last chance to make a damaged hull ready before or after the [[galewall|Galewall]].

## The Hatching Sign

Ashwall crews distinguish between two kinds of eruption lightning. The first is vertical: storm discharge running from cloud to stone, ordinary enough that no one marks it. The second moves sideways through the ash column — branching, lateral, holding for a breath before it goes dark. That is the sign. Crews who see it know what it means and know roughly how long they have before something emerges from the vent.

[[arclight-phoenix|Arclight phoenixes]] are born inside the Ashwall volcanoes. The volcanic discharge is what hatches them — the egg left behind when a phoenix dies requires lightning to open, and the vent systems provide it continuously and at close range. The bird that climbs out of the stone is already oriented toward the storm edge. It flies west into the [[galewall|Galewall]] and does not come back east until it has died again somewhere inside the weather.

How long this has been happening is not recorded. The oldest Ashwall pilot families mark the sign in their log books as a navigational note — *lateral vent-fire, westward departure, expected increase in Galewall activity* — without commentary.

## The Lightning-Burned Survivor

The Ashwalls are where Galewall stories become evidence. A ship that survives the storm belt reaches these spires damaged, wet, and short on certainty; pilots and repair crews can still read the hull better than the crew can read its own fear.

One survivor from a failed crossing described a white bird made of stormlight moving through the rigging before the mainmast came down. The account is treated cautiously, but the Ashwall repairs gave it weight: burns ran along contact points rather than down from a single strike, and several iron fittings were magnetized hard enough to pull nails from a workbench. Since then, some Ashwall pilots mark bright, lateral stormlight as a possible [[arclight-phoenix|arclight phoenix]] sign rather than ordinary weather.

## Fauna

Giant bats roost in the vent caves throughout the spire chain — the volcanic heat keeps the interior fissures warm enough year-round, and the bat colonies are large enough that a repair crew working below a roost at dusk learns not to do that again. The same fissure systems hold giant scorpions in the upper rock faces. The volcanic warmth maintains occupied dark in crevices that look like handholds from a distance. Ashwall repair crews have developed the practice of sending a second hand to watch the stone while the first works it.

Giant vultures work the clifftops and high updrafts in numbers that spike after a wreck. Pilots treat a vulture count above the normal baseline as rough early intelligence about whether anything has come through the storm in pieces recently.

High-wind stories from crews who have sheltered in the Ashwall channels include harpies in the storm gaps — voices in the wrong place, sounds that do not match the wind's direction.

## Hazards

Storm-edge approaches, hard landings, giant bats in warm vent caves, giant scorpions in handhold fissures, giant vultures after wrecks, harpy stories in storm gaps, and arclight phoenix hatch events that signal Galewall activity.

Ashwall Islands

Overview

The water turns dark before the islands appear — cold, deep blue fading toward black, the warm green smell of the Scatter long gone. Then the spires rise: black volcanic stone, steep-sided, cloud dragging across the upper heights and surf bursting white against the bases. The air carries salt and something mineral beneath it, a thin sulphur bite from the vents in the high stone.

Sailors running the western passage know the Ashwalls as a threshold. Outbound, they are the last solid ground before the Galewall. Inbound, they are the first proof of survival. Ashwall crews treat them accordingly — not as a destination, but as a reckoning point. The navigation tradition out here runs on stars and instruments and the kind of careful attention that keeps you alive when there is nothing ahead but open water.

The spires are not empty just because they are hard to land on. Giant bats roost in warm vent caves, giant vultures work the cliffs after wrecks, and high-wind crews still tell harpy stories about voices in the storm gaps. Most pilots file those stories under weather until someone follows the wrong sound inland.

The vent fissures in the high stone also hold giant scorpions. The volcanic heat keeps the crevices warm through cold sea air, and the same crack systems that look like good handholds on the cliff face can run back several feet into occupied dark. A carpenter from a repair crew — name passed around Ashwall crews as Duvane — was attacked in a fissure while assessing a fouled spar: claw across the forearm, sting through the boot, two days down from the poison. He described not seeing it at all before both claws were engaged. Ashwall repair work now typically sends two hands up the stone face, with one watching the rock instead of the job.

Routes & Access

Sailors running the western passage know the Ashwalls as a threshold. Outbound, they are the last solid ground before the Galewall. Inbound, they are the first proof of survival. Ashwall crews treat them accordingly — not as a destination, but as a reckoning point.

People & Power

The Ashwalls are governed in practice by the crews who can survive and work them: pilots, repair hands, storm readers, and families whose log books preserve practical signs before theory.

Trade & Resources

The Ashwalls are not a market destination. Their value is navigational and practical: repair lee, storm-edge proof, pilot knowledge, emergency work, and the last chance to make a damaged hull ready before or after the Galewall.

The Hatching Sign

Ashwall crews distinguish between two kinds of eruption lightning. The first is vertical: storm discharge running from cloud to stone, ordinary enough that no one marks it. The second moves sideways through the ash column — branching, lateral, holding for a breath before it goes dark. That is the sign. Crews who see it know what it means and know roughly how long they have before something emerges from the vent.

Arclight phoenixes are born inside the Ashwall volcanoes. The volcanic discharge is what hatches them — the egg left behind when a phoenix dies requires lightning to open, and the vent systems provide it continuously and at close range. The bird that climbs out of the stone is already oriented toward the storm edge. It flies west into the Galewall and does not come back east until it has died again somewhere inside the weather.

How long this has been happening is not recorded. The oldest Ashwall pilot families mark the sign in their log books as a navigational note — lateral vent-fire, westward departure, expected increase in Galewall activity — without commentary.

The Lightning-Burned Survivor

The Ashwalls are where Galewall stories become evidence. A ship that survives the storm belt reaches these spires damaged, wet, and short on certainty; pilots and repair crews can still read the hull better than the crew can read its own fear.

One survivor from a failed crossing described a white bird made of stormlight moving through the rigging before the mainmast came down. The account is treated cautiously, but the Ashwall repairs gave it weight: burns ran along contact points rather than down from a single strike, and several iron fittings were magnetized hard enough to pull nails from a workbench. Since then, some Ashwall pilots mark bright, lateral stormlight as a possible arclight phoenix sign rather than ordinary weather.

Fauna

Giant bats roost in the vent caves throughout the spire chain — the volcanic heat keeps the interior fissures warm enough year-round, and the bat colonies are large enough that a repair crew working below a roost at dusk learns not to do that again. The same fissure systems hold giant scorpions in the upper rock faces. The volcanic warmth maintains occupied dark in crevices that look like handholds from a distance. Ashwall repair crews have developed the practice of sending a second hand to watch the stone while the first works it.

Giant vultures work the clifftops and high updrafts in numbers that spike after a wreck. Pilots treat a vulture count above the normal baseline as rough early intelligence about whether anything has come through the storm in pieces recently.

High-wind stories from crews who have sheltered in the Ashwall channels include harpies in the storm gaps — voices in the wrong place, sounds that do not match the wind’s direction.

Hazards

Storm-edge approaches, hard landings, giant bats in warm vent caves, giant scorpions in handhold fissures, giant vultures after wrecks, harpy stories in storm gaps, and arclight phoenix hatch events that signal Galewall activity.

# The Shattered Sea

![[The-Shattered-Sea.webp|Aerial view of the Shattered Sea island chain with turquoise reefs and scattered green islands]]

## Overview

The Shattered Sea is a warm archipelago of roughly sixty thousand square miles: reef, deep channel, cliff port, free harbour, old ruin, colonial ledger, storm belt, and routes that punish anyone who mistakes a chart for the truth.

Two island arcs curve east to west across a wide channel of open water called the Central Strait. The northern arc is the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] — five large, fortified, [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]]-held islands where authority has faces and ledgers. The southern arc is the [[midchain|Midchain]] — dozens of low limestone and coral islands, free ports, reef channels, and water that can feed a careful crew and swallow a careless one.

Between them: the Strait, the trade route, the inspection chokepoint. West of the western entrance: the [[galewall|Galewall]], the permanent storm belt and the only route to the colonial homelands. East of the eastern exit: the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] and the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] — the planar trench, the last frontier, the place that ends expeditions.

Nobody owns the Shattered Sea. The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] claims the northern arc. The [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] controls the money. [[umberlee|Umberlee]] controls the water tribute. Pilots, free ports, smugglers, and local bosses control the rest. Authority here is local, layered, and negotiated at each port.

## Power & Governance

**Dravosi Crown:** Controls the northern arc and the Strait inspection regime. Fleet, forts, harbourmasters, ledgers.

**Tessarine Concordat:** Controls the credit, insurance, and trade underwriting. No forts — just obligation.

**Umberlee and the Waveservants:** Water tribute is practical infrastructure. [[waveservants|Waveservants]] collect at every harbour. Skipping tribute is a choice captains make once.

**Local power:** Every free port has its own council, boss, or factor. Authority in the Midchain is neighbourhood by neighbourhood.

## Navigation

The Scatter Current runs east through the Central Strait and turns north at the eastern end. Eastbound ships get half a knot for free. Westbound ships earn every mile. Pilots earn their fee because every chart in the Scatter has been wrong at least once — reef lines shift, new shoals appear, and the Drowned Maw's compass drift increases the further east you go.

# Al Fondale

![[Al-Fondale.png|Al Fondale, a warm canal-side tavern in Le Paludi with amber light spilling into the narrow waterway]]

## Overview

Al Fondale sits on a side canal off Le Paludi's lower channel, in the part of [[calveno|Calveno]] where the buildings lean close enough that the upper floors almost touch. [[bice-riva|Bice]] and [[aldo-riva|Aldo Riva]] have run it for twenty-two years. Aldo cooks. Bice manages the room.

It is the kind of place that has been there long enough to stop advertising. People who eat here know about it. People who need to know about it find out.

> [!read-aloud]
> The canal narrows here until the stone walls on both sides are close enough to touch from a punt. Al Fondale is the building with the oil lamp burning amber in the ground-floor window and the smell of onions and rendered fat drifting through the half-open door. Inside: low ceiling, worn tables, someone moving in the kitchen at the back. The canal outside is quiet. In here it is warm.

## Description

The ground floor is one main room: eight tables, a low bar, and a kitchen behind a half-wall. The ceiling is original stone. The tables are worn to the specific smooth that comes from thirty years of elbows and plates.

Four rooms upstairs. Small, beds clean, linens changed. During [[il-gioco-delle-beffe|Il Gioco delle Beffe]] festival week, the noise of Le Paludi comes straight through. Bice does not apologize for this. She does charge more.

> [!dm]
> The cellar is below the kitchen, accessed through a door behind the back shelf of dry goods. Against the north wall, behind a row of barrels set on a timber skid, is a stone panel with a catch mechanism. The passage beyond connects to the Warren's drainage network within forty feet.
>
> Nona established this entrance two years ago. Bice was told once, did not ask questions, and has not raised the subject since. She redirects anyone who lingers near the cellar door with a second portion and a topic change.
>
> **Unstable condition:** A Dravosi watch officer has taken a corner table three evenings running. He is eating, not asking questions, but he is watching the room — specifically who comes and goes from the back. If he builds a pattern of who uses the cellar stairs over two more days, it becomes an actionable report. The Rattle gets called. Nona hears. The entrance gets closed.
>
> **Link:** Perrin — Passage connection through Nona; Bice will confirm Perrin is known to Nona if Perrin identifies themselves.

## People & Operations

**[[bice-riva|Bice Riva]]** — Halfling, white-haired, barely clears the tabletops. Puts food in front of people before they finish deciding. Calls everyone *caro*. Does not ask where people are from or how long they intend to stay.

**[[aldo-riva|Aldo Riva]]** — Dwarf, white-bearded, runs the kitchen and comes out to talk about it. Has been in Le Paludi long enough to have watched the canal layout change twice.

Street-side entrance and a narrow canal-side door Bice keeps latched from inside. If the window lamp is lit, the kitchen is running. If it is out, Bice has decided the day is done.

# The Overland Track

## Overview

The Overland Track is the muddy southern switchback road connecting South Harbour to [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] across [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]]. The crossing takes roughly a day and a half on foot or by mount, assuming the weather has not recently made a point.

Wagons break axles daily on corduroy logs laid over the worst mud. The road climbs through wet interior ridge country, then drops again toward the opposite coast, never quite deciding whether it wants to be a road or a tolerated wound in the island.

Locals call it the toll road because every legitimate crossing gives the [[dravosi-crown|Crown]] another chance to count bodies, cargo, and coin.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Muddy island switchback road and toll route |
| Location | [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]], between South Harbour and [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] |
| Controlled By | [[dravosi-crown|The Dravosi Crown]] |
| Access | Open toll road; slow, muddy, and hazardous after weather |
| Known For | Broken wagon axles, Crown tolls, giant axe beak ambush ground, and spider culverts |

## Description

The road crosses wet interior ridge country, climbs through switchbacks, runs over corduroy logs through the worst mud, and drops toward the opposite coast. Official enough for tolls and rough enough that carts, mounts, and tired crews all pay for the crossing in more than coin.

## Notable Features

**Southern Switchbacks** — Muddy climbs where pack animals slow and wagons become predictable targets.

**Corduroy Mud Sections** — Log-laid stretches over the worst mud; useful until a wagon breaks an axle on them.

**Drainage Culverts** — Old stone catchment boxes that create warm, dark spider habitat.

## Fauna

The road concentrates the kind of prey a giant axe beak can use — pack animals slow in the mud, wagons stop at switchbacks, and the ridge above gives a running bird room to pace a caravan before dropping onto it. The ridge country is giant axe beak territory.

Giant boars work the wetter ridge sections where the road runs close to interior scrub. Crown track crews flag fresh wallow sign near the road when they find it.

The drainage culverts along the lower switchbacks are giant wolf spider habitat — warm, dark, rarely disturbed. Track maintenance crews carry poles for this reason.

## Hazards

Mud, broken axles, toll delays, switchback choke points, giant axe beak ambushes, boar sounders, and wolf spiders in drainage structures.

A hull conversion and repainting yard in Calveno's outer harbour, southwest approach — specialises in prize conversions and vessel re-identification, no Canal Commission filing on quiet work.

# Acqua Nera

![[Dario-Vanni.webp|Dario Vanni, proprietor of Acqua Nera boatyard]]

## Overview

Acqua Nera sits at the outer harbour on [[calveno|Calveno]]'s southwest approach, past the Arsenal fortified canal and well clear of the Mercatura's line of sight. It does legitimate prize conversion work — captured vessels bought at auction that need their previous owners scrubbed off before sale — which means the business of changing a hull's appearance is normal here. [[dario-vanni|Dario Vanni]] charges more for jobs that don't go through the Canal Commission, and he does not ask where the vessel came from.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Hull conversion and repainting yard |
| Location | [[calveno|Calveno]], outer harbour, southwest approach |
| Operated By | [[dario-vanni|Dario Vanni]] |
| Public Access | Walk-in for assessment; discreet work by negotiation only |
| Known For | Prize conversions; re-identification work for vessels that need a new history |

## Description

A low stone building against the outer harbour wall with a single wide slip open to the water. The slip can take a vessel up to 90 feet without hauling out. The smell is tar, pine resin, and the particular mineral sharpness of the pigment mixes Vanni makes himself. Finished vessels leave looking like they have always been what they now claim to be.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[dario-vanni|Dario Vanni]]** — Shell worn and paint-scarred along the right rim from decades of drydock work. Deliberate, with the unhurried manner of someone who is never surprised by what a customer needs. Runs two workers who do not ask questions because Vanni does not answer them. Prices discreet work at double the standard rate, cited without embarrassment.

**Sample lines:**

- *"Prize conversion or something else? — same rate either way, before you answer."*
- *"I don't need the story. I need the name you want on the board and the colour you want on the hull."*
- *"She'll float out of here looking like she was built somewhere else. What she actually is — that's your concern."*

## Services

*Discreet rate: double standard pricing. No Canal Commission filing. No record kept of the vessel's previous appearance.*

- Hull repaint, full colour
- Registry plate removal and replacement
- Nameboard replacement (carved and fitted)
- Hull caulking and copper work

## Access & Security

Outer harbour, past the Arsenal canal — accessible by sea directly into the slip, or on foot from the Arsenal end of the southwest district. No appointment needed for assessment. Discreet work is agreed in a private conversation after assessment; Vanni will not commit in writing.

An eccentric magical curio dealer in the Velo Quarter — lanterns at all hours, things on the shelves that don't look the same twice, and an old man who knows the previous owner of everything and will not tell you how it ended.

# The Cabinet of Morsani

![[Prospero-Morsani.webp|Prospero Morsani, gnome curio dealer and proprietor of the Cabinet of Morsani]]

## Overview

The Cabinet of Morsani is in the Velo Quarter, where [[calveno|Calveno]] stops enforcing its normal rules about closing hours. It sells magical and exotic items of uncertain provenance. [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]] insists everything in the shop has a previous owner and he knows the story. The stories always end before the interesting part.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Magical curio and exotic item dealer |
| Location | [[calveno|Calveno]], The Velo Quarter |
| Operated By | [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]] |
| Public Access | Open at irregular hours; lanterns signal availability |
| Known For | Items of unusual provenance, stories without endings, stock that varies week to week |

## Description

Lanterns on at all hours — outside, inside, several on chains over the canal-facing window. The shop is narrow but unexpectedly deep; the shelves go high and curve at the back where the original wall has been extended into a space that doesn't quite fit the building's exterior.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]]** — A gnome whose theatrical impulse has hardened into identity over a very long life, trailing rings on every finger. Greets customers by name if he has met them before and by an accurate physical description if he hasn't. Every item has a previous owner and he knows the story; the stories just never get to the point.

## Stock

*Stock turns over irregularly. Morsani does not produce a static catalogue.*

- 400 gp — [[compass-of-the-drowned|Compass of the Drowned]] — *"The previous owner was a navigator who — well. The compass works."*
- 250 gp — [[ringmakers-regret|Ringmaker's Regret]] — *"Two fifty, or a trade if what you're offering has a sufficiently interesting story."*
- 90 gp — [[preserved-specimen-unknown|Preserved specimen, unknown origin]] — *"I have documentation of the previous three owners. The first one is the interesting part."*
- 80 gp — [[salt-lantern|Salt Lantern]] — *"Came through Port Tidefall. The captain who brought it — there's a story there."*
- 180 gp — [[the-uncharted-coast|The Uncharted Coast]] — *"Two hundred miles of coastline on no published chart. The surveyor's notes are — the price is one eighty."*

## Access & Security

The lanterns outside indicate whether Morsani is in. When all lanterns are lit, walk in. The door is never locked while he is there.

# Calveno — District Layout

Calveno has no docks. Movement is by flat-bottomed boat (faster, 2–5 cp per trip) or on foot along canal walkways and bridges (free, slower, more exposure). The city runs east–west along the main canal with the Arsenal in the southwest and the Velo Quarter on a separate island north of the Bridge.

---

## Districts

### Mercatura

The commercial spine. The main canal runs through it from the harbour mouth inward; buildings press close on both sides. The Tessarine factor house anchors the harbour end.

**Tone:** Loud, transactional, open. Numbers are said out loud. Nothing is confidential by default.

> [!read-aloud]
> The smell hits before the sound does — salt, rope, and something frying. Then the noise: boats on both sides of the main canal, voices calling across the water, the creak of rigging. At the harbour end, pale stone and no signage. The Tessarine factor house is the tallest building on the block.

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| Tessarine factor house | Harbour end. Tracks every deal worth tracking. |
| [[moretti-and-sons|Moretti & Sons]] | Canal-front chandlery. Giacomo at the counter. |
| [[waveservant-shrine|Waveservant Shrine]] | Canal-side. Umberlee tribute in full view of passing boats. |
| Beffa registration table | Festival week only. Bridge side of the Mercatura. |

---

### The Bridge

Three-tier stone crossing at the main canal's midpoint. Bottom tier: vendors, food, bodies. Middle tier: shuttered shops. Top tier: plain stone, narrow staircase that turns out of sight.

**Tone:** Transitional. Everyone passes through.

> [!read-aloud]
> The arch puts everything in shadow before you're under it. Bottom tier: vendors, food, bodies pressed close on both sides. A staircase leads to the upper levels and turns out of sight after three steps. Voices up there — words indistinct.

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| [[ponte-bassa|Ponte Bassa]] | Canal-level at the base of the Bridge. Oleandro's inn/tavern. |
| Batta Zusto | Top tier. Brokers unusual commissions. |
| Festival pinch point | Bottom of the arch — crowd compression point. |

---

### Le Paludi

The oldest part of the city. Buildings shorter, foundations settled unevenly. The channels narrow until two boats cannot pass without touching; the water moves differently — slower, darker.

**Tone:** Close, unhurried. Correct business done correctly; incorrect business done quietly.

> [!read-aloud]
> The walkway narrows past the arch — paving stones older, less even, the canal walls close enough to touch on both sides. The water here barely moves. Sound carries differently; a conversation two doors down is fully audible, which means yours is too.

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| [[al-fondale|Al Fondale]] | Side-canal tavern. Good food, cheap wine, keeper asks nothing. Warren cellar access. |
| [[casa-lupo|Casa Lupo]] | General goods. Ettore prices from memory; has not been wrong. |
| [[studio-orsini|Studio Orsini]] | Off the mapped path. Marta does not ask what the compounds are for. |
| [[warren|Warren]] entry | Beneath Le Paludi. Access via Tangle routes; surface-visible only to those who know. |

**From The Bridge:** Ten minutes on foot through the narrowing canal network. Five minutes by boat.

---

### The Arsenal

Walled shipyard in the southwest. A fortified canal separates it from the rest of the city. Non-House commissions: fourteen-month wait.

**Tone:** Closed. Entry requires a reason that holds up at the checkpoint.

> [!read-aloud]
> The pitch smell arrives before the walls do — sharp, fresh timber underneath it. The fortified canal on your left is still. The checkpoint arch appears before the wall proper. A guard with a ledger watches the water.

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] | Private basin on the Arsenal's southern edge; not Canal Commission-flagged. |
| [[carpenters-slip|Carpenters' Slip]] | Just outside the Arsenal wall. Savia Brentino; no Commission paperwork if she decides it's urgent. |
| [[acqua-nera|Acqua Nera]] | Outer harbour, south anchorage. Dario Vanni; hull conversion; double rate for quiet work. |
| Arsenal gate | Dravosi Canal Commission checkpoint. Sergeant with a ledger. |

---

### Velo Quarter

A separate island attached by two low canal bridges. Lanterns at all hours. Music from more than one direction. Authority stops at the bridges.

**Tone:** Permissive. The crowd is watching performances, not deals.

> [!read-aloud]
> The light changes before you reach the far side of the bridge — warmer, from lanterns hung at different heights. Two songs from different directions, not competing. The buildings here are painted in colours the rest of Calveno doesn't permit. Whatever governs this island, it is not the Canal Commission.

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| [[cabinet-of-morsani|Cabinet of Morsani]] | Prospero's curio shop. Magical items; he knows the previous owner of everything. |
| [[giacinto|Giacinto]]'s theatrical booth | Wigs, prosthetics, ornamental beards, stage paint. |
| [[kats-curios|Cat's Curios]] | Referral only. No sign. Best artificer work in the Scatter. |
| Festival performance squares | Multiple stages active during the Beffa. |

**Getting here:** Two low canal bridges connect north from the Bridge district. Ten minutes from the Bridge on foot.

---

|---|---|---|---|
| Harbour mouth | Mercatura | direct | direct |
| Mercatura | The Bridge | 5 min | 2 min |
| The Bridge | Le Paludi | 10 min | 5 min |
| The Bridge | Velo Quarter | 10 min | — (foot only) |

# Calveno — Improv Reference

Quick-build tools for names, locations, and NPCs that fit the city. Use when the party goes somewhere you didn't prep.

## Linguistic Roots

| Culture | Root | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| Calveno human | Northern Italian / Venetian | Melodic, vowel-ending, names that sound like a trade city evolved them over centuries |
| Tessarine | Elevated Italian / Genoese noble | Longer, more formal, surnames that imply old money and lineage |
| Rattkin | Short Anglo + descriptor surname | One syllable or two; surname is a visible physical trait |
| Canal city halfling | Absorbed Italian first names, Anglo surnames | First names match the city; surnames stayed from wherever they came from |

---

**Surnames:** Arman, Balestri, Candiani, Cerutti, Dolfin, Falier, Grimani, Loredan, Mareschi, Pesaro, Priuli, Rimini, Sanudo, Segalla, Sordi, Trevisan, Trivani, Veniero

**Surnames:** Cardinali, Esposito, Fieschi, Imperiali, Malvasia, Principia, Santucci, Spirito

## Location Naming

Calveno places are named from observable facts, not mythology.

**Patterns:**

| Structure | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Al + noun | *Al Fondale* | "at the bottom" |
| La + noun | *La Vasca* | "the basin" |
| Il + noun | *Il Bivio* | "the fork" |
| Casa + descriptor | *Casa Lupo* | "wolf house" |
| Ponte + descriptor | *Ponte Bassa* | "low bridge" |
| Studio + surname | *Studio Orsini* | owner's name |
| Acqua + colour | *Acqua Nera* | "black water" |

**Useful Italian nouns for places:** Arco (arch), Bivio (fork), Corda (rope), Ferro (iron), Fondo (bottom), Gatta (cat), Muro (wall), Passo (pass), Rosso (red), Sasso (stone), Stretto (narrow), Trave (beam), Vento (wind)

**Urban vocabulary (Venetian):**

| Word | What it describes |
|---|---|
| Calle | Narrow lane between buildings |
| Fondamenta | Canal-side walkway |
| Rio | Inner city canal |
| Campo | Small square |
| Sotoportego | Covered passage through a building |
| Ruga | Wider lane with shops on both sides |

## How Calvenans Talk

Every conversation in Calveno has a transaction under it, stated or implied.

**Common openings:**

- "Who sent you?" — before answering anything useful
- "That's not cheap." — before the price
- "Someone will have heard about this." — before helping with something private
- "Let's say—" — before a number
- "I know a man." / "I know a woman." — before a referral
- "Paid in full, witnessed, no argument." — closing a deal

**Common hedges:**

- "You understand I can't—" *(then does the thing, for a price)*
- "That's between you and whoever you're asking about." *(not a refusal; an invitation)*
- "I only remember boats." *(deniability; they remember everything)*

**Tessarine voice:**
More patient, more formal. They wait. They record.

- "I wonder if you've considered—" *(a better offer that serves them more)*
- "That's already in our ledger." *(they know more than you thought)*
- "Naturally, we'd be happy to facilitate—" *(a condition is coming)*

**Rattkin voice (Warren, Passage, Black-Jaw):**
Direct, concrete, no performance.

- "What do you need." *(not a question)*
- "That costs a favour." *(specific currency; they track these)*
- "Nona will know." *(sometimes a warning, sometimes a reassurance)*

Quick-reference for Calveno — the canal city, its districts, key people, and how it works.

# Calveno — Player Reference

The oldest commercial centre in the Scatter. Pale stone buildings rise four and five stories straight from the water, detailed where they face the canal, bare on the backs where nobody is meant to look. No docks, no streets wide enough for a cart — flat-bottomed boats are the only way through. Deals are struck in the open, where the right people can see who smiled and who didn't. That's not incidental. That's how the city works.

## Key Facts

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Travel Time | 3 days from Tidefall on good wind; a week on bad |
| Power | Seven hereditary merchant families hold Council seats; [[tessarine-concordat|The Tessarine Concordat]] holds debt leverage over six of the seven |
| Access | Flat-bottomed boats through canals; no docks or cart streets |
| Known For | Openly visible dealmaking, canal navigation, hereditary merchant power, and hidden Rattkin infrastructure |

## Districts

**The Mercatura** — The commercial artery running straight from the harbour inward. Boats press from both sides; the air smells of salt, spice, and coin in volume. The Tessarine factor building anchors the harbour end — a full story taller than everything around it, pale stone, no signage.

**The Bridge** — Three-tier stone arch at the main canal crossing. Lowest level: vendors, food, noise. Middle tier: shuttered shops. Top tier: plain stone, a staircase that turns out of sight, and voices you can hear but not make out. Intelligence and money-changing operate here.

**The Arsenal** — Walled shipyard in the southwest, separated by a fortified canal. Fourteen-month wait for non-House commissions.

**[[le-paludi|Le Paludi]]** — The oldest district. Shorter buildings, foundations settled unevenly. Channels too narrow for two boats abreast. A secondary market with no Mercatura records — prices spoken once, quietly. The original drainage network runs beneath it.

**The Velo Quarter** — A separate island reached by two low bridges. Lanterns at all hours, music from several directions at once, buildings painted in colours the rest of Calveno doesn't allow. Whatever authority governs the city stops at the bridges.

## Key People

**[[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]]** — Tessarine Concordat envoy. Holds debt leverage over six of the Seven Houses.

**[[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]]** — Rattkin matriarch and senior Tangle elder. Perrin's grandmother. Operates beneath Le Paludi.

**[[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]]** — Artificer, referral only. The foremost practitioner in the Scatter. Works out of [[kats-curios|Cat's Curios]], a narrow door in a side-street with no sign.

**[[anzolo|Anzolo]]** — A contact vouched for by Nona Black-Jaw. "A nice young man who always helps an old lady out with chores."

## How It Works

Being seen with the right person here carries the same weight as whatever you said to them. Privacy exists — it's just expensive, and someone is always selling it.

Beneath Le Paludi's drainage network sits [[warren|The Warren]], the only fixed Rattkin settlement in the Scatter. The city above has no idea what's down there. The [[the-passage|Passage]] runs its anchor point through it, and the Tangle monitors money flows and canal traffic both — which means they usually know what's moving through this city before the people moving it do.

# Carpenters' Slip

Narrow independent boatyard in [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]], squeezed between two larger buildings near the Arsenal wall. Smell of fresh timber, linseed oil, hot caulking iron. One covered slip for dry work, one canal-side berth for assessment.

The legitimate front is real — [[savia-brentino|Savia Brentino]] does hull repair, mast work, and emergency jobs the Arsenal queue won't touch. The off-book service is re-silhouetting: changing a vessel's hull profile, rail height, transom shape, and rig geometry so it no longer reads as what it was built as.

---

## Access Gate

> [!dm]
> **Savia does not take cold approaches for discreet work.** Three ships tried this month; she refused all three and logged their hulls. A [[warren|Warren]] introduction is required — [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] or another Tangle contact vouching in person. Without it, Savia offers only her public services and quotes standard Arsenal-adjacent rates.

Perrin has the connection through Nona. If the party approaches without a Warren introduction, Savia assesses the hull, quotes legitimate repair, and says nothing about re-silhouetting. She will not hint.

---

## Re-Silhouette Service

**Cost:** 220 gp + one Tangle favour (owed to the [[warren|Warren]], terms set later)
**Duration:** 5 days, vessel slipped the entire time
**What changes:** Transom profile, rail height, bowsprit angle, rig geometry. The hull stops reading as a Crown cutter to anyone trained in ship identification.
**What does not change:** Waterline length, keel, displacement. The ship still sails the same.

> [!mechanic]
> After re-silhouetting, passive recognition of the *Uncertainty* as the ex-*HCS Surety* requires DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) by someone who has seen Crown cutter blueprints. Without the work, any sailor with Crown navy experience recognises the hull lines on a DC 10 check.

**The Tangle favour:** Unspecified at time of agreement. The Warren calls it in later, through Nona or another contact. Perrin agreed to one unconditional favour already — this is a second, owed by the party collectively. **Savia will not negotiate on this point.** The favour is not optional; it is part of the price.

---

## Savia Brentino (Quick Reference)

**[[savia-brentino|Savia Brentino]]:** Dwarf, compact, sawdust in her eyebrows. Speaks in structural assessments — diagnosis is greeting, prognosis is farewell. Does not quote timelines she cannot keep and does not explain herself twice.

**Sample lines (discreet work):**

- *"A repaint does not make a cutter stop reading as a cutter. I do the geometry."*
- *"Five days. She stays slipped the whole time. Your crew finds somewhere else to sleep."*
- *"The Warren sent you, so I'll do the work. The terms are the terms."*

**Sample lines (cold approach / no introduction):**

- *"Transom's carrying too much. I can fix that. Anything else you need is at the Arsenal."*
- *"I don't do cosmetic work."*

---

## Legitimate Services (Public)

- Hull inspection (written assessment)
- Hull caulking, plank repair (minor to moderate)
- Mast work (stepping, splicing, repair; up to two masts)
- Rudder repair or replacement
- Emergency repair (double rate, Savia decides priority)

Walk-in for assessment; work begins after deposit.

---

## If the Party Ignores the Disguise Problem

> [!dm]
> The [[hcs-surety|*Uncertainty*]] still reads as a Crown cutter. Consequences escalate by geography:
>
> - **Calveno and neutral ports:** Low risk. Locals don't care about Crown hull lines.
> - **Crown-friendly waters (Dravosi patrol routes, Knighton-allied ports):** The hull gets flagged. Port inspectors board for registration check. The *Surety* is listed as missing — seized by pirates or lost. A boarding reveals the name change and triggers immediate impound or pursuit.
> - **Open sea, Dravosi navy encounter:** **Rupert Knighton** has standing orders on the *Surety*. Recognition is automatic at close range. Engagement follows.
>
> Timeline: Knighton's ships are already en route to intercept (see [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] faction clock). Every session without re-silhouetting narrows the window.

## Current Hooks

- Three vessels refused discreet work this month for lack of a Warren introduction. Savia logged the hulls. At least one was [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi]] — a patrol cutter out of Kalowe asking questions on the causeways about independent yards.
- The five-day slipping window overlaps with the *Uncertainty*'s existing repair at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]]. If timed together, the party loses ship access for the full duration. If done sequentially, they are shipbound in Calveno for 10 days total.

## Overview

Casa Lupo is a general goods shop in the lower canal zone of Le Paludi, the oldest district in [[calveno|Calveno]]. It sells what people actually need rather than what ships need.

## Description

Low ceiling, oil lamps on iron hooks, floorboards that have been settling unevenly for a century and have reached a comfortable arrangement with gravity. The shelves go to the ceiling on three walls. The smell is candle wax, dried herbs, and something faintly mineral that was probably the previous shop's business.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[ettore-lupo|Ettore Lupo]]** — Seventy-something, moves with the energy conservation of a man who has decided he has already moved enough. Prices everything from memory and has not been wrong. Will tell you clearly if he does not have something. Will not tell you where to get it unless he has formed an opinion of you.

## Stock

Lanterns, lamp oil, candles, rope, canvas and cloth, needles and thread, cooking tools, dried herbs and spice, basic medicines, writing supplies, locks and keys, tool sundries. Ask for what you need; stock changes.

## Notable

- Ettore keeps a sealed account of who in Le Paludi bought what and when, going back forty years. He has never been asked about it and does not volunteer its existence.
- Jean-Claude visited to ask about shortbow; Ettore redirected him to [[studio-orsini|Studio Orsini]] for the whip shark egg inquiry.
