# Cat's Curios

![[Catarina-DaVirelli.webp|Catarina Da'Virelli, proprietor of Cat's Curios]]

## Overview

Cat's Curios is a referral-only artificer workshop in [[calveno|Calveno]], hidden behind a narrow side-street door with brass fittings and no name. It belongs to [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]], who does not advertise, does not take walk-ins, and does not expand her circle casually.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Referral-only artificer workshop |
| Location | [[calveno|Calveno]], side-street — no sign |
| Operated By | [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]] |
| Public Access | Referral only; no walk-ins |
| Known For | The best artificer work in the Scatter and a locked cabinet of dark-alloy pieces |

## Description

A narrow door in a Calveno side-street — brass fittings, no name. Inside: long benches of half-finished mechanisms, a low forge, the smell of hot oil and soldering flux, and a locked glass cabinet along one wall holding pieces that don't belong to this century.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]]** — Works from the bench and does not offer chairs. All transactions happen on the workshop floor. The circle of people who can reach her is deliberately small.

## Notable Areas

**Workshop Floor** — Long benches, precision tools racked by size, half-finished mechanisms in various states of assembly.

**Specimen Cabinet** — A locked glass case along the east wall. Dark-alloy pieces, faintly iridescent, tooling marks too fine for any current forge in the Scatter. Trade only; no cash price.

## Stock / Services

- Artificer commission — *"Describe the mechanism. I'll tell you if it's something I'll do, and what it takes."*
- Mechanism repair — *"Bring it in. I'll assess it on the bench."*
- Antheri-alloy mechanisms (specimen cabinet) — trade only; no cash price

## Access

There is no sign and no public shopfront. Access depends on referral, reputation, and Da'Virelli's willingness to accept the visitor.

## Current Hooks

- A party that needs the Scatter's best artificer work needs a referral from someone Catarina trusts.
- The dark-alloy pieces in the specimen cabinet connect to the [[antheri-ruins|Antheri Ruins]] salvage economy.

The Black-Jaw family's private dry dock deep in Le Paludi — a covered basin cut from old foundation stone, used for vessels the family needs kept out of sight. Officially a derelict tanning facility. Password: garden.

# La Vasca

## Overview

The Black-Jaw Run has operated a private basin in [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]] for three generations. The canal approach is unremarkable — a low stone arch barely wide enough for a keel, flush with the waterline, indistinguishable from the drainage culverts on either side. On the far side of the arch, the channel widens into a covered basin cut from old foundation stone: high enough for a mast to stand, long enough for a patrol cutter or a heavy caravel. The dry dock cradle is iron and timber, hand-operated, original equipment from when the building above it was still a tanning yard. It still works. The tannery has not operated in forty years.

Outside, the building looks like what it officially is: a disused storage facility with a rotted roof and a collapsed beam visible through the upper windows. The beam is real. It is also not structural.

Within the Passage, the place is called La Vasca — the Basin. New members learn it as an address, not an explanation.

**Access password:** *garden*

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Location | Le Paludi, deep canal, Calveno |
| Access | Canal approach only; arch unmarked and below sight line from the bank |
| Capacity | One vessel up to 90 ft; dry dock cradle rated to 80 tons |
| Known To | Black-Jaw Run members and vouched Passage contacts only |
| Officially | Derelict tanning facility; Canal Commission records show inactive |

## Description

The basin smells of old stone, bilge, and the particular mineral damp of a space that has not seen direct sunlight in decades. A single oil lamp on a chain over the cradle. The walls are original foundation stone — Le Paludi is built on layers of older Calveno, and the basin is somewhere in the middle stratum. Rattkin-scale tool racks run along the port wall: caulking mallets, copper tacks, pitch brushes, paint pigments in sealed crocks. The starboard wall holds spare timber, a hand-pump bilge rig, and a folding worktable covered in old manifests that nobody has cleared in years.

A narrow passage in the aft wall connects to the Warren's outer channels — technically accessible on foot at low tide, not comfortable, and not discussed with anyone who hasn't already been introduced.

## People & Operations

**[[cobb|Cobb]]** — A young Rattkin in his late teens, grey-brown fur, hands hardened from caulking work. He keeps the Basin running: cradle maintained, tool stock managed, vouched vessels escorted in through the arch, word sent up the chain when the Basin is used.

He will have the cradle ready before he asks any questions, and he will not ask many. What he will do — early, calmly, without confrontation — is tell Perrin that Nona has been asking after him and will know he is here within the hour regardless.

> [!dm]
> Cobb is not the threat. He's the clock. Using the Basin is not a secret — it is a known event being reported through proper channels to the person who runs those channels. The warmth is genuine. The reporting is also genuine. These are not in conflict. Play Cobb as someone doing his job correctly, which in this case means being helpful and honest about exactly what being helpful costs.
>
> If a player tries to ask Cobb not to tell Nona: he pauses, looks at Perrin with something between sympathy and mild disbelief, and says *"I can't do that."* Not unkind. Just: no.

**Sample lines:**

- *"She's been asking around. I got a description three weeks ago — fancy rat, olive hood, oversized sword. Said to send word if he came through."*
- *"Basin's free. I'll have the cradle ready in an hour. Your shipwright know how to use a hand-pump rig?"*
- *"You should go see her before she comes to you. It'll go better."*

## Services

- [[registry-plate-removal|Registry plate removal]] — Removal and disposal of a vessel's registry plate. No record of prior markings kept.
- [[hull-caulking|Hull caulking]] — Basic maintenance between major jobs.
- [[timber-and-fittings|Timber and fittings]] — Stock from the starboard wall; varies by recent turnover.

## Current State

[[hcs-surety|Uncertainty]] in cradle. 5-day repair estimate.

## Current Hooks

- Cobb will report Perrin's arrival to the Warren within the hour.
- The old manifests on the worktable are Black-Jaw shipping records going back thirty years.

# Moretti & Sons Chandlery

![[Giacomo-Moretti.webp|Giacomo Moretti, halfling chandler and proprietor of Moretti & Sons]]

## Overview

Moretti & Sons is [[calveno|Calveno]]'s main ship outfitter on the Mercatura, a long low warehouse with a canal-side loading door wide enough for two boats abreast. It handles practical shipboard needs — rope, provisions, tools, canvas, lamp oil — efficiently and without ceremony.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Ship chandlery and outfitter |
| Location | [[calveno|Calveno]], Mercatura canal front |
| Operated By | [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]] |
| Public Access | Open to all; canal-side loading available |
| Known For | Fair prices on naval supplies and a proprietor who remembers every regular customer |

## Description

A warehouse built flush with the Mercatura canal, long and low, with a loading door that opens directly onto the water. The smell inside is rope and tar and salt, in that order. The counter runs the full length of the interior. Giacomo works from behind it.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]]** — A halfling in his middle years, grey at the temples. Can quote the current market price of oakum, sail canvas, lamp oil, and rope in bulk without looking anything up. Gives a discount if you've moored at Calveno before and he remembers you; he usually does. Does not bargain on provisions.

## Stock / Services

- 1 gp — [[hempen-rope|Hemp rope (50 ft)]] — *"Standard rigging weight. Heavier gauge in the back if you need it."*
- 10 gp — [[silk-rope|Silk rope (50 ft)]] — *"Small quantities. I don't always have it — if you need it, buy it now."*
- by weight — [[oakum|Oakum]] and [[tar|tar]] — *"Caulking tools for hire if you don't own a set."*
- by grade — Sail canvas (per sq yd) — *"Three grades. Tell me what you're patching."*
- 6 sp — [[lamp-oil|Lamp oil (per gallon)]] — *"Standard grade for general use. Sea-lantern grade costs four more per gallon and doesn't fog up in salt air."*
- varies — [[signal-lantern|Signal lanterns]] — *"Clear, red, green, shuttered. Spare panels too."*
- 1 gp — [[block-and-tackle|Block and tackle sets]] — *"Single or double. Iron-fitted."*
- 2 sp — Ship's biscuit (10 lb) — *"Hardtack. Keeps. That's the whole recommendation."*
- 3 sp — Salt pork (10 lb) — *"Barrelled, ready to cask."*
- 2 sp — [[dried-salt-fish|Salted fish (10 lb)]] — *"Local catch. I know the supplier."*
- 3 sp — [[dried-beans|Dried legumes (10 lb)]] — *"Mixed. Shelf-stable."*
- 1 sp — Vinegar (quart) — *"For the casks. Also edible, technically."*
- 8 sp — Fresh water cask (40 gal) — *"Drawn this morning. I don't fill yesterday's water."*
- 5 sp — [[marlinspike|Marlinspike]] — *"Good steel."*
- varies — [[iron-cleat|Spare fittings]] — *"Cleats, rings, bolts, pins — sorted by size on the east wall."*
- varies — [[canvas-bag|Canvas bags and netting]] — *"Multiple sizes. Cargo net is a special order, two days."*
- 1 gp/yd — [[oilskin-canvas|Oilskin canvas]] — *"Waterproofed. For covers and gear bags."*
- 4 sp/bolt — [[canvas-cloth|Canvas cloth]] — *"Unfinished. Cutting and hemming extra."*
- 5 sp/50 ft — [[light-rope|Light rope]] — *"Not rigging grade. Fine for everything else."*
- 1 gp 5 sp — [[rigging-block|Rigging block]] — *"Iron-strapped oak shell."*
- 4 sp — [[linseed-oil|Linseed oil]], quart — *"Wood and canvas treatment. Not the lamp grade."*
- 5 sp — [[needles-and-thread|Needles and thread]], sail kit — *"Curved sail needles, waxed twine. For canvas work."*
- 2 sp — [[cooking-tools|Cooking tools]] (basic) — *"Pot, knife, fire striker. Galley fit."*
- 3 sp — [[writing-supplies|Writing supplies]] — *"Ink, quill, paper, wax seal."*

## Current Hooks

- Giacomo is currently holding a disputed cargo: a crate whose papers were good but whose manifest was wrong. He has notified the Tessarine factor house and is waiting for someone to come and be wrong about it in front of him.

Canal-level tavern built into the bridge masonry at the main Calveno crossing — cheap food, basic beds, and a proprietor who has been watching boats arrive for thirty years.

# The Ponte Bassa

![[Oleandro-Fuschi.webp|Oleandro Fuschi, proprietor of the Ponte Bassa]]

## Overview

The Ponte Bassa is a canal-side tavern built into the bridge-level masonry at the main Calveno crossing. It is the kind of place people go to eat cheaply in public view of the canal, which in Calveno means in public view of everyone.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Tavern and inn |
| Location | [[calveno|Calveno]], The Bridge, canal level |
| Operated By | [[oleandro-fuschi|Oleandro Fuschi]] |
| Public Access | Open |
| Known For | Fish broth, cheap wine, and a proprietor who knows every boat that has moored here in two decades |

## Description

The low ceiling on the canal side is where the bridge arch comes down; the back half of the room has clearance. Seating is open to the water — anyone on a passing boat can see who is eating and with whom, which most Calveno regulars treat as a feature. The kitchen smells of fish stock and cheap wine. Upstairs: beds, basic, available by the night.

## People & Operations

**Proprietor: [[oleandro-fuschi|Oleandro Fuschi]]** — Wide-shouldered, green-grey, soft-spoken. Keeps a mental ledger of every vessel that has moored at the bridge canal in twenty years; he has never been caught wrong about one. If you're looking for someone who came through Calveno recently, Oleandro either knows or knows who would.

## Stock / Services

- 3 sp — [[fish-broth|Fish broth]] — *"Bowl, not cup. Bread comes with it."*
- 5 sp — [[grilled-canal-eel|Grilled canal eel]] — *"House specialty. It's an acquired taste."*
- 4 sp — [[preserved-meat-plate|Preserved meat plate]] — *"Salted pork, olives, hard cheese. For sitting over a long conversation."*
- 2 sp — [[common-wine|Cheap wine, carafe]]
- ask — [[house-spirits|House spirits]] — *"Comes in a clay cup. No label."*
- 2 sp — [[hammock-berth|Bed, shared room]] — *"Three per room."*
- ask — [[canal-boat-hire\|Canal boat hire]] — *"Two boats. Half-day or full day. I don't ask where you're going."*

## Current Hooks

- A captain left a sealed letter with Oleandro three weeks ago "for the next person asking." He has not opened it.

Upstairs: beds, basic, available by the night.

People & Operations

Proprietor: Oleandro Fuschi — Wide-shouldered, green-grey, soft-spoken. Keeps a mental ledger of every vessel that has moored at the bridge canal in twenty years; he has never been caught wrong about one. If you’re looking for someone who came through Calveno recently, Oleandro either knows or knows who would.

# Waveservant Shrine — Calveno

[[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s waterfront shrine in [[calveno|Calveno]], set into a pale stone arch along the Mercatura canal front where boats pass close enough to read the posted tribute terms.

The shrine opens directly onto the canal — a low arch of pale stone, deep enough to block the worst wind off the water, shallow enough that anyone on a passing boat can see who is inside and what they are doing. The basin is fed from the channel directly. A ring of tallow candles burns behind a glass screen. The posted tribute terms face outward, toward the canal, not the door.

In a city that runs on witnessed transactions, the shrine fits without effort. Captains pay before they sail or after they survive. Both are acceptable. Neither is optional.

## Function

Operated on a tithe-and-communion model. A junior attendant manages the candles and basin; a senior [[waveservants|Waveservant]] manages tribute collection, blessing, and the ledger. In Calveno the ledger is kept more formally than at most ports — witnessed commerce has a culture here, and the shrine absorbed it.

## Current State

> [!dm]
> [[umberlee-servant|An unnamed Waveservant]] is waiting here for [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]]. Has been all day. Not sleeping until he comes. She reached up for him at the dock and said his name. The shrine is her fixed point now.
>
> Determine before the shrine scene: what is the message? Why Delmar specifically, and what does she know about the Crowded captains?

## Access

Open to anyone approaching by canal or on foot along the Mercatura. Defaulting on tribute is treated like any commercial default in Calveno: publicly, efficiently, and everyone remembers.

# High Line

## Overview

A fishing hamlet built into the northeastern cliffs of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]], where the cold upwellings come in thick with yellowtail and the rock face drops straight to the water. There is no beach. There are no docks. What there is: massive counterweighted wooden winches bolted to the cliff edge, lowering nets down the face and hauling the catch back up.

The settlement is vertical — ladders, rope platforms, creaking stairways cut into stone, winch-baskets that double as the only transport between levels. The fisherfolk here know every handhold and wind angle. Visitors take longer to learn which gaps are fatal.

## Description

The settlement is vertical — ladders, rope platforms, creaking stairways cut into stone, winch-baskets that double as transport between levels. The fisherfolk here know every handhold and wind angle.

**Winch Line** — Massive counterweighted wooden winches bolted to the cliff edge lower nets down the face and haul the catch back up.

**Rope Platforms** — Work stages, ladders, creaking stairs cut into stone, and winch-baskets that double as transport between levels.

## Fauna

The cold upwelling that makes High Line's nets worth the effort draws hunter sharks into the water column below the cliffs. Winch operators have learned to read the surface for shark sign before sending repair crews down the net face on rope stages. Giant crabs occupy the boulder field at the base of the cliff and can be harvested when surf is low, but the crabs are large enough that the harvesting crew goes armed.

The northern cliff faces carry harpies — not every stretch, but close enough to the upper platforms that the hamlet posts watches during low-wind conditions, when the birds are most active and the winch operation is noisiest.

## Hazards

Hunter sharks below the cliff face, giant crabs at the base, harpies on the northern faces, and vertical drops throughout.

# Kalowe

## Overview

Kalowe is built across three low limestone islands connected by stone causeways over a lagoon that sits dead calm behind its reef. The reef breaks the ocean swell before it reaches the harbour; inside, the water is flat enough to mirror the palms, and the dry-dock cranes are the first thing visible above the treeline on approach.

It is the only Tier 2 dry dock in the [[midchain|Midchain]] outside colonial administration, which is why ships that cannot afford to be seen at Tidefall end up here. Unregistered vessels, hired crews, cargo that skipped the ledger, and people working hard to be difficult to locate — Kalowe is where those things move.

There is no colonial authority here, which is not the same as no authority. The Island Council runs nine seats on a non-interference doctrine, the harbour has its own bosses and money and grudges, and enough people are watching at any given moment to keep most disputes verbal until well after dark. Missing papers are forgiven faster than missing payment.

Kalowe is also the normal meeting place of [[chain-council|the Chain Council]], the occasional Midchain assembly that forms when independent islands need to answer a shared problem without surrendering their independence.

# Murrat

## Overview

Murrat sits roughly midway between [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and the western edge of the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], a limestone reef island low enough that the canopy is the first thing you see above the horizon. From the approach it looks like every other uninhabited Midchain island: dense forest, pale cliff faces above the waterline, reef running out ahead of the hull.

It isn't on most working charts. Pilots avoid it. The island is [[moucheron|Moucheron]] territory and they attack anything that lands — no protocol, no one to negotiate with. Any party that comes ashore is treated as prey.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Inhabited wilderness island |
| Region | [[midchain|The Midchain]], between [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and [[verdant-teeth|The Verdant Teeth]] |
| Controlled By | [[moucheron|Moucheron]] villages |
| Access | Avoided; pilots refuse; no safe landing point |
| Known For | Moucheron villages; hostile to all outsiders; avoided by all sailors |

## Geography

The island is a single irregular limestone mass, larger than it looks from a distance. The reef extends further east than charts show — responsible for at least two groundings. The interior rises to a low central ridge. Fresh water exists (springs and an interior lake), which explains why the island supports multiple permanent villages.

The canopy is thick. Landing parties who survived long enough to leave accounts described not seeing more than twenty feet in any direction on the ground. The Moucherons fly at sixty feet and see everything.

## Settlements & Sites

The villages are built into the cliff faces — stone platforms in natural limestone hollows, rope bridges between them. Invisible from the water. A ship close enough to see the platforms has already been seen by everyone in them.

## Hazards

**Moucherons.** Villages can scramble a response within minutes of a landing. They fly 60 feet and spot movement through the canopy from above. Multiple squads will respond — killing the first wave does not end the encounter.

**Fauna.** The interior has giant constrictor snakes, giant spiders, giant apes, and giant frogs. A party that breaks away from the Moucherons moves directly into their hunting grounds.

**Eastern reef shelf.** Extends further east than most charts show. Sharp limestone, outgoing tide pulls toward it.

- A merchant out of Kalowe is asking for charts of Murrat's interior — there's a story about a cache left by an early explorer who landed before anyone told him what the island was.
- A grounded vessel on the eastern reef shelf is visible from the Kalowe-to-Verdant-Teeth route. Three days now. No sign of the crew.

TypeInhabited wilderness island
Region[[midchain
Controlled By[[moucheron
AccessAvoided; pilots refuse; no safe landing point
Known ForMoucheron villages; hostile to all outsiders; avoided by all sailors

Geography

The island is a single irregular limestone mass, larger than it looks from a distance. The reef extends further east than charts show — responsible for at least two groundings. The interior rises to a low central ridge. Fresh water exists (springs and an interior lake), which explains why the island supports multiple permanent villages.

The canopy is thick. Landing parties who survived long enough to leave accounts described not seeing more than twenty feet in any direction on the ground. The Moucherons fly at sixty feet and see everything.

Settlements & Sites

The villages are built into the cliff faces — stone platforms in natural limestone hollows, rope bridges between them. Invisible from the water. A ship close enough to see the platforms has already been seen by everyone in them.

Hazards

Moucherons. Villages can scramble a response within minutes of a landing. They fly 60 feet and spot movement through the canopy from above. Multiple squads will respond — killing the first wave does not end the encounter.

Fauna. The interior has giant constrictor snakes, giant spiders, giant apes, and giant frogs. A party that breaks away from the Moucherons moves directly into their hunting grounds.

Eastern reef shelf. Extends further east than most charts show. Sharp limestone, outgoing tide pulls toward it.

Current Hooks

  • A merchant out of Kalowe is asking for charts of Murrat’s interior — there’s a story about a cache left by an early explorer who landed before anyone told him what the island was.
  • A grounded vessel on the eastern reef shelf is visible from the Kalowe-to-Verdant-Teeth route. Three days now. No sign of the crew.

# Port Tidefall

![[Port-Tidefall.webp|Fortified cliffside port city built in tiers above a busy harbor]]

## Overview

Port Tidefall is carved directly into the cliff face of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]] in three tiers: Dockfront at the waterline, the Shelf mid-cliff, and [[fort-crestwall|Fort Crestwall]] at the crown with cannon pointed seaward. The harbour mouth is narrow, the [[inspection-pier|inspection pier]] extends to starboard before any ship reaches the dock, and three nooses hang from the gate arch above the entrance — empty, freshly painted black. Nobody in port remembers when they went up.

Every ship entering the western Strait is expected to stop, answer questions, and produce the right paper in the right order. Most do.

# South Harbour

## Overview

South Harbour faces the calmer Strait side of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]], where the island slopes into tidal mudflats and shallow estuaries. Dravosi ledgers call it a secondary anchorage. In practice it is a working sprawl of fishing fleets, independent shipwrights, small traders, and repair crews doing the work that keeps the island functional while the Crown's attention stays focused on [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] to the west.

Crown authority here is real but intermittent — patrols arrive unevenly, and the tidal mud makes armored inspection difficult when the tide is against you. [[waveservants|The Waveservants]] maintain a quiet unofficial presence among the fishing fleets. Small cargo that might draw questions at Tidefall frequently arrives here first.

# The Low Lamp

## Overview

The Low Lamp is the social heart of the [[warren|Warren]] — a wide, low-ceilinged chamber dug into the widest section of the old drainage corridor, where Kin have gathered to eat, trade news, and conduct open business for as long as anyone currently alive can remember. It is the first place a trusted guest is taken when they enter the Warren.

Long communal tables of dark, scarred wood. Oil lamps set into wall niches. The central lamp — older and larger than all the others, hanging on a chain from the highest point of the ceiling — gives the place its name. Nobody knows exactly how old it is. Nobody has let it go out to find out.

Business is conducted here openly — debts acknowledged, introductions made, news exchanged — but the convention holds that no Tangle business is brought to these tables. What happens in the Low Lamp is Kin business, visible to all. What requires privacy goes elsewhere.

## Proprietor

**[[essa-two-tooth|Essa Two-Tooth]]** — A Rattkin elder who runs the Low Lamp with her grand-nephew Pip. She moves slowly and hears everything. Every person who enters is, in her assessment, too thin. She provides food before any discussion. If you eat, you have acknowledged the Low Lamp's claim on your goodwill. This is the point.

# Marrow's

## Overview

Marrow's is a cargo broker's stall carved into the rock off the Warren's north channel corridor — three steps down from the main passage, easy to miss if you don't know it's there. Marrow handles things that needed to move without appearing on a manifest: sealed documents, consignment packages, cargo that required a different kind of routing than the surface city offers.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Cargo broker / logistics specialist |
| Location | [[warren|The Warren]], north channel corridor |
| Operated By | [[marrow|Marrow]] |
| Public Access | Kin and Kin-introduced only |
| Known For | Moving things that needed to not be seen |

## Description

Three steps down from the north channel corridor is an alcove carved into the rock. Two walls hold shelves, most of them empty in a way that suggests recent turnover rather than slow business. A brass scale sits on the central table, polished on the pan surfaces and scratched everywhere else. The single lamp illuminates the table without lighting the back of the room.

Marrow is usually already seated when anyone enters and usually already watching the door. Lean, with one ear notched at the tip, wearing clothes that settle into the stone colour without effort. He weighs everything twice on the brass scale. Nobody has asked him why.

## People & Operations

**[[marrow|Marrow]]** gives no other name and is not asked for one. Has operated from this alcove for at least fifteen years. Accepts Kin by default. Dry need a Kin introduction and Marrow's own read of the situation — he has turned away people with good introductions before and offered no explanation.

## Stock / Services

- 5 gp+ — [[document-transit|Document transit]] — *"Price reflects content weight. Not physical weight. No questions."*
- 10 gp + 5% — [[cargo-brokerage|Small cargo brokerage]] — *"Three-week hold. Stated value. Non-negotiable terms."*
- 1 gp/wk — [[consignment-storage|Consignment storage]] — *"Three weeks. Hard limit. After that — my concern, not yours."*
- 15 gp+ — [[passage-network-introduction|Passage network introduction]] — *"Kin by default. Dry by my read and a Kin introduction. No guarantees."*

## Access & Security

The alcove is not marked. Finding it requires someone who already knows where it is.

The deep, dry governing chambers of the Warren — where the seven Tangle elders meet, where Nona Black-Jaw keeps her apartments, and where the Passage's oldest routing memory is held.

# The Tangle Chambers

| | |
|---|---|
| **Location** | [[warren|The Warren]], deep southern section |
| **Access** | Tangle summons only — even long-established Kin guests are not admitted without invitation |

## Overview

The Tangle Chambers occupy the deepest, driest section of the [[warren|Warren]] — a set of interconnected rooms carved into the rock at the Warren's southern end where the ceiling unexpectedly lifts and Calveno's noise no longer reaches. This is where the seven elders of the Tangle deliberate, where [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]]'s apartments are, and where the [[the-passage|Passage's]] most sensitive routing memory has been maintained for generations.

## Description

The corridors at the Warren's southern end are different. The stone is older here — tooled rather than broken. The ceiling lifts unexpectedly in the main passage, high enough that a human could stand comfortably. Nobody knows why. The arguments about it are old enough to be running jokes.

Two rope bridges cross short flooded sections on the approach. The central chambers beyond are all dry stone, swept clean, with oil lamps burning behind glass. The smell is paper, oil, and old stone — the archive smell.

## Function

The Tangle deliberates here when business requires the full council. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona's]] apartments in the south rooms serve as the Black-Jaw family's private residence and, effectively, the Passage's operational centre in [[calveno|Calveno]]. The archive rooms hold routing records and network intelligence accumulated across generations, written in shard-notation that only Kin can read.

## People & Operations

The **Tangle** is seven senior Rattkin elders. They meet when they need to. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] chairs by convention and has done so long enough that the convention feels like law.

The Black-Jaw family maintains the chambers: lamps trimmed, corridors swept, archive rooms dry, bridges inspected. This is not ceremonial — it is the work.

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] grew up moving through these rooms. He knows the way without thinking about it.

## Access & Security

No formal guard at the approach. Every Rattkin in the Warren knows these corridors and knows how to make an uninvited presence known to the appropriate elder. Kin guests with long-standing Warren access do not enter without a specific summons. Dry guests have not entered in living memory, with four acknowledged exceptions.

## Current Hooks

- The Tangle has sent one message through the Passage to Perrin's last known port of call. He has not responded.
- A summons from Nona carries no deadline and no expiration date. She does not send reminders.

![[Colla.webp|Colla, proprietor of The Splint]]

## Overview

The Splint is the Warren's healer and apothecary, occupying a small dry room off the east passages. Run by **Colla**, a young Rattkin who trained under his aunt. The name is old Kin slang — something close to "the fixing place."

The walls are shelved floor to ceiling with clay jars, labeled in a small, careful hand. Dried plants hang in bundles. The central table serves as both counter and treatment surface and is kept scrupulously clear between patients. Colla works in silence and moves with the economy of someone who knows exactly where everything is in the dark.

## Proprietor

**[[colla|Colla]]** — Late twenties. Silences are not hostile; he simply does not see the point of conversation during a procedure. His expression makes clear his limited patience for people who arrive with injuries they could have avoided. He will write down his reasoning if asked.

His surface-side contact is a herbalist in Le Paludi named Dosia, who supplies ingredients he cannot source underground.

| ask | [[custom-preparation\|Custom preparation]] (commission; 1–3 days) |

## Current Hooks

- Colla needs brine-sage — a low-tidal marsh plant used in several wound preparations — that has become nearly impossible to source since a Dravosi trade restriction tightened last season. He'll pay 30 gp per reliable bundle or equivalent services.
- Someone came to the Splint three weeks ago with injuries Colla found concerning. He reported it to the Tangle. He has not seen that person since and does not discuss it further.

# The Shelfworks

![[The-Shelfworks.webp|Coral shelf dropping into deep blue water with workboats gathered near the edge]]

## Overview

You find the Shelfworks by following the boats. There is no island, no lighthouse, no harbour wall. Just open ocean with anchored salvage vessels, marker buoys, air-pump stations, and dive lines running straight down into water clear enough to make the depth look kinder than it is.

At forty feet, sunlight catches pale Antheri stonework. Walls still stand. Archways are still arched. Fish move through rooms that once held something other than fish. Coral has taken the lintels. Small reef sharks treat the old halls as territory.

Then the shelf ends. Twenty metres east of the last visible wall, the ruins drop away with no visible bottom. The water there is a different colour — darker, directionless, the kind of blue that has no floor in it. Experienced salvagers do not look east if they can help it.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Open-water Antheri salvage site |
| Location | Western shelf of the Drowned Maw |
| Controlled By | Contested by independent crews, [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]], [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]], and pirate pressure |
| Access | Open-water dive site; crew, pumps, rope discipline, and weather window required |
| Known For | Air-pump barges, dark-alloy salvage, upper ruins, and the drop-off nobody looks at |

## History

In 1488 DR, [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]] salvaged functional [[antheri|Antheri]] components from the upper ruins and returned to Calveno with them. The wave of prospectors, scholars, and criminal contractors that followed became the Shelfworks Goldrush. The goldrush thinned the easy pickings from the upper shelf. What remains is harder to reach, harder to identify, and harder to get back to the surface intact.

The [[red-lady|*Red Lady*]] wreck sits on the eastern edge of the Shelfworks shelf. The [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] is still aboard.

## What's Here

**Upper ruins (40–80 ft):** Accessible by free-diving or short air-pump runs. Walls, archways, collapsed floors. Dark-alloy fittings that resist corrosion and cut differently than anything modern. Most portable pieces are gone; fixed architectural components remain.

**Mid-shelf (80–150 ft):** Requires air pumps. Intact room structures with sealed chambers. The [[antheri-ruins|Antheri Ruins]] proper begin here — architecture built for beings that didn't need floors or standard-height doorways.

**The drop-off (150 ft+):** The shelf ends and the water column opens into the Drowned Maw. Nothing survives an uncontrolled descent into that water. Nobody looks at it if they can help it.

## Hazards

Reef sharks in the upper ruins. Hunter sharks along the shelf edge. Giant squid in the deeper channels. The [[the-glass-debt|Glass Debt]] occasionally makes salvage traffic change course. At the drop-off: the Drowned Maw itself.

## Current Hooks

- The [[red-lady|*Red Lady*]] wreck on the eastern shelf edge. The [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] is aboard.
- [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]] trades for intact Antheri metalwork — the Shelfworks is the source.
- [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] standing purchase orders for intact structural Antheri pieces; Da'Virelli has not accepted them.

- [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina Da'Virelli]] — foremost expert on Antheri materials

# Sorn

![[Sorn.webp|Forested island with a pale beach and dense jungle rising inland]]

## Overview

From the water, Sorn reads as an unbroken wall of green — limestone ridge above the canopy, jungle running all the way to the reef line, no harbour, no smoke, nothing that looks like an invitation. The western shore has a strip of pale sand where the treeline has been cut back a few metres, wide enough for a few boats to pull up. That is the only point on the island where outsiders are expected to conduct business.

Sorn is the agricultural interior of the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] — the island where the Grung work runs. The Botukuri clan holds the island; their name is on thirty years of Midchain trade accounts. A purple-caste garrison maintains the beach. Intermediaries come to the waterline and conduct business there. Nobody from the interior comes out, and nobody from the water goes in.

The raids out of the Teeth have been getting worse, and Sorn is not where the raids come from, which is one of the few pieces of information about it that most traders find reassuring.

> [!dm]
> **Jean-Claude connection:** [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]] fled from Sorn. [[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]] leads the garrison and a hunter unit tracking deserters. She also supplies Grung hunting toxin to the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] — Jean-Claude identified her compound in the Session 01 canister. See [[the-canister|The Canister]].

## Trade & Resources

Interior agriculture, resin shipments, pigments, and alchemical specimens traded through intermediaries at the beach.

## Fauna

Giant wasps audible above the cut-back treeline. [[giant-centipede|Giant centipedes]] carried out on hooked poles. Grung patrols keep flooded interior paths clear of [[giant-frog|giant frogs]]. Giant apes apply pressure from the ridgelines. Traders see only aftermath: repaired palisades, delayed resin shipments, guards returning with crushed equipment.

## Current Hooks

- Delays in resin shipments and repaired palisades hint at giant ape pressure inland.
- Sorn is not where the recent Verdant Teeth raids originate.

# The Sunken Crown

> *Five small islands around a blue wound in the sea.*

## Overview

The Sunken Crown is a small island region in the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]], northeast of the Drowned Maw crossing. Five low islands ring a vast Blue Hole that occupies most of the region's usable geography. The islands are not a broad archipelago — they are the exposed rim of something drowned: black stone, salt grass, wind-bent scrub, and cliffs that show old waterlines like scars.

Colonial charts thin out before these waters. Most pilots treat the region as a rumour or a navigation note to avoid. The people who live here have been here longer than any outside record acknowledges.

The waters around the Blue Hole have been unsettled lately. Currents reversing without warning, fish avoiding channels they have always run, weather turning faster than the sky gives notice.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Blue Hole reef-region and five-island cluster |
| Parent Region | [[outer-reach|The Outer Reach]] |
| Major Places | [[keth-naar\|Keth-Naar]], [[vel-orn\|Vel Orn]], [[ral-arn\|Ral-Arn]], [[dath-mar\|Dath-Mar]], [[meth-var\|Meth-Var]] |
| Controlled By | Keth-Naar elders, watch rotations, and shrine authority |
| Known For | A vast Blue Hole, Tabaxi watch culture, failing sea blessing, and dragon turtle nesting |

## Geography

The Blue Hole occupies most of the Sunken Crown. From any high point it reads as a near-perfect dark circle inside the reef rim — deep enough that soundings fail quickly, warm in places from lingering volcanic activity, clear enough near the edges that large shadows can be seen moving far below. The boundary between turquoise shallows and indigo drop is clean and sudden.

## Major Locations

|---|---|---|
| [[keth-naar\|Keth-Naar]] | town / island | Main settlement; Tabaxi hunting community, black basalt promontories. |

## Access

Requires crossing east of the Drowned Maw into the Outer Reach — six hours over the Maw, then open water. The five islands are surrounded by reefs and channels that do not behave consistently. Without local knowledge: reef damage risk or being drawn toward the Blue Hole's drop-off.

## People & Power

The Tabaxi of [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] organize the region through elders, watch rotations, seasonal knowledge, refuge practice, and shrine obligations.

> [!dm]
> Without the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]], the shrine still marks debts and remembers the drowned, but its deepest function — stabilizing the Blue Hole and protecting nesting waters — is failing. See [[sunken-crown-blessing-crisis|Sunken Crown Blessing Crisis]]. The Pearl was stolen from [[vel-orn|Vel Orn]] by [[delmar-fisk|Fisk's fleet]].

## Fauna

Giant lizards bask on the black stone, giant bats crowd wind-cut caves, and scavenger birds gather wherever storm or tide leaves food behind. The [[sawek|Sawek]] is rumoured in the Blue Hole. Dragon turtle wyrmlings nest on the outer beaches of Dath-Mar and Meth-Var — the elders know the sites; outsiders do not.

# The Tail

## Overview

The Tail is the eastern end of the [[shattered-sea|Verdant Scatter]], where both island arcs narrow and converge near the Drowned Maw. The islands here grow fewer, taller, and more vertical: high cliffs, wind exposure, and faces of stone dropping straight into cold deep water.

The communities here have lived beside the trench for generations. They know the shelf edge, the fog schedules, the reefs that changed last season, and where the Maw's discolouration begins on a clear day. Less settled than the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]], not empty, and not forgiving.

The Tail is where piracy stops being a tavern story and starts affecting routing. Shelfworks crews, longliners, and Maw-crossing vessels all pass through tight weather windows, which gives a patient [[pirate-captain|pirate captain]] something to plan around.

## Geography

Both island arcs narrow here, forcing traffic into compressed channels. The shelf edge drops sharply into Maw-adjacent water. Cold upwelling produces some of the most productive fishing grounds in the Scatter — and the predators that follow productive grounds.

Morning fog hangs late in the eastern channels before burning off. Compass variance begins near the Maw's influence zone.

## Hazards

[[giant-shark|Giant sharks]] work the cold shelf. Giant vultures ride cliff thermals. Giant axe beaks and giant bats on the island interiors. Harpies rumoured in the cliff systems. The Glass Debt makes Shelfworks traffic change course when she's active. The Velvet Noose is a worse rumour.

## Current Hooks

- Tight weather windows and compressed routing create ambush geometry for patient pirates.
- Salvage crews staging for the [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] move through here — most contracts route through the [[tail-staging-island|Tail Staging Island]] near the Maw's western edge.
- The [[the-glass-debt|Glass Debt]] has been sighted in the eastern channels within the last fortnight.

# The Drowned Maw

![[The-Drowned-Maw.webp|Vast dark blue ocean sinkhole spiraling into deep water]]

## Overview

The Drowned Maw is a north-south trench running along the eastern edge of the [[verdant-scatter|Verdant Scatter]], 40 to 90 miles across. The approach is visible before any other landmark: the water changes colour from the blue-green of the Scatter shallows to something deeper and less defined, a blue with no bottom in it. The surface goes flat. Not calm — still, in a way that open ocean normally isn't. No current runs over it. Seabirds that follow ships across the Scatter turn back at the edge. No fish school over it. No sounding line has found the bottom.

Compasses drift within five miles and don't recover until you're through. Most captains navigate the crossing by stars and run it fast. Nobody anchors over the Maw. That particular piece of advice circulates without much explanation, and experienced sailors don't ask for one.

Ships cross routinely — it's the only route east to the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] — and most have no trouble. The ones that do have trouble come back quiet, which is its own kind of information.

> [!dm]
> **True nature:** Imperial-restricted trench. The [[antheri-ruins|Antheri]] built into the western wall, descending toward a planar fissure at the bottom where the mortal sea touches the [[elemental-plane-of-water|Elemental Plane of Water]]. When the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] sank near the fissure, it turned passive elemental leakage into a directed attractor. The Leviathan forced through soon after.

## Geography

The Drowned Maw is a north-south trench running along the eastern edge of the [[verdant-scatter|Verdant Scatter]], 40 to 90 miles across. The boundary is not marked on most charts: one watch you're in trade winds; the next, nothing. Seabirds turn back at the edge. No fish school over it. No sounding line has found the bottom.

## Routes & Access

Compasses drift within five miles and don't recover until you're through. Most captains navigate the crossing by stars and run it fast. Nobody anchors over the Maw.

Ships cross routinely — it's the only route east to the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] — and most have no trouble. The ones that do have trouble come back quiet.

## People & Power

The [[high-eyrie|Sentinels of the High Eyrie]] have kept aerial observation of the Maw's surface for two centuries. Their records are the most complete in the Scatter. The Waveservants dislike questions about what they think is down there, which tells you something, though not what.

## Trade & Resources

On the Maw's western rim, forty feet down, there are ruins: old stone buildings, dark-alloy fittings, construction that exceeds anything currently being made. The [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] are the current gold rush of the Scatter, with salvage crews on site most weeks. The upper shelf is accessible. What lies below it is not.

## The Vestra Water

Sailors have started using "Vestra water" for the bad stretch near the Maw where [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] lost the *Vestra* and survived alone. The public version is simple enough to travel: an ordinary fishing day, sudden heat through the hull, water boiling around the rails, then a strike from below hard enough that the ship stopped being a ship.

What hit the *Vestra* remains argued rather than proven. Perrin's signs match the old leviathan chapter in [[clydes-bestiary-of-oceanic-creatures|Clyde's Bestiary]], but they also match the practical warnings attached to [[ancient-dragon-turtle|ancient dragon turtles]]: scalding fog, heat before impact, and a shell-dark mass rising under the keel. Most captains do not care which name is correct. They care that someone survived long enough to say the water went hot before the ship died.

## The Shelfworks

On the Maw's western rim, forty feet down, there are ruins: old stone buildings, dark-alloy fittings, construction that exceeds anything currently being made. The [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] are the current gold rush of the Scatter, with salvage crews on site most weeks. The upper shelf is accessible. What lies below it is not.

> [!dm]
> The lower Shelfworks dive tier is currently abandoned — no crews will work below 60 feet after a heat event at 80 feet cooked a crew's bait line without warning. The Shelfworks gold rush is pulling safety architecture off a deeper Antheri containment system, and the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] signal is making the Maw more dangerous. One Maw crossing ship has logged a warm water patch and dead-fish smell on the Shelfworks approach; the pilot filed it as a vent anomaly.

## Who's Been Watching

The [[high-eyrie|Sentinels of the High Eyrie]] have kept aerial observation of the Maw's surface for two centuries. Their records are the most complete in the Scatter. The Waveservants dislike questions about what they think is down there, which tells you something, though not what.

## Fauna

The Maw's inhabitants are arranged by depth. The rim is [[whip-shark|whip shark]] water — fast, surface-oriented predators that follow ships slowing at the crossing and work the shelf edge where the floor drops away. The deeper shelf approach carries giant squid at night: the drop-off creates a thermal boundary that certain prey species follow upward in darkness, and the squids follow the prey.

Below the shelf, the scale stops being useful for practical planning. The Maw has room for large things: kraken, [[dragon-turtle|dragon turtles]], [[leviathan|Leviathan]]. What exists at what depth is not established in any record the pilot community considers reliable. What the records show is that some ships cross without incident, some come back with crews that don't discuss what they saw, and some don't come back.

## Hazards

Compass drift, star-only navigation, still water, no anchoring, whip sharks at the rim, giant squid at night near the drop-off, [[pirate-captain|pirate]] pressure around salvage traffic, kraken and [[dragon-turtle|dragon turtle]] rumours, and the leviathan thread.

## Current Hooks

- "Vestra water" is now a public sailor phrase for the bad stretch where Perrin lost the *Vestra* and survived alone.
- The [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] gold rush is pulling safety architecture off a deeper Antheri containment system.
- [[the-glass-debt|The Glass Debt]] is known for making Maw-adjacent salvage traffic change course.
- [[the-velvet-noose|The Velvet Noose]] is mostly a rumour in these waters, which is still enough to make a convoy wait for daylight.

The Drowned Maw

Overview

The Drowned Maw is a north-south trench running along the eastern edge of the Verdant Scatter, 40 to 90 miles across. The approach is visible before any other landmark: the water changes colour from the blue-green of the Scatter shallows to something deeper and less defined, a blue with no bottom in it. The surface goes flat. Not calm — still, in a way that open ocean normally isn’t. No current runs over it. Seabirds that follow ships across the Scatter turn back at the edge. No fish school over it. No sounding line has found the bottom.

Compasses drift within five miles and don’t recover until you’re through. Most captains navigate the crossing by stars and run it fast. Nobody anchors over the Maw. That particular piece of advice circulates without much explanation, and experienced sailors don’t ask for one.

Ships cross routinely — it’s the only route east to the Outer Reach — and most have no trouble. The ones that do have trouble come back quiet, which is its own kind of information.

DM Note

True nature: Imperial-restricted trench. The Antheri built into the western wall, descending toward a planar fissure at the bottom where the mortal sea touches the Elemental Plane of Water. When the Pearl of Souls sank near the fissure, it turned passive elemental leakage into a directed attractor. The Leviathan forced through soon after.

Rook’s access: Barnaby Rook accessed the Maw illegally twice. Kept no record of what he found. Crissdalynn discovered this in his chart archive aboard the Uncertainty. The deliberate absence of records is its own data point — he didn’t want anyone knowing.

Crissdalynn’s task: She was close to completing a mapping task for Master Kyzil when the Red Lady went down. The mapping is incomplete. She knows it.

# Vel-Orn

Vel-Orn is the barren black-stone island that holds [[umberlee-shrine|Umberlee's shrine]] in the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]]. The name carries the local tabaxi sense of water-debt. Outsiders call it Shrine Island.

The people of [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] treat Vel-Orn as a boundary, not a destination — visible from the Lookout Stone as a black point across the water, but not welcoming. The island has no natural harbour, no village, no hunting ground, and no refuge worth seeking.

Its cultural role is debt and restraint. The living do not go there for ordinary reasons. It is where offerings pass into Umberlee's account, where the drowned are remembered, and where visitors are expected to behave as if the sea is listening.

## Approach

No dock, no welcome fire, and no beach worth naming. A skiff has to find a break in the stone and time the surge. Keth-Naar guides do not speak loudly on the crossing, keep their hands visible, and do not bring fresh blood onto the rock.

## Fauna

Giant bats cling under the black overhangs. Raven swarms gather after offerings or wreckage. Giant vultures circle after storms and land on the highest exposed rock.

## Hazards

Sharp black stone, surge timing, no freshwater, storm-displaced bats, ravens, giant vultures, shrine taboo, and the failed protection after the Pearl's theft.

# The Verdant Scatter

## Overview

The Verdant Scatter is the primary archipelago of the [[shattered-sea|Shattered Sea]], running east to west between the [[galewall|Galewall]] and the Drowned Maw. It is not one island chain so much as two arcs with a shipping road between them.

The northern arc is the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]: five larger, mountainous islands with deep harbours, forested highlands, fortifications, inspections, and the Dravosi Crown's strongest regional foothold.

The southern arc is the [[midchain|Midchain]]: dozens of smaller islands packed close together, with free ports, reefs, local councils, pilot families, and routes that make more sense to people who learned them from grandparents than from charts.

Between them runs the [[central-strait|Central Strait]], the main navigable corridor through the region. To the east, both arcs narrow and converge at [[tail|the Tail]], where the water grows colder and the Maw starts shaping every decision.

## People & Power

The northern arc carries the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]]'s strongest regional authority. The southern arc belongs more to island councils, free ports, pilot families, market bosses, Grung trade boundaries, and local arrangements that do not fit comfortably into a colonial ledger.

## Trade & Resources

The Scatter moves inspected Crown cargo, free-port repair work, fish, shellfish, local market goods, Grung exports, salvage traffic, and contraband. Its economy depends on knowing when the official route is worth the price and when the local route is worth the risk.

## Piracy Scale

The Scatter's pirate threats scale with geography. The [[knifes-wake|Knife's Wake]] makes single bad channel choices expensive. The [[the-bad-receipt|Bad Receipt]] turns Midchain paperwork into a weapon. The [[the-glass-debt|Glass Debt]] is what happens when piracy grows large enough that convoys, patrols, and councils all have to react.

# The Verdant Teeth

## Overview

Five closely grouped islands sit two days south of [[kalowe|Kalowe]], where low reef-fringed coasts rise into limestone ridges and thick rainforest swallows the high ground. From the water, the islands look less like separate places than a single green wall broken by reefs, pale sand, and the occasional gap in the trees that no sensible pilot treats as an invitation.

The [[grung-clans|Grung clans]] hold the cluster completely. Every Midchain chart from the last thirty years marks the interiors with some version of the same warning: do not approach. Outsiders who cross the tree line do not come back, and the locals talk about that as a rule of navigation, not a rumour.

Coastal settlements across the Midchain have noticed more raids coming from the direction of the Teeth in recent years. The [[chain-council|Chain Council]] has heard the complaints. For now, [[veth|Veth's]] beach remains open for trade.

> [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]] was born here and fled. [[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]] still leads Sorn's garrison and supplies Grung toxin to the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]]. Jean-Claude is wanted as a deserter.

# Veth

Veth is the largest island in the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], and the only place in the cluster where outsiders are expected to make contact with the [[grung-clans|Grung clans]]. That contact is narrow by design. No harbour. No pier. No visible village. Just a western beach, reef water, and a wall of rainforest climbing toward limestone ridges inland.

Traders anchor offshore and wait. Blue-caste intermediaries come down to the waterline, handle the exchange, and leave again by the same controlled path. Everyone else stays where they are supposed to be. Outsiders do not go inland, do not follow the intermediaries, and do not address higher-caste Grung directly.

From the water, the important thing about Veth is how little of it can be seen. The island permits commerce at the edge and keeps everything else above the sightline.

## Trade

Veth takes preserved food, worked timber, salvaged metal, rope, and materials used in poison-crafting. In return: carved bone, resin pieces, pigments, alchemical specimens, and other goods from the interior.

## Hazards

Beyond the narrow beach permission: giant venomous snakes on warm stone, giant spiders in the upper green, [[giant-frog|giant frogs]] wherever water sits long enough. The limestone ridges above the beach hold giant scorpions — they work the rock face at night and occasionally reach the beach by dawn.

Merchants who describe Veth as safe mean the beach, during trade, while watched.

# The Warren

The Warren is the fixed Rattkin settlement beneath [[calveno|Calveno]], built into the old drainage channels below the Le Paludi / Saltmarsh district. Calveno grew above it. The Rattkin were already there.

Rattkin origin point for [[the-passage|the Passage]]. The network formed out of the Warren in 1240 DR to evade colonial pressure from the [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] and [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]]. Brown-rat work defines much of the Warren's physical logic: tunnels, Holds, subsurface routes, and maps of harbour construction before outsiders know those spaces have become routes.

The [[black-jaw-run|Black-Jaw Run]] anchors the Warren in Calveno. The Tangle's most sensitive routing intelligence sits here.

Most Dry know the Warren as rumour. Kin speak of it with more precision and less decoration — it is home, anchor, and warning all at once. Access is not obtained by asking. A person may be shown a door and still know almost nothing about what lies past it.

## At a Glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Type | Hidden Rattkin settlement |
| Location | Beneath Calveno, below Le Paludi / Saltmarsh drainage network |
| Controlled By | [[the-passage|The Passage]] and Kin elders |
| Public Access | None; invitation and kin trust only |
| Primary Economy | Shelter, routes, memory, information, hidden holds, kin support |
| Known For | The deepest fixed anchor of the Passage in the Shattered Sea |

## Physical Character

Low stone corridors and dry chambers cut into the old marsh channels, with rope bridges over flooded sections and oil lamps set into wall niches. The ceilings are low enough that most humans feel the place in their shoulders. The air smells of old stone, standing water, lamp oil, and the warmth of people living where water was supposed to go.

The sound of Calveno filters down through disguised vents: faint voices, water traffic, market noise, footsteps above. The city is always overhead, but never fully present.

## Places

| Place | Notes |
|---|---|
| [[low-lamp|The Low Lamp]] | Communal tavern and gathering hall. Essa Two-Tooth runs it. Everyone gets called too thin. |
| [[marrows|Marrow's]] | Sealed cargo, documents, and deniable logistics. Kin introduction required. Three-week consignment limit. |
| [[the-splint|The Splint]] | Colla sets bones and stocks the Warren's only reliable healing preparations. |
| [[tangle-chambers|The Tangle Chambers]] | Where the seven Tangle elders deliberate and [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] keeps her apartments. Summons only. |

## The Rattle

The Warren's alarm system. When Dravosi enter Le Paludi, someone begins striking a pan in a steady rhythm — faster when contact is close. Another household answers. Then another, then the Low Lamp, then hidden kitchens, pipes, vents. The sound travels through old stone, drainage tunnels, and cistern walls until it seems to come from everywhere at once.

To Kin, the meaning is clear: Dravosi are here. Those who cannot fight hide and lock their doors. Those who can fight answer the call. Subterfuge, sabotage, ambushes, improvised incendiaries — the Warren uses everything available when the odds are asymmetrical.

To the Dravosi, the Rattle is maddening. No one is brandishing a weapon. No one is technically obstructing an officer. No one can be arrested for washing pans or repairing cookware in a crowded district full of kitchens and canal workers. But every Crown officer feels it: surrounded, watched, counted, tracked.

**Two quick taps after the Rattle stops** means the threat has been dealt with.

## Current Hooks

- The Warren usually knows what is moving through Calveno before the people moving it do.
- Do not mark a suspected entrance, boast about being invited, or mistake a rumour for permission.
- The collector tunnels below the Warren now host Grung [[calveno-sewers-grung-magazines|blackpowder magazines]] — Nona suspects something is building but does not know the full scope.

# The *Brass Cat*

> [!read-aloud]

Amidships, brass-framed glass sits flush in the deck over a sealed compartment below. Four brass constructs move through the rigging and across the planks with precise, silent regularity, never glancing up, never wasting motion.

---

## Overview

[[catarina-davirelli|Catarina DaVirelli]]'s personal prototype: an experimental Tier 2 schooner built for surface sailing, underwater operation, and long-term self-contained travel. She is not for sale.

A 95-foot two-masted schooner with a conventional timber topside, copper-sheathed lower hull, and a sealed midship life-support compartment built around Da'Virelli's air containment system. Full submersion capability, a functioning onboard garden, and a clockwork crew that lets DaVirelli operate the vessel alone.

The Red Lady, raised by Umberlee as pressure on Delmar Fisk — always upwind, always where you are going. She cannot kill Fisk without losing five captains' souls. She is not trying to kill him.

# The *Dead Lady*

> *She is always upwind, regardless of actual wind direction. She does not pursue. She is already where you are going.*

**Type:** Brigantine (spectral), Tier 2 | **Owner:** [[umberlee|Umberlee]] | **Status:** Dormant until triggered

The [[red-lady|*Red Lady*]], raised by [[umberlee|Umberlee]] as a punishment instrument. She exists to compel [[delmar-fisk|Fisk]] to retrieve the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]], not to kill him. Umberlee cannot kill Fisk without losing the five captains' souls into the Maw a second time. She knows this. The *Dead Lady* is pressure, not execution.

---

## Appearance

Her hull matches the *Red Lady*'s outline exactly: same length, same rigging, same dark red paint — now the colour of old blood in water. The figurehead is the same carved woman, eyes still forward. Her wake does not foam. She makes no sound at any distance. Other ships that sight her know immediately what she is.

---

## Stat Block

> [!mechanic]
> Combat stats apply at Stage 3 and 4 only. Before that she is a presence, not a combatant.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Hull Points** | 230 |
| **Hull AC** | 14 (partially incorporeal) |
| **Speed (any wind / calm)** | 90 miles/day |
| **Speed (night, open water)** | 120 miles/day |
| **Gun Mounts** | 14 (7 per side) |
| **Weapons** | 12 × Spectral Cannon; 2 × Swivel |

**Damage Immunity:** Poison, psychic, non-magical physical.
**Damage Resistance:** Fire, cold, necrotic.
**Damage Vulnerability:** Radiant, force.
**Destroying her:** Reduces to 0 HP disperses for 1d4 weeks; Umberlee reconstitutes her. Permanent destruction requires a campaign-significant ritual.

---

## Crew

Rank-and-file sailors of Fisk's original five-ship fleet (not the captains, who are in Fisk's mind). Approximately 30 crew. Recognisable as individuals to anyone who sailed with the fleet. They do not speak.

If Fisk sees them close enough to identify faces, he will recognise them. The five captains in his mind will also recognise them.

**Type:** Shadow stat block, ship-appropriate. Can move through solid hull material. Do not initiate boarding before Stage 3.

**She has no captain.** Umberlee drives her directly. Nothing to bargain with, deceive, or remove.

---

## Special Properties

**Dead Reckoning.** Always knows where Fisk is. Navigation tricks, false trails, fog, and weather do not affect her course.

**Forbidding Tide.** Ships within 1 mile: reversed currents and unnatural headwinds. Tier 1 ships −20 miles/day; Tier 2 ships −10 miles/day. Passive and constant.

**Spectral Boarding.** Her crew pass through solid hull material — boarding requires no entry points.

**The Voice Below Deck.** When within half a mile of Fisk, he hears voices from below her waterline — his crew, calling up through the hull. The five captains hear it too. Not a mechanical effect; information delivered without a save.

**Umberlee's Wake.** Creatures overboard within 300 feet: DC 16 Strength save or pulled 30 feet toward her hull at the start of each turn.

---

## Spectral Cannons

Silent at firing — the shot arrives with only displaced water.

- **vs. crew:** 4d10 cold damage; DC 14 Con save or gain 1 exhaustion level
- **vs. hull:** Double damage against Tier 1 vessel hull material

---

## Deployment

### Trigger

[[waveservants|Waveservants]] deliver Umberlee's terms once she learns Fisk survived and is operating. She sets a deadline (8–12 weeks from first contact) to demonstrate movement toward retrieving the Pearl. If the deadline passes without action, the *Dead Lady* is dispatched.

---

### Stage 1 — Contact

A Waveservant delivers Umberlee's terms directly to Fisk: retrieve the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] from the Maw and return it. She names the deadline. She does not describe the consequence.

---

### Stage 2 — Sighting

The *Dead Lady* appears on the horizon. Matches the party's heading but does not close. Visible at dawn and dusk. Other ships give the party distance. Ports show visible unease. Not a Reputation loss yet — a warning.

---

### Stage 3 — Approach

Closes to weapon range but does not fire on Fisk's vessel directly. Attacks other ships in the party's company. Circles rather than closes. Her crew board other vessels — not Fisk's.

**Reputation loss:** 1 step with factions/ports aware of the situation.

---

### Stage 4 — Escalation

Begins targeting Fisk's ship's hull. Will not kill Fisk — but will destroy his ship and take anyone who enters the water. Her crew board through the hull. The party cannot sail, cannot port, cannot operate.

---

### Resolution

| Path | Outcome |
|---|---|
| **Compliance** | Fisk demonstrates movement toward the Maw. Umberlee stands the *Dead Lady* down to the horizon. Returns if progress stops. |
| **Appeasement** | Significant offering + deed of service to Waveservants buys a deadline extension. Does not buy a Stage 4 reversal. |
| **Destruction** | Disperses 1d4 weeks. Umberlee reconstitutes. Underlying situation unresolved. |
| **Negotiation** | Fisk has real leverage — Umberlee needs him alive and cannot retrieve the Pearl herself. A player who works this out and pushes has a genuine position with a goddess. See [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] for the full leverage shape. |

---

The Fernen

Overview

A two-masted brigantine, mid-sized, fourth ship of the fleet. Plain-hulled — dark brown below the waterline, weathered timber above. Six gun mounts, three per side. She rode at a moderate draft, neither as deep as the Heft nor as light as the Narrow. A working ship without distinguishing characteristics.

Below decks: crew quarters, a compact galley, and a hold fitted for long-range independent operation — extended provisions, an oversized water cistern, and a navigator’s station charting the full eastern Scatter.

Captained by Sienne Orre.

The Sinking

Lost simultaneously with the rest of Fisk’s Fleet when Umberlee opened the Drowned Maw beneath them. All hands lost.

# HCS *Constancy*

> [!read-aloud]
> A two-masted frigate on a grey hull, twelve cannon ports per side on the main gun deck and eight more above on the upper deck. The white stripe runs bow to stern at the upper deck rail. Crown pennant at the mainmast. A rating officer is already visible at the rail before the ship finishes its turn into your wind. She is not threatening you. She is waiting for you to make the next move.

---

## Overview

A two-masted heavy frigate, 140 feet on the waterline, built at the Harwick Naval Yard to the Crown Admiralty's standard patrol specification. The *Constancy* is the class the Crown uses when it needs a ship that can enforce, not merely inspect: enough guns to discourage resistance, enough cargo space to transport seized goods and prisoners, and enough range to operate in the Scatter for months without returning to Tidefall.

Hull is naval grey. White Admiralty stripe at the upper deck rail, narrower than the *Ordinance*'s but identically maintained. Brass registry plate at the bow. Crown pennant at the mainmast. The stern cabin is a working captain's office — two sealed document drawers, a rating ledger bolted to the desk, and a speaking tube that runs to the gun deck below.

The name is not incidental. The Crown names its patrol class after virtues because a patrol ship represents the steady, unremarkable presence of law. The *Constancy* is not the ship that arrives for a crisis. It is the ship that was already there.

---

## Purpose

Where the *Ordinance* settles matters, the *Constancy* creates the conditions that require settling:

- Conducts **Rating Inspections** on vessels transiting Crown waters — hull registry, cargo manifest, crew papers, and charter documentation.
- Executes **Impound Orders** issued by civil or Admiralty authority.
- Escorts **Crown convoys** through contested reef passages and Greyteeth approaches.
- Maintains **patrol presence** along assigned routes, logging every vessel encountered.
- Suppresses **unlicensed privateering** in Crown waters by force if necessary.

The *Constancy* does not outrun threats. It discourages them.

## Special Facilities

### Inspection Office *(Special — 2 space units)*

A dedicated compartment off the main gun deck, fitted with a Crown registry desk, scales and weights station, and a locked evidence cabinet. Hireling: **Rating Officer** (specialist — ship's legal officer, not a crew role).

*Active (Director):* Once per Bastion Turn, the Rating Officer may conduct a formal inspection of a named vessel or individual. On success, produces a Crown-certified rating: legal status, outstanding fees, or registered infractions. Admissible in any Crown civil or Admiralty proceeding.

*Passive (All):* Crown-flagged vessels in the same harbour are treated as inspected for the week. Non-Crown captains formally rated by this ship's officer make Deception checks at disadvantage when presenting forged papers to any Crown official with access to the registry network.

### Brig and Holding Deck *(Special — 2 space units)*

A reinforced below-decks section forward of the magazine, fitted with iron cell doors, marine guard post, and four holding compartments for up to twelve prisoners. Hireling: **Marine Sergeant** (double-role: serves as Bosun on crew roster).

*Active (Director):* Once per Bastion Turn, the Marine Sergeant may process one prisoner per holding compartment: sworn depositions, extraction, or prisoner transfer to Crown civil authority.

*Passive (All):* Can hold and transport persons under Crown warrant without additional cost. Escape attempts made at disadvantage — the cells are below the waterline.

---

## Layout

**Weather Deck** — Wheel, compass, signal flags, Crown lamp array. Captain's cabin aft. Four swivel mounts amidships. Marine station at rail.

**Upper Gun Deck** — Eight guns per side, 18-lb long cannon. Inspection Office aft. Officers' berths and mess forward.

**Main Gun Deck** — Twelve guns per side, 18-lb long cannon. Primary fighting deck. Crew berths and mess forward. Armorer's station amidships.

**Below Decks (Orlop)** — Brig and Holding Deck forward. Surgeon's berth. Stores.

**Hold** — Magazine and shot locker aft. 75 tons cargo capacity.

## Overview

A three-deck Ship of the Line, 210 feet on the waterline, built at the Harwick Naval Yard in the Crown Islands. The *Ordinance* was the largest vessel the Crown commissioned — the only Tier 4 hull in the Shattered Sea at its commissioning, and the clearest possible statement that the Crown's authority is not an argument it intends to have twice.

The hull is naval grey. A white Admiralty stripe runs the full length at weather deck level. Cannon ports number forty-two per side across three gun decks, fitted with cast-iron 24-pounder long guns. Six stern chasers and six bow chasers extend the battery. Total mounted guns: 96. The figurehead is Tyr — robed, blindfolded, scales extended, gilded at the scales and sandals, face left unpainted.

---

## Purpose

The *Ordinance* does not patrol. It arrives. In practice:

- **Mobile Admiralty Court** — hears military tribunals, issues commissions, revokes privateer licenses, renders Crown judgements.
- **Fleet Command** — carries an Admiral's staff and signals complement.
- **Deterrent** — reputation travels weeks ahead of the ship.

## Special Facilities

### Admiralty Court *(Special — 2 space units)*

Sealed chamber on the upper stern with raised dais, Tyr's symbol in brass, witness rail. Hireling: **Judge-Advocate** (ship's legal officer).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn, issue one Crown legal instrument — commission, revocation, warrant, impound order, or letters of marque. Full Admiralty authority, enforceable in all Crown-held ports.

*Passive:* Crown officers gain advantage on Intimidation checks against parties subject to Crown law.

### Registry Vault *(Special — 2 space units)*

Steel-doored archive below the waterline with fireproof caskets and a copying press. Hireling: **Ship's Registrar** (not a crew role).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn — produce certified document copy, forge Crown certificate (DC 18 Investigation to detect), or locate named individual's Crown registration.

*Passive:* Generates a legal paper trail for every port visited, vessel inspected, and order issued.

### Gunner's Magazine *(Special — 2 space units)*

Reinforced lower-deck compartment with alchemical desiccant and Crown-standard powder-charge casting equipment. Hireling: **Gunner-Warden** (double-role: Gunner on crew roster).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn — prepare specialist shot order (grapeshot, chain shot, or alchemical incendiary). Applies in the next combat encounter.

*Passive:* Cannon attacks deal maximum damage on a confirmed critical hit. Magazine has never misfired.

# HCS *Sovereign*

![[banners/HCS-Sovereign.webp]]

> [!read-aloud]
> Three gun decks rise above a grey hull painted the colour of deep water — fifteen cannon ports per side on the lower deck alone, all closed, brass fittings catching light at every seam. A white Admiralty stripe runs the full length of the ship at the spar deck rail, wider than any other Crown vessel in the Scatter. Three mastheads carry the Crown pennant. The figurehead is a robed figure holding a crown aloft, not offering it — claiming it. She moves slowly. She does not need to move quickly.

---

## Overview

A first-rate ship of the line, 215 feet on the waterline, built at the Harwick Naval Yard over six years and commissioned as the definitive expression of Dravosi naval power. ## Special Facilities

### Grand Magazine *(Special — 2 space units)*

A reinforced double-chamber below the lower gun deck, climate-controlled with alchemical desiccant. Forward chamber: prepared shot for all three gun decks. Aft chamber: specialist rounds — chain, bar, heated, grapeshot — in separate sealed lockers. Hireling: **Master Gunner** (double-role: Gunner on crew roster).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn — prepare a specialist shot order for any one deck. Applies automatically in the next combat encounter.

*Passive:* Cannon attacks deal maximum damage on a confirmed critical hit. On a natural 1 on any cannon attack, the gun misfires but does not explode; cleared as an action.

### Admiral's War Room *(Special — 2 space units)*

Full stern cabin spanning the width of the spar deck — glazed windows, chart table, signals rack, dispatch archive. Hireling: **Flag Lieutenant** (specialist — not a crew role).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn — transmit fleet orders, reposition a Crown naval asset in the Scatter, or prepare a tactical assessment (provides advantage on the next navigation check or ship-to-ship encounter involving the target).

*Passive:* While the *Sovereign* is in a region, all Crown naval assets in that region treat the Captain role as filled by a skilled officer. Hostile captains within visual range must make DC 14 Wisdom save at the start of each encounter or start shaken (disadvantage on attacks until they succeed).

### Battle Surgeon's Deck *(Special — 2 space units)*

Full surgical deck on the orlop level, below the waterline. Two operating tables, mass-casualty medicine cabinet, amputation kit, ten-cot recovery bay. Hirelings: **Ship's Surgeon** + **Surgeon's Mate** (double-role: Cook on crew roster).

*Active:* Once per Bastion Turn — emergency surgery (stabilise + remove one exhaustion level), produce three Potions of Healing, or treat disease/poison in up to four crew simultaneously.

*Passive:* On a short rest aboard, each PC rolls Hit Dice twice and takes the higher result. On a long rest aboard after combat, each PC recovers one additional Hit Die.

---

## Layout

**Spar Deck** — Wheel and compass aft. Signal station. Two heavy carronades at quarterdeck, two at forecastle. Eight 12-lb guns per side amidships. Admiral's War Room full stern deckhouse.

**Upper Gun Deck** — Fifteen 12-lb guns per side. Officers' quarters aft with flag captain's anteroom. Marine barracks and armoury forward.

**Main Gun Deck** — Fourteen 24-lb guns per side. Primary fighting deck. Lower ports sealed in heavy weather.

**Lower Gun Deck** — Fifteen 32-lb guns per side. Heaviest weight of shot in the fleet. Grand Magazine directly below. Ports sealed except in calm water or harbour.

**Orlop Deck** — No guns. Battle Surgeon's Deck forward. Carpenter's stores, chain locker, bosun's supplies.

**Hold** — 100 tons cargo; typically stores for extended deep-water operations.

---

## Tactical Notes

The *Sovereign* does not chase. It presents a broadside and lets the other vessel decide. Against anything Tier 3 or below, a single full broadside from the lower gun deck ends the engagement. Its answer to shallow water, fast pursuit, and fire ships is: avoid them. A competent enemy uses those three things against it.
