# Uncertainty — DM Guide

Companion to [[hcs-surety-owners-manual|the Owner's Manual]]. The Manual tells players what to roll; this tells you what happens when they do.

The ship is now sailing as [[uncertainty|the Uncertainty]] — private registry, Crown markings removed, La Vasca refit complete. The Crown recognition clock is active. See below.

---

## Navigation Failures

Players roll **Intelligence (Navigator's Tools)** against a DC you set. On a failure, delay the voyage by **1d4 days** and introduce a complication scaled to the waters:

| Waters | Complication Ideas |
|---|---|
| Charted, calm (DC 10) | Minor course deviation. Bad weather front adds a day. Missed a supply stop. |
| Unfamiliar, reef approaches (DC 14) | Grounded on a sandbar (Carpenter's DC 14 to free, half-day lost). Hostile vessel spotted. A port the party intended to bypass gets threaded too close — awkward questions. |
| Maw approaches, active storm (DC 18) | Separated from landmarks in fog for 1d4 days. Emergency hull damage (**2d10**). A crew member overboard (DC 13 Athletics or lost). The compass starts behaving strangely even after the Maw. |

Don't use the same complication twice in a row. Failures in charted waters should feel inconvenient; failures near the Maw should feel dangerous.

**Crown charts and advantage.** The *Uncertainty*'s chart set covers the Central Strait and Crown Islands — Admiralty markings scraped, Calveno notation overlaid. The coverage is real and grants advantage in those waters. Midchain charts are contradictory; grant no advantage and feel free to introduce complications even on a success if the charts are the source of the route.

**Shallow draft.** The helmsman has advantage on Dexterity checks to navigate reef channels and shallow coastal passages. This is a real operational edge — Crown patrol cutters drawing 8 ft cannot follow into 4 ft of water.

---

## Chase Complications

Chases use range bands (Boarding / Cannon / Distant). Two rounds at Distant = quarry escapes. Call one complication per chase, at a dramatically appropriate moment.

| Complication Type | Check Called | Failure Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fog bank | **DC 14 Perception** (Navigator or lookout) | Both ships move to Distant regardless of speed this round; quarry may escape |
| Reef channel | **DC 14 Intelligence (Navigator's Tools)** | Pursuing ship's speed drops one band for **1d4** rounds |
| Wind shift | **DC 12 Dexterity (Bosun)** | Pursuing ship loses one band of movement this round |
| Shallow draft warning | **DC 14 Intelligence (Navigator's Tools)** | Larger vessel runs aground; pursuit ends or continues by jolly boat |

**Ram in a chase.** If the party is pursuing and reaches Boarding range, the helmsman can use the Ram action instead of standard maneuvering. Fleeing vessels at Boarding range take 2d10 (party takes half); DC 13 Strength save or pushed 15 ft and next turn's movement halved. Dramatically effective against slower targets; risky against vessels of equal speed.

---

## Crew Casualties

When Hull Integrity crosses these thresholds during combat, roll for crew losses. Each threshold fires once per engagement.

| Hull Integrity Remaining | Roll |
|---|---|
| First time below 97 HP | 1 NPC crew member incapacitated |
| First time below 65 HP | **1d4** NPC crew incapacitated |
| First time below 33 HP | **2d4** NPC crew incapacitated or killed |

*Thresholds scaled to 130 HP.*

**PCs are never on the casualty table.** They take damage from specific attacks only.

**Announcing casualties.** Name the ones who go down. If a named NPC crew member is involved, pull from the muster. If a specific hireling fills a role, a casualty can take that role offline mid-fight.

**Minimum complement impact.** If casualties drop the vessel below 4 crew, all ship checks go to disadvantage and speed drops 20%. If a specific role goes unfilled mid-combat (Gunner down), the no-Gunner rule applies immediately.

---

## Bastion — Facility Events

When a facility is assigned **Maintain**, roll a Facility Event.

| Roll (d6) | Shipboard Event |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Hostile contact.** A vessel has been tracking the *Uncertainty*. Run as an encounter or surface at a dramatically appropriate moment. |
| 2 | **Beneficial contact.** A passing ship offers trade, intelligence, or an unexpected opportunity. |
| 3 | **Facility damage.** A storm or rough seas damage one facility. Repair requires a Carpenter's check and one day. |
| 4 | **Windfall.** Favourable current — voyage shortened by **1d4** days. |
| 5 | **Hireling issue.** A crew member has a matter requiring officer attention — dispute, health issue, demand for back pay, a rumour they want to act on. |
| 6 | **Clear sailing.** No event this week. |

---

## Bastion — Defence of the Vessel

When the Officer Complement is absent and a hostile action event occurs, resolve it with dice.

Roll **6d6**. Each result of **1** kills one Defender. If all Defenders are lost, one facility (your choice — pick the most narratively interesting) goes dormant for the following week.

| Vessel Condition | Defence Modifier |
|---|---|
| Officer Complement aboard | Don't roll — play it out |
| Vessel in port, complement absent | Standard 2024 bastion defence |
| Underway, full experienced crew | +3 to each die (results of 1–3 don't kill) |
| Underway, skeleton crew | No modifier |
| Underway, below minimum complement | −1 to each die (results of 1–2 kill) |

The Weapons Locker upgrades Defender dice from **d6 to d8** while stocked.

**Keeping Defenders stocked.** A single Recruit order fills up to 12 Defenders. Don't let the party forget this — it's cheap insurance.

## Crown Registration — Timeline (NOW ACTIVE)

The *Uncertainty* was registered as HCS Surety, active Crown patrol vessel out of [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]], under Lieutenant B. Rook. The ship has been missing since Session 01. The refit at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] completed approximately when Session 03 ended. **The clock is running.**

- **Weeks 1–2:** No action. Patrol cutters sometimes run long without check-in. *(Party is likely in this window.)*
- **Week 3:** Harbourmaster's Register flags the vessel as overdue. Query to nearest Crown waypoint.
- **Week 4–5:** Listed missing. Description circulated to Crown ports in the Eastern Crown Islands.
- **Week 6+:** If spotted operating under Crown colours — boarding and inspection authorised. If operating under different colours or no colours and identified by hull or crew — wanted vessel at Crown ports.

**The Calveno refit changes the clock:** the identity erasure (paint, name, registry plate, flags) handles port authority at a glance. It does not handle a Dravosi naval officer who has served on this class of vessel. A cutter's profile is distinctive.

**What slows the clock:**

- Operating far from Crown waters (Midchain, Outer Reach)
- No Crown colours flying (done — nothing flies)
- Avoiding Crown ports and inspection vessels

**What accelerates it:**

- Operating in the Central Strait or Crown Islands
- Delmar Fisk walking openly in Crown ports (he is already a known name; see [[surety-missing|Crown Search]])
- The vessel being spotted by anyone who served on the Eastern Islands patrol circuit

See [[kalowe-takowan|Ship Disguise — Kalowe]] for further identity options. See [[surety-missing|Surety — Crown Search]] for the active search situation.

## Running Notes

**When to abstract vs. play out.** Routine passages don't need navigation rolls. Call for one when the waters are actually dangerous or unfamiliar, when failure would be interesting, or when the party has made a choice that deserves a consequence.

**Ship combat pacing.** Ship combat works best when boarding is the goal. The *Uncertainty* at Tier 1 cannot absorb extended broadside exchange with anything larger than herself. Position enemies accordingly. If the party is taking a prize: chain shot to slow, grapeshot to suppress the deck, board. The ram opens an alternative — use it for dramatic moments, not every engagement.

**The ram telegraphs intent.** Anyone watching the approach sees the prow and knows what is coming. Use this — let NPCs react before contact. Some will scatter; some will brace; some will target the helmsman.

**Crew personalities.** Give at least two crew members names and a single trait. When casualties happen, name the ones who go down. [[sem-holst|Sem Holst]], [[old-faas|Old Faas]], and [[thunk|Mr. Thunk]] are already named — use them. Geoffrey Draves is an ex-Crown carpenter who chose the party; that choice can surface in interesting moments.

**Upkeep as pressure.** ~32 gp/week is a soft pressure tool. Miss a week — fine. Miss three — someone isn't getting paid and the party hears about it. The Provisions Store Harvest order can reduce this pressure if managed.

**The missing Cook and Surgeon.** The Surgeon's Berth is installed and stocked but locked behind a hireling. Alys Kuiper not returning from shore leave is a clean departure — no drama, no loose thread unless you build one. The Cook gap means no long-rest HP recovery bonus at sea until someone fills the role. 4 gp/week is the cheapest operational gap on the ship.

Uncertainty — DM Guide

Companion to the Owner’s Manual. The Manual tells players what to roll; this tells you what happens when they do.

The ship is now sailing as the Uncertainty — private registry, Crown markings removed, La Vasca refit complete. The Crown recognition clock is active. See below.

Navigation Failures

Players roll Intelligence (Navigator’s Tools) against a DC you set. On a failure, delay the voyage by 1d4 days and introduce a complication scaled to the waters:

WatersComplication Ideas
Charted, calm (DC 10)Minor course deviation. Bad weather front adds a day. Missed a supply stop.
Unfamiliar, reef approaches (DC 14)Grounded on a sandbar (Carpenter’s DC 14 to free, half-day lost). Hostile vessel spotted. A port the party intended to bypass gets threaded too close — awkward questions.
Maw approaches, active storm (DC 18)Separated from landmarks in fog for 1d4 days. Emergency hull damage (2d10). A crew member overboard (DC 13 Athletics or lost). The compass starts behaving strangely even after the Maw.

Don’t use the same complication twice in a row. Failures in charted waters should feel inconvenient; failures near the Maw should feel dangerous.

Crown charts and advantage. The Uncertainty’s chart set covers the Central Strait and Crown Islands — Admiralty markings scraped, Calveno notation overlaid. The coverage is real and grants advantage in those waters. Midchain charts are contradictory; grant no advantage and feel free to introduce complications even on a success if the charts are the source of the route.

Shallow draft. The helmsman has advantage on Dexterity checks to navigate reef channels and shallow coastal passages. This is a real operational edge — Crown patrol cutters drawing 8 ft cannot follow into 4 ft of water.

Chase Complications

Chases use range bands (Boarding / Cannon / Distant). Two rounds at Distant = quarry escapes. Call one complication per chase, at a dramatically appropriate moment.

Complication TypeCheck CalledFailure Result
Fog bankDC 14 Perception (Navigator or lookout)Both ships move to Distant regardless of speed this round; quarry may escape
Reef channelDC 14 Intelligence (Navigator’s Tools)Pursuing ship’s speed drops one band for 1d4 rounds
Wind shiftDC 12 Dexterity (Bosun)Pursuing ship loses one band of movement this round
Shallow draft warningDC 14 Intelligence (Navigator’s Tools)Larger vessel runs aground; pursuit ends or continues by jolly boat

Ram in a chase. If the party is pursuing and reaches Boarding range, the helmsman can use the Ram action instead of standard maneuvering. Fleeing vessels at Boarding range take 2d10 (party takes half); DC 13 Strength save or pushed 15 ft and next turn’s movement halved. Dramatically effective against slower targets; risky against vessels of equal speed.

Crew Casualties

When Hull Integrity crosses these thresholds during combat, roll for crew losses. Each threshold fires once per engagement.

Hull Integrity RemainingRoll
First time below 97 HP1 NPC crew member incapacitated
First time below 65 HP1d4 NPC crew incapacitated
First time below 33 HP2d4 NPC crew incapacitated or killed

Thresholds scaled to 130 HP.

PCs are never on the casualty table. They take damage from specific attacks only.

Announcing casualties. Name the ones who go down. If a named NPC crew member is involved, pull from the muster. If a specific hireling fills a role, a casualty can take that role offline mid-fight.

Minimum complement impact. If casualties drop the vessel below 4 crew, all ship checks go to disadvantage and speed drops 20%. If a specific role goes unfilled mid-combat (Gunner down), the no-Gunner rule applies immediately.

Bastion — Facility Events

When a facility is assigned Maintain, roll a Facility Event.

Roll (d6)Shipboard Event
1Hostile contact. A vessel has been tracking the Uncertainty. Run as an encounter or surface at a dramatically appropriate moment.
2Beneficial contact. A passing ship offers trade, intelligence, or an unexpected opportunity.
3Facility damage. A storm or rough seas damage one facility. Repair requires a Carpenter’s check and one day.
4Windfall. Favourable current — voyage shortened by 1d4 days.
5Hireling issue. A crew member has a matter requiring officer attention — dispute, health issue, demand for back pay, a rumour they want to act on.
6Clear sailing. No event this week.

Bastion — Defence of the Vessel

When the Officer Complement is absent and a hostile action event occurs, resolve it with dice.

Roll 6d6. Each result of 1 kills one Defender. If all Defenders are lost, one facility (your choice — pick the most narratively interesting) goes dormant for the following week.

Vessel ConditionDefence Modifier
Officer Complement aboardDon’t roll — play it out
Vessel in port, complement absentStandard 2024 bastion defence
Underway, full experienced crew+3 to each die (results of 1–3 don’t kill)
Underway, skeleton crewNo modifier
Underway, below minimum complement−1 to each die (results of 1–2 kill)

The Weapons Locker upgrades Defender dice from d6 to d8 while stocked.

Keeping Defenders stocked. A single Recruit order fills up to 12 Defenders. Don’t let the party forget this — it’s cheap insurance.

Crown Registration — Timeline (NOW ACTIVE)

The Uncertainty was registered as HCS Surety, active Crown patrol vessel out of Port Tidefall, under Lieutenant B. Rook. The ship has been missing since Session 01. The refit at La Vasca completed approximately when Session 03 ended. The clock is running.

  • Weeks 1–2: No action. Patrol cutters sometimes run long without check-in. (Party is likely in this window.)
  • Week 3: Harbourmaster’s Register flags the vessel as overdue. Query to nearest Crown waypoint.
  • Week 4–5: Listed missing. Description circulated to Crown ports in the Eastern Crown Islands.
  • Week 6+: If spotted operating under Crown colours — boarding and inspection authorised. If operating under different colours or no colours and identified by hull or crew — wanted vessel at Crown ports.

The Calveno refit changes the clock: the identity erasure (paint, name, registry plate, flags) handles port authority at a glance. It does not handle a Dravosi naval officer who has served on this class of vessel. A cutter’s profile is distinctive.

What slows the clock:

  • Operating far from Crown waters (Midchain, Outer Reach)
  • No Crown colours flying (done — nothing flies)
  • Avoiding Crown ports and inspection vessels

What accelerates it:

  • Operating in the Central Strait or Crown Islands
  • Delmar Fisk walking openly in Crown ports (he is already a known name; see Crown Search)
  • The vessel being spotted by anyone who served on the Eastern Islands patrol circuit

See Ship Disguise — Kalowe for further identity options. See Surety — Crown Search for the active search situation.

**Private Vessel *UNCERTAINTY***

## Article I — Vessel Particulars

The *[[uncertainty|Uncertainty]]* is a Tier 1 patrol cutter, refitted for private independent operation. Her two cannon are sufficient to discourage uncooperative traffic and adequate for boarding-range combat. She is fast, draws little water, and carries a ram bow fitted at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]]. She may be taken through reef passages and canal approaches that would strand anything larger — including the Crown vessels she was built alongside.

### Vessel Statistics

| Particulars | Specification |
|---|---|
| **Classification** | Patrol cutter, Tier 1 (private) |
| **Hull Integrity** | 130 points |
| **Hull AC** | 11 (13 against head-on strikes) |
| **Rate of Passage — favourable wind** | 70 miles/day |
| **Rate of Passage — poor wind** | 30 miles/day |
| **Rate of Passage — calm, oars deployed** | 15 miles/day |
| **Minimum Draft** | 4 ft (standard cutter: ~8 ft) |
| **Crew Complement — minimum / full** | 4 / 10 |
| **Cargo Capacity** | 15 tons |
| **Ordnance** | 2 × 6-lb cannon (port and starboard); 2 × swivel gun (bow, stern); Ram |
| **Weekly Upkeep** | ~32 gp |
| **Condition** | Pristine |

**On Hull Integrity and Armour Class.** Hull Integrity functions as hit points. When it reaches zero, the vessel is sinking. Hull AC represents the difficulty of landing a meaningful strike against a ship-scale target. The forward hull has AC 13 against head-on strikes only — the reinforced bow from the ram fitting.

**On Repairs.** At-sea repair requires a skilled Carpenter aboard. During a short rest, the Carpenter makes an **Intelligence (Carpenter's Tools) DC 15** check; on a success, the vessel recovers **2d8 + proficiency bonus** Hull Integrity. Mending Resin (2 doses in the carpenter's locker) can repair **2d8 Hull HP over 8 hours** without a roll; this does not repair structural damage. In port, repairs run 1 gp per Hull Point at 25 Hull Points per workday.

---

## Article II — Special Modifications

### Ram Bow

The forward hull has been rebuilt with doubled planking, iron-pin cross-bracing, and an iron-capped ram plate.

**Ram Attack.** Helmsman's action. The ship must move at least 20 feet in a straight line before the strike. Both ships take **2d10 bludgeoning damage**; the *Uncertainty* takes half (rounded down) due to the reinforced bow. A target of Tier 1 or smaller must succeed on a **DC 13 Strength save** or be pushed 15 feet and have its next turn's movement halved.

The ram is not subtle. Anyone watching the approach sees the intent before contact.

### Shallow Draft

The keel depth has been reduced by 18 inches.

**Shallow Draft.** The *Uncertainty* can operate in water as shallow as **4 feet** (standard patrol cutter minimum: ~8 ft). This opens river mouths, tidal flats, lagoon approaches, and Calveno's inner canal network. The helmsman has **advantage** on Dexterity checks to navigate reef channels and shallow coastal passages. **Trade-off:** Speed in poor wind is 30 miles/day instead of 35.

---

## Article III — Deck Arrangement

**Weather Deck.** Open upper deck. Bow swivel gun with 360° arc. Two 6-lb cannon amidships, one per side. Ram plate at the waterline forward. Quarterdeck is raised two feet at the stern; attacks from it against deck-level targets have advantage, and ascending costs an additional five feet of movement. Rigging may be climbed with a **DC 10 Athletics** check as an action. The mainmast boom may be swung as an improvised weapon (**DC 12 Strength** check): **DC 13 Dexterity** save or 1d8 bludgeoning and pushed ten feet.

**Gun Deck.** Interior living space, ~6'4" overhead. Crew quarters forward, galley hatch, Weapons Locker amidships, chart table, Surgeon's Berth, crew mess aft. The Weapons Locker may be accessed as a bonus action. Signal lantern partner unit stowed near the chart table.

**Hold.** Galley (cast-iron stove) directly below crew mess, connected by iron ladder. Provisions Store occupying the former brig space. Powder magazine aft.

Full deck-by-deck dimensions and tactical notes: [[hcs-surety-layout|Deck Layouts]].

## Article IV — Ship's Company

Each role below must be filled for the vessel to operate at standard. A role may be filled by a crew member or a hired professional. An unfilled role cannot perform its function or does so at disadvantage.

**On minimum complement.** The *Uncertainty* requires a minimum of four souls to operate. Below that number, all ship-related checks are made with disadvantage and rate of passage is reduced by twenty percent.

### Roles and Rates of Pay

| Role | Function | Key Ability | Rate | Actions While in Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Captain** | Strategic command — where to sail, what to target, when to fight or run. Final authority in action. | Charisma | — | **Action:** *Rallying Order* — one creature within 60 ft gains advantage on their next check or attack before the start of your next turn. |
| **Quartermaster** | Crew welfare, discipline, stores management, internal order. Senior to the Bosun. | Charisma | 10 gp/wk | **Action:** *Crew's Voice* — one ally rerolls any failed check, attack, or save. **Reaction:** *Fair Witness* — crew member within 60 ft rolls death save or Frightened save with advantage. |
| **Navigator** | Course-plotting, reef avoidance, Maw crossing | Intelligence (Navigator's Tools) | 10 gp/wk | **Action:** Navigation check (see Article V). **Reaction:** *Hazard Warning* — declare before a navigation check; vessel rolls with advantage. |
| **Bosun** | Rigging, sails, deck crew management | Str or Dex | 8 gp/wk | **Action:** *Trim Sails* — DC 10 Dex; success grants helmsman one extra band this turn. **Reaction:** *Brace!* — one creature aboard halves damage from a ram or collision. |
| **Gunner** | Ordnance direction and maintenance | Dexterity | 8 gp/wk | **Action:** Salvo, Aimed Shot, or Reload (see Article VII). |
| **Carpenter** | Hull repair, damage control | Intelligence (Carpenter's Tools) | 6 gp/wk | **Action:** Emergency Repair (Article I). **Bonus Action:** *Plug the Breach* — DC 10 Int (Carpenter's Tools); success stops fire spread for one round. |
| **Cook** | Provisions management and crew sustenance | Wisdom | 4 gp/wk | No combat action. Each crew member recovers an additional **1d6 HP** on a long rest. |
| **Surgeon** | Treatment of wounds and casualties | Wisdom (Medicine) | 8 gp/wk | **Action:** Stabilize one incapacitated creature (DC 10 Wis/Medicine) or restore **1d6 + 4 HP** (expends one Healer's Kit use). **Bonus Action:** *Field Triage* — DC 10 Wis (Medicine); success gives one creature advantage on their next death save. |
| **Marine** | Boarding actions, armed watch, vessel security | Str or Dex | 14 gp/wk | **Action:** Attack, Grapple, or Shove. **Bonus Action:** *Hold the Rail* — one boarding enemy makes DC 13 Athletics or is shoved back. |
| **Ordinary Sailor** | All other duties | — | 2 gp/wk | **Action:** Help — grant one creature advantage on their next check or attack this round. |

**Required always:** Captain, Bosun.
**Required for open-water passages:** Navigator.
**Required when ordnance is employed:** Gunner.
**Required for at-sea repair:** Carpenter.
**Required on voyages exceeding three days:** Cook.
**Required to operate the Surgeon's Berth:** Surgeon.
**Required for boarding operations:** Marine.

**Current gaps:** Navigator (partially covered by Crissdalynn on known routes), Cook, Surgeon. [[oleandro-fuschi|Oleandro]] at Ponte Bassa can direct you to available crew in Calveno.

## Article VI — Passage and Navigation

| Conditions | DC |

| Familiar or charted waters, clear weather | 10 |
| Unfamiliar waters, reef approaches, poor visibility | 14 |
| Maw approaches, active storm, uncharted shallows | 18 |

On a success, the passage proceeds without incident. On a failure, the voyage is delayed and complications arise. The *Uncertainty*'s navigational chart set covers the Crown Islands and Central Strait — coverage is good. Within five miles of the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]], standard compasses fail; celestial navigation remains unaffected.

**Shallow draft advantage.** The helmsman has advantage on Dexterity checks to navigate reef channels and shallow coastal passages.

**On long rests at sea.** Standard rules apply. If the Cook role is filled, each character recovers an additional **1d6 HP**. If a storm strikes during the rest period, each character makes a **DC 12 Constitution** save; failure means the rest confers no benefit.

## Article VII — Action Against Hostile Vessels

Ships act in initiative order as creatures do.

### Range Bands

| Band | Description | What's Possible |
|---|---|---|
| **Boarding** | Ships alongside, locked, or grappled | Crew can board. Cannon hit automatically — no attack roll. Swivels effective. |
| **Cannon** | Standard engagement distance | Normal cannon fire. Swivels cannot reach. |
| **Distant** | Extreme range | Cannon fire at disadvantage. Swivels cannot reach. |

The helmsman uses their **Action** to move the vessel one band. Dash moves an additional band. When both vessels have been Distant for two consecutive rounds, the quarry escapes.

### Ramming

Helmsman's action at Boarding range (see Article II — Ram Bow for full mechanics). Both vessels halt upon impact; the ramming vessel may not use the Helm action until the start of its next turn.

### Ordnance Statistics

| Ordnance | Damage | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 6-lb cannon | d8 hull damage | Effective at Cannon and Boarding range |
| Swivel gun | d6 crew damage | Boarding range only; cannot damage hull |

Attack roll: **Dexterity + proficiency** vs. target Hull AC. Hit: roll damage. Miss: half damage. Critical hit: maximum damage.

### Gunner's Actions

**Salvo.** All guns bearing on the target fire simultaneously. One attack roll vs. Hull AC. Hit: full damage from all guns on that side. Miss: half damage. All fired guns must reload before the next Salvo.

**Aimed Shot.** One gun at −2 to the attack roll. On a hit, the targeted component is disabled rather than dealing standard hull damage. That gun must reload before firing again.

**Reload — All Guns.** All guns reload in parallel. No attack is made this round.

### Shot Types

| Shot Type | Effect — Hit | Effect — Miss | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Round Shot** | Full hull damage | Half hull damage | Standard; always available |
| **Chain Shot** | Speed drops one band. Three reductions = dead in the water. | Half reduction | Use to slow a fleeing vessel or set up boarding |
| **Grapeshot** | All exposed deck crew: DC 14 Dex or incapacitated; PCs take 2d6 (save halves) | PCs save with advantage | Boarding range only; cannot damage hull |

Any PC aware of incoming grapeshot may drop below deck as a Reaction before it lands.

## Article VIII — Ship's Facilities and Weekly Management

Each week, the Officer Complement conducts a **Facility Review**. All special facilities are assigned an order.

| Facility | Status | Function |
|---|---|---|
| **Weapons Locker** | Commissioned | Upgrades defender dice from d6 to d8 while stocked. Trade order: buy or sell arms at volume. |
| **Surgeon's Berth** | Commissioned (needs Surgeon hireling) | Once per weekly review: stabilize all incapacitated crew; remove one disease or poison over eight hours; or cast *Lesser Restoration* without expending a spell slot. |
| **Provisions Store** | Commissioned | Harvest order: produces rations, Healer's Kits, Healing Potions, or antitoxin each week. |
| **Chart Archive** | — | *Upgrade option.* Replaces Provisions Store if installed. Research order: yields three pieces of intelligence. |

### Weekly Facility Orders

| Order | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Craft** | Produce items or magical items permitted by the facility. |
| **Empower** | Trigger the facility's active operational effect. |
| **Harvest** | Collect facility outputs — potions, rations, poisons, materials. |
| **Maintain** | No directed activity. A facility event may occur. |
| **Recruit** | Engage hirelings, Defenders, or specialist personnel. |
| **Research** | Gather intelligence, lore, or item identification. |
| **Trade** | Generate income via commerce. |

Any facility that goes three consecutive weeks without orders goes dormant — hirelings have found other employment. Reactivating a dormant facility costs 100 gp and one week in port.

### On Defenders

Defenders are the vessel's hired security — enlisted via a Recruit order to the Crew Berths. They absorb hostile action events when the Officer Complement is absent. A single Recruit order enlists up to twelve. Keep them recruited.

## Article IX — Vessel Standing and Port Records

The *Uncertainty* carries no flag and no identifiable marking. She reads as a private working coastal vessel at a glance. She does not read that way to a Dravosi naval officer who has served on this class of vessel.

| Standing | Practical Effect |
|---|---|
| **Respected** | Reduced berthing fees; willing hirelings; faction contacts accessible. |
| **Known** | Treated according to actual conduct. Neutral default. |
| **Wanted** | Port access restricted or denied; bounties registered. |
| **Notorious** | Capable crew seek the vessel out; some quarries surrender rather than engage. |

The *Uncertainty*'s prior Crown registration is an active liability. See [[hcs-surety-dm-guide|DM Guide]] for the Crown recognition timeline.

# HCS Warrant

> [!read-aloud]
> A Crown brigantine comes on under full sail, naval grey from waterline to rail, the white stripe catching the light in a way the patrol cutters never quite manage at this distance. Twelve gun ports run down each side, six per beam, and the brass registry plate at the bow is large enough to read before she's within hailing range. A rating officer is already at the rail with a speaking trumpet. The Crown pennant at the masthead isn't moving — she's coming downwind and making you feel it. Whatever she is, she isn't asking.

---

## Current State

The *HCS Warrant* is the Crown's primary enforcement brigantine on the [[central-strait|Central Strait]] western patrol route, crewed from Harwick and working the approaches to [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]]. She is larger and better armed than either of Tidefall's patrol cutters and operates under a different mandate: where the cutters run waypoints and board small traders, the *Warrant* compels compliance from vessels the cutters couldn't safely challenge alone.

[[commander-gideon-ault|Commander Gideon Ault]] commands under sealed Admiralty orders. His commission authority includes vessel detention, cargo seizure, crew arrest, and the authority to issue provisional privateer letters to vessels assisting in enforcement actions.

## Layout

**Weather Deck** — Helm and binnacle aft, belfry and capstan amidships. Swivel guns cover bow and stern. Twelve cannon below with hinged covers. Crown pennant at masthead in all conditions underway.

**Captain's Cabin and Officers** — Full-width stern cabin; captain's chart table, commission papers, and a lockable iron Captain's Locker (DC 18). Three-cabin officer suite forward. Rating officer's writing desk amidships where inspection paperwork is drafted and sealed.

**Crew Quarters** — Twenty hammock berths forward lower deck. Working galley with copper range amidships.

**Below the Waterline** — Magazine aft (two keys: Ault and sealed at Harwick Admiralty). Inspection bond store (seized cargo pending determination). Prisoner hold with iron grating and six individual cages.

## Crew

24 ratings from Harwick's naval pool. Three Patrol-Lieutenant watch officers. Warrant gunner, warrant carpenter. Two rating inspectors — specifically trained in cargo inspection and manifest verification — who board alongside the armed party during enforcement actions.

**Enforcement posture:** The *Warrant* positions before hailing — comes downwind and close before any communication is attempted. A vessel that sees twelve gun ports and a rating officer with a speaking trumpet has already made its calculation.

**Privateer letters:** Ault can issue on his own commission authority, recorded in Harwick's admiralty ledger on the next resupply.

**Prize posture:** Detaining the *Warrant* is noticed within a week at Harwick. The Admiralty's response is a sealed order to every Crown vessel in the Strait.

# Ironmantle

A Valcoran-built remnant sloop, single-masted, its hull plated with iron below the waterline. The iron sits visibly heavy in the water, dark and surface-corroded where it emerges at the waterline, running into cleaner metal below. The timber hull above is old. The join between iron and wood is uneven in a way that no current shipwright would produce. Four iron-tipped sweep oars rack along the inner hull. In choppy water, the hull makes a low resonance that carries up through the deck planking.

## Current State

**Hull:** Worn. Iron plating below waterline intact but shows significant surface corrosion. Timber frame beneath is sound. Repairs to the iron require Valcoran methods no current carpenter knows — standard repairs apply to the timber; iron sections are treated with pitch and rust inhibitor (included in upkeep, effective but not permanent).

**Below Decks:** Small stern cabin, iron-braced walls. Lockable. Fits one occupant. Five hammock hooks forward in a low-ceilinged space. The iron ribbing makes below-decks cramped and loud underway. Minimal hold — iron framing eats cargo space significantly. No galley.

**Identifying features:** Iron plating visible when she heels. Immediately recognisable to anyone who knows Valcoran construction. Distinctive low resonance in choppy water.

## Strengths and Weaknesses

**Strengths:**

- Highest HP and AC of any Tier 1 vessel. Absorbs punishment that would sink a standard sloop.
- Gun mounts more stable in rough weather — no accuracy penalty.
- The iron construction is a psychological deterrent.

**Weaknesses:**

- Speed. Slowest Tier 1 in standard conditions.
- Maneuverability. Does not respond quickly.
- Maintenance. 40 gp/week upkeep is nearly double a standard sloop.
- Structural modification requires ironworking tools.

## Bastion Notes

**Available space:** 4 units. Nothing installed. Iron bracing throughout makes structural modifications difficult. A Carpenter's Shop (1 unit) can be installed in the hold space without ironwork. All other facilities requiring dedicated rooms need a specialist.

A Tier 1 armed pirate cutter built for ambush, boarding, and reef-channel escapes — dangerous against soft prizes, but too small to trade broadsides with real naval power.

# The *Knife's Wake*

> [!read-aloud]
> A low cutter comes on with patched tan canvas and a tired brown hull, the kind of working boat that should smell of fish and wet rope. Then the gunports open. Black-painted teeth show along the rail, boarding hooks come up from behind the bulwark, and the false trade pennant drops before the real flag rises: a narrow black streamer cut like a knife wound.

---

## Overview

The *Knife's Wake* is a Tier 1 pirate cutter built for ambush, intimidation, and clean withdrawal rather than honest freight or naval battle. She passes at distance as a worn coastal trader. Up close, the disguise fails on purpose — her gunports are too well-cut, her rail too clear of clutter, and her deck crew too ready to move.

She is a small-water predator. In reef channels, fog, harbour approaches, and the last hour before dusk, the *Knife's Wake* is exactly the wrong ship to let come alongside. In open water against a Crown patrol vessel or a properly crewed brigantine, she runs.

## Purpose

The *Knife's Wake* takes small valuable prizes: payroll chests, passenger jewels, locked dispatch boxes, contraband, spell components, officers worth ransoming, and cargo whose owner cannot safely report the loss.

Her best attack is a short deception — approaches under false colours, fires one disabling volley, and boards before the other crew finds its discipline.

## Layout

**Weather Deck** — Kept clear for rapid boarding. Four light cannons sit amidships behind removable false cargo screens. Swivel positions at bow and stern. Boarding hooks and weighted lines stowed under the rail.

**Aft Cabin** — One narrow bunk, bolted chart shelf, locked strongbox, rack of false pennants. Real papers in oilcloth below a removable sole plank.

**Below Decks** — Cramped crew hammocks forward, powder and shot amidships, plunder cages aft.

## Operational Notes

**Ambush posture:** Prefers dusk, fog, port congestion, shoals, and damaged targets. First volley aims at sails, rudder, and morale.

**Weakness:** Cannot win a sustained gun duel. A disciplined patrol cutter that keeps distance and refuses the boarding angle has the advantage.

**Legal risk:** The hull is not registered cleanly, and several fittings likely came from ships whose owners still have friends in port offices.

# The *Loud Argument*

## Overview

A gun brig — the combat vessel of [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]]. Fifth ship of the fleet. Captained by [[bastian-crev|Bastian Crev]].

# Nimmik Vollask

> [!read-aloud]
> The ship is unmistakable before it is even close: a boxy two-masted brig painted the colour of a construction hazard, wide enough to look wrong on the water, tall enough that the freeboard seems like a design error. On both sides, in lettering two feet high, painted black against the orange hull, are two words in a script you don't recognise. They do not need translation. A cheerful figure waves from the rail — not a gnome, though gnomes are visible through every porthole and hatch opening and at least one appears to be dangling by a rope from the rigging with a clipboard.

---

## Overview

*Nimmik Vollask* is a Tier 2 cargo brig operated by a company of some sixty gnomish staff who live and work in a ship built to their scale. The decks, holds, passageways, and ladders are sized for gnomes. The hull, however, is not sized for anything in particular. It is sized for cargo. Anyone who reads Gnomish has not yet mentioned what the name translates to in mixed company.

The ship is wide, boxy, and tall for its class, with a centre of gravity that maritime engineers have described as "hypothetical." It teeters alarmingly at the slightest shift in wind or ballast, which it does on a rolling schedule as gnomes move between tasks below decks.

The service model is simple. Pull alongside — or flag the *Depot* down on the water, which it will accommodate — and find [[cotter-foss|Cotter Foss]] at the rail. Tell Cotter what you need. Pay Cotter. Accept complimentary coffee and a plate of gnomish meatballs, which are small, dense, and improbably good. Wait. Below decks, sixty gnomes locate, pack, wrap, and stage your order with a logistical efficiency that is difficult to reconcile with what the ship looks like from the outside. When ready, the bundle clears the hold hatch with a yell, sails across the gap, and lands in your hold. If it does not land in your hold, that is a missed shot, which Cotter will note in the log and apologise for in writing.

The *Nimmik Vollask* carries ship stores, chandlery goods, provisions, common alchemical supplies, rope, canvas, basic tools, and a rotating selection of mildly unusual items that gnome buyers have negotiated in bulk from sources Cotter does not fully understand but has stopped questioning.

---

## Layout

**Weather deck** — scaled to gnomes, so roughly shin-height railings by human measure. Hatch covers, coil-rope staging areas, and two cargo cranes (gnome-operated, surprisingly capable). The bundle-delivery yeet originates from the main cargo hatch. Cotter operates out of a small folding table near the starboard rail with a ledger, a coffee pot, and a stool.

**Between-decks (gnome scale)** — full working floor, 4.5 ft clearance. Gnome-width corridors, gnome-height berths, gnome-sized equipment. Non-gnomes who have been below report it as an experience they have not sought to repeat. The organisation is categorical and dense: rope by type and diameter, canvas by weight and bolt, provisions in labelled casks by date and content. The gnomes know where everything is at all times.

**Lower hold** — the deepest and largest space, entirely useless as standing room for anyone else. This is where bulk orders stage for delivery.

---

The gnomes do not have a single captain. They operate by rotating shift leads and an internal logistics committee whose decisions Cotter does not ask to understand. Cotter is the interface.

---

## History

The company was founded by the current gnomish staff collectively, under circumstances Cotter describes as "a business arrangement I was brought in to facilitate and have since become load-bearing for." The hull is clearly older than the interior fitout, and the orange paint is applied over at least two previous colours. The *Nimmik Vollask* has been operating the Central Strait circuit for approximately four years. It has never sunk, which the gnomes cite as evidence of competence and Cotter cites as evidence of luck and adequate ballast.

Delmar Fisk's flagship — a privateer-rigged brigantine that led five ships into the Drowned Maw and did not come back. Wreck sits at the Shelfworks eastern edge with the Pearl of Souls still aboard.

# The *Red Lady*

> [!read-aloud]
> A two-masted brigantine rides low in the water, her hull stained a deep, even red from waterline to rail. Seven cannon ports line each side beneath the gun deck, and swivel mounts sit at bow and stern. At the prow, a pale wooden figurehead of a cloaked woman leans forward with one hand open at her side. The ship is long, clean-lined, and built with the hard, practical look of a vessel meant to chase, fight, and keep going.

---

## Overview

A two-masted brigantine, built by the [[chain-council|Chain Council]], 96 feet on the waterline, privateer-rigged. The hull ran dark red from waterline to rail — not painted, stained deep into the wood, uniform and deliberate. The figurehead was a cloaked woman carved in pale wood, eyes forward, one hand open at her side. Two gun decks, seven cannon ports per side, swivel mounts fore and aft.

Built for extended independent operations: fast enough to disengage, armed enough to press, fitted for months without port resupply. She was in prime condition when she sank.

---

## Crew and Command

[[rael-corven|Rael Corven]] served as flag captain. [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] commanded as Admiral. [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]] served as navigator and crow for nearly two years.

Every new hand went through Rael's training program before touching a line in action. He knew every name aboard and built each sailor's duties around their specific capabilities. The ship's reputation as the best-run vessel in the fleet was not incidental — it was a direct result of how he ran it.

---

## The Sinking

Umberlee's retribution came as fog — thick enough to swallow the water from the deck, surrounding all five ships at once. A rogue trench opened in the fleet's path and drove them 80 feet down. The walls closed and swallowed the fleet whole.

Crissdalynn dove from the crow's nest, grabbed Fisk, and flew them clear. They heard Umberlee's laughter on the wind, then her rage, as the ships went under. The *Red Lady* went down with the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] still aboard.

The five ships lost: *Red Lady*, *[[the-narrow|The Narrow]]*, *[[heft|Heft]]*, *[[fernen|Fernen]]*, *[[loud-argument|Loud Argument]]*. Two survivors.

---

## Wreck

The *Red Lady* lies at the [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] eastern shelf descent, below [[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s domain boundary. The Pearl of Souls is aboard — the active attractor pulling entities through the Maw fissure. The Fleet Intelligence Room may contain records of who commissioned the Pearl theft.

[[rael-corven|Rael Corven]]'s Cloak of Useful Things went down with the ship — potentially recoverable on a deeper dive.

See [[pearl-of-souls|Maw Pearl Crisis]] for the full salvage situation.

A hard-used two-masted merchant brig captained by Beaumont Sel, working the Midchain cargo run — home port Kalowe.

# The Saltwright

> [!read-aloud]
> A two-masted merchant brig rides broad and low in the water, her hull worked pale grey-brown by years of salt and weather. Nothing about her is ornamental: no figurehead, no bright rail, no paint left where the sea could take it. Below, the smell is brine, old cedar, and the cold deep water pressing through the seams. Every timber sounds used.

A two-masted merchant brig out of [[kalowe|Kalowe]], built for trade rather than display. Old, plain, and thoroughly practical: a deep hold, a small captain's cabin, and no space wasted on comfort or prestige. [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] has captained her on the Midchain cargo run for eleven years.

## Current Status

Departed with [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] at dawn after Session 02. No longer the party's vessel — the party now commands the [[hcs-surety|Uncertainty]] (ex-HCS Surety). Beaumont's whereabouts since are not established.

## Layout

**Weather Deck.** Plain and unadorned — a working surface for sail handling and loading. The stern is covered: a low deckhouse aft of the mainmast shelters the captain's quarters beneath it.

**Captain's Quarters.** Set into the covered stern at weather deck level. Small and practical. Beaumont keeps a lockbox under the bed.

**Gun Deck.** Middle deck, below the weather deck. Gun ports are plugged against the sea. The forward section has been converted to crew's mess and additional storage. Two 12-pound guns remain aboard, dismounted and lashed down aft.

**Cargo Hold.** Lowest deck. Roughly six feet of headroom. Cargo stacked tight among barrels, crates, and sacks. Two lanterns hang amidships. A gap above the waterline in the aft corner lets in fresh air and a sliver of outside light.

The Saltwright

Read Aloud

A two-masted merchant brig rides broad and low in the water, her hull worked pale grey-brown by years of salt and weather. Nothing about her is ornamental: no figurehead, no bright rail, no paint left where the sea could take it. Below, the smell is brine, old cedar, and the cold deep water pressing through the seams. Every timber sounds used.

A two-masted merchant brig out of Kalowe, built for trade rather than display. Old, plain, and thoroughly practical: a deep hold, a small captain’s cabin, and no space wasted on comfort or prestige. Beaumont Sel has captained her on the Midchain cargo run for eleven years.

Current Status

Departed with Beaumont Sel at dawn after Session 02. No longer the party’s vessel — the party now commands the Uncertainty (ex-HCS Surety). Beaumont’s whereabouts since are not established.

Layout

Weather Deck. Plain and unadorned — a working surface for sail handling and loading. The stern is covered: a low deckhouse aft of the mainmast shelters the captain’s quarters beneath it.

Captain’s Quarters. Set into the covered stern at weather deck level. Small and practical. Beaumont keeps a lockbox under the bed.

Gun Deck. Middle deck, below the weather deck. Gun ports are plugged against the sea. The forward section has been converted to crew’s mess and additional storage. Two 12-pound guns remain aboard, dismounted and lashed down aft.

Cargo Hold. Lowest deck. Roughly six feet of headroom. Cargo stacked tight among barrels, crates, and sacks. Two lanterns hang amidships. A gap above the waterline in the aft corner lets in fresh air and a sliver of outside light.

# Tessarine Factor *Amberreach*

> [!read-aloud]
> The ship comes in low and wide, her pale grey hull sitting deep in the water with the deliberate weight of something built to carry rather than chase. The beam is broader than a brigantine has any business being, the freeboard heavy, and the cargo ports along her sides are sealed and numbered in neat stencilled figures. A Tessarine pennant flies at the masthead — not the Crown's military pennant, just the Concordat's registry mark rendered in cloth. There are gun ports, and they are open, and no one is particularly rushing toward them.

## Overview

A Tier 3 Tessarine cargo galleon on the fixed commercial schedule between [[calveno|Calveno]] and the western approaches through the Central Strait. She runs on a fixed schedule — departures logged three ports in advance, arrival windows insured through Tessarine underwriting, losses settled at ninety percent of assessed value within forty days. Merchants along the route do not need to like the Concordat. They need their cargo to arrive.

Senior Factor [[oriana-becht|Oriana Becht]] holds authority to sign instruments aboard in the field — credit extensions up to 2,000 gp, route underwriting renewals, salvage financing, and provisional letters of cargo obligation.

| **Speed (poor wind)** | 30 miles/day |

| **Upkeep** | ~350 gp/week |

## Layout (Summary)

**Weather Deck.** Cargo logistics focus: davits, winches, cargo booms. Tessarine pennant and factor's authority pennant both fly.

**Gun Deck / Factor Suite.** 16 cannon, widely spaced for cargo movement. Factor suite at stern: Becht's cabin (Captain's Locker DC 18), contract office, sealed correspondence.

**Crew/Passenger Deck.** 60 hammocks forward; galley; six private merchant passenger cabins aft.

**Hold.** Four sealed cargo compartments; numbered sealed manifests. One reserved for Tessarine bonded cargo with legally significant wax seals. Forward compartment is the sealed bond store.

## Commercial Posture

The *Amberreach* does not need to fire to compel compliance — she compels compliance by arriving on schedule. The gun ports are open as a reminder that the Concordat has not forgotten the world has pirates. She does not board; she is boarded, and survives it.

**The bonded compartment:** Sealed manifests are legally protected from Crown inspection under the commercial treaty between the Concordat and the Dravosi Admiralty. Both parties resent this. Neither has found a way to dissolve it.

# The *Bad Receipt*

> [!read-aloud]
> A two-masted schooner cuts low through the channel under patched cream canvas and a merchant pennant that looks correct until it matters. Her hull is black-green, stained like old ink, with removable brass registry plates bolted over older scars. When the side screens drop, cannon mouths show in a neat row beneath cargo netting, and the figurehead resolves into a carved clerk holding a ship's hook behind his back.

## Overview

The *Bad Receipt* is a Tier 2 armed pirate schooner built for [[midchain|Midchain]] work: false papers, quick pursuit, selective violence, and retreat through channels where Crown captains start arguing with their own charts. She was refitted at [[kalowe|Kalowe]] from a seized courier hull.

She is not a slaughter ship. Her captain wants cargo, letters of marque, ransomable officers, and anything whose owner cannot report the theft without explaining why it was aboard. The crew prefers a disabled rudder, a terrified deck, and a signed transfer under duress.

Below decks: crew hammocks, a chart table bolted to the forward bulkhead, and a shallow hold fitted with diving equipment and survey gear. Built to go places other ships couldn't and come back with information.

# The *Quorum*

> [!read-aloud]
> A single-masted cutter sits low at the Kalowe dock, hull tarred black to the rail with no livery and no figurehead. The waterline is copper-sheathed, the rigging is tight and spare, and a plain reef-pilot's pennant hangs from the mast. She looks like a working boat that has been given very good rope.

## Overview

A single-masted cutter, 48 feet on the waterline, built at the [[kalowe|Kalowe]] dry dock and kept by the [[chain-council|Chain Council]] as a dispatch vessel. No flag, no figurehead, no painted name — the *Quorum* is stenciled in small letters on the transom and nowhere else. Hull tarred black with a copper-sheathed waterline.

She moves what the Council cannot trust to ordinary couriers: sealed commission documents, vote records, draft proposals, representatives who need to arrive without announcing themselves. A Kalowe pilot on standing retainer navigates the back channels and reef passages that Dravosi patrol routes avoid.

The name is procedural. The Chain Council only has authority when enough affected representatives are present. The boat named *Quorum* is the Council's reminder that legitimacy is not a fixed thing.

## Stats

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | 1 (Speed-Built) |
| **Hull Points** | 80 |
| **Hull AC** | 11 |
| **Speed (good wind)** | 88 miles/day |
| **Speed (poor wind)** | 44 miles/day |
| **Speed (calm)** | 12 miles/day |
| **Maneuverability** | Excellent |
| **Crew (min/full)** | 2 / 8 |
| **Cargo** | 8 tons |
| **Gun Mounts** | 2 (swivel, rail-mounted) |
| **Upkeep** | ~30 gp/week |

## Layout

**Weather Deck.** Mast and boom forward, wheel aft. Two covered swivel mounts amidships. Working space is the whole deck.

**Stern Cabin.** Low-headroom compartment sealed with iron latches. Locked chest bolted to deck; fold-down chart table; two bench seats. Three people maximum. Not comfortable.

**Below Decks.** Shallow hold — water casks, lamp stores, sailcloth, rope. Crew hammocks slung forward. No galley.

# The *Tallow Bell*

> [!read-aloud]
> A small grey sloop moves toward the harbour mouth with its sail reefed neat and low, the canvas stained the colour of old candle smoke. No bright paint marks the hull. A bronze handbell hangs beneath the short bowsprit, dark with salt, and the stern rail is crowded with sealed oilcloth bundles, rope coils, and covered basins that smell faintly of brine and tallow.

## Overview

A Tier 1 Waveservant shrine sloop used to move clergy between working harbours. She carries priests, shrine attendants, tribute ledgers, candles, storm tokens, small sealed offerings, and ritual supplies.

The ship is deliberately plain. Salt-grey hull, smoke-stained sail, no carved figurehead, no faction pennant beyond a narrow grey streamer at the mast. The only ornament is the bronze bell under the bowsprit, rung once when departing a shrine harbour and once when entering another. Sailors know the sound. Most make room.

The *Tallow Bell* is neutral in the same way the [[waveservants|Waveservants]] are neutral: not kind, not warm, not uninvolved.

## Stats

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | 1 (Crew-Optimized) |
| **Hull Points** | 95 |
| **Hull AC** | 10 |
| **Speed (good wind)** | 70 miles/day |
| **Speed (poor wind)** | 35 miles/day |
| **Speed (calm)** | 15 miles/day with sweeps |
| **Crew (min/full)** | 3 / 8 |
| **Cargo** | 14 tons |
| **Gun Mounts** | 2 (swivel, usually covered) |
| **Upkeep** | ~32 gp/week |

## Operational Notes

**Neutral passage:** Most captains avoid interfering with Waveservant vessels — not out of affection. Robbing a shrine sloop means explaining to every harbour why the sea's collectors should still treat you normally.

**Defence:** Swivel guns for warning shots and discouraging desperate theft. The *Tallow Bell* does not win fights. She survives by being more trouble to harm than she is worth.

**At sea rites:** If a captain pays for an open-water blessing, the ship comes alongside, the basin is uncovered, terms are spoken, coin or token is accepted, and the bell rings once. The Waveservants do not linger.

**As a prize:** A bad idea — little money, many witnesses, and religious consequences.

**As a clue:** Her ledgers can point toward unpaid voyages, missing ships, or someone who paid tribute under a false name.

# Uncertainty

The bow carries a ram plate fitted flush with the waterline, iron-edged, and above it a carved hardwood figure: a woman mid-stride, hands empty, face forward. ## Overview

The *Uncertainty* is the former [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] — a Dravosi Crown patrol cutter taken as a prize in Session 01, damaged by a whip shark in Session 03, and fully refitted at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] under [[cobb|Cobb]]'s direction on [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]]'s account. All Crown identity has been removed. Repainted, renamed, fitted with a ramming prow, equipped with a new figurehead, and stocked for extended operation.

Nona's standing instruction: *the ship leaves La Vasca complete or it does not leave.* After her grandson nearly died on the last run, she is not interested in moderation.

She is fast for her size, nimble in reef passages, and can operate in four feet of water — shallower than any Crown vessel of her class. The ram is not subtle. Everything else is.

## Refit Modifications

### Identity Erasure

All Crown identity removed or destroyed:

- **Registry plate** cut and melted down at La Vasca
- **Stern board** re-carved: *Uncertainty* in Calveno Roman script
- **Paint** stripped and repainted: weathered brown-black, no markings, no waterline stripe
- **Pennant and signal flags** locked away below; nothing flies
- **Interior markings** scraped; Crown charts redrawn with Calveno notation

What cannot be fully hidden: the hull silhouette. A Crown cutter's profile is distinctive to anyone who served on this class. Paint and name handle port authority at a glance. They do not handle a Dravosi naval officer who knows what to look for. See [[hcs-surety-dm-guide|DM Guide]] for Crown recognition timeline.

### Ram Bow

Forward hull rebuilt with doubled planking, iron-pin cross-bracing, and an iron-capped ram plate running three feet along the keel.

> [!mechanic]
> **Ram Attack.** Helmsman's action. Ship must move 20+ feet in a straight line before the strike. Both ships take **2d10 bludgeoning**; *Uncertainty* takes half (reinforced bow). Tier 1 or smaller target: **DC 13 Strength save** or pushed 15 ft and next turn's movement halved. Forward hull has **AC 13** vs. head-on strikes only.

### Shallow Keel

Keel depth reduced by 18 inches — ballast redistributed, garboard strakes faired back.

> [!mechanic]
> **Shallow Draft.** Can operate in water as shallow as **4 feet** (standard cutter minimum: ~8 ft). Opens river mouths, tidal flats, lagoon approaches, and Calveno's inner canal network. Helmsman has **advantage** on Dex checks to navigate reef channels. Trade-off: Speed (poor wind) 30 miles/day instead of 35.

### Figurehead

Lost to the whip shark in Session 03. Replaced by a Le Paludi canal-ship carver on Nona's account. A woman, mid-stride, hands open at her sides. Calveno features. No expression of hope or fear. She is simply going. She is not named.

# The *Vestra*

![[The-Vestra.webp]]

> [!read-aloud]
> A small two-masted brig rides low in the water, old-built and hard-worked, her topsides painted a deep green that has been reapplied so many times it no longer matches from plank to plank. At the prow stands a rat figurehead with one hand extended, palm up. She is compact, practical, and clearly modified for a small crew travelling light.

## Overview

A small two-masted brig, older than most Midchain traffic, sized for a Rattkin captain and a light crew. Built and captained by Vincenzo Black-Jaw, who left her to the family when he died. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] re-rigged her and added two gun mounts before she was lost.

She wasn't just transportation. She was his contacts, his capital, his crew, and his working life.

## The Sinking

The *Vestra* went down too fast for anyone aboard to understand what was happening. Something struck the hull from below. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] survived. The rest of the crew are assumed dead.

## Session History

In Session 03, Perrin told [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] enough for her to understand there were no known survivors. She ordered consolation for the Vestra's crew and called off the attacks she had set in motion against Perrin.

Perrin does not know what destroyed the ship.

> [!dm]
> The [[leviathan|Leviathan]] destroyed the Vestra. Perrin survived because [[perrins-cloak-of-the-manta-ray|his Cloak of the Manta Ray]] kept him alive in the water; [[auralis|Auralis]] found and recovered him. Perrin does not know about Auralis's role — he believes the cloak alone saved him. The warlock pact formed in that moment without his awareness. A surviving crew member is a live pressure — if one appears, make the reunion useful and painful: relief first, then the cost of Perrin's silence.

The Vestra

Read Aloud

A small two-masted brig rides low in the water, old-built and hard-worked, her topsides painted a deep green that has been reapplied so many times it no longer matches from plank to plank. At the prow stands a rat figurehead with one hand extended, palm up. She is compact, practical, and clearly modified for a small crew travelling light.

Overview

A small two-masted brig, older than most Midchain traffic, sized for a Rattkin captain and a light crew. Built and captained by Vincenzo Black-Jaw, who left her to the family when he died. Perrin re-rigged her and added two gun mounts before she was lost.

She wasn’t just transportation. She was his contacts, his capital, his crew, and his working life.

The Sinking

The Vestra went down too fast for anyone aboard to understand what was happening. Something struck the hull from below. Perrin survived. The rest of the crew are assumed dead.

Session History

In Session 03, Perrin told Nona enough for her to understand there were no known survivors. She ordered consolation for the Vestra’s crew and called off the attacks she had set in motion against Perrin.

Perrin does not know what destroyed the ship.

DM Note

The Leviathan destroyed the Vestra. Perrin survived because his Cloak of the Manta Ray kept him alive in the water; Auralis found and recovered him. Perrin does not know about Auralis’s role — he believes the cloak alone saved him. The warlock pact formed in that moment without his awareness. A surviving crew member is a live pressure — if one appears, make the reunion useful and painful: relief first, then the cost of Perrin’s silence.

Connections

  • Perrin Black-Jaw — captain and last owner
  • Nona Black-Jaw — widow of its original captain Vincenzo
  • Leviathan — destroyed it
  • Keth-Naar — Perrin washed ashore here

A Grung Tier 1 war proa — a double-outrigger raiding vessel built from Verdant Teeth ironpillar hardwood, designed to beach on any shore and disembark a raiding party faster than the target can respond.

# *Vethka*

> [!read-aloud]
> Low on the water — lower than any cutter you have seen. The hull is carved from a single timber dark as heartwood, sealed with amber resin that catches the light like wet skin. Two outrigger floats ride the surface to port and starboard, lashed to the hull with braided vine cord. The bow is carved into a blunt open jaw, painted in purple and blue in alternating stripe-bands, and a line of small bones hangs from the prow to the first outrigger crossbeam. There is no wheel, no cabin, no raised deck. Twelve Grung can crouch below the rail without showing a silhouette. You smell resin first. Underneath that, something sour and sharp that is not the sea.

## Overview

*Vethka* is the Grung term for this class of vessel — not a proper name but a caste-designation: roughly, *the waterline that moves toward you*. Every raiding proa built to the standard pattern is called *vethka* by those who crew them.

The hull is single-piece ironpillar hardwood from the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], adze-worked by orange-caste artisans, sealed inside and out with boiled tree resin. The result does not absorb water, does not swell in rain, and sheds spray without effort. From more than half a mile away on a dark night, a *vethka* running low with no sail set reads as debris. This is by design.

## Caste and Crew

The *vethka* is a blue-and-purple operation. Blue-caste scouts navigate and pilot. Purple-caste warriors handle the assault. Orange-caste artisans build the vessel. The poison preparation bench — a narrow work surface sealed with flat resin, forward of amidships — is red-caste design. Purple-caste warriors touch it. No other caste does.

## Stats

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | 1 (Speed-Built) |
| **Hull Points** | 70 |
| **Hull AC** | 11 |
| **Maneuverability** | Excellent |
| **Profile** | Very Low |
| **Crew (min/full)** | 2 / 12 |
| **Cargo** | 2 tons |

## Tactical Profile

> [!dm]
> In reef country, a *vethka* cannot be caught by anything with a keel. Grung Standing Leap means the crew is over the rail before the bow stops moving. The double outrigger lets it handle reef passages that would shred deeper hulls. Its threat is surprise, speed, and the poison bench — not a gun fight.

## Connections

- [[grung-clans|Grung Clans]] — builders and operators
- [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] — source of ironpillar hardwood

Public FAQ for using the Shattered Sea campaign wiki, including where to start, how navigation-safety works, and how to use the wiki with a chatbot.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Where should I start?

Start with [[player-primer|The Shattered Sea Player Primer]]. It gives you the campaign tone, major geography, factions, character creation options, ship rules, and the kind of trouble the campaign expects.

After that, use [[campaign-overview|Campaign Overview]] as the dense reference page and [[shattered-sea|The Shattered Sea]] as the root navigation hub.

## Is this wiki safe for players?

Yes. This wiki is written for players. It covers common knowledge, onboarding material, published rules references, playable species, faction summaries, and setting lore.

Everything navigable on the public wiki is public and can be read. Nothing private is ever published. If you follow a link and get a 404, that is a spoiler boundary, not an error; the missing page simply is not public yet. This makes the whole wiki spoiler-safe.

## What should I read before Session Zero?

Read these:

1. [[player-primer|The Shattered Sea Player Primer]]
2. [[mortis|Mortis]]
3. [[ship-stats|Ship Stats]] (Optional)
4. [[ship-bastion|Ship Bastion]] (Optional)
5. Any homebrew species page you are considering from [[wiki/lore/species/index|Playable Species]]

You do not need to memorize the setting. You need a character with a reason to be aboard the *Saltwright*, a reason to cross dangerous water, and a problem that could follow them into port.

## What species can I play?

Standard 2024 species are available, plus the Shattered Sea options in [[wiki/lore/species/index|Playable Species]]:

- [[aarakocra|Aarakocra]]
- [[grung|Grung]]
- [[rattkin|Rattkin]]
- [[tabaxi|Tabaxi]]

For setting context, read the linked species page and any linked faction or lore pages.

## What campaign rules are different?

The main public rules references are:

- [[ship-stats|Ship Stats]] — ship tiers, crew, cargo, travel, weapons, upgrades, and upkeep.
- [[ship-bastion|Ship Bastion]] — the party ship as a shared mobile bastion.
- [[bastions|Bastions]] — 2024 Bastion rules reference.
- [[mortis|Mortis]] — death, consequence, and targeted benefits.

## How do I use this wiki with ChatGPT or another chatbot?

Paste this into your first message, or save it as project instructions:

```plain text
Use the public Shattered Sea campaign wiki as your source for campaign questions. Start from the public root page, follow public links as needed, and do not invent details for pages or links that are not available.
```

## Why does ChatGPT say it cannot find the wiki?

Usually one of these is happening:

- Instant mode is enabled.
- The model did not actually open the public wiki.
- The model cannot access remote URLs in that chat.
- The chat is using a lightweight mode that does not reliably follow retrieval instructions.
- The link you followed is intentionally unpublished, which appears as a 404.

If your chatbot cannot browse the public site, use the fallback context bundle.

## What does a 404 mean?

The page is not public. It may exist in the campaign notes, but it has not been published to the player-facing wiki. Treat the absence as part of the spoiler protection system.
