rules/subsystems

  • Bastions — 2024 rules for player-owned strongholds; characters gain a Bastion at level 5 and issue orders to its special facilities every 7 in-game days.
  • Carpenter’s Shop — Ship facility (Smithy Tier 1) that lets hirelings craft from Smith’s Tools or commission magic armaments at level 9+.
  • Chart Archive — Ship facility (Library Tier 1) that lets a hireling research a topic over 7 days and return up to three previously unknown facts.
  • Crew Berths — Ship facility (Barrack Tier 1) that adds up to 4 Bastion Defenders per Recruit order.
  • Expanded Cargo Hold — Tier 1 bastion facility. Storehouse adapted for the ship — buy or sell nonmagical trade goods up to a value ceiling that scales with level, with a profit margin on sales that also increases with level.
  • Ship Bastion — The Shattered Sea — Shared mobile bastion rules for the party ship — pooled facilities, weekly turns, defenders, upkeep, and ship space limits.
  • Ship Combat — Rules for ship’s guns, broadsides, shot types, and multi-deck volleys — expands the 2024 DMG vehicle rules.
  • Ship Mechanics — Hub page for all Shattered Sea ship rules — tiers, crew, operations, bastion, upgrades, and combat.
  • Ship Operations — Travel speeds, navigation checks, upkeep costs, acquiring a ship, living quarters, and ship reputation for Shattered Sea play.
  • Ship Stats — The Shattered Sea — Ship tiers, vehicle statistics, crew roles, minimum crew requirements, and upkeep for Shattered Sea play.
  • Ship Upgrades — The Shattered Sea — Purchaseable magical enhancements and installed ship gear — catalog by rarity and availability.
  • Ships & Bastion — Quick Reference — Play-table cheat sheet for ship tiers, crew roles, operations, bastion, and guns — consolidated quick reference.
  • Surgeon’s Berth — Tier 1 homebrew ship bastion facility — stabilizes downed crew, removes conditions, or grants Lesser Restoration once per Bastion Turn. Requires the Surgeon role filled.
  • Weapons Locker — Tier 1 bastion facility — stocking it upgrades defender death dice from d6 to d8 for one Bastion Turn. Cost halved if the ship also has a Carpenter’s Shop.

  • Art Style Guide — Visual style guide for AI-generated campaign art — agents read this before every image generation task
  • BLM Prep Framework — Brennan Lee Mulligan’s prep methodology: reactive toys over predicted outcomes, narrative tentpoles that Schrödinger into position, player gravity as the essential anchor. Read before generating session prep, NPC toys, or faction structures.
  • Character Creation: Three Pillars — Pointy Hat’s three-pillar framework for character identity before mechanics: Gimmick (surface), Conflict (wound), Want (engine). Use before helping create or evaluate any PC concept.
  • Character Interview Guide — A blank questionnaire for players to establish character foundations before or during session zero. No wrong answers.
  • City Creation Guide (Theme Park Method) — Pointy Hat’s Theme Park Method for city design: choose one legible theme, build attractions players can interact with (not a lore museum), adapt every element to the theme. Read before creating any city, port, or district hub.
  • Crissdalynn Primer — Agent quick reference for spotlighting and fairly pressuring Crissdalynn’s flight, loyalty, and darkness vulnerabilities.
  • Delmar Primer — Agent quick reference for spotlighting and fairly pressuring Delmar’s precision damage, crew loyalty, and low-magic rogue profile.

  • Dungeon Creation Method — Pointy Hat’s 5-step dungeon framework: one-word theme → mechanics that express it → goal → varied encounters → climax that synthesizes all. Use before generating any dungeon, ruin, or enclosed site.
  • Lines and Veils — Hard content boundaries for the Shattered Sea campaign — lines are fully forbidden, veils fade to black. Agent-facing: apply these boundaries when generating any campaign content.
  • Mystery-Making Framework — Pointy Hat’s mystery-building method: define culprit, motive, and method first; then place at least 3 clues per core question. Use before creating any investigation, clue set, or mystery arc.
  • One-Shot Modular Method (MMOS) — Pointy Hat’s 7-step modular one-shot framework (MMOS): two paths, one key, modular encounters, one non-modular showdown, two endings. Core principle: most encounters must be skippable without breaking the session.
  • Party Combat Primer — Shattered Sea — Agent quick reference for party-wide encounter tuning at level 4 — PC combat roles, observed patterns (sessions 1–4), lighting asymmetry, resource budget, and fair pressure distribution.
  • Party Crew — Roster of crew hired by the party — update after each session with new hires, departures, and role changes.
  • Party Session Primer — Shattered Sea — Stub — party not yet defined. Populate after session zero.

  • Situations Not Stories — Core prep principle: write situations, not stories. Drop the players into something interesting and find out what they do. Whatever they do next is the story.

  • Warren — Ferrin Locke — Three Passage surface operations were intercepted. The common thread leads to Ferrin Locke — a Dry canal broker coerced into feeding route timing to Dravosi intelligence. He wants out.
  • Warren — Grung in the Sewers — Nona assigns the party to investigate Grung sightings in the tunnels under Calveno — reports are too consistent to dismiss. They find signs of real Grung presence, unexplained markings, and no clean answers. First hint that something is building.

Ancient aquatic civilization that built upward from the bottom of the Drowned Maw around a planar fissure. Their city, biomancy, soul-pledge technology, and disappearance all remain active archaeology threads.

# The Antheri

Ancient aquatic humanoid civilization. At its height around -2000 DR, the Antheri built into the western wall of [[the-drowned-maw|the Drowned Maw]], reaching toward the planar boundary with the [[elemental-plane-of-water|Elemental Plane of Water]].

The common salvage assumption is wrong. The Antheri did not begin on the safe upper shelf and build down. Their oldest work is at the bottom, anchored near the fissure. The visible [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] are newer upper structures and exhaust systems for the deep engine below.

## Origin

The Antheri began as surface nomads in the sunlit sea. A localized current collapse drove them downward toward hydrothermal vents and the remaining food chain. Survival forced a chemosynthetic turn: vent bacteria, tube worms, magically sustained kelp gardens, and body adaptations for pressure, darkness, and deep water.

They discovered the Maw by following those vents deeper. The fissure at the trench floor bled elemental power. Early attempts to harness it killed entire settlements. Their society reorganized around the people who could keep the city alive: architects, biomancers, and planar engineers.

## Physical Evidence

No preserved record confirms exact appearance. The ruins imply:

- Humanoid bodies about 5-6 feet tall.
- Narrower shoulders than a standard human.
- Five-fingered hands.
- No stairs, walkways, air pockets, or pressure bulkheads.
- Architecture designed for open-water movement in three dimensions.

> [!dm]
> The exact physical form is intentionally unresolved. Do not specify it until a stronger source establishes it.

## The Vertical City

| Tier | Depth | What It Means |
|---|---:|---|
| Shelfworks | 60-200 ft. | Salvageable upper structures. Recent damage is mostly salvage and entity incursion, not original collapse. |
| Mid-Works | 200-500 ft. | Residential and research zone. Better preserved. Soul-pledge symbolic language appears integrated into structure, not decoration. |
| Deep Works | 500+ ft. | Boundary-zone conditions dominate. Pristine, singular-purpose structures. Soul-pledge chamber and fissure-oriented terminus are here. |

> [!mechanic]
> Reaching the Deep Works requires more than water breathing. Elemental diffusion causes ongoing Constitution saves, exhaustion risk, spell failure chances, and instrument unreliability.

## Technology

- **Corrosion-proof composite stone:** does not foul or carry biological growth.
- **Bio-metallurgic alloy:** current metallurgy cannot reproduce it.
- **Bioluminescent data channels:** algae seeded into capillary-like alloy geometry pulsed light through the city.
- **Accelerated aquaculture:** deep kelp systems regrew harvestable mass within days.
- **Living infrastructure:** pressure regulators grown from sponge-like tissue; transit currents driven by stimulated cilia networks.
- **Soul-binding:** formal ritual architecture and repeated symbolic vocabulary. [[auralis|Auralis]] is one known product, not the whole tradition.

## The Soul-Pledge

The soul-pledge chamber predates Auralis and appears built for repeated use. The Antheri combined biomancy, soul-binding, and planar mechanics to extract a consciousness from a body and bind it into an artificial immortal framework.

[[auralis|Auralis]] is not a natural deity. He is Antheri technology pushed to its endpoint: a manufactured guardian capable of surviving at the bottom of the trench and holding a specific purpose.

> [!dm]
> If other soul-pledges remain active, they may still be protecting things the party has not reached. Do not decide that until a source or table event demands it.

## The Fall

The Antheri vanished in -495 DR. The ruin record supports rapid failure, not slow decline:

- No evidence of external attack on the shelf structures.
- No mass casualty evidence in the residential tier.
- Workspaces abandoned mid-process.
- Deep activity was ongoing at the time of collapse.
- The fissure widened after the city was built around it.

The strongest DM-facing implication from the source: the upper city may be sealed exhaust infrastructure for a planar engine that is still running. Salvagers at the Shelfworks may be dismantling safety systems without understanding them.

## What Current Civilizations Know

- **Sailors and civilians:** old underwater ruins; valuable material; dangerous diving.
- **[[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] salvage interests:** know the Antheri name and basic shelf layout, not the depth or function of the full city.
- **Scholars:** no working public translation of Antheri symbolic language.
- **[[catarina-davirelli|Catarina DaVirelli]]:** best living non-Antheri expert on salvageable Antheri material culture.
- **Halythion Remembrancers:** may know the outside sequence of the Antheri fall, if the party reaches them and earns access.

Dense reference overview of the Shattered Sea campaign — geography, powers, religion, starting situation, and the edges of the map. Player-facing.

# The Shattered Sea — Campaign Overview

*1495 DR. Sixty thousand square miles of reef, deep channel, colonial paperwork, old gods, and water that remembers.*

---

## The Shape of the World

The [[shattered-sea|Shattered Sea]] is an archipelago in two main arcs separated by a wide channel. To the west, the [[galewall|Galewall]] — a permanent tropical storm belt — marks the edge of the colonial homelands. To the east, the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] — a vast deep-sea trench — marks the edge of the charts. Between them, the Scatter Current runs clockwise and the politics run crooked.

### Western Gateway

The [[galewall|Galewall]] is a three-week crossing under the right pilot. Most sailors treat it as a dare with a fee attached. The [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]] sit at its eastern edge: cold volcanic spires that break the swells and shelter nothing.

### The Crown Islands

The northern arc. Five large, mountainous, heavily administered islands under the [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]]. Rich, fortified, and governed from behind a ledger.

- **Calder's Tooth** guards the western mouth of the [[central-strait|Central Strait]]. Its cliff face holds [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] — the Crown's main fortress-port, carved into tiers from the waterline up to Fort Crestwall at the summit. Inspection here is mandatory, enforceable, and profitable.
- **[[calveno|Calveno]]** is the oldest commercial city in the Scatter: canal-threaded pale stone, public negotiations, and debts that travel faster than ships. Home of the [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]]'s deepest roots and Rattkin infrastructure below the waterline.

### The Central Strait

The Scatter's main east-west highway, forty to eighty miles wide, current pushing east. The [[central-strait|Strait]] is reliable because the Crown enforces rules at its western mouth. Those rules have fees attached.

### The Midchain

The southern arc. Dozens of small, close-packed islands with reefs, jungle, hidden channels, and local arrangements that do not survive contact with colonial paperwork.

- **[[kalowe|Kalowe]]** is the primary Midchain free port, built across three reef islands over a natural lagoon. No colonial authority. Not the same as no politics. The standard port for unregistered vessels, black-market cargo, crew-for-hire, and people who need to become harder to find.
- **[[verdant-teeth|The Verdant Teeth]]** are five closely grouped islands south of Kalowe held by [[grung-clans|Grung clans]]. Charts mark the interiors with some version of "do not approach." Outsiders trade at designated beaches and stay at the waterline.

### The Tail and the Maw

Where both arcs narrow toward the deep water. The Tail is high cliffs, serious pilots, longline grounds, and salvage staging. [[high-eyrie|The High Eyrie]] — a basalt sea-stack monastery of the [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]] — sits on the northeastern Crown coast watching the Maw.

The [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] is to the east: vast, dark, compass-drifting, quiet in weather that should chop the surface to pieces. Ships cross it for salvage, pilgrimage, research, and profit. [[shelfworks|The Shelfworks]] on the western shelf is the main salvage staging ground.

---

## Powers on the Water

| Power | Method | Stronghold | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] | Naval force, inspection law, paperwork | Port Tidefall, Crown Islands | Law as weapon |
| [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] | Credit, debt, contracts, insurance | Calveno | Debt as politics |
| [[waveservants|Waveservants]] | Tribute, blessing, religious infrastructure | Every working harbour | Transactional neutrality |
| [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]] | Observation, record-keeping, aerial mobility | The High Eyrie | Non-aligned record-keepers |
| [[the-passage|The Passage]] | Hidden routes, Rattkin couriers, port infrastructure | The Warren, Calveno | Below the surface |
| [[grung-clans|Grung Clans]] | Territory, poison, waterline trade, coastal raids | Verdant Teeth | Deteriorating |

The Crown and the Concordat are rivals whose legal systems recognize each other. [[the-passage|The Passage]] operates entirely outside colonial records, which is its value. [[waveservants|The Waveservants]] collect from all of them.

---

## Faith and the Price of Sailing

[[umberlee|Umberlee]] is the Bitch Queen, goddess of storms, shipwrecks, and the sea's destructive appetite. No one has to love her to pay her. That is the point.

In the Shattered Sea her worship is not fringe — it is port infrastructure. A harbour may change flags and governors; the Umberlee shrine near the waterline usually remains. The [[waveservants|Waveservants]] collect tribute without distinction. A blessing is not a promise of safety. It is an acknowledgement that proper respect has been shown.

*Sailors who do not pay do not sail confidently.*

---

## Peoples of the Scatter

Most sourcebook species have a place in the Scatter. The setting adds four homebrew-native options — [[lore/species/aarakocra|Aarakocra]], [[lore/species/grung|Grung]], [[lore/species/rattkin|Rattkin]], and [[lore/species/tabaxi|Tabaxi]] — each with deep roots in its economy, politics, or geography.

---

## The Starting Situation

The *[[saltwright|Saltwright]]* is captained by **[[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]]** — an alligator-snapping tortle who has survived eleven years on the Midchain route by treating danger as weather. You are aboard for your own reason.

**Questions to answer before Session Zero:**

- Why are you aboard?
- What do you want badly enough to cross dangerous water for?
- What kind of trouble follows you onto a ship?
- What would make you stay with a crew when leaving would be easier?

---

## The Edges of the Map

The [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] is the eastern boundary of what is administrated, inspected, named, and argued over. Beyond it, the [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] has no colonial presence, no reliable resupply, and few landmarks a western pilot would trust.

The Maw itself is not forbidden. Ships go there for salvage, pilgrimage, research, desperation, and profit. The [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels]] watch it and record what they see. Every chart grows less confident near the edge.

There are things in the Scatter that do not fit the economy yet: impossible stone, wrong currents, missing ships, old records, sailors who will not say what they saw east of the charts. The edges of the map are where the sea stops being navigable and starts being a question.

Canonical chronology for Shattered Sea pre-campaign history and early sessions. Anchors the Antheri, Drowned Maw, Fisk fleet disaster, Perrin's shipwreck, and Session 01 sequence.

# Campaign Timeline

**Current Year:** 1495 DR

## The Age Of The Antheri

- **-2000 DR:** [[antheri|The Antheri]] civilization is at its height. They build into the western wall of [[the-drowned-maw|the Drowned Maw]], descending toward the planar boundary with the [[elemental-plane-of-water|Elemental Plane of Water]]. Their engineering includes corrosion-proof composite stone, living machinery, and underwater architecture beyond current use. [[auralis|Auralis]] is born during this period; his pre-pledge identity is lost. The deepest Antheri construction, now called the [[antheri-ruins|Antheri Ruins]], points directly down the Maw toward the fissure at the bottom.
- **-495 DR:** The Antheri vanish. No external attack, no mass casualty, no clear collapse; the civilization stops leaving evidence. The planar breach between the Elemental Plane of Water and the Maw widens beyond the conditions the city was built to survive. Auralis, bound by soul-pledge to guard Antheri creations, survives as the sole living Antheri.

## The Shattered Sea Takes Shape

- **895 DR:** [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]] establish their Kensei monastic tradition at [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]] to counter the [[waveservants|Waveservants]] of [[umberlee|Umberlee]], a predatory tribute network extorting sailors for favorable weather.
- **1195 DR:** The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] establishes its first colonial presence in the Shattered Sea, claims the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]], and places inspection forces at the western entrance to the [[central-strait|Central Strait]], forming [[tidefall|Port Tidefall]].
- **1210 DR:** The [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] arrives, forms the Seven Houses of [[calveno|Calveno]], and begins its system of obligation.
- **1240 DR:** The [[the-passage|Passage]] Rattkin network forms out of [[warren|the Warren]] to evade colonial pressure from the Tessarine Concordat and Dravosi Crown.
- **1295 DR:** The Sentinels of the Eyrie begin their current unbroken observation record of the Drowned Maw, the ledger series still running in 1495 DR.

## The Years Before

- **1488 DR:** [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina DaVirelli]] salvages functional Antheri components from the [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] above the Antheri Ruins and reverse-engineers several into working devices. The resulting rush of prospectors, scholars, and criminal contractors becomes the Shelfworks Goldrush. Catarina returns to Calveno and puts her workshop into production. Her most visible creation is the [[clockwork-owl-familiar|Clockwork Owl Familiar]].
- **1490 DR:** [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] commissions and purchases [[salvaged-antheri-plate|Salvaged Antheri Plate]] from Catarina's workshop in Calveno, sized to cover the cannonball breach in his shell.
- **1493 DR:** [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]] is banished from High Eyrie at age 14 for treating her assigned pilgrimage, mapping the Drowned Maw from inside a storm, as a joke. [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]], who staked his reputation on her readiness, approves the decision. The banishment is permanent until the task is complete.
- **1493 DR:** Crissdalynn meets [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] and ships aboard the [[red-lady|Red Lady]] as navigator and crow in the crow's nest, beginning one year and ten months of service.
- **1494 DR:** [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude Tabarnack]] plans to desert the [[grung-clans|Grung Clans]] and leave the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]]. [[pell|Pell]] is tortured to death in reprisal after [[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]] reports Jean-Claude's intentions. Haunted by the slaves' deaths, Jean-Claude escapes east through the [[midchain|Midchain]] and lives rough to avoid leaving a trail.
- **1495 DR:** Simone's purple-and-black coloration slowly transitions to purple and gold, elevating her to warlord-tier status among the Grung, just below pure gold. She leads [[sorn|Sorn]]'s garrison and assembles a small elite unit of purple Grung familiar with Jean-Claude's methods, dedicated to running down deserters.

## Final Days Before Session 01

- **Day -35 approx., 1495 DR:** An unknown contractor engages the [[chain-council|Chain Council]] to assemble a five-ship fleet under [[admiral-fisk|Admiral Fisk]]. Target: a Pearl of Souls, an Umberlee artifact held in the Blue Shrine on [[vel-orn|Vel Orn]] in the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]]. Fleet: [[red-lady|Red Lady]] (flagship), [[the-narrow|The Narrow]], [[heft|Heft]], [[fernen|Fernen]], and [[loud-argument|Loud Argument]]. Crissdalynn has already served aboard the Red Lady for nearly two years. See [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]].
- **Day -7:** The fleet passes [[keth-naar|Keth Naar]] en route to Vel Orn. [[stripes-bitemore|Stripes Bitemore]] is on the island; his tribe has watched the seas turn wrong for days.
- **Day -6:** Delmar, Crissdalynn, and the crews of Fisk's fleet steal the Pearl of Souls from Umberlee's shrine without alerting the Waveservants. The Pearl departs Vel Orn aboard the Red Lady.
- **Day -5:** Umberlee's retribution finds the fleet over the Drowned Maw. Fog engulfs all five ships. A rogue trench opens and drives the fleet 80 feet down; the water closes overhead. Crissdalynn dives from the crow's nest, grabs Delmar, and flies them both clear. The Pearl sinks near the Red Lady wreck. Umberlee presses the souls of all five captains into Fisk as the hulls go down. The crews are drawn into the Pearl.
- **Day -5, minutes after sinking:** The Pearl settles near the material-plane fissure at the Maw's floor and continues functioning, drawing souls and accumulating divine energy. The fissure shifts from passive elemental leakage into a directed attractor, rapidly pulling entities through from the Elemental Plane of Water.
- **Day -5, three hours after sinking:** The [[leviathan|Leviathan]] forces the fissure wider from the Elemental Plane of Water into the mortal sea. Auralis wakes and reads the Leviathan as a parasitic invader in his realm. He begins moving for the first time since the Antheri fell.
- **Day -4:** The Leviathan destroys the [[vestra|Vestra]] and shipwrecks [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] on Keth Naar. Perrin barely survives. He believes [[perrins-cloak-of-the-manta-ray|his cloak]] saved him; the source says Auralis actually did. Perrin forged a warlock pact in the wreck without knowing it, then limped the beach and stowed away aboard the [[saltwright|Saltwright]] in Keth Naar harbor.
- **Day -4:** Belmore's tribe reads the seas as actively wrong and sends Stripes Bitemore to find the cause. He finds the Saltwright in harbor and barters passage west with Beaumont.
- **Day -3:** Beaumont crosses back east through the Drowned Maw and finds Delmar and Crissdalynn on driftwood, the only two survivors of five ships. He pulls them aboard the Saltwright and gives them free passage west to [[tidefall|Port Tidefall]]. Perrin is already hidden in the hold. Stripes is a paying passenger.
- **Day -1 / four months after Jean-Claude's escape:** Jean-Claude has been running the Midchain for months since his escape from Sorn. Simone's hunter unit has followed his trail east. He is one island ahead of them.

## Session 01

- **Jean-Claude leaps aboard:** Jean-Claude hears dogs behind him on a Midchain island and leaps onto the Saltwright as it passes. The current party is now aboard.

Current Year: 1495 DR

The Age Of The Antheri

  • -2000 DR: The Antheri civilization is at its height. They build into the western wall of the Drowned Maw, descending toward the planar boundary with the Elemental Plane of Water. Their engineering includes corrosion-proof composite stone, living machinery, and underwater architecture beyond current use. Auralis is born during this period; his pre-pledge identity is lost. # Il Gioco delle Beffe

Calveno's five-day prank festival. Teams design elaborate public hoaxes, execute them on willing marks, and leave their registered symbol at the scene to claim the score.

[[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] left the party to attend festival business after the ship reached [[calveno|Calveno]].

## Structure

| Day | Name | What Happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | La Scelta, the Choosing | Registration at the Mercatura bridge. Teams declare mark, category, scale, stake, and symbol. Marks are notified that morning. |
| 2-4 | La Finestra, the Window | Execution window. Teams may strike at any hour and can use false alarms, sabotage, and misdirection. |
| 5 | Il Giudizio, the Judgment | Pranks are presented. Marks score surprise; committee scores craft and recovery. Winner announced at sundown. |

## Rules That Matter at the Table

- Standard entry stake is 25 gp; Legendary-scale entries pay 50 gp.
- Scoring is out of 20: Craft 10, Surprise 5, Recovery 5.
- First place takes 60 percent of the pool, second 25 percent, third the remainder.
- The Beffa Medallion is a bronze laughing mask awarded to the winning team leader.
- A mark who was genuinely fooled often pays a goodwill gift of 10-50 gp.
- Every team must leave its registered symbol at the scene. No symbol, no score.
- A stolen symbol used in another team's prank is a recognized gambit called a *beffa doppia*.

## Current Hooks

- Registration is tomorrow morning from the party's current Calveno state.
- Several Legendary declarations are expected, so the prize pool should be large.
- [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]] has signed the Accord for twenty years and has never been successfully pranked.
- A [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine]] factor is on the list for the first time.
- [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]] appears on the winner plaque, but his entry has no description.
- The Six-Hour Wake record has stood for forty years.

## Last Ten Winners

| Recency | Winner | Symbol | Mark | Prank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Last year | The Restoration Society | Painter's brush | Mercatura committee offices | Installed a duplicate Governor's Portrait with a moustache. |
| 2 years ago | The Empty Ledger | Blank open book | Tessarine factor Aldovar Fen | Made an insured ship disappear from every known register. |
| 3 years ago | The Herons | Wading heron | Canal inspector Brun Cask | Two teams nested false inspection findings into each other. |
| 4 years ago | Sable & Pepper | Salt shaker and sprig | Lucia Farro | Convinced her a famous dead sea captain had survived in Keth Naar. |
| 5 years ago | The Blind Canal | Looped rope | Matteo Carver | Rerouted a maintenance canal so he filed four reports on the same stretch. |
| 6 years ago | Il Velo | Half-mask | [[oleandro-fuschi|Oleandro Fuschi]] | Adjusted every tavern element by inches and swapped each wine for a near match. |
| 7 years ago | The Usual Suspects | Crossed quills | Piet Ondra | Convinced a Chain Council observer that Calveno redefined a fathom. |
| 8 years ago | The Devout | Closed eye | [[waveservants|Waveservant]] Senior Matha | Forged a tide-tithe prophecy in the shrine donation box. |
| 9 years ago | The Flagmen | Three-color band | Crob | Created a fake canal-boat health flag regulation. |
| 10 years ago | The Quiet Tide | Still waterline | Valco | Replaced inventory contents with equal-weight substitutes before audit. |

Rules That Matter at the Table

Calveno's annual open bardic competition — multiple bands playing simultaneously across the canal district for three hours while crowds move between them, judged by which stage holds the most people at the end.

# Il Palio delle Voci Contese

> *The contest of the warring voices. Every year Calveno remembers it cannot decide what it loves, and makes the music fight for it.*

## Overview

**Il Palio delle Voci Contese** — the Grand Contest of the Warring Voices — is [[calveno|Calveno]]'s open bardic competition, held across three nights in the canal district each year. Multiple bands claim stages simultaneously across the Mercatura, the Velo Quarter, and the Le Paludi waterfront. The crowd is the judge: it moves freely between stages all evening, and whichever band draws the densest sustained crowd through the Grande Finale wins the Palio banner and the purse.

There are no judges. There is no panel. The crowd votes with its feet, continuously, in real time. A band that peaks too early loses the audience to whoever is building slower. A band that never quite gets there loses to whoever is peaking at the right moment. The tactics are as much theatrical as musical.

Any group may enter. Entry is free. The competition organisers — a rotating committee of Mercatura merchant families — care about spectacle, not pedigree.

## The Stages

Three stages are constructed each year, each with its own character:

**Il Palco della Mercatura** — The primary stage, built on the wide plaza at the main canal bridge. Largest capacity. Worst acoustics. The crowd here is merchants, factors, and officers who came because it is visible and stayed because they were seen.

**Il Palco del Velo** — The Velo Quarter stage, set up across the low bridges where Calveno stops enforcing its rules. Smaller, louder, unpredictable. The crowd here came specifically for this and has opinions.

**Il Palco delle Acque** — The waterfront stage on the Le Paludi canal dock, torchlit, half the audience arriving and departing by boat. The acoustic carry over the water is remarkable. This stage favours volume and visual drama.

Bands are assigned a home stage by draw, but may play off-stage busking and crowd work between sets to pull audience from other stages.

## The Competition Structure

**La Prova** *(The Trial — first night)* — All bands play short opening sets. No elimination, but the crowd forms initial impressions that are difficult to shift. The band that dominates La Prova does not always win, but the band that embarrasses itself here rarely recovers.

**La Sfida** *(The Challenge — second night)* — Full sets, rivalries visible. Crowd movement between stages accelerates. Bands may interact — a show of solidarity, a deliberate clash of schedules, a stunt that upstages someone else's set. The organisers look the other way.

**Il Grande Finale** *(The final night)* — All bands play simultaneously, maximum effort, for three hours. The winning band is the one with the crowd at midnight.

## Entering

Any group that shows up at the Mercatura committee office three days before La Prova can register. The committee asks for a band name and a home stage preference. It does not ask for references.

Groups without a full complement can recruit additional performers in Calveno before registration closes. The city has musicians, and musicians who want a shot at the Palio without the risk of leading their own band are findable at the [[ponte-bassa|Ponte Bassa]] most evenings.

Roles in a Palio band are not limited to performers. Stage crew — riggers, pyrotechnic handlers, lighting, dramatic prop work — contributes materially to a band's impact. Crowd work between sets is legal and effective. The Palio is won by all of this together, not just the music.

## The Prize

The Palio itself is a painted banner, commissioned fresh each year, depicting something the organisers consider representative of Calveno's character. Winning it carries the kind of social weight in Calveno that money cannot directly buy. The purse is 300 gp, split among registered band members.

Past winners are commemorated on a plaque at the Mercatura committee offices. The plaque is visible from the street. Calveno takes this seriously.

## Current Competitors

**La Canzone Nera** *(The Black Song)* — Four human musicians from the interior, technically flawless. Their set is precise, their stage is immaculate, and they are completely boring. Favoured by the Council families. They win La Prova on execution and then watch their crowd erode over two nights.

**Il Vento di Seta** *(The Silk Wind)* — A halfling trio with a Tessarine booking agent and a crowd that already knows all the words. They play the same set every year, perfectly, and the crowd that loves them is devoted and returns exactly to the same size. They have placed second three times.

**Le Ossa del Toro** *(The Bones of the Bull)* — An orc and tortle two-piece using drums and a massive horn. Loud, physical, no finesse. Their crowd surges and compresses and occasionally knocks people into the canal. They have never placed higher than third. They have never cared.

## Current Hooks

- Registration closes in three days. The committee office is on the Mercatura, two buildings from the Tessarine factor house.
- A halfling fiddle player at the [[ponte-bassa|Ponte Bassa]] has been watching the door every night this week, waiting for someone to ask him if he's available.
- [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]] has attended every Palio for as long as anyone can remember. He usually appears at the winning stage just before midnight, which the crowd has started to read as an omen.

Regional demographics of the Shattered Sea: who lives where, who sails through, and why the population mix changes farther east.

# Peoples of the Shattered Sea

The Shattered Sea sits at the edge of the colonial world. West of the Galewall is the known: kingdoms, records, recognized law. East of it is the Scatter, and the Scatter does not ask where you came from.

The further east you travel, the less the colonial map means. The [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] look like the western homelands transplanted to warmer water. [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and the [[midchain|Midchain]] look like what happens when those homelands stop being able to enforce anything. The Tail and the Outer Reach look like what was here before the homelands arrived.

This is not a census. The sea moves people too quickly for counts to hold.

## Presence Terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Dominant | The majority of any given town or crew. |
| Common | Reliably present. You will see them every day. No one comments on it. |
| Present | Visible in any large port. You might go a week without one in a small settlement. |
| Rare | Occasional. Noticed. Not remarkable enough to cause trouble. |
| Isolated | A specific community exists. Everywhere else: almost never. |

---

## The Crown Islands

*Dravosi colonial core. The western homelands with a tropical accent.*

The Crown Islands are the oldest colonial foothold in the Scatter. The majority population is human and came with the Dravosi flag. [[rattkin|Rattkin]] are present in every Crown port even though the Dravosi Crown's relationship with [[the-passage|The Passage]] is adversarial. The Warren prefers it that way.

| Species | Presence | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Human | Dominant | Dravosi colonial stock; also Tessarine merchants and independent families. |
| Halfling | Common | Chandlers, bookkeepers, small merchants. |
| Dwarf | Common | Naval engineering, fortification work, armaments manufacture. |
| [[rattkin|Rattkin]] | Common | Port infrastructure, message networks, The Passage. Officially discouraged; practically irreplaceable. |
| Gnome | Present | Instrument makers, cartographers, Tessarine ledger work. |
| Tiefling | Present | Mixed colonial heritage. More visible in Calveno than in Tidefall. |
| Orc | Present | Dock crews, ship labour, garrison soldiers. Often underranked relative to competence. |
| Dragonborn | Present | Scattered across military and merchant roles. |
| Aasimar | Rare | Occasional pilgrims and Tyr-aligned advocates. |
| [[aarakocra|Aarakocra]] | Rare | Mostly [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels]]. High Eyrie maintains a small permanent population near the eastern Crown approaches. |
| Other | Rare | The Galewall crossing drops all kinds onto Crown docks. Most do not stay long. |

---

## The Central Strait

*The main highway. The most transient, and therefore the most everything.*

The Strait is not a place people live — it is a place people pass through. Port Tidefall processes hundreds of ships a year. Calveno turns over its dockside population on the tide. [[calveno|Calveno]] specifically skews more diverse than the rest of the Crown Islands — the [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] does not care about your heritage. It cares about your credit.

| Species | Presence | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Human | Dominant | Still the majority, but less so than the interior Crown Islands. |
| Halfling | Common | Merchants. Calveno's counting houses run heavy halfling. |
| Dwarf | Common | Port engineering and armaments. |
| [[rattkin|Rattkin]] | Common | Higher density than the Crown interior. Every major port in the Strait has a Run. |
| Orc | Common | Crew and dock work. A mixed crew on the Strait is more common than a human-only one. |
| Tortle | Common | Island-adapted, long-lived, calm under pressure. Excellent captains and pilots. [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] is the most visible example. |
| Tiefling | Present | Tessarine merchant families in particular. |
| Gnome | Present | Navigation instruments, trade tools. |
| Dragonborn | Present | Military and merchant both. |
| Water Genasi | Present | Natural affinity for this work. Unremarkable on a working ship. |

## On the Water

Ships are their own demographic. A working crew in the Scatter does not look like any port's population — it looks like whoever the captain could hire and keep.

A Midchain free-trade crew might be half orc and tortle with a rattkin pilot and a grung surgeon who does not discuss what caste they left. A Crown naval vessel runs formally human with dwarf engineers and a rattkin aboard in an unofficial capacity everyone pretends not to notice. A [[the-passage|Passage]] runner has no species requirement and one rule.

The ship is the smallest unit of real integration in the Scatter. It works because it has to.

Peoples of the Shattered Sea

The Shattered Sea sits at the edge of the colonial world. West of the Galewall is the known: kingdoms, records, recognized law. East of it is the Scatter, and the Scatter does not ask where you came from.

The further east you travel, the less the colonial map means. The Crown Islands look like the western homelands transplanted to warmer water. Kalowe and the Midchain look like what happens when those homelands stop being able to enforce anything. The Tail and the Outer Reach look like what was here before the homelands arrived.

Playable reptilian humanoids with natural armor, bite attacks, and a pragmatic cognition that processes the world in terms of utility and survival. Lizardfolk in the Shattered Sea are hull-workers, salvagers, and tidal-zone settlers.

# Lizardfolk

Medium reptilian humanoids with scaled hides, powerful jaws, and a cognitive architecture that prioritizes survival over sentiment. Lizardfolk evaluate before they react. They eat what's available. They build with what's there. Waste is the only sin that registers without translation.

In the Shattered Sea, lizardfolk occupy the tidal margins — mangrove coasts, river deltas, brackish flats where the water shifts between salt and fresh. Their settlements look temporary to outsiders. Most have stood for generations. Lizardfolk build low, build in water, and relocate without grief when the tide pattern changes. The structure served its purpose. The next one will too.

At sea, lizardfolk crew as hull-workers, salvagers, and underwater repair hands. They hold their breath for a quarter-hour, work in cold water without slowing, and their natural armor means fewer injuries from barnacle-crusted keels and broken hull planking. A ship with a lizardfolk hull-team puts in for careening half as often. [[bastian-crev|Bastian Crev]], captain of the [[loud-argument|*Loud Argument*]] in [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]], came up through salvage work before Fisk gave him a command.

## Table Traits

- **Size:** Medium
- **Speed:** 30 ft.; swim speed equal to walking speed
- **Bite:** Natural melee weapon; 1d6 slashing on a hit.
- **Hold Breath:** Up to 15 minutes.
- **Hungry Jaws:** Once per long rest, bonus action bite attack. On hit, gain temporary HP equal to proficiency bonus.
- **Natural Armor:** Unarmored AC = 13 + Dexterity modifier. Compatible with shields.
- **Nature's Intuition:** Proficiency in two of the following: Animal Handling, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

## Culture

Lizardfolk pragmatism is real, but the word "cold" is wrong. A lizardfolk parent will die for a clutch without hesitation — the calculation is instant, not absent. What warm-blooded species read as emotional flatness is efficiency. A lizardfolk who sees a wounded ally doesn't feel distress and then act; they skip the first step. The help arrives at the same speed. The facial expression doesn't.

**Learned warmth.** Lizardfolk who spend years embedded in warm-blooded crews develop something that outsiders call emotional range. Whether it's learned performance or genuine feeling is a question lizardfolk themselves cannot answer and most stop asking. A lizardfolk who laughs at a friend's joke after ten years of friendship — is that mimicry or joy? The lizardfolk doesn't know. The laugh is real either way.

**Tidal settlements.** Lizardfolk communities organize around the tide cycle rather than the solar day. Activity peaks at low tide (building, foraging, crafting) and drops at high tide (rest, egg-tending, oral tradition). Visitors who arrive at high tide find a quiet village. Visitors who arrive at low tide find organized industry that puts most shipyards to shame.

**Crafting.** Lizardfolk waste nothing. Bone becomes tools. Hide becomes armor. Shell becomes currency. A lizardfolk artisan produces work that is ugly by human aesthetic standards and functionally superior by every other measure. The rare lizardfolk who learns decorative craft from another culture produces objects that unsettle — technically perfect ornamentation applied with an efficiency that strips the warmth out of the art form.

## Naming

Lizardfolk true-names in their own tongue are descriptive and functional: *Holds-Still, Sees-Under-Water, Bites-Twice.* When working among other species, lizardfolk adopt a **use-name** — something pronounceable by warm-blooded tongues, often borrowed from whatever culture they're embedded in. The use-name is not a mask. It's a tool, and lizardfolk do not distinguish between a useful tool and a real one.

Lizardfolk place-names follow Malay and Austronesian roots when rendered in Common: open syllables, nasal consonants, tidal or water references. *Tanjung, Teluk, Rawa, Pasang.*

  • Natural Armor: Unarmored AC = 13 + Dexterity modifier. Compatible with shields.
  • Nature’s Intuition: Proficiency in two of the following: Animal Handling, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

Culture

Lizardfolk pragmatism is real, but the word “cold” is wrong. A lizardfolk parent will die for a clutch without hesitation — the calculation is instant, not absent. What warm-blooded species read as emotional flatness is efficiency. A lizardfolk who sees a wounded ally doesn’t feel distress and then act; they skip the first step. The help arrives at the same speed. The facial expression doesn’t.

Learned warmth. Lizardfolk who spend years embedded in warm-blooded crews develop something that outsiders call emotional range. Whether it’s learned performance or genuine feeling is a question lizardfolk themselves cannot answer and most stop asking. A lizardfolk who laughs at a friend’s joke after ten years of friendship — is that mimicry or joy? The lizardfolk doesn’t know. The laugh is real either way.

Tidal settlements. Lizardfolk communities organize around the tide cycle rather than the solar day. Activity peaks at low tide (building, foraging, crafting) and drops at high tide (rest, egg-tending, oral tradition). Visitors who arrive at high tide find a quiet village. Visitors who arrive at low tide find organized industry that puts most shipyards to shame.

Crafting. Lizardfolk waste nothing. Bone becomes tools. Hide becomes armor. Shell becomes currency. A lizardfolk artisan produces work that is ugly by human aesthetic standards and functionally superior by every other measure. The rare lizardfolk who learns decorative craft from another culture produces objects that unsettle — technically perfect ornamentation applied with an efficiency that strips the warmth out of the art form.

Naming

Lizardfolk true-names in their own tongue are descriptive and functional: Holds-Still, Sees-Under-Water, Bites-Twice. When working among other species, lizardfolk adopt a use-name — something pronounceable by warm-blooded tongues, often borrowed from whatever culture they’re embedded in. The use-name is not a mask. It’s a tool, and lizardfolk do not distinguish between a useful tool and a real one.

Lizardfolk place-names follow Malay and Austronesian roots when rendered in Common: open syllables, nasal consonants, tidal or water references. Tanjung, Teluk, Rawa, Pasang.

Playable large-framed humanoids with horns, labyrinthine spatial memory, and a cultural identity built around passages. Minotaur navigators are the most sought-after pilots in the Shattered Sea.

# Minotaur

Medium humanoids built heavy — bovine heads, thick curving horns, broad shoulders, hooved feet. A minotaur who has walked a passage once can walk it blindfolded twenty years later. The same faculty works on currents, channel marks, and reef lines.

In the Shattered Sea, minotaurs are navigators. Not exclusively — some farm, some fight, some run chandleries — but the species' cultural gravity pulls toward passage-work: piloting ships through blind channels, mapping reef systems, maintaining the mental charts that keep vessels off the rocks. A minotaur pilot is the most expensive crew hire in the [[midchain|Midchain]] and worth every coin. [[sienne-orre|Sienne Orre]], captain of the [[fernen|*Fernen*]] in [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]], ran the fleet's perimeter survey operations — her passage-sense made her the natural choice.

Minotaur populations cluster wherever the water is difficult. Narrow straits, tidal channels, reef knots — the passages that kill ships are the passages minotaurs settle near and learn young. Smaller communities exist in every major port. A minotaur neighborhood is easy to identify from the architecture: the hallways turn.

## Table Traits

- **Size:** Medium (upper end — minotaurs are broad and heavy)
- **Speed:** 30 ft.
- **Horns:** Natural melee weapon; 1d6 piercing on a hit.
- **Goring Rush:** After moving 20+ ft. straight toward a target, bonus action Horn attack. On hit, target makes a Strength save or is pushed 10 ft.
- **Hammering Horns:** After hitting with a melee attack on your turn, bonus action to shove the target with horns. Strength save or pushed 10 ft. and knocked prone.
- **Labyrinthine Recall:** Perfect recall of any path traveled. Advantage on checks to navigate or avoid becoming lost.

## Culture

Minotaur society organizes around **passages** — the word covers physical routes, life stages, and the transitions between them. A young minotaur's first solo navigation of a difficult channel is their passage-rite; the channel becomes part of how close friends refer to them.

Minotaur interiors are complex by design. Switchback hallways, rooms accessible from three sides, staircases that double back. A straight corridor feels to a minotaur the way a windowless room feels to a human — not wrong, exactly, but exposed. Guests are not expected to find the kitchen. The host guides them. This is hospitality, not a test.

**At sea.** A minotaur pilot commands absolute authority over helm and heading in narrow water. A captain who overrides the pilot in a channel is a captain who wants to sink. This convention holds across the Shattered Sea regardless of a ship's flag — even Crown naval officers defer to the pilot in a reef passage.

**Temperament.** Minotaurs run warm and slow. Anger builds visibly — the breathing changes, the head drops, the horns come forward — and a minotaur at that point is extraordinarily dangerous. Most never reach it. The ones who do remember the occasion for the rest of their lives. The stereotype of the raging bull is built from the exceptions, not the rule. A working minotaur pilot radiates the same focused calm as a surgeon mid-operation.

## Naming

Minotaur personal names draw from Greek and Minoan roots: strong consonants, open vowels, -os/-as/-is endings. *Stavra, Kosmos, Thekla, Andronikos.* Sea-going minotaurs in mixed crews often adopt local naming conventions — a minotaur in Calveno waters might carry a name indistinguishable from a Tessarine human. The passage-name tradition persists informally among close kin.

Playable small humanoids built for infiltration, survival, swimming, and impossible spaces. Rattkin are the oldest continuous presence in every major Shattered Sea port.

# Rattkin

Small humanoids calibrated for getting into places they are not supposed to be. A locked cargo hold is a delay. A drainage pipe is a road. A ship's bilge is a neighborhood.

Rattkin are the oldest continuous presence in every major Shattered Sea port. Their fixed origin point is [[warren|the Warren]], and their living network is [[the-passage|the Passage]]. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] is a fancy-rat rattkin PC from the Calveno Run.

## Table Traits

- **Size:** Small
- **Speed:** 30 ft.; swim speed equal to walking speed
- **Boneless:** Can move through spaces as Tiny; speed is halved while doing so. Advantage to escape Grappled or Restrained.
- **Keen Senses:** Advantage on hearing- or smell-based Perception; can sense hidden or invisible creatures within 5 ft. by scent.
- **Scurry:** Disengage movement can pass through Large or smaller creatures without provoking opportunity attacks.
- **Survivor:** Advantage against Poisoned and disease; resistance to poison damage.
- **Pack Tactics:** Limited reaction attack when an ally hits a nearby creature.

## Varieties

| Variety | Role |
|---|---|
| Black Rat | Climbers, riggers, roofline workers, elevated port infrastructure |
| Brown Rat | Burrowers, Hold-maintainers, sewer and bilge route mappers |
| Fancy Rat | Social infiltrators and long-term outside contacts |

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Kin | Other rattkin; the in-group |
| Dry | Non-rattkin |
| Run | A rattkin community network in a port or city |
| Hold | A Passage waypoint or safe house |

# Sea Elf

*Medium Humanoid (Elf)*

Sea elves adapted to aquatic environments. Can breathe air and water, have cold resistance, and can communicate simple ideas to aquatic beasts. In the Shattered Sea, sea elves are centered at [[halythion|Halythion]] and tied to the worship of Deep Sashelas.

| | |
|---|---|

| **Speed** | 30 ft. walking; swimming speed equal to walking speed |

## Traits *(Monsters of the Multiverse — current version)*

**Child of the Sea.** Breathe air and water; resistance to cold damage.

**Darkvision.** 60 ft. Discern colors in darkness as shades of gray.

**Fey Ancestry.** Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the charmed condition.

**Friend of the Sea.** Communicate simple ideas to any Beast with a swimming speed.

**Trance.** No need to sleep; cannot be magically put to sleep. Long rest requires 4 hours of trance. End of trance: gain two proficiencies (weapon or tool) from elven memory, retained until next long rest.

# The Galewall Runner's Drop

> *They sailed straight into the Galewall. Most people call that suicide. They called it a route.*

A legendary privateer treasure cache rumored to be hidden on one of the volcanic [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]], deposited there during a desperate flight from the Dravosi Admiralty in the early colonial period.

## The Myth

In the early days of colonial occupation, an infamous privateer executed a flawless heist of a Dravosi payroll fleet. Hunted by the full Admiralty, the crew attempted the impossible: outrunning the navy by sailing straight into the [[galewall|Galewall]].

## What Happened

The permanent storm belt shattered the ship's masts and pushed it back out, sinking and ruined. Before the ship slipped beneath the waves, the crew reportedly rowed the heavy lockboxes onto the black, sulfur-vented shores of one of the Ashwall Islands. The privateer's name is lost to history. The heist is corroborated by missing Dravosi payroll records from the colonial era.

The cache is supposedly marked by a massive carving of a rat extending its hand, cut into the volcanic rock near the drop site. The carving predates any known colonial settlement of the Ashwall chain.

## The Catch

- Toxic sulfur vents make extended land exploration dangerous without alchemical protection.
- Shifting volcanic rock causes landmarks to change season-to-season.
- The island on which the cache sits is not identified in any surviving record.
- The rat carving, if it survives, may have been buried, eroded, or submerged by volcanic activity.

No successful recovery has been recorded.

## Connections

- [[galewall|The Galewall]] — the storm belt the privateer sailed through
- [[ashwall-islands|Ashwall Islands]] — the volcanic chain; exact island unknown
- [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] — the payroll fleet that was robbed

A legendary underwater sinkhole in the eastern Midchain where a century of shipwrecks lie at the bottom — guarded by an ancient Sawek and animated crews.

# The Grandfather Hole

> *The water turns an unnatural, freezing black. Reef divers know better than to dive there.*

A legendary underwater sinkhole somewhere in the eastern [[midchain|Midchain]], avoided by every experienced reef diver out of [[kalowe|Kalowe]] and feared in port taverns throughout the region.

## The Myth

Midchain reef divers know to mark and avoid [[sawek|Sawek]] lairs. But tavern tales speak of a single, massive sinkhole where the water turns an unnatural, freezing black. The sea around it drops temperature faster than any natural current can account for.

## What Is Known

The Grandfather Hole is territory claimed by an ancient [[sawek|Sawek]] large enough to pull a Tier 3 galleon down by the keel. At the bottom lies a century of undisturbed shipwrecks: a tangled, rotting reef of shattered hulls, lost cargo, and scattered gold accumulated over generations of the beast's predation.

The ambient magic of the Blue Hole has animated the drowned sailors trapped within the wreck-reef — any salvagers must contend with the beast above and undead crews below.

## The Catch

- No reliable charting of the sinkhole's location exists.
- Surviving or bypassing the ancient Sawek.
- Fighting through animated undead sailors in lightless, freezing water.

No successful salvage has ever been recorded.

## Connections

- [[sawek|Sawek]] — the Grandfather Hole is the confirmed lair of an apex specimen
- [[kalowe|Kalowe]] — reef diving community maintains the strongest oral tradition; divers mark its approximate quadrant but refuse to dive it
- [[midchain|Midchain]] — sinkhole sits somewhere in the eastern arc; exact location unknown and deliberately uncharted

# The Tithe of the Bitch Queen

> *Taking a single coin invites Umberlee's direct, personal spite. The sea follows you home.*

A legendary collection of divine treasure scattered across the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]] seafloor — the physical accumulation of beautiful things [[umberlee|Umberlee]] claimed from mortal ships over centuries.

## The Myth

Before the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] was stolen, it was widely believed that Umberlee maintained a physical collection of the most beautiful treasures her storms had claimed. Not a formal hoard — an unconscious curation. The finest things the sea had taken, kept.

## What Is Known

The Tithe is scattered across the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]] seafloor, not consolidated in one location. Unblemished jewels, pristine statues, gold bars that never tarnish — items with apparent divine preservation. Accessible only through tidal caves that breach the surface during the lowest tides of the decade.

## The Catch

Taking a single coin from the Tithe invites [[umberlee|Umberlee's]] direct, personal spite:

- Sailors who possess a piece cannot sail without drawing unnatural localized squalls that follow their ship.
- Squalls persist until the item is returned to saltwater.
- No theological workaround is documented in Waveservant records.
- The curse is on the object, not the bearer — transferring the item transfers the problem.

## Relationship to the Pearl of Souls

The Tithe predates the theft of the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]]. The Pearl's theft has complicated the theological picture: the Tithe represents what Umberlee passively accumulates; the Pearl represents something actively stolen from her. Waveservants will not discuss whether the Pearl belongs to the Tithe in any formal sense.

## Connections

- [[umberlee|Umberlee]] — the divine authority; the squall-curse is hers
- [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]] — the seafloor region where the cache is located
- [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] — the stolen artifact; its theft contextualizes the Tithe myth
- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — his theft of the Pearl is the most famous recent instance of taking from Umberlee's collection

# The Vault of the First Factor

> *The Tessarine don't use conventional traps. No one who has entered without credentials has returned.*

A legendary hidden depository constructed by the earliest [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine Concordat]] Envoy to the Shattered Sea, built to hold the physical collateral of the region's most desperate debtors.

## The Myth

The Tessarine Concordat never leaves its true wealth exposed in [[calveno|Calveno]]. The earliest Envoy built a hidden depository on an uncharted, jungle-choked limestone spire somewhere in the [[midchain|Midchain]], designed to hold the physical collateral of captains, governors, and merchants who could not meet their notes.

## What Is Known

The vault is not a simple treasure hoard — it is a localized museum of institutional desperation. Known contents from oral tradition:

- Masterwork weapons surrendered by captains who couldn't pay
- Magical family heirlooms
- Locked chests of trade-bars from governors and colonial administrators

The vault predates the modern Concordat structure. No current Tessarine official will confirm its existence, which most observers interpret as confirmation.

## The Catch

The vault's defenses are entirely magical and entirely lethal to the uncredentialed:

- No conventional traps — pressure plates, locks, and mechanical triggers have never been reported
- Very advanced magical protections of an unspecified nature
- No one who has entered without proper Tessarine credentials has returned
- Location on an uncharted limestone spire means finding it is itself a significant navigation challenge

## Connections

- [[calveno|Calveno]] — Concordat regional base; the vault is deliberately not here
- [[midchain|Midchain]] — the vault sits on an uncharted limestone spire somewhere in the interior

# Umberlee and the Waveservants

Umberlee is the sea as sailors fear it: black water under moonless cloud, a mast cracking in a squall, a reef where the chart promised depth, the wave that takes one person and leaves the rest alive to remember it. Her common title is the Bitch Queen. In the Shattered Sea, the name is spoken with caution more often than blasphemy.

No one has to love Umberlee to pay her. That is the point.

## What Sailors Know

Umberlee is worshiped because the sea kills, not because she is kind. Captains give tribute before risky crossings. Deckhands mutter her name when the wind turns wrong. Survivors pay after landfall because gratitude and fear look much the same at a shrine basin.

Her worship is ordinary port infrastructure. A harbor may change flags, governors, tariffs, languages, and laws; the Umberlee shrine usually remains where sailors can find it.

## The Waveservants

The [[waveservants|Waveservants]] are Umberlee's clergy in the Shattered Sea. They are collectors, witnesses, and ritual functionaries for a goddess who does not ask twice.

They wear salt-bleached grey robes, keep their hems damp, and smell of tallow and brine even in open air. They refuse almost no one because tribute from an enemy spends as cleanly as tribute from a friend.

Their neutrality is practical. A shrine that takes sides stops collecting from half the harbor.

## Shrines and Tribute

Most ports of any size keep an Umberlee shrine close to the waterline or harbor entry.

- Basin of seawater.
- Low candles burning in tallow.
- Posted fees, spoken terms, or a clerk who knows both.
- Offerings from crews that survived what they had no right to survive.
- A priest who treats the exchange as business already settled.

Payment is not always coin. Rope, fish bones, brass buttons, broken compass needles, carved tokens, or a captain's private promise may appear on an offering shelf. Coin is simpler. Coin is preferred.

## Player Character Hooks

- A sailor who pays because ritual is cheaper than regret.
- A former Waveservant attendant who knows what crews leave behind.
- A storm survivor who believes Umberlee spared them for a reason.
- A skeptic who still drops coin in the basin when no one is watching.
- A divine caster whose relationship with the sea is transactional, resentful, reverent, or all three.

# Calveno — Jean-Claude Beats

## How to Use This File

The roleplay beat does not require Warren access or plot setup. Drop it through ordinary [[calveno|Calveno]] city movement — Velo Quarter, any errand. Jean-Claude's player doesn't need to have done anything specific to earn it.

For combat, pull from [[calveno-street-encounters|Calveno — Street Encounters]] (Combat Escalations — Jean-Claude Arc section) when the handler investigation heats up.

---

## Arrival Observation — The Bridge Pillar

**When:** As soon as any PC crosses into open Calveno on Day 1 — the Mercatura, the Bridge, anywhere with a crowd. Private sensory note to Jean-Claude's player; no announcement to the group.

A Grung in a festival half-mask is standing at the Bridge pillar in the single position that gives sightlines to three exits without appearing to watch any of them.

Jean-Claude has stood in that position. He knows what it means.

> [!dm]
> Private note, not read-aloud. Let his player choose whether to tell the party. This is the first observable sign of the handler cell. It does not require Jean-Claude to act — it only requires him to notice.

Connection: [[calveno-beffa-grung-raid|Calveno — Beffa Grung Raid]] | [[calveno-jean-claude-beats|Jean-Claude combat escalation → Street Encounters]]

---

## Roleplay Beat — The Moustache Craftsman

**Where:** The Velo Quarter. A narrow booth selling theatrical accessories — wigs, prosthetics, ornamental beards, stage paint.

> [!read-aloud]
> A narrow booth between a wig maker and a vendor of theatrical smoke. The boards are covered in prosthetics, false beards, and a row of spectacles the man inside is not wearing. The spirit gum smell reaches you from three feet away. He has not looked up.

**Roleplay Prompt:** *The theatrical craftsman who made Jean-Claude's moustache and has several professional follow-up questions about how it's holding up.*

**Anchor:** Retired special effects technician who ran into their best work in a thrift store and cannot let it go — specific, proprietary, just a little wounded.

---

### Voice & Delivery

[[giacinto|Giacinto]] is a gnome, late sixties, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead, permanently smelling of spirit gum. He does not look up immediately. When he does, his eyes go straight to the moustache, not the face. He points.

> *"That's one of mine. The cut on the inner edge, right corner — I do that by hand. Nobody else does that. Who are you wearing it for?"*

He will not accept "I made it myself." He will offer to re-seal the edges for free, which he delivers in the tone of a doctor concerned about a healing wound. He is not suspicious. He is professionally invested. When Jean-Claude explains that the moustache is his *disguise* — that the principle is: if Grung read identity from colour, other peoples must read it from some equivalent visible signal, and facial hair appears to be the mechanism, and yes, it has held up across fourteen ports — Giacinto will stop, look at him, and say:

> *"That's. Hm. That's wrong. And I'm going to explain why, and I think you're going to find it interesting."*

He then explains, at length and with genuine enthusiasm, exactly which visible signals humans do and do not read. He does not tell Jean-Claude to take the moustache off. He thinks the moustache is actually doing real work, just not the work Jean-Claude believes it is — the beret is drawing more attention than a disguise should, but together the combination reads as "performer," which is its own kind of invisible in a festival city.

> *"Nobody looks twice at a performer. The moustache says 'I am in a costume.' The beret says 'I do not care that you know.' Together? Invisible. Don't change anything."*

**Performance hooks:**

- He takes out a small box of spirit gum and starts reapplying it to the moustache's corners before anyone has agreed to this. He has assumed permission.
- If Jean-Claude asks how Giacinto knows which signals humans read: *"I've made faces for fifty years. I know what people look at."*
- If another PC tries to tell Jean-Claude the disguise doesn't work: Giacinto disagrees with them, loudly, on professional grounds.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Primary Goal** | Have his craft acknowledged and properly maintained |
| **Active Problem** | The moustache's inner-edge seal is starting to lift on the right side |
| **Off-Screen Action** | Preparing ten sets of accessories for registered Beffa teams this week |

The handlers are already in Calveno. These details are available whenever the party is in the right place — use one or two per session day, not all at once. None announce themselves as clues. They read as festival texture until they don't.

**Use these as ambient colour first.** Only give them weight if players reach for them. If no one notices, note it and move on.

---

## Location-Keyed Observations

**Ponte Bassa / Le Paludi canals**

- A pair of small figures in festival half-masks bought one length of rope from a canal supply stall and spent ten minutes watching the boat traffic before leaving without asking for change. The stall keeper mentions it if anyone buys rope — they were very specific about knowing which boatmen sleep aboard overnight.
- A Le Paludi local is grumbling that someone was measuring one of the storm-drain overflow hatches this morning with a knotted cord, called herself a Canal Commission inspector, and had no lantern. The hatch is in a section of the district that has no active maintenance flagged.
- A ferryman points out an access grate in the Le Paludi wall, now set slightly off its seating. He noticed it yesterday. It has not been reported because no one is sure whose job that is during festival week.

**The Bridge / Mercatura**

- A Beffa team registered two days ago under a name no one recognises. Their declared category is "Crowd / Notable." When the registration clerk asked their concept, one of them said: *"We want to know how many people you can move through the pinch point in one minute before the ones at the back lose sight of the ones at the front."* The clerk wrote it down verbatim — in two years of registration he had never received a crowd-compression timing query as a prank concept.
- A small figure in a short cloak has been standing at the same Bridge pillar on two separate mornings, at different hours. Not watching performers. Watching the crowd compress and expand at the narrowest point.

**Ponte Bassa / Moretti & Sons**

- Giacomo Moretti mentions, while filling an order, that a buyer this morning wanted to know which of his regular dock customers take their lunch break aboard their vessel and which come ashore. *"Bought nothing. Asked three questions about my customers and left."* He found it rude. He does not connect it to anything.

**Harbour approach / La Vasca**

- One regular Crown-adjacent commercial observer — a factor's representative who checks the south anchorage every morning and has done so for two years — did not appear on two consecutive days this week. Cobb, if asked, can name which two days. A harbour regular: *"He's never missed a morning run. Someone said his firm called him in. But his firm is closed for the festival."*
- Three small, low-profile fishing hulls arrived at anchor in the outer Calven Roads two nights ago. They are flying no pennant. They have not approached the harbour. They are sitting very still for fishing vessels.

**Velo (festival entertainment district)**

- A blue-caste Grung is watching a crowd performance from the edge of a Velo square. He is not enjoying it. He is watching how the crowd moves when a performer creates a scene — where people face, where the gaps open, how long it takes for a knot of onlookers to dissolve. Jean-Claude can read this immediately *(see Jean-Claude — Handler Recognition below)*.

---

## Jean-Claude — Handler Recognition

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] was blue-caste. He ran capture operations. He knows the difference between a Grung enjoying a city and a Grung working one.

If Jean-Claude is in any public space, offer him one of these — once per day, quiet and unprompted. Do not offer more than one per session:

- **Crowd positioning.** A Grung at the Bridge or Velo is standing in the one position that gives them sightlines to three exits without appearing to watch any of them. Jean-Claude has stood in that position. It is not instinctive unless someone taught you to stand there.
- **Target assessment.** A small figure in festival colours near the harbour briefly looks at a working dockhand — takes in his build, his tools, whether he is wearing a guild mark — and looks away. It is not a glance. It is an appraisal. Jean-Claude has made that look hundreds of times.
- **Exit logic.** One of the trade-cover Grung in the city walks a specific Le Paludi route twice. Not shopping. Not visiting anyone. Walking the route at pace and marking the time. Jean-Claude recognises it: someone ran that route and handed the time to the handlers.

None of these are proof. All of them are dread.

> [!dm]
> Offer these as private sensory notes to Jean-Claude's player: *"That Grung's been standing in the exit-watch position for ten minutes."* Let the player decide what Jean-Claude does with it. Do not announce to the table.

---

## Grung-Normalizing Pranks

![[grung-mask-vendor-stylefix.webp|Archer-style adult animated illustration, clean vector-like linework, strong ink contours, cel-shaded lighting, poster-composition staging, expressive grounded faces, saturated adventure palette. Scene art, 16:9 widescreen cinematic. A Velo mask vendor's stall during La Finestra, packed with green Grung masks with wide mouths painted in caste colours hanging from hooks; majority-human festival-goers try them on and laugh, with visible minority populations of Rattkin, lizardfolk, aarakocra, elves, dwarves, and orcs in the street. Across the narrow street, a small figure in a hat and oversized cloak watches quietly. Dense Calveno festival street, masks, awnings, canal stone, comic mood with a surveillance undertone. No written symbols or labels. Negative constraints: no text, no watermarks, no logos, no gore, no photorealism, no anime/chibi, no pixel art, no stock-photo aesthetic.]]

During La Finestra, several Beffa pranks incorporate Grung elements — costumes, props, themes. These are not coincidences. Shadowy figures (purple-caste handlers in bad disguises) paid Calveno locals to make Grung a part of their prank this year. The effect: by Day 3 of the festival, seeing a small green figure in the streets reads as "Beffa costume" rather than "foreign threat."

These are background texture unless the party investigates. If they do, the trail leads to handlers.

**Ponte Bassa / Le Paludi:**

- A Beffa team executes a prank in which a "Grung raider" leaps from a canal boat and "kidnaps" a mark's lunch from his hands. The crowd laughs. The Grung costume is surprisingly accurate — the proportions are right, the colouring is specific, and the standing leap is real. The performer is short, very agile, and leaves before anyone asks questions. If anyone investigates: the performer was hired three days ago by a stranger in a hat who paid 10 gp and asked no questions.

**The Bridge / Mercatura:**

- A street comedian near the registration desk is doing a bit about Grung raiders showing up to register for the Beffa. *"What's your team name?" "The Snatch-and-Grab." "And your mark?" "Everyone."* The crowd treats it as absurdist humour. The comedian was paid 5 gp by a small figure with a moustache who said it was "for the festival spirit." If pushed: the figure had an accent the comedian couldn't place and skin he thought was painted.

**Velo (festival entertainment district):**

- A mask vendor is selling a new line of "Grung masks" — green, wide-mouthed, painted with caste colours. They are selling well. The vendor says a supplier approached him a week before the festival with the moulds and a bulk discount he couldn't refuse. The supplier was accompanied by two assistants in hats who did not speak.

> [!dm]
> None of these are flagged as suspicious by the city. During La Finestra, strange costumes and themed pranks are the norm. The Grung-normalizing effect is deliberate: by the time a real Grung emerges from a sewer breach on Day 5, the crowd's first instinct is "another Beffa bit." The desensitization is the point. If the party investigates the money trail behind any of these pranks, it leads to a purple-caste handler — fake moustache, bad hat, amphibian skin under the festival cloak. Catching one is a raid-disruption beat ([[calveno-beffa-grung-raid#Blocks — How the Party Can Disrupt This|Blocks]]).

---

## If Players Pull On Any Of This

Give the next layer, not the answer.

| They investigate... | What they find |
|---|---|
| The Canal Commission inspector with no lantern | No inspector matching the description is on duty this week. The hatch she was measuring connects to the main collector under the Mercatura. |
| The Beffa registration entry | The registered team name is a string of words in a Verdant Teeth dialect. Roughly: "the patience of still water." |
| The three anchored hulls | They are low-profile, sealed with dark resin, double-outrigged, and too clean for fishing. Anyone with Grung or Midchain maritime knowledge identifies them as *vethka*. They are sitting on the seaward side of the patrol minimum. |
| The missing Crown observer | His firm confirms they did not call him in. He has not reported to work. He is not at his rooms. His landlady says he left with a small bag three nights ago and seemed calm. |
| The Velo Grung watching the crowd | If approached, he is polite and says he is here for the festival. His Midchain accent is from Karath, not Veth. He has no trade goods, no festival registration, and no declared purpose for being this far west. |
