Jean-Claude was blue-caste. He ran capture operations. He knows the difference between a Grung enjoying a city and a Grung working one.

If Jean-Claude is in any public space, offer him one of these — once per day, quiet and unprompted. Do not offer more than one per session:

  • Crowd positioning. A Grung at the Bridge or Velo is standing in the one position that gives them sightlines to three exits without appearing to watch any of them. Jean-Claude has stood in that position. It is not instinctive unless someone taught you to stand there.
  • Target assessment. A small figure in festival colours near the harbour briefly looks at a working dockhand — takes in his build, his tools, whether he is wearing a guild mark — and looks away. It is not a glance. It is an appraisal. Jean-Claude has made that look hundreds of times.
  • Exit logic. One of the trade-cover Grung in the city walks a specific Le Paludi route twice. Not shopping. Not visiting anyone. Walking the route at pace and marking the time. Jean-Claude recognises it: someone ran that route and handed the time to the handlers.

None of these are proof. All of them are dread.

DM Note

Offer these as private sensory notes to Jean-Claude’s player:

“That Grung’s been standing in the exit-watch position for ten minutes.” Let the player decide what Jean-Claude does with it. Do not announce to the table.

Grung-Normalizing Pranks

During La Finestra, several Beffa pranks incorporate Grung elements — costumes, props, themes. These are not coincidences. Shadowy figures (purple-caste handlers in bad disguises) paid Calveno locals to make Grung a part of their prank this year. The effect: by Day 3 of the festival, seeing a small green figure in the streets reads as “Beffa costume” rather than “foreign threat.”

These are background texture unless the party investigates. If they do, the trail leads to handlers.

Ponte Bassa / Le Paludi:

  • A Beffa team executes a prank in which a “Grung raider” leaps from a canal boat and “kidnaps” a mark’s lunch from his hands. The crowd laughs. The Grung costume is surprisingly accurate — the proportions are right, the colouring is specific, and the standing leap is real. The performer is short, very agile, and leaves before anyone asks questions. If anyone investigates: the performer was hired three days ago by a stranger in a hat who paid 10 gp and asked no questions.

The Bridge / Mercatura:

  • A street comedian near the registration desk is doing a bit about Grung raiders showing up to register for the Beffa. “What’s your team name?” “The Snatch-and-Grab.” “And your mark?” “Everyone.” The crowd treats it as absurdist humour. The comedian was paid 5 gp by a small figure with a moustache who said it was “for the festival spirit.” If pushed: the figure had an accent the comedian couldn’t place and skin he thought was painted.

Velo (festival entertainment district):

  • A mask vendor is selling a new line of “Grung masks” — green, wide-mouthed, painted with caste colours. They are selling well. The vendor says a supplier approached him a week before the festival with the moulds and a bulk discount he couldn’t refuse. The supplier was accompanied by two assistants in hats who did not speak.
DM Note

None of these are flagged as suspicious by the city. During La Finestra, strange costumes and themed pranks are the norm. The Grung-normalizing effect is deliberate: by the time a real Grung emerges from a sewer breach on Day 5, the crowd’s first instinct is “another Beffa bit.” The desensitization is the point. If the party investigates the money trail behind any of these pranks, it leads to a purple-caste handler — fake moustache, bad hat, amphibian skin under the festival cloak. Catching one is a raid-disruption beat (Blocks).

# Calveno Sandbox Run Guide

## Island Premise

Use after the Calveno approach puts the *[[hcs-surety|Uncertainty]]* into [[la-vasca|La Vasca]]. The ship is no longer the whole play space. It is the party's live problem inside a city that can answer almost any direction they choose with a person, a price, and a consequence.

Keep the first Calveno days open. [[branca|Branca]], [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]], [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]], the [[il-gioco-delle-beffe|Beffa]], shops, rumours, and the Warren are not a scene order.

## Strong Start

> [!read-aloud]
> The cradle under the *Surety* begins to groan upward, wet timber and iron taking the ship's weight one slow inch at a time. Beyond La Vasca's stone arch, Calveno keeps moving: a skiff glides past with festival cloth piled higher than its pilot, voices carry down the Le Paludi canal in fragments of bargaining and laughter, and somewhere farther up toward the Mercatura a bell marks the turn of the working day. Sem is already naming repairs. Cobb is already naming who will hear you are here.

Then stop. Ask what matters first: the ship, Perrin's family, supplies, a look at the city, privacy, money, worship, a side commission, or something else.

## The Festival Is Background

The [[il-gioco-delle-beffe|Beffa]] runs during the party's Calveno stay and does not require their participation. If they ignore it, it proceeds — cloth in the streets, nervous marks, rival team gossip, daily results at sundown. Use it as ambient city texture and as a clock (five days of structured cover). Only build it as a scene if the players ask, follow crowds, or actively engage.

The non-Festival islands below are the primary sandbox content. They do not depend on the Beffa and do not close if the festival ends.

---

## Rides

Five rides for this city. Each one connects to the party goal (hide the Surety, navigate what the city wants in return) and serves specific players. None are scripted — all have open outcomes.

---

### The Warren Route

*Players: Perrin · Delmar*
*Goal connection: De-marks the Surety and buys five weeks before courtesy-stop watch lists harden*

[[savia-brentino|Savia Brentino]] at the [[carpenters-slip|Carpenters' Slip]] does hull work without Canal Commission filings. She will not take a cold approach — three ships this month already tried and are now on her list. A [[the-passage|Passage]]/Warren introduction changes the shape of the request. The job is 220 gp and five city days, plus one Tangle favour: recorded but unassigned. Complication: Savia says it once, flatly, at the end of the assessment — *"She'll still read as a cutter to anyone who knows cutters. That's not a paint problem."* The party decides what that means and what they do about the bow registry plate.

### Nona's Table

*Players: Perrin (primary) · anyone who follows*
*Goal connection: Opens the Warren network — ship papers, intelligence, hidden routes, full Tangle access*

[[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] already knows Perrin is here. The reunion happens in [[warren|the Warren]], in her kitchen, with full Black-Jaw hospitality: food first, talk second, terms third. Complication: Nona does not yet know the [[vestra|Vestra]] is gone. She will name what the Tangle is owed before the meal is done — not as a threat, as an accounting. The favour balance is real. The party owes more than they have been told.

### Red Lady Salvage Money

*Players: Delmar · Crissdalynn*
*Goal connection: Names who is racing the party to the Maw and how far ahead they are*

Unusual broker rates are moving through Calveno toward a salvage commission targeting the [[red-lady|Red Lady]]. [[batta-zusto|Batta Zusto]] on the Bridge's top tier is the accessible link between the money and the unknown spender. He will trade the commissioner's name for a confirmed cut of the actual salvage. Complication: Accepting Zusto's terms makes the party's Red Lady interest public in the city where Tessarine factors record everything. The same broker network that surfaces the wreck for them will also report what they asked about.

### The Handler Cell

*Players: Jean-Claude (primary) · all when it escalates*
*Goal connection: Disrupts [[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]]'s raid preparation; earns standing with the Warren's intelligence network*

Blue-caste Grung handlers are running reconnaissance in Calveno under festival cover. Jean-Claude is the only one in the party who can read what they are doing. If he acts — follows, confronts, captures, or reports to [[warren|the Warren]] — the raid loses a lane. Complication: Acting makes the party visible to Simone's network. Not acting lets the prep complete unobserved. A third option exists: take a handler alive. That handler knows the extraction plan. That handler also knows Jean-Claude's face and has a report to file. Combat: [[calveno-street-encounters|Calveno — Street Encounters]], "Handler Cell."

### Il Gioco delle Beffe

*Players: all*
*Goal connection: Festival cover for five days; civic reputation; the Beffa's normalizing effect accelerates the raid threat*

Registration opens the morning after the Surety docks. [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]] has an unbroken twenty-year Accord record and the committee finds this professionally embarrassing. The party can enter, bet, watch, recruit contacts, or use the five-day window as cover for other work. Complication: The Beffa trains Calveno to enjoy public deception and to hesitate before taking a staged scene seriously. Simone's handlers are operating under exactly that cover. Every day the festival runs without interruption is a day the raid's window grows easier to hold open.

---

## How the Rides Connect

**The Warren Route** needs **Nona's Table** first. The Tangle introduction comes through Nona — a cold approach to Savia fails. If the party goes to Savia without Nona, she refuses and adds them to her list of suspicious vessels. If the route goes clean, the Tangle holds a favour payable on its own schedule.

[[warren-nonas-table|**Nona's Table**]] opens three follow-on islands regardless of whether the Warren Route is requested: [[warren-bela-silt-paw|Bela Silt-Paw]] (timed — 2 to 3 days), [[warren-marrows-crate|Marrow's Crate]] (leads to [[warren-ferrin-locke|Ferrin Locke]] and the handler network), and Ferrin Locke (the leak, Serin Haut, and the Petra Venn thread). None of these require the ship job.

[[red-lady-salvage-money|**Red Lady Salvage Money**]] runs independently from Day 1. If Delmar or Crissdalynn ask loudly or feed the broker network, the commission assembles faster. Accepting Zusto's terms makes their interest visible to the same network Tessarine factors use — which may reach the commission's backer before the party reaches the Maw.

**The Handler Cell** connects to the Grung raid ([[calveno-beffa-grung-raid|see active situation]]). Disrupting one cell removes one extraction lane; the raid's overall clock continues until the plan is exposed at a higher level. If Jean-Claude does not act, Simone learns the party is in Calveno through other observation anyway — the timing is less certain but the exposure comes.

**Il Gioco delle Beffe** cannot be meaningfully stopped. Its connection to the Handler Cell is environmental: the more the festival normalizes staged scenes, the more the raid depends on Calveno hesitating at the critical moment. If the party engages the Beffa seriously, they gain social capital and festival cover that can serve all other rides. If they ignore it, it still moves — and the hesitation still builds.

## Run Calveno By These Rules

1. **Answer intention, not route.** If they want supplies, give a chandler. If they want rumours, give a table, ferryman, queue, shrine, or market stall. If they want privacy, make the cost visible.
2. **Every useful answer has a witness.** Calveno records people through memory, public deals, favours, ledgers, and who saw whom in which boat.
3. **Private access costs one thing.** Pick coin, a favour, a referral, a delay, or exposure. Do not charge all five unless they are pushing into a protected secret.
4. **Put PC gravity in the first layer.** Family and Passage pull Perrin. Maw salvage and Umberlee pull Delmar. Kyzil and Red Lady traces pull Crissdalynn. Grung range, slavery, and handler logic pull Jean-Claude.
5. **Tick clocks for elapsed time and ignored pressure.** Do not punish a choice by making its unchosen alternatives vanish. Let them move.

## Secrets And Clues

Keep these unassigned. Give them to the first action that earns them.

- A Calveno repaint does not erase a Crown cutter's silhouette. False papers and plate choices matter.
- Cobb reporting Perrin is not betrayal. It is how Black-Jaw help works.
- Nona does not yet know the *[[vestra|Vestra]]* is gone.
- The city is preparing for a festival that rewards public deception and clean recovery.
- Three vessels have already asked Savia about discreet work this month.
- Unusual broker money is building a Maw salvage job aimed at the *Red Lady*.
- One sailor can name a recent Grung strike farther west than old assumptions allowed.
- One harbour regular can name a Crown-adjacent commercial eye that is absent on a schedule someone knew in advance.
- Branca has waited in Calveno because Umberlee knew Delmar was coming before he did.
- Kyzil searched east of Midchain, corrected course, and arrived because Crissdalynn was seen alive.

**Raid-adjacent (use one if players are looking in the right direction):**

- The sewer collector under the Mercatura has three access hatches. Two were opened and re-seated sometime this week. The Canal Commission has no record of it because their festival-week inspection cycle skips that section.
- The Dravosi patrol schedule for the Calven Roads has a three-day minimum gap starting on Day 4 of the Beffa. It is not secret. Any harbour factor with the right contacts can quote the dates. The question is who else already has them.
- The Beffa Medallion committee clerk noticed that one registered team — small, masked, extremely specific about crowd timing — never came back to verify their symbol registration. Teams who don't return for verification are automatically disqualified. This has never happened before.

## If They Surprise You

Use this four-step answer.

1. **Place the request.** ([[calveno-districts|district map]]) Public deal: Mercatura or Bridge. Quiet practical work: Le Paludi. Vice, music, strange trade: Velo. Official ship scale: Arsenal edge or outer harbour.
2. **Give one competent local.** They know their work and want something small now: a sale, a witness, a referral, a favour, a better story, or not to be dragged into trouble.
3. **Attach one live pressure.** Pick ship exposure, Warren memory, Beffa bustle, Tessarine ledgers, Red Lady salvage, or Grung foreshadowing.
4. **Let the choice stand.** If the party declines, note what changed and move the clock. Do not have a different NPC repeat the same hook until they comply.

## Session Priorities

- Make the ship the first priority, then decide how much Warren credit or public yard exposure that is worth.
- Follow personal pressure first: Perrin into family, Delmar toward Branca or Maw salvage, Crissdalynn toward Kyzil or Red Lady traces, Jean-Claude toward anti-slavery and Grung oddities.
- Treat Calveno as a city to use: shop, gossip, worship, bet, explore, make money, or make a private arrangement for a public problem.

## Rewards and Costs

- **Rewards:** repaired ship progress, papers or referrals, Calveno reputation, festival play, Warren trust, salvage intelligence, new local faces.
- **Costs:** Tangle debt, observed deals, city days spent, Crown exposure left unresolved, Tessarine or broker attention, pressure the party lets move off-screen.

## Exit States

- **Resolved:** the party has picked its first Calveno priorities, the *Surety* work is moving, and each engaged pressure has a clear next state.
- **Complicated:** they get what they asked for through a favour, witness, delay, or risky referral that will matter later.
- **Ignored:** the ship work and city clocks move anyway; Nona, the Beffa, salvage money, and converging NPCs choose their own next appearances.

## Agency Guardrails

- Do not turn Perrin's family route into a city guide service. It solves access and creates relationship pressure.
- Do not force [[branca|Branca]], [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]], [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]], or the [[il-gioco-delle-beffe|Beffa]] into a fixed order. They each move when their own condition is met.
- Do not use shops as menus only. Each visit should reveal a person and a Calveno pressure, even if the answer is just a sale.
- Do not make surprise plans fail because the planned hook was elsewhere. Charge a Calveno cost and let the new direction become real.
- Do not resolve the hidden raid or salvage truth through ambient exposition. Foreshadow conditions first.

Calveno Sandbox Run Guide

Island Premise

Use after the Calveno approach puts the Uncertainty into La Vasca. The ship is no longer the whole play space. It is the party’s live problem inside a city that can answer almost any direction they choose with a person, a price, and a consequence.

Keep the first Calveno days open. Branca, Master Kyzil, Nona Black-Jaw, the Beffa, shops, rumours, and the Warren are not a scene order.

Strong Start

Read Aloud

The cradle under the

Surety begins to groan upward, wet timber and iron taking the ship’s weight one slow inch at a time. Beyond La Vasca’s stone arch, Calveno keeps moving: a skiff glides past with festival cloth piled higher than its pilot, voices carry down the Le Paludi canal in fragments of bargaining and laughter, and somewhere farther up toward the Mercatura a bell marks the turn of the working day. Sem is already naming repairs. Cobb is already naming who will hear you are here.

Then stop. Ask what matters first: the ship, Perrin’s family, supplies, a look at the city, privacy, money, worship, a side commission, or something else.

The Festival Is Background

The Beffa runs during the party’s Calveno stay and does not require their participation. If they ignore it, it proceeds — cloth in the streets, nervous marks, rival team gossip, daily results at sundown. Use it as ambient city texture and as a clock (five days of structured cover). Only build it as a scene if the players ask, follow crowds, or actively engage.

The non-Festival islands below are the primary sandbox content. They do not depend on the Beffa and do not close if the festival ends.

Rides

Five rides for this city. Each one connects to the party goal (hide the Surety, navigate what the city wants in return) and serves specific players. None are scripted — all have open outcomes.

The Warren Route

Players: Perrin · Delmar Goal connection: De-marks the Surety and buys five weeks before courtesy-stop watch lists harden

Savia Brentino at the Carpenters’ Slip does hull work without Canal Commission filings. She will not take a cold approach — three ships this month already tried and are now on her list. A Passage/Warren introduction changes the shape of the request. The job is 220 gp and five city days, plus one Tangle favour: recorded but unassigned. Complication: Savia says it once, flatly, at the end of the assessment — “She’ll still read as a cutter to anyone who knows cutters. That’s not a paint problem.” The party decides what that means and what they do about the bow registry plate.

Nona’s Table

Players: Perrin (primary) · anyone who follows Goal connection: Opens the Warren network — ship papers, intelligence, hidden routes, full Tangle access

Nona Black-Jaw already knows Perrin is here. The reunion happens in the Warren, in her kitchen, with full Black-Jaw hospitality: food first, talk second, terms third. Complication: Nona does not yet know the Vestra is gone. She will name what the Tangle is owed before the meal is done — not as a threat, as an accounting. The favour balance is real. The party owes more than they have been told.

Red Lady Salvage Money

Players: Delmar · Crissdalynn Goal connection: Names who is racing the party to the Maw and how far ahead they are

Unusual broker rates are moving through Calveno toward a salvage commission targeting the Red Lady. Batta Zusto on the Bridge’s top tier is the accessible link between the money and the unknown spender. He will trade the commissioner’s name for a confirmed cut of the actual salvage. Complication: Accepting Zusto’s terms makes the party’s Red Lady interest public in the city where Tessarine factors record everything. The same broker network that surfaces the wreck for them will also report what they asked about.

The Handler Cell

Players: Jean-Claude (primary) · all when it escalates Goal connection: Disrupts Simone Tabarnack‘s raid preparation; earns standing with the Warren’s intelligence network

Blue-caste Grung handlers are running reconnaissance in Calveno under festival cover. Jean-Claude is the only one in the party who can read what they are doing. If he acts — follows, confronts, captures, or reports to the Warren — the raid loses a lane. Complication: Acting makes the party visible to Simone’s network. Not acting lets the prep complete unobserved. A third option exists: take a handler alive. That handler knows the extraction plan. That handler also knows Jean-Claude’s face and has a report to file. Combat: Calveno — Street Encounters, “Handler Cell.”

Il Gioco delle Beffe

Players: all Goal connection: Festival cover for five days; civic reputation; the Beffa’s normalizing effect accelerates the raid threat

Registration opens the morning after the Surety docks. Giacomo Moretti has an unbroken twenty-year Accord record and the committee finds this professionally embarrassing. The party can enter, bet, watch, recruit contacts, or use the five-day window as cover for other work. Complication: The Beffa trains Calveno to enjoy public deception and to hesitate before taking a staged scene seriously. Simone’s handlers are operating under exactly that cover. Every day the festival runs without interruption is a day the raid’s window grows easier to hold open.

How the Rides Connect

The Warren Route needs Nona’s Table first. The Tangle introduction comes through Nona — a cold approach to Savia fails. If the party goes to Savia without Nona, she refuses and adds them to her list of suspicious vessels. If the route goes clean, the Tangle holds a favour payable on its own schedule.

[[warren-nonas-table|Nona’s Table]] opens three follow-on islands regardless of whether the Warren Route is requested: Bela Silt-Paw (timed — 2 to 3 days), Marrow’s Crate (leads to Ferrin Locke and the handler network), and Ferrin Locke (the leak, Serin Haut, and the Petra Venn thread). None of these require the ship job.

[[red-lady-salvage-money|Red Lady Salvage Money]] runs independently from Day 1. If Delmar or Crissdalynn ask loudly or feed the broker network, the commission assembles faster. Accepting Zusto’s terms makes their interest visible to the same network Tessarine factors use — which may reach the commission’s backer before the party reaches the Maw.

The Handler Cell connects to the Grung raid (see active situation). Disrupting one cell removes one extraction lane; the raid’s overall clock continues until the plan is exposed at a higher level. If Jean-Claude does not act, Simone learns the party is in Calveno through other observation anyway — the timing is less certain but the exposure comes.

Il Gioco delle Beffe cannot be meaningfully stopped. Its connection to the Handler Cell is environmental: the more the festival normalizes staged scenes, the more the raid depends on Calveno hesitating at the critical moment. If the party engages the Beffa seriously, they gain social capital and festival cover that can serve all other rides. If they ignore it, it still moves — and the hesitation still builds.

Run Calveno By These Rules

  1. Answer intention, not route. If they want supplies, give a chandler. If they want rumours, give a table, ferryman, queue, shrine, or market stall. If they want privacy, make the cost visible.
  2. Every useful answer has a witness. Calveno records people through memory, public deals, favours, ledgers, and who saw whom in which boat.
  3. Private access costs one thing. Pick coin, a favour, a referral, a delay, or exposure. Do not charge all five unless they are pushing into a protected secret.
  4. Put PC gravity in the first layer. Family and Passage pull Perrin. Maw salvage and Umberlee pull Delmar. Kyzil and Red Lady traces pull Crissdalynn. Grung range, slavery, and handler logic pull Jean-Claude.
  5. Tick clocks for elapsed time and ignored pressure. Do not punish a choice by making its unchosen alternatives vanish. Let them move.

Loaded Guns

Secrets And Clues

Keep these unassigned. Give them to the first action that earns them.

  • A Calveno repaint does not erase a Crown cutter’s silhouette. False papers and plate choices matter.
  • Cobb reporting Perrin is not betrayal. It is how Black-Jaw help works.
  • Nona does not yet know the Vestra is gone.
  • The city is preparing for a festival that rewards public deception and clean recovery.
  • Three vessels have already asked Savia about discreet work this month.
  • Unusual broker money is building a Maw salvage job aimed at the Red Lady.
  • One sailor can name a recent Grung strike farther west than old assumptions allowed.
  • One harbour regular can name a Crown-adjacent commercial eye that is absent on a schedule someone knew in advance.
  • Branca has waited in Calveno because Umberlee knew Delmar was coming before he did.
  • Kyzil searched east of Midchain, corrected course, and arrived because Crissdalynn was seen alive.

Raid-adjacent (use one if players are looking in the right direction):

  • The sewer collector under the Mercatura has three access hatches. Two were opened and re-seated sometime this week. The Canal Commission has no record of it because their festival-week inspection cycle skips that section.
  • The Dravosi patrol schedule for the Calven Roads has a three-day minimum gap starting on Day 4 of the Beffa. It is not secret. Any harbour factor with the right contacts can quote the dates. The question is who else already has them.
  • The Beffa Medallion committee clerk noticed that one registered team — small, masked, extremely specific about crowd timing — never came back to verify their symbol registration. Teams who don’t return for verification are automatically disqualified. This has never happened before.

If They Surprise You

Use this four-step answer.

  1. Place the request. (district map) Public deal: Mercatura or Bridge. Quiet practical work: Le Paludi. Vice, music, strange trade: Velo. Official ship scale: Arsenal edge or outer harbour.
  2. Give one competent local. They know their work and want something small now: a sale, a witness, a referral, a favour, a better story, or not to be dragged into trouble.
  3. Attach one live pressure. Pick ship exposure, Warren memory, Beffa bustle, Tessarine ledgers, Red Lady salvage, or Grung foreshadowing.
  4. Let the choice stand. If the party declines, note what changed and move the clock. Do not have a different NPC repeat the same hook until they comply.

Raid Prep — What the City Is Already Showing

The handlers are already in Calveno. Location-keyed observations and Jean-Claude handler recognition beats — one or two per session day, used as ambient colour — are in the full reference file.

→ Calveno — Raid Prep Signs

Session Priorities

  • Make the ship the first priority, then decide how much Warren credit or public yard exposure that is worth.
  • Follow personal pressure first: Perrin into family, Delmar toward Branca or Maw salvage, Crissdalynn toward Kyzil or Red Lady traces, Jean-Claude toward anti-slavery and Grung oddities.
  • Treat Calveno as a city to use: shop, gossip, worship, bet, explore, make money, or make a private arrangement for a public problem.

Rewards and Costs

  • Rewards: repaired ship progress, papers or referrals, Calveno reputation, festival play, Warren trust, salvage intelligence, new local faces.
  • Costs: Tangle debt, observed deals, city days spent, Crown exposure left unresolved, Tessarine or broker attention, pressure the party lets move off-screen.

Exit States

  • Resolved: the party has picked its first Calveno priorities, the Surety work is moving, and each engaged pressure has a clear next state.
  • Complicated: they get what they asked for through a favour, witness, delay, or risky referral that will matter later.
  • Ignored: the ship work and city clocks move anyway; Nona, the Beffa, salvage money, and converging NPCs choose their own next appearances.

Agency Guardrails

  • Do not turn Perrin’s family route into a city guide service. It solves access and creates relationship pressure.
  • Do not force Branca, Master Kyzil, Nona Black-Jaw, or the Beffa into a fixed order. They each move when their own condition is met.
  • Do not use shops as menus only. Each visit should reveal a person and a Calveno pressure, even if the answer is just a sale.
  • Do not make surprise plans fail because the planned hook was elsewhere. Charge a Calveno cost and let the new direction become real.
  • Do not resolve the hidden raid or salvage truth through ambient exposition. Foreshadow conditions first.

# Calveno — Street Encounters

Drop these when the scene needs texture, the party is restless, or you want to press a specific PC. None are mandatory. All can be played social-first and allowed to escalate, or bypassed entirely with no consequence.

## 1. The Wrong Mark

**Setup:** A Beffa team — three young [[calveno|Calveno]] dockworkers with a bucket of fish oil, a rope, and a signed permission slip from someone they have clearly coerced — has targeted one of the party as their mark. They have been following for two blocks. They have the wrong person, and they are about to commit.

> [!read-aloud]
> The oil lands before the sound reaches you — a wide cold splash from above, and a cheer from the balcony. Three young Calvenans lean over the railing, rope still swinging. The crowd turns. Someone laughs. The smell arrives a moment later: fish, and not the fresh kind.

**What happens:** DC 12 Dexterity save or the PC is drenched in fish oil and loses the contents of one jacket pocket to the splash.

**If pursued:** Three Commoners and one Spy (the team captain). Catch check: DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics through festival crowd. If cornered: they fold immediately. They have a written Beffa permit, a team name (*La Trota Gloriosa*), and a completely wrong name for their intended target.

> [!dm]
> Pull this when the Beffa needs to feel real and ambient rather than plot-adjacent. The permit is real. The name on it belongs to a Tessarine factor who has been running a Beffa team for six years and apparently has enemies — a loose thread, not a prepared character.

## 2. Ponte Muscle

**Setup:** A broad man in a dockworker's coat is blocking a canal walkway on one of the Bridge district footbridges, collecting a "festival toll" from anyone trying to cross. Two friends wait on the far side. The man they are currently collecting from is clearly not going to pay.

> [!read-aloud]
> A broad man in a dockworker's coat stands in the middle of the walkway. Not moving through it — standing in it. His two friends wait on the far side of the bridge. There is a man between him and you who is nearly out of options.

**What the party can do:**

- Pay (2 cp each — this is about the delay, not the money)
- Push past without paying: DC 10 Persuasion or Intimidation; failure brings the two friends off the far side
- Intervene for the man being held: the man being held turns out to be a Passage runner for a Warren contact, and [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]] hears about it within a day

> [!mechanic]
> If combat: 1 Thug (leader, AC 11, HP 32, club +4, 2d4+2) and 2 Bandits (AC 12, HP 11, scimitar +3, 1d6+1). They do not fight to the death — at half HP the leader calls it off.

> [!dm]
> The Passage runner is named Orso. He is not a significant character. If the party helps him, Nona knows before they reach the Warren. She does not mention it first; she waits to see if they do.

## 3. The Chase

**Setup:** Someone has just lifted a purse — either from a party member or from a well-dressed merchant who immediately starts screaming. The thief is already moving, weaving into the Beffa crowd.

> [!read-aloud]
> A hand lifts clean from a coat pocket and disappears into the crowd. The merchant reaches for his purse and finds air. He spins in a full circle. Ten feet ahead of you, a small shape is already three bodies deep and not slowing down.

**The thief:** Fen, a teenage halfling, fast and small, working the festival crowds for three days. Not violent. Not part of any operation. Use Spy stats, +5 Stealth, +5 Acrobatics.

> [!mechanic]
> **Chase structure:** Three checks, each DC 12. Acrobatics for cutting through the crowd, Athletics for straightaways, Perception to keep eyes on. Two successes: cornered in a dead-end calle off Le Paludi. One success: Fen makes it to a canal and goes in the water (swim check, then either resurfaces in the Rialto or ducks into a maintenance hatch). Zero successes: gone.

**If cornered:** Fen has the purse, a folding knife she will not use, and a sob story that is about 40% true. DC 14 Insight to pick the true parts. The true part: she is paying off a debt to a Bridge district broker who found her working his territory.

> [!dm]
> Fen carries a maintenance hatch key she will not explain. It fits the sewer network below the Bridge connector. She doesn't know this — she stole it thinking it was worth something. It is worth something. Leave it in her possession unless the party is specifically looking for it. The key is a loaded gun for the [[warren-grung-sewers|Warren — Grung in the Sewers]] investigation.

## 4. A Man in the Canal

**Setup:** Late evening, narrow calle beside a Le Paludi canal. A man goes in — tripped by festival crowd surge, pushed by persons unknown, or stepped off a gangplank he misjudged. He is not swimming. The canal current runs under a low stone arch twelve feet away; past the arch it is dark and fast.

> [!read-aloud]
> The sound is wrong — not a splash, a drop. A man surfaces in the canal beside the walkway, already turned the wrong direction. He is not swimming. Twelve feet ahead, the canal narrows under a stone arch into the dark. The current is pulling.

> [!mechanic]
> Two rounds before he goes under the arch. DC 10 Athletics to swim out in round one; DC 12 in round two (current pulling). A rope thrown from the bank: DC 10 Dexterity to land it on him, DC 12 Strength to haul against the current. A boat pole, a Beffa banner pole, an awning rope — the canal side has options if someone looks (DC 8 Perception).

**Who he is (roll or choose):**

| d4 | Identity | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Tessarine factor's ledger clerk, drunk on festival wine | His employer gives the party a minor factor discount as thanks — 10% off one Calveno merchant purchase |
| 2 | A Dravosi junior watch officer, off duty and embarrassed | He owes the party a favour he cannot officially acknowledge; the party has his name |
| 3 | A Warren Kin runner, Passage courier | Nona hears. The party's Tangle credit goes up without them knowing why |
| 4 | The thief from encounter 3, if she ran into the canal during the chase | She still has the purse |

> [!dm]
> Use the watch-and-do-nothing outcome only if it creates interesting character pressure, not as punishment.

## 5. Papers at the Gate

**Setup:** A Dravosi canal-gate checkpoint at the entry to the Arsenal district, staffed by one watch sergeant (Veteran) and four guards.

> [!read-aloud]
> The canal gate is a stone arch with a portcullis drawn halfway. A sergeant in Dravosi grey leans against the frame with a ledger. He looks at the party the way men who have been standing in one place for six hours look at things that require effort.

**He wants:** Ship registry or travelling papers. For the *Uncertainty*: the new Calveno private-vessel papers (if Perrin arranged them through the Warren) or an explanation. For PCs on foot: guild affiliation, residential address, or a credible reason to be at the Arsenal end during a festival.

**Delmar:** Any Dravosi officer who has served on this class of cutter will clock the *Uncertainty*'s silhouette. The sergeant has not — he is Canal Commission, not Navy. But DC 14 Charisma (Deception) to maintain the Fisk persona under direct questioning; the sergeant asks the same question twice, slightly differently.

**[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]:** DC 12 Deception with working papers. DC 15 without. If the sergeant has received a flag notice for a deserter matching his description: DC 17, disadvantage.

> [!mechanic]
> **If it goes wrong:** The sergeant calls for two more guards (now 6 total) and asks the party to step to the side. Window for talking out of this closes after three rounds; after that he sends for a lieutenant. Sergeant: Veteran stats (AC 17, HP 58, multiattack, +5 to hit). Guards: AC 16, HP 11, spear +3. The sergeant will not draw first; he will call for backup.

> [!dm]
> This works best as a papers check the party can pass with preparation, not a fight they stumble into. If Perrin handled the Warren ship papers, this is where that investment pays off cleanly.

## 6. The Festival Drunk

**Setup:** The Mercatura, mid-afternoon, festival crowd. A very large half-orc in a sellsword's rig is at the centre of a growing circle of space. He has knocked over a wine stall and is currently singing something in what might be Orcish.

> [!read-aloud]
> A ring of empty space has opened in the Mercatura crowd. At the centre of it, a half-orc in a sellsword's rig holds a wine bottle in one hand and his sword — still sheathed — in the other. A wooden stall is on its side behind him. The stall owner is looking at you.

> [!mechanic]
> **Gost:** Berserker stats, CR 2, AC 13, HP 67, greataxe +5, 2d12+3. Not violent yet. Watch is four minutes away.

**What the party can do:**

- Talk him down: DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) or DC 10 Intimidation. Jean-Claude telling him the watch is coming and this is going to be a bad four minutes: automatic success.
- Get him moving: DC 10 if someone offers to buy him another drink somewhere quieter. No fight, no watch.
- Wait for the watch: Gost ends up in a holding cell.
- Let it escalate: he throws the bottle; now there are two problems.

**If he fights:** Reckless Attack, no Danger Sense (too drunk). First two rounds he is at disadvantage on saves; after that the adrenaline is burning the alcohol.

> [!dm]

## Combat Escalations — Jean-Claude Arc

These three encounters connect to the handler cell plot. Unlike the general encounters above, they require setup: Jean-Claude active in the city, or the party already moving on the [[warren-marrows-crate|Marrow's Crate]] / [[warren-ferrin-locke|Ferrin Locke]] investigation. Do not drop them cold.

### Handler Cell

**Setup:** Jean-Claude spots what looks like handler reconnaissance — a pair of Grung in nondescript trade clothes asking systematic questions about boat shifts, bridge crush timing, or which yard workers sleep aboard. He is the only one in the party who recognises it.

> [!read-aloud]
> Two figures in trade clothes at the same Bridge pillar Jean-Claude clocked earlier — different position now, same posture. They are not watching the performer. They are watching the crowd move around the performer. The hour is wrong for the spot.

**Trigger:** Jean-Claude's player acts on the suspicion (confirms with Insight DC 13, or just acts on it). If the party engages, the handlers try to withdraw and break contact. If cornered, they fight.

**Location:** Le Paludi — narrow canal, 5 ft alleys, two boats tied at the nearest mooring. Poor light. Festival crowd two streets over.

> [!mechanic]
> **Blue-Caste Handler × 2.** HP 16, AC 13. Scout (MM p.349). Shortbow +4, 1d8+3 piercing + Grung Poison (DC 11 Con or Poisoned 1 min). Standing Leap 20 ft as part of movement. Breaks and runs at half HP.

> [!dm]

> [!read-aloud]

1. The Wrong Mark

Setup: A Beffa team — three young Calveno dockworkers with a bucket of fish oil, a rope, and a signed permission slip from someone they have clearly coerced — has targeted one of the party as their mark. They have been following for two blocks. They have the wrong person, and they are about to commit.

Read Aloud

The oil lands before the sound reaches you — a wide cold splash from above, and a cheer from the balcony. Three young Calvenans lean over the railing, rope still swinging. The crowd turns. Someone laughs. The smell arrives a moment later: fish, and not the fresh kind.

What happens: DC 12 Dexterity save or the PC is drenched in fish oil and loses the contents of one jacket pocket to the splash.

If pursued: Three Commoners and one Spy (the team captain). Catch check: DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics through festival crowd. If cornered: they fold immediately. They have a written Beffa permit, a team name (La Trota Gloriosa), and a completely wrong name for their intended target.

DM Note

Pull this when the Beffa needs to feel real and ambient rather than plot-adjacent. The permit is real. The name on it belongs to a Tessarine factor who has been running a Beffa team for six years and apparently has enemies — a loose thread, not a prepared character.

2. Ponte Muscle

Setup: A broad man in a dockworker’s coat is blocking a canal walkway on one of the Bridge district footbridges, collecting a “festival toll” from anyone trying to cross. Two friends wait on the far side. The man they are currently collecting from is clearly not going to pay.

Read Aloud

A broad man in a dockworker’s coat stands in the middle of the walkway. Not moving through it — standing in it. His two friends wait on the far side of the bridge. There is a man between him and you who is nearly out of options.

What the party can do:

  • Pay (2 cp each — this is about the delay, not the money)
  • Push past without paying: DC 10 Persuasion or Intimidation; failure brings the two friends off the far side
  • Intervene for the man being held: the man being held turns out to be a Passage runner for a Warren contact, and Nona hears about it within a day
Mechanic

If combat: 1 Thug (leader, AC 11, HP 32, club +4, 2d4+2) and 2 Bandits (AC 12, HP 11, scimitar +3, 1d6+1). They do not fight to the death — at half HP the leader calls it off.

DM Note

The Passage runner is named Orso. He is not a significant character. If the party helps him, Nona knows before they reach the Warren. She does not mention it first; she waits to see if they do.

3. The Chase

Setup: Someone has just lifted a purse — either from a party member or from a well-dressed merchant who immediately starts screaming. The thief is already moving, weaving into the Beffa crowd.

Read Aloud

A hand lifts clean from a coat pocket and disappears into the crowd. The merchant reaches for his purse and finds air. He spins in a full circle. Ten feet ahead of you, a small shape is already three bodies deep and not slowing down.

The thief: Fen, a teenage halfling, fast and small, working the festival crowds for three days. Not violent. Not part of any operation. Use Spy stats, +5 Stealth, +5 Acrobatics.

Mechanic

Chase structure: Three checks, each DC 12. Acrobatics for cutting through the crowd, Athletics for straightaways, Perception to keep eyes on. Two successes: cornered in a dead-end calle off Le Paludi. One success: Fen makes it to a canal and goes in the water (swim check, then either resurfaces in the Rialto or ducks into a maintenance hatch). Zero successes: gone.

If cornered: Fen has the purse, a folding knife she will not use, and a sob story that is about 40% true. DC 14 Insight to pick the true parts. The true part: she is paying off a debt to a Bridge district broker who found her working his territory.

DM Note

Fen carries a maintenance hatch key she will not explain. It fits the sewer network below the Bridge connector. She doesn’t know this — she stole it thinking it was worth something. It is worth something. Leave it in her possession unless the party is specifically looking for it. The key is a loaded gun for the Warren — Grung in the Sewers investigation.

4. A Man in the Canal

Setup: Late evening, narrow calle beside a Le Paludi canal. A man goes in — tripped by festival crowd surge, pushed by persons unknown, or stepped off a gangplank he misjudged. He is not swimming. The canal current runs under a low stone arch twelve feet away; past the arch it is dark and fast.

Read Aloud

The sound is wrong — not a splash, a drop. A man surfaces in the canal beside the walkway, already turned the wrong direction. He is not swimming. Twelve feet ahead, the canal narrows under a stone arch into the dark. The current is pulling.

Mechanic

Two rounds before he goes under the arch. DC 10 Athletics to swim out in round one; DC 12 in round two (current pulling). A rope thrown from the bank: DC 10 Dexterity to land it on him, DC 12 Strength to haul against the current. A boat pole, a Beffa banner pole, an awning rope — the canal side has options if someone looks (DC 8 Perception).

Who he is (roll or choose):

d4IdentityConsequence
1A Tessarine factor’s ledger clerk, drunk on festival wineHis employer gives the party a minor factor discount as thanks — 10% off one Calveno merchant purchase
2A Dravosi junior watch officer, off duty and embarrassedHe owes the party a favour he cannot officially acknowledge; the party has his name
3A Warren Kin runner, Passage courierNona hears. The party’s Tangle credit goes up without them knowing why
4The thief from encounter 3, if she ran into the canal during the chaseShe still has the purse

Use the watch-and-do-nothing outcome only if it creates interesting character pressure, not as punishment.

5. Papers at the Gate

Setup: A Dravosi canal-gate checkpoint at the entry to the Arsenal district, staffed by one watch sergeant (Veteran) and four guards.

Read Aloud

The canal gate is a stone arch with a portcullis drawn halfway. A sergeant in Dravosi grey leans against the frame with a ledger. He looks at the party the way men who have been standing in one place for six hours look at things that require effort.

He wants: Ship registry or travelling papers. For the Uncertainty: the new Calveno private-vessel papers (if Perrin arranged them through the Warren) or an explanation. For PCs on foot: guild affiliation, residential address, or a credible reason to be at the Arsenal end during a festival.

Delmar: Any Dravosi officer who has served on this class of cutter will clock the Uncertainty’s silhouette. The sergeant has not — he is Canal Commission, not Navy. But DC 14 Charisma (Deception) to maintain the Fisk persona under direct questioning; the sergeant asks the same question twice, slightly differently.

Jean-Claude: DC 12 Deception with working papers. DC 15 without. If the sergeant has received a flag notice for a deserter matching his description: DC 17, disadvantage.

Mechanic

If it goes wrong: The sergeant calls for two more guards (now 6 total) and asks the party to step to the side. Window for talking out of this closes after three rounds; after that he sends for a lieutenant. Sergeant: Veteran stats (AC 17, HP 58, multiattack, +5 to hit). Guards: AC 16, HP 11, spear +3. DM Note

This works best as a papers check the party can pass with preparation, not a fight they stumble into. If Perrin handled the Warren ship papers, this is where that investment pays off cleanly.

6. The Festival Drunk

DM mechanics for running the Beffa as a five-day skill challenge — phase structure, team symbol system, mark selection, rival teams, prize table, and running notes. Beffe registration opens tomorrow morning at the Mercatura bridge.

# Il Gioco delle Beffe — DM Notes

*Public lore: [[il-gioco-delle-beffe|Il Gioco delle Beffe]]*
*Current status: Registration opens tomorrow morning at the Mercatura bridge.*

---

## Situation

The Beffa is a five-day festival structured as a multi-phase team skill challenge. Every party member contributes through their own best skills. The money is real. The social capital is better. The fun comes from asking each player what *their character* does — then assigning skills to match.

The multi-day execution window (Days 2–4) is the core design element. Marks are nervous for three full days. Teams can strike early, wait, or false-alarm their mark first. That uncertainty is the game.

---

## The Team Symbol

On Day One, the party registers their symbol with the committee. Let the players design it — a sigil, a stamp, a wax seal shape, a color band, anything. It belongs to them.

Mechanically, the symbol is proof of authorship. The team must leave it at the scene for the prank to count. How they leave it is their problem and part of the fun. It should be the last thing the mark finds — not a tip-off, not a clue, but a signature delivered after the fall.

**Beffa doppia (optional):** a rival team can attempt to steal the party's registered symbol and place it on their own prank. Requires knowing the symbol (possible if they observed registration) and a contested Stealth check against the party's Perception during Phase 2. If it works, the committee adjudicates. The rules on this are historically contested and the committee enjoys the chaos.

---

## Mark Selection

| Mark | Difficulty | Mark Bonus | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[[giacomo-moretti\|Giacomo Moretti]]** (halfling chandler) | Hard | 20 gp | Twenty-year clean record. Extremely suspicious. Watching for it. |
| **[[iacopo-fieschi\|Iacopo Fieschi]]** (Tessarine envoy) | Medium-Hard | 30–50 gp + Concordat goodwill | First time on the list. Proud. Getting him is a political statement. |
| **Canal Commission inspector** | Medium | 15 gp | Classic target. Expects administrative tricks; theatrical ones catch him. |
| **A Waveservant junior** | Easy | 10 gp + crowd approval | Crowd loves religious targets. Marks often enjoy the goodwill from being a sport. |
| **A Council family member** | Very Hard | 50 gp | The committee has been waiting. High risk, high reward. |

The party may propose their own mark from the Accord list. Assign DC and bonus accordingly.

---

## Phase Structure

### Phase 1 — La Scelta: Design (Day 1)

*No checks. Pure roleplay.*

The party picks their mark, designs their concept, and registers their symbol. The key question is not "what is the prank" but **"what does each character do?"**

| What they say | Likely check |
|---|---|
| "I scout the mark's daily routine" | Investigation or Perception |
| "I create a distraction in the market" | Performance or Deception |
| "I acquire a prop without being noticed" | Sleight of Hand or Stealth |
| "I plant false information in advance" | Deception or Persuasion |
| "I build a physical element" | Tool check or Athletics |
| "I recruit a civilian accomplice" | Persuasion |
| "I research the mark's weaknesses" | History or Insight |
| "I use magic for preparation" | Arcana or direct spell |

**Declare scale:** Minor (DC 12), Notable (DC 14), Legendary (DC 17, 50 gp stake). The party decides.

---

### Phase 2 — La Preparazione: Setup (Days 2–4, any day chosen)

*Each party member makes one check based on Phase 1 commitments.*

The party decides when during the window to strike. Earlier = less risk of sabotage; later = more time to prep and a more relaxed mark.

**Complications on failure:**

- A prop is wrong → disadvantage on one Phase 3 check
- The mark spotted something → raise Phase 3 DC by 2
- A rival team noticed → they attempt a counter move
- A committee adjudicator observed more than intended → pointed question on judgment day

**Rival interference:** one rival team may attempt to sabotage preparation. Contested Stealth vs. Perception. If the rival succeeds, assign a complication. If the party succeeds, they identify the rival — and earn a free sabotage action against them in Phase 3.

**False-alarm gambit:** the party may deliberately tip off their mark on an early day to lower their guard before the real strike. Deception check (DC = mark's Wisdom + 2). Success: mark's Phase 3 save at disadvantage. Failure: mark is now actively suspicious — DC raised by 3.

---

### Phase 3 — L'Esecuzione: The Strike (chosen day)

*Each party member makes one live-pressure check. The mark makes a Wisdom save. The symbol must be placed.*

**The mark's save:** DC = 8 + number of party successes in Phase 2.

- Fails: completely fooled. Scores 4–5.
- Succeeds by 1–4: partially fooled, something felt off. Scores 2–3.
- Succeeds by 5+: spotted the trick. Scores 0–1. The prank still proceeds — craft and recovery can still win it.

**Party checks:** each player makes the execution version of their Phase 2 role. Failure = something goes visibly wrong — crowd notices, judges note it.

**Placing the symbol:** one party member must place the team symbol during or at the end of the prank, without tipping off the mark prematurely. Sleight of Hand or Deception, DC 12. Failure: symbol found too early, reducing Surprise by 1.

**Recovery check:** after the prank, one party member walks it back. Performance or Persuasion (Deception or Medicine as alternates). Good recovery is worth up to 2 extra craft points from the committee.

---

## Rival Teams

Present their results at sundown on Day Five. You do not need to play them out — just describe what happened.

**The Candle Brothers** — two humans, twelve consecutive entries, four second-place finishes. Technically brilliant, emotionally inert. They will score 13–15 regardless of their prank.

**Serena Voss** — a halfling factor who entered on a dare, going for the Tessarine factor as her mark. No team. No experience. One very good idea. Roll her score secretly: 2d6+4. If she rolls high, the party has real competition — and she wants to buy everyone drinks regardless of result.

**Party Unknown** — three people in matching grey coats, registered under a name nobody recognizes, declared "Compound / Legendary," and refused to state their mark. Roll their score at Day Five: 1d20. On 1–8: disqualified (the crowd loves it). On 9–14: score 11. On 15–19: score 16. On 20: score 19 — the party needs to beat or tie this to win.

---

## Scoring

| Element | Maximum | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Craft | 10 | Committee — Phase 2 and 3 quality |
| Surprise | 5 | Mark's self-score |
| Recovery | 5 | Recovery check |
| **Total** | **20** | |

---

## Prize Table

| Party Score | Result | Prize |
|---|---|---|
| Highest | Win | 60% of pool + Beffa Medallion + mark bonus |
| Second | Second | 25% of pool + mark bonus (if applicable) |
| Third | Third | Remainder of pool |
| Below all rivals | Respectable loss | Mark bonus only (if mark was fooled) |
| Disqualified | Disqualified | Stake lost; crowd applauds anyway |

**Pool estimate:** 4 teams × 25 gp standard, plus any Legendary stakes. Typical pool: 125–200 gp. Party wins 60% = 75–120 gp + mark bonus + side bets.

**Side betting:** party may bet on themselves at registration, max 50 gp at 2:1 (Notable) or 4:1 (Legendary).

---

## Key Facts

- [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]]'s plaque entry is the only one without a prank description. He will not explain.
- [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]] signs the Accord every year and enjoys the festival. He finds the attempts flattering. He will never say this.
- Committee adjudicators are genuinely bad at not being noticed. DC 10 Perception identifies one during Phase 2.
- The beffa doppia has succeeded exactly twice in the festival's history. Both rulings took three days. One is still disputed.

---

## Running Notes

**Ask what each character does, not what the plan is.** The party's plan is their business. Your job is to assign a skill to whatever they commit to in Phase 1 and hold them to it in Phase 2.

**Play the mark.** When the prank lands, embody whoever they picked. Be genuinely fooled by good ideas. The mark's reaction is the scene.

**The window creates tension for free.** On Days 2 and 3, describe marks being jumpy, rivals seen in unexpected places, committee adjudicators moving through the district. The uncertainty is doing the work.

**The medallion matters more than the money.** In Calveno, the Beffa Medallion is social proof that you are clever enough to deceive people in public and charming enough to get away with it. The Council cannot buy it. [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] will mention it to [[cosimo-verantio|Cosimo]]. [[prospero-morsani|Morsani]] will nod at the party across the Mercatura, and the nod will mean something.

---

## Involved Parties

- [[giacomo-moretti|Giacomo Moretti]] — twenty-year clean record; extremely suspicious
- [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] — first-year mark; Tessarine implications if pranked
- [[prospero-morsani|Prospero Morsani]] — former winner; present every year; watching
- [[cosimo-verantio|Cosimo Verantio]] — will hear about the result

## Locations

- [[calveno|Calveno]] — the whole city is the stage
- [[moretti-and-sons|Moretti & Sons Chandlery]] — if Giacomo is the mark
- [[cabinet-of-morsani|The Cabinet of Morsani]] — Morsani is here pre-festival

## Consequences

- **Win:** Calveno social capital, medallion on the ship, Cosimo and Fieschi aware, Morsani nods
- **Lose honourably:** mark pays the bonus if the prank was good; Serena Voss wants to buy drinks
- **Disqualified:** the crowd loves a dramatic disqualification; not actually bad for reputation

Mechanically, the symbol is proof of authorship. The team must leave it at the scene for the prank to count. How they leave it is their problem and part of the fun. It should be the last thing the mark finds — not a tip-off, not a clue, but a signature delivered after the fall.

Beffa doppia (optional): a rival team can attempt to steal the party’s registered symbol and place it on their own prank. Requires knowing the symbol (possible if they observed registration) and a contested Stealth check against the party’s Perception during Phase 2. If it works, the committee adjudicates. The rules on this are historically contested and the committee enjoys the chaos.

Mark Selection

MarkDifficultyMark BonusNotes
Giacomo Moretti (halfling chandler)Hard20 gpTwenty-year clean record. Extremely suspicious. Watching for it.
Iacopo Fieschi (Tessarine envoy)Medium-Hard30–50 gp + Concordat goodwillFirst time on the list. Proud. Getting him is a political statement.
Canal Commission inspectorMedium15 gpClassic target. Expects administrative tricks; theatrical ones catch him.
A Waveservant juniorEasy10 gp + crowd approvalCrowd loves religious targets. Marks often enjoy the goodwill from being a sport.
A Council family memberVery Hard50 gpThe committee has been waiting. High risk, high reward.

The party may propose their own mark from the Accord list. Assign DC and bonus accordingly.

Phase Structure

Phase 1 — La Scelta: Design (Day 1)

No checks. Pure roleplay.

The party picks their mark, designs their concept, and registers their symbol. The key question is not “what is the prank” but “what does each character do?”

What they sayLikely check
”I scout the mark’s daily routine”Investigation or Perception
”I create a distraction in the market”Performance or Deception
”I acquire a prop without being noticed”Sleight of Hand or Stealth
”I plant false information in advance”Deception or Persuasion
”I build a physical element”Tool check or Athletics
”I recruit a civilian accomplice”Persuasion
”I research the mark’s weaknesses”History or Insight
”I use magic for preparation”Arcana or direct spell

Declare scale: Minor (DC 12), Notable (DC 14), Legendary (DC 17, 50 gp stake). The party decides.

Phase 2 — La Preparazione: Setup (Days 2–4, any day chosen)

Each party member makes one check based on Phase 1 commitments.

The party decides when during the window to strike. Earlier = less risk of sabotage; later = more time to prep and a more relaxed mark.

Complications on failure:

  • A prop is wrong → disadvantage on one Phase 3 check
  • The mark spotted something → raise Phase 3 DC by 2
  • A rival team noticed → they attempt a counter move
  • A committee adjudicator observed more than intended → pointed question on judgment day

Rival interference: one rival team may attempt to sabotage preparation. Contested Stealth vs. Perception. If the rival succeeds, assign a complication. If the party succeeds, they identify the rival — and earn a free sabotage action against them in Phase 3.

False-alarm gambit: the party may deliberately tip off their mark on an early day to lower their guard before the real strike. Deception check (DC = mark’s Wisdom + 2). Success: mark’s Phase 3 save at disadvantage. Failure: mark is now actively suspicious — DC raised by 3.

Phase 3 — L’Esecuzione: The Strike (chosen day)

Each party member makes one live-pressure check. The mark makes a Wisdom save. The symbol must be placed.

The mark’s save: DC = 8 + number of party successes in Phase 2.

  • Fails: completely fooled. Scores 4–5.
  • Succeeds by 1–4: partially fooled, something felt off. Scores 2–3.
  • Succeeds by 5+: spotted the trick. Scores 0–1. The prank still proceeds — craft and recovery can still win it.

Party checks: each player makes the execution version of their Phase 2 role. Failure = something goes visibly wrong — crowd notices, judges note it.

Placing the symbol: one party member must place the team symbol during or at the end of the prank, without tipping off the mark prematurely. Sleight of Hand or Deception, DC 12. Failure: symbol found too early, reducing Surprise by 1.

Recovery check: after the prank, one party member walks it back. Performance or Persuasion (Deception or Medicine as alternates). Good recovery is worth up to 2 extra craft points from the committee.

Rival Teams

Present their results at sundown on Day Five. You do not need to play them out — just describe what happened.

The Candle Brothers — two humans, twelve consecutive entries, four second-place finishes. Technically brilliant, emotionally inert. They will score 13–15 regardless of their prank.

Serena Voss — a halfling factor who entered on a dare, going for the Tessarine factor as her mark. No team. No experience. One very good idea. Roll her score secretly: 2d6+4. If she rolls high, the party has real competition — and she wants to buy everyone drinks regardless of result.

Party Unknown — three people in matching grey coats, registered under a name nobody recognizes, declared “Compound / Legendary,” and refused to state their mark. Roll their score at Day Five: 1d20. On 1–8: disqualified (the crowd loves it). On 9–14: score 11. On 15–19: score 16. On 20: score 19 — the party needs to beat or tie this to win.

Scoring

ElementMaximumSource
Craft10Committee — Phase 2 and 3 quality
Surprise5Mark’s self-score
Recovery5Recovery check
Total20

Prize Table

Party ScoreResultPrize
HighestWin60% of pool + Beffa Medallion + mark bonus
SecondSecond25% of pool + mark bonus (if applicable)
ThirdThirdRemainder of pool
Below all rivalsRespectable lossMark bonus only (if mark was fooled)
DisqualifiedDisqualifiedStake lost; crowd applauds anyway

Pool estimate: 4 teams × 25 gp standard, plus any Legendary stakes. Typical pool: 125–200 gp. Party wins 60% = 75–120 gp + mark bonus + side bets.

Side betting: party may bet on themselves at registration, max 50 gp at 2:1 (Notable) or 4:1 (Legendary).

Key Facts

  • Prospero Morsani‘s plaque entry is the only one without a prank description. He will not explain.
  • Giacomo Moretti signs the Accord every year and enjoys the festival. He finds the attempts flattering. He will never say this.
  • Committee adjudicators are genuinely bad at not being noticed. DC 10 Perception identifies one during Phase 2.
  • The beffa doppia has succeeded exactly twice in the festival’s history. Both rulings took three days. One is still disputed.

Running Notes

Ask what each character does, not what the plan is. The party’s plan is their business. Your job is to assign a skill to whatever they commit to in Phase 1 and hold them to it in Phase 2.

Play the mark. When the prank lands, embody whoever they picked. Be genuinely fooled by good ideas. The mark’s reaction is the scene.

The window creates tension for free. On Days 2 and 3, describe marks being jumpy, rivals seen in unexpected places, committee adjudicators moving through the district. The uncertainty is doing the work.

The medallion matters more than the money. In Calveno, the Beffa Medallion is social proof that you are clever enough to deceive people in public and charming enough to get away with it. The Council cannot buy it. Iacopo Fieschi will mention it to Cosimo. Morsani will nod at the party across the Mercatura, and the nod will mean something.

Involved Parties

  • Giacomo Moretti — twenty-year clean record; extremely suspicious
  • Iacopo Fieschi — first-year mark; Tessarine implications if pranked
  • Prospero Morsani — former winner; present every year; watching
  • Cosimo Verantio — will hear about the result

Locations

  • Calveno — the whole city is the stage
  • Moretti & Sons Chandlery — if Giacomo is the mark
  • The Cabinet of Morsani — Morsani is here pre-festival

Consequences

  • Win: Calveno social capital, medallion on the ship, Cosimo and Fieschi aware, Morsani nods
  • Lose honourably: mark pays the bonus if the prank was good; Serena Voss wants to buy drinks
  • Disqualified: the crowd loves a dramatic disqualification; not actually bad for reputation

DM mechanics for running the Mud Pits as a party attraction at Kalowe — calibration table, opponent roster, betting mechanics, and crowd-as-social-resource.

# The Mud Pits — DM Notes

The Mud Pits are a sandbox attraction designed to drain the party's resources and win them local reputation. [[bala-tane|Bala Tane]] calibrates the fight to the crowd's entertainment, not to party safety — she will send them enough to make it interesting, which means enough to genuinely threaten them.

**Public page:** [[the-mud-pits|The Mud Pits]]

## Running the Fight

**Goal:** exhaust the party (hit dice, spell slots, resources) while giving them something satisfying to win. Don't kill anyone — the crowd would actually hate it.

**Format:** Brawl to unconsciousness (0 HP). No death saving throws. Lethal damage does not apply unless a fighter deliberately chooses it — Bala stops that and ejects the fighter.

**Mud effects:** Difficult terrain throughout. Any creature knocked prone must succeed on a DC 12 STR save to stand as a bonus action or spend full movement to rise. Ranged attacks from outside the pit have half cover on targets inside.

## Calibration Table

| Party Size | Base Matchup | Crowd Reaction |
|---|---|---|
| 1 PC | 2–3 dock bruisers (CR 1/8) | Curious; picks sides early |
| 2 PCs | 3–4 bruisers or 1 veteran + 2 bruisers | Invested; bets split 60/40 |
| 3 PCs | 4–5 bruisers or 2 veterans | Loud; lots of side money |
| Full party (4–5) | 6–8 opponents or special matchup | Frenzy; Bala watching closely |

**Bruiser:** Guard or Thug statblock (MM). Remove lethal special attacks.
**Veteran:** Use Veteran (MM). Bala uses these for upset matchups she wants to be close.

Increase difficulty by adding one opponent at a time if the party is winning too cleanly. Bala calls it "Kalowe rules." The crowd knows what it means.

## Opponent Roster

**Standard card** — Mixed orc, human, tortle dockworkers who fight on weekends. Reliable. Underpaid. Good sports about losing.

**Vort Kessen (champion)** — Retired orc sailor, late fifties, built like he was assembled from ship timbers. Use Gladiator (MM). Fights defensively and patiently; wins by outlasting people. Beat Vort and Bala pays the champion's cut (50gp bonus) and the crowd buys drinks all evening. Vort buys his own drink and nods.

**The Mud Moucheron (special event)** — Bala occasionally books a [[moucheron|Moucheron]] between contracts. Use Moucheron statblock without proboscis drain (honour rules). The crowd loses their minds. The party will have heard the warnings. This is technically safe. Bala finds the look on their faces very satisfying.

**Escaped Giant Crab (chaos event)** — Once per campaign, a giant crab from the lagoon gets into the pit. Bala lets the fight happen for two rounds before calling it. No entry fee refunds.

## Betting Mechanics

Bala's runners set opening odds on her read. If the party looks capable, they open as slight underdogs (2:1). Upsets pay more.

Party can bet on themselves (max 20gp per fighter through the runners; higher bets go directly to Bala and she will remember). Side bets between spectators are unregulated.

**The crowd as resource:** after a win, bettors who won on the party become friendly. The harbour boss has a runner here most nights — a win against a stiff matchup gets the party a meeting. Vort, if beaten, tells them one true thing about Kalowe he has never told anyone, because he respects the outcome.

## Triggers

- Party arrives in Kalowe and hears crowd noise from the second island
- [[the-flat-water|Reweti Kahurangi]] mentions it at the Flat Water
- The party has money and wants a fight

## Bala's Tell

When she says "Kalowe rules" before announcing the opponent count, she is adding a fighter. The crowd knows what it means.

## Consequences

- **Win:** local reputation in Kalowe, crowd goodwill, possible harbour boss introduction
- **Lose honourably:** Bala offers a rematch at a discount; the crowd is still warm
- **Refuse after showing up:** Bala remembers; the crowd boos

## Connections

- [[the-mud-pits|The Mud Pits]] — site
- [[bala-tane|Bala Tane]] — pit boss
- [[kalowe|Kalowe]]
- [[moucheron|Moucheron]]
- [[five-blades|Five Blades]] — watching from the rim; interested if the party wins or loses impressively

# Port Tidefall — Dockfront Opportunities

## Situation

Port Tidefall is overfull, resentful, and full of small useful doors. The party can find ship options, impound schedules, a buried cache, a Tessarine salvage job, Waveservant pressure on [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]], and personal/social hooks without treating each building as a separate situation.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Offers. Tidefall puts useful trouble on counters, notice boards, bar tables, and shrine shelves. |
| Unstable Condition | The port is processing too many ships, too much gossip, and too many private agendas after the Surety incident. |
| Consequence | Small opportunities can solve immediate needs, but each one exposes a PC to a different watcher. |
| Link of Relevance | [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] needs ships/tithe/social cover; [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] needs refuge; [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] reacts to coercion; Stripes is recognized by Waveservants. |

---

## Key Opportunities

### Anchor & Line (Dockfront Bar)

- **Front-room intel:** garrison over capacity; Rook impounded a catch on a technicality; Tessarine Trade House had a quiet diving accident.
- **Back section:** canvas-separated; Crown patrols only check the front by informal six-year arrangement. Perrin can shelter here.
- **Vrtek** has pocket contents from a Crown coat: four coins, brass button, candle stub, carved fish, Dravosi rating stamp, and a **sealed note he cannot read**.
- **Sosse** tells Perrin after the third drink that Vrtek has something official that does not belong to him.
- **Jean-Claude hook:** six dockfront labourers drink here from sixth bell; two know Maret is held in the Trade House back room. DC 11 Persuasion/Insight gets them talking.

### Hook & Ledger (Impound Intel Bar)

- Impound clerk is selling tomorrow's berth adjustments and release notes to cover gambling debt.
- DC 13 Insight spots him before he names a price; DC 13 Perception notices three tables listening without looking.
- Card alcove hosts freight factors and labour middlemen. DC 11 Persuasion joins the next negotiation; DC 16 Insight identifies real authority.
- Locked back drawer: copied impound schedule, unpaid Fort Crestwall sergeant marker, half-finished list of tomorrow's secondary inspections.

### Inspection Pier Cache

- Vrtek's note identifies a cache: **3rd piling from harbour mouth, south face, 2 ft below mussel line at spring low.**
- Low-tide window: ~2 hours starting at third bell.
- Contents: 740 gp old Dravosi gold, 60 gp Tessarine silver, 40 gp jade fish, and an oilskin letter proving a Crown inspector took bribes 15 years ago.
- Rook periodically checked the waterline. Perrin's silhouette matches a nearby bounty notice — he should coordinate from outside or approach from the water side.
- DC sequence: Pier 4 Investigation 11; mussel line Nature/Survival 10; approach Stealth 13; quiet Stealth 12; clay seal Athletics 12; chest free Athletics 14; exit Athletics/Stealth 13/12.

### Harbourmaster Board

| Item | Notes |
|---|---|
| Greyteeth Runner for sale | 1,400 gp |
| Lasting Insult in impound | Clears for 374 gp + ~3 gp/day accrual |
| Salvor's Claim | 40% of ~800 gp from reef wreck; prior team failed; lapses in 10 days |
| "the Runner, Kalowe" card | Below official notices; will be pulled once noticed |
| Charts | Crown Islands/Central Strait 25 gp; Midchain partial survey 75 gp (ask chart clerk specifically) |

### Lasting Insult

- Third berth in South Harbour Impound; hull sound, serviceable.
- Legal acquisition: pay 374 gp + accrual.
- Night acquisition: single chain padlock, DC 18 Thieves' Tools; only witness is the clerk if awake.
- Clerk accepts full payment, Admiral's commission, or Harbourmaster's writ. No partial payment, barter, charm, or corruption.

### Tessarine Trade House — Maret

- **Maret**, human dockworker, sole survivor of a prior salvage dive, is held in the back office on Concordat debt-recovery hold.
- He is not frightened of the creature; he is frightened of going back alone. DC 12 Insight.
- **Salvage terms:** 40% recovered cargo (~320 gp if manifest accurate); 10-day deadline; 30–40 ft depth; hold at 35 ft; one large unknown creature using wreck as den; cargo includes diplomatic pouches, one strongbox, five luxury crates.
- Jean-Claude likely acts if he understands a dockworker is being held under debt law.

### Waveservant Shrine

- **Senior Waveservant** knows Delmar is in port and his 15 gp tithe appointment is overdue.
- Senior knows Stripes by what he is, not just who he is; cannot be rushed or deflected.
- Recent offering hook: compass needle wrapped in oilcloth, left within two days, petitioner unknown.

### Maggie Porcelain Pots

[[margaret-porcelain-pots|Maggie]] does not know Delmar is married. She heard his fleet went down and did not reach out — no bad blood, she just does not chase. Her pottery business can organically cross the party's path across islands; she always returns home.

- **Jean-Claude notices coercion:** Maret's debt hold or labour deals become immediate moral pressure.
- **Delmar delays Waveservants:** polite shrine pressure ties to the broader Pearl crisis.
- **Perrin uses Anchor & Line refuge:** safe for now, but Vrtek's note and bounty silhouette pull him back into risk.

# Red Lady — Salvage Money

## Island Premise

Someone is quietly assembling a salvage commission for a Maw wreck, and the money moving through Calveno's broker network is unusual enough that Savia Brentino has turned away three enquiries and the Tangle has taken note. The accessible thread is Batta Zusto, a mid-tier broker on the Bridge who is not the funder but knows where the work orders are going. Delmar and Crissdalynn are the PCs for whom this matters most. The question underneath the money is whether the party finds the commission before it finds them.

---

## Strong Start

One of two entry points — use the first that applies.

**If Delmar asks about the Maw or the Red Lady:**
> [!read-aloud]
> The chandler lowers his voice without being asked. "You're not the first person to ask about Maw salvage this month. There's money moving. Serious money. Three separate buyers, or one buyer with three hands — nobody's sure. Whoever it is, they're not advertising a target."

# Shepherd Grigori — Narrative Island

## Island Premise

The party unknowingly shared a ship with a Hierarch sorcerer-lich whose phylactery is not an object — it is a living network of noble heirs whose incurable conditions he cured. As long as any of them live, he cannot be permanently destroyed. He was not hiding. He passed his own test and decided the party met his threshold. He was genuinely helpful. He was also counting down to a Calveno visit to a hemophiliac Tessarine heir.

**The cure happened.** He arrived at the Tessarine household, managed an acute bleed episode first, and completed the binding procedure. The heir is now sitting up and asking for food. Grigori has departed Calveno. The network expanded by one.

---

## True Nature

**Shepherd Grigori is a [[khlysty|Khlysty]] Hierarch sorcerer-lich.**

His phylactery is a living network: noble heirs across the Shattered Sea whose incurable illnesses he cured. Each living heir is an anchor for his continued existence. He reforms from death more slowly or quickly depending on how many anchors remain. He is always expanding the network.

**The cure is the trap.** The healing is real. The patient is genuinely better. They never know they have been bound.

**He considers himself a benefactor.** This is not a lie he tells others — he believes it. The horror is that he is not wrong about the results. Only the mechanism.

Play his CHA 21 as real. Play the warmth and the faith as absolutely genuine.

---

## Current State (Post-Calveno)

Grigori has left the *Uncertainty* and departed Calveno on his own timeline. Within a day of his departure, rumours circulate:

> *A dying Tessarine heir recovered overnight. A man came after dark, was with the patient for twenty minutes, and left without asking for anything. The servants say he smelled like wine and something else. Someone says he was singing under his breath the whole time.*

The family is not publicizing this. The rumours come from the servants.

**The Tessarine heir is now a living phylactery.** The family does not know. The heir does not know. The only record is Grigori's.

---

## Calveno Target — Resolved

The hemophiliac Tessarine heir from a powerful family. The condition was worsening; the family had exhausted conventional physicians. Grigori arrived with World Tick 2026-05-26 showing a setback — the heir in an acute bleed episode, binding procedure delayed. He managed the acute crisis first, then completed the binding on a subsequent visit. Done before his departure.

The heir's Tessarine connections make this addition particularly valuable — the [[tessarine-concordat|Concordat]]'s reach extends into courts where Grigori does not yet have anchors.

---
