## Loaded Guns

- **The heir is recovering.** Interrupting now would require finding Grigori, learning the truth, and confronting what reversing the cure means for a child who is breathing without pain.
- **He liked the party.** This is not a performance. His warmth toward people who meet his threshold is genuine. He will tell them things nobles usually keep quiet.
- **He knows the courts.** More royal households than anyone the party can afford. He shares freely — fair exchange, in his mind.
- **Khlysty mark.** DC 18 Religion or History, having seen Khlysty iconography elsewhere first: a small sect symbol, not displayed but not hidden.
- **Alys Kuiper.** The ship's surgeon did not return from shore leave. A man visited her at her Le Paludi boarding house. She left the next morning. This is the full extent of what is findable. Don't invent more unless you have a prepared thread for it.

---

## Clocks

- **Network expansion:** The Tessarine heir has been added. Grigori is operating on his own timeline, expanding further. Each new anchor makes him harder to permanently kill.
- **Pattern recognition:** This thread goes dormant until a healed-noble NPC surfaces, someone connects the Calveno rumour to other miraculous recoveries, or Grigori reaches out to the party again.

---

## Player Choices (Available Now)

- **Let it go and think nothing of it:** cure happened, network expanded, party doesn't know — until a pattern surfaces later.
- **Investigate the Calveno rumour:** they find the Tessarine household, the servant accounts, the recovered heir. They may learn what he is.
- **Confront him if they find him:** he is honest. He does not consider himself a monster. He will ask what they think should be done about the child who is now breathing without pain.
- **Combat:** CR 19 at party level 4. This is a death scenario.

---

## Rewards and Costs

- **Intelligence:** Grigori will freely share what he knows about Crown courts, noble politics, and the routes he travels — if the party finds him again.
- **Tessarine contact:** the heir's grateful family is now a potential future contact. They do not know the party was involved.
- **Phylactery revelation:** learning the network's scope is a campaign-level reframe — several healed-noble NPCs may retroactively become potential plot elements.

## Running Notes

**The frame:** Rasputin as an undead sorcerer. The cult of personality is the weapon. The miracle is the mechanism.

**Play the warmth as real.** Grigori is not performing goodness. He heals people. He improves their lives. His theology is internally consistent and he lives by it. If you play him as secretly menacing, players will sense it. If you play him as genuinely warm, the revelation lands properly when it comes.

**He asks good questions.** CHA 21, decades of practice. He knows how to make people feel seen. He is actually curious.

Play the warmth as real. Grigori is not performing goodness. He heals people. He improves their lives. His theology is internally consistent and he lives by it. If you play him as secretly menacing, players will sense it. If you play him as genuinely warm, the revelation lands properly when it comes.

He asks good questions. CHA 21, decades of practice. He knows how to make people feel seen. He is actually curious.

The phylactery problem is a campaign-level hook. It surfaces naturally when the party meets an NPC who survived something unsurvivable, or when someone points at a Tessarine heir and says “he was dying three weeks ago.”

# Warren — Bela Silt-Paw

## Island Premise

[[bela-silt-paw|Bela Silt-Paw]], 22, took her first solo deep-route assignment fourteen days ago and has not come back. A Water Weird has claimed the flooded central chamber on the survey route. Bela is alive in a dry shelf beyond it — broken forearm, message shard, emergency rations — but she cannot pass the Weird and the Warren does not have anyone else who can go in. The Tangle knows she is probably still alive. The clock is 2-3 days.

---

## Strong Start

> [!read-aloud]
> The passage narrows to shoulder-width and then drops. At the bottom of four stone steps the water begins — black, still, lamp-warm from the torch Bela left wedged in the wall above the first shelf. Her kit bag is floating against the approach tunnel entrance. She did not take it back through.

Give the party a beat to look around: the torch, the kit bag, the water depth (knee-height on a human here, deeper ahead), the silence. Then the Weird in the central channel moves.

---

## Site

```text
[Approach tunnel] — 5ft wide, low ceiling
     ↓
[Entry shelf] — 3ft water, 8ft ceiling, 6ft × 8ft flat shelf
     ↓ (main channel)
[Central chamber] — 8ft water, 8ft ceiling at peak, 20ft × 40ft
                 ← WATER WEIRD claims this channel
     ↓ (west approach tunnel — optional second Weird)
[Far shelf] — 3ft water, 8ft ceiling, 6ft × 8ft shelf
     ↓ (dry alcove, 2 steps up)
[Dry alcove] — BELA IS HERE: broken arm, shard, rations, 1 torch stub
```

**Approach tunnels:** 5ft wide, 5ft ceiling. Medium creatures squeeze. Small creatures move normally. No swimming room — anyone in the tunnel while it's flooding has seconds, not rounds.

**Entry shelf:** 3ft deep. A human is wading. Bela's kit bag is floating at the entrance. No current.

**Central chamber:** 8ft deep in the main channel. The Weird occupies this space. The ceiling peaks to 8ft in the center, slopes lower at the edges. A creature wading the shelf edges (where the floor rises, depth ~4ft) is technically in the shallows — but only if they stay pressed to the wall.

**Far shelf and dry alcove:** Same profile as the entry shelf. Two steps up brings someone into the dry alcove where Bela is. Small ledge cache hidden behind a loose stone she knows.

---

## The Weird

> [!mechanic]
> **Water Weird** (MM p.299). AC 13, HP 58, Speed 0ft / Swim 60ft. Constrict +5 to hit, 3d8+3 bludgeoning, grappled target (DC 13 Str to escape). **Transparent in water:** DC 15 Perception to detect while still. **Regenerates 10 HP/round** in contact with water unless hit by fire or cold damage that round.

> [!dm]
> The Weird attacks only when a creature enters the main channel water. It ignores creatures on the entry and far shelves. It will not pursue into approach tunnels. The shelf edges (4ft depth, wall-pressed) are possible traverse routes — the Weird can reach them but must move to do so and loses its transparent bonus when moving. Half-cover from the wall. Not safe. Less immediately fatal. **Optional escalation:** a second Weird on the west approach tunnel activates if the party tries to collapse or drain the central chamber rather than defeat the existing Weird.

**Regeneration counter:** fire or cold damage suppresses regeneration for the round. An alchemist's fire (5ft splash), a cold cantrip, or a scroll creates a window. The Weird drops fast when this is sustained.

---

## Bela

Bela Silt-Paw: young Rattkin, 22, first-generation Passage runner. She took the assignment because she wanted the credit. She fell when the Weird surfaced unexpectedly and broke her left forearm on the alcove step. She has kept it splinted with her own kit, has stayed put as trained, and has been signalling on her message shard every few hours.

**Condition on rescue:** broken forearm (splinted), exhausted (one level), dehydrated (rolled Perception checks at disadvantage). She is calm in the way that frightened people get when they have been frightened for too long and have run out of new fear to feel.

**Her shard.** The message shard is a small Passage communication device — carved bone, paired with a receiver at the Tangle. She has been signalling her location. If someone in the party has Rattkin contacts or a Passage connection, the shard is recognizable.

**The cache.** Behind the loose stone in the dry alcove: 340 gp (mixed coin, Passage operational funds), 2 potions of water breathing, and a sealed wax-and-leather dispatch marked with a Dravosi naval seal. The dispatch is two years old. Bela knows it is there — it was part of her assignment to map this cache for the Tangle. She will tell the party if asked.

**The dispatch.** Sealed, DM to open or hold. Contents: Commendant Ulrik Faste's fraudulent supply contract — timber substitutions and keel-iron shortfalls over a three-year period, signed off against falsified inspection reports. Worth approximately 500 gp to a Tessarine rival, a Calveno merchant who lost a contract, or a Dravosi political enemy of Faste. Worth more to the Passage as Tangle leverage. Commendant Faste is not a named antagonist yet — leave it closed until the party chooses to open it.

---

## Rewards

| Outcome | Reward |
|---|---|
| Bela alive and shard recovered | 200 gp from the Tangle, access to the harbour-foundation route, major Tangle goodwill |
| Weird cleared (one or both) | Route declared open; Tangle asks what the party wants for clearing a blocked channel |
| Cache recovered and disclosed to Tangle | Tangle registers the find; Faste dispatch becomes a Passage asset the party can reference |
| Cache recovered and kept | 340 gp + 2 potions of water breathing + dispatch; Tangle does not ask (they don't know it's there) |
| Bela dead | Tangle goodwill goes cold; shard and harbour-foundation route lost; Nona does not mention it again |

---

## Loaded Guns

- The message shard keeps signalling while Bela is alive. If the rescue takes too long, the signals stop. The Tangle notices immediately.
- The harbour-foundation route Bela was mapping bypasses Canal Commission checkpoints entirely — useful for moving people or cargo without paperwork.

---

## Clocks

> [!mechanic]
> **Bela's rations:** 2-3 days from session start. Tick: her shard signals become irregular, then stop.
> **The route:** until the Weird is cleared, the Tangle's sub-level drainage access is compromised.

---

## Player Choices

- Fight the Weird directly in the central channel (dangerous; home advantage)
- Traverse the shelf edge (very dangerous without a plan; viable with good tactics and Bela's knowledge)
- Use water breathing (the potions are in the cache on the far side — the party may not know this yet)
- Fire or cold tactics to suppress regeneration (viable; the Weird burns fast if you sustain the damage)
- Drain or redirect the chamber (structural; the Tangle will ask questions; the optional second Weird appears)

---

## Exit States

- **Resolved:** Bela out alive, Weird destroyed, route cleared, cache recovered and disclosed or kept.
- **Complicated:** Bela out alive but the Weird survives; the route is not cleared; the Tangle is grateful but the problem is half-solved.
- **Ignored:** Bela's shard goes quiet. The Tangle closes the route, cuts the loss, and does not explain it to the party.

# Warren — Ferrin Locke

## Island Premise

Three Passage surface operations have been intercepted in the last three months. A pattern exists. The Tangle identified a canal broker named Faro as a common thread; Faro leads to Ferrin Locke, who has been feeding technically accurate but slightly delayed route timing to a Dravosi intelligence handler under Tessarine cover. Ferrin is not a traitor — he is a frightened man with an old smuggling conviction being squeezed by someone who knows exactly how to hold it over him. He wants to stop. He does not know how to stop safely.

---

## Strong Start

Deliver through a [[warren|Warren]] contact or Nona directly: *"We have three intercepts in three months. They share a canal broker named Faro. Faro's clients include a man named Ferrin Locke — chandlery factor in Le Paludi, mid-tier, clean reputation except for a conviction from twelve years ago. Find out if Locke is the leak and what it costs to close it."*

The Tangle does not specify how. They want it stopped and they want the handler identified.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Extracts. The party finds a frightened man inside an intelligence operation and decides what to do with both. |
| Unstable Condition | Petra Venn's next check-in with Ferrin is 9 days from when the party begins asking. After that, the operation resets or she knows it's compromised. |
| Consequence | Ferrin's fate and Venn's outcome determine whether the leak closes cleanly or leaves a loose end the Tangle will remember. |
| Link of Relevance | Jean-Claude hook (Grung travel documentation query); Venn's room may also contain Ferrin's cooperation agreement, accessible via Marrow's Crate investigation. |

---

## The Investigation

**Step one: broker Faro.** Canal district inquiry on the three intercept routes (DC 12, Tangle provides the route details). Succeeds: Faro is a known mid-level broker who handled logistics for all three operations. He works from a canal-side office in Le Paludi.

**Step two: Faro to Locke.** Confronting or surveilling Faro (DC 10 — he is not a trained intelligence asset and Insight DC 10 reads his discomfort immediately). He will give up Locke under mild pressure. He does not know Locke is a source — he only knows Locke asked for route details on behalf of a client.

**Step three: Ferrin Locke.** Ferrin is a broad-shouldered human, early forties, runs a minor chandlery factor from a waterfront office in Le Paludi. He has a wife and a daughter. He has the look of someone who has not slept well in three months.

> [!read-aloud]
> A waterfront office in Le Paludi, facing the canal. No nameplate on the door. It opens before the third knock — Ferrin Locke, broad-shouldered, early forties, already stepping back to let you in. He has the look of a man who expected someone to come eventually and is not relieved that they did.

He will not volunteer anything. He is aware he is being watched and that watching him is how someone finds Venn.

- **If offered a way out:** he talks freely. DC 10 Insight to confirm he is telling the truth.
- **If pressured:** DC 15 Persuasion or Intimidation. He talks, but he is shaking, and everything he says is accurate.
- **If treated with basic human decency:** DC 13 Insight to read how frightened he is. After that, he talks without needing a roll.

**What he knows:**

- Handler's name: Petra Venn, posing as a Tessarine trade arbitration consultant. Meets him every nine days at a coffeehouse in Le Paludi.
- What he provides: route timing for Passage surface operations, gathered passively through Faro and two other brokers who do not know they are sources.
- The conviction: smuggling, twelve years ago, petty and resolved. Venn has documentation. He does not believe the Crown will be lenient if she surfaces it.
- The thing he did not report to Venn: approximately four months ago, Venn gave him a standing query — flag any Grung passenger travelling with false documentation through Calveno's broker network. He noticed. He said nothing to her. He says it now.

---

## Jean-Claude Hook

Venn's Grung passenger query is months old and unfulfilled. If Jean-Claude is involved in this scene and Ferrin treats him as trustworthy, Ferrin mentions it unprompted. A Dravosi intelligence handler has been looking for a Grung traveller with false papers. She did not say why. She asked four months ago and has not asked again, which Ferrin finds more unnerving, not less.

> [!dm]
> Do not assign this as Jean-Claude's backstory — surface it and let the player decide what it means.

---

## Petra Venn

Dravosi intelligence attaché. Tessarine trade arbitration consultant cover. Operating in Calveno four months. Professional, patient, not violent by preference.

**Venn's next check-in:** 9 days from when the party begins asking questions. If the party moves slowly, she arrives at the coffeehouse and reads that something has changed. If the party is fast, they can intercept her on her terms or on theirs.

> [!read-aloud]
> A canal-facing coffeehouse in Le Paludi. Corner table, window seat. The woman in trade arbitration clothes has a document open in front of her that she has not turned in twenty minutes. When the door opens, her eyes move to it before anything else.

**Venn's lodgings** (locatable via Ferrin's description, DC 12 Le Paludi inquiry): a rented room above a canal-facing notary's office. Strongbox contents: codebook (500 gp value to Tangle or rivals), 420 gp operational coin, list of three non-Passage informants, and Ferrin Locke's signed cooperation agreement.

> [!dm]
> If the party already found Haut's room via [[warren-marrows-crate|Warren — Marrow's Crate]], Ferrin's cooperation agreement is already in hand — confirming his account and giving the party leverage without needing to locate Venn separately.

---

## Outcome Options

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Expose Locke to the Tangle | Leak stops; Ferrin disappears non-lethally (Passage handles it); 300 gp and trust |
| Help Locke escape Calveno | Protected contact outside the network; Passage owes a debt for the loose end they didn't have to clean up |
| Neutralize Venn before the check-in | Leak stops at source; codebook and operational coin available; Ferrin is free |
| Turn Venn over to the Tangle | As above; Passage handles the rest; they will not say what happens to her |
| Sell codebook to a third party | 500 gp; Venn notices within a week; Passage eventually asks where it came from |
| Nothing — let the 9-day clock expire | Venn concludes the network is compromised, closes Ferrin, and goes quiet; the Tangle loses the thread and operations exposure continues through a new asset |

---

## Loaded Guns

- Ferrin's wife and daughter are not leverage unless someone makes them leverage. They are in Le Paludi. This is enough context.
- The Grung passenger query is months old and unfulfilled. Venn has moved on to other priorities. But the query existed and Dravosi records are not deleted — it is still somewhere.
- If Venn and [[serin-haut|Serin Haut]] are both active in Calveno, they are aware of each other but not running coordinated operations. The party bumping into both may cause one or both to accelerate their timelines.

---

## Clocks

> [!mechanic]
> **Venn check-in:** 9 days from inquiry start. Tick at day 3, day 6, day 9. On day 9 she arrives at the coffeehouse.
> **Ferrin's nerve:** each day the party delays after meeting him, he considers going directly to Venn. He won't — he's too frightened — but his fear is visible if they check in on him.

---

## Player Choices

- Extract Ferrin first, then find Venn (safe approach; Venn may go quiet before they reach her)
- Find Venn first, then deal with Ferrin (faster; riskier; Venn may have already made Ferrin)
- Use Ferrin as bait for Venn's next check-in (elegant; Ferrin needs to agree; his wife is in Le Paludi)
- Give the Tangle the name and step back (clean; the Tangle handles it; the party gets credit without knowing what happened)

---

## Exit States

- **Resolved:** leak closed, Venn neutralised or turned over, Ferrin's situation settled. Tangle registers the close.
- **Complicated:** Ferrin protected but Venn escapes; or Venn neutralised but Ferrin exposed; one loose end remains.
- **Ignored:** Venn's check-in arrives, she reads the changed situation, closes the operation, and starts over with a new asset. The intercepts stop for a few weeks, then resume.

## Island Premise

Three Calveno residents have reported sighting what each described, independently, as a large green humanoid in the sewer access tunnels and canal maintenance corridors beneath Le Paludi and the Bridge district. One report is from a Warren runner who works the sub-level drainage routes — she is not given to exaggeration. The other two are from Dry residents whose descriptions match the runner's.

Grung in Calveno is not a thing that happens. Calveno is a northern commercial city across the Central Strait. The gap between Grung territory and Calveno's sewer network is enormous. That is what makes this worth investigating, and also what makes Nona reluctant to mention it to anyone who would dismiss it on those grounds alone.

She does not have anyone who knows Grung. Then Perrin walks into her kitchen and tells her Jean-Claude is crew.

> *"Before the other things. I need to know what is in the tunnels under my city."*

Down here it smells like low tide and old stone and something else you haven't placed yet.

## What the Party Finds

**Physical signs:** Boot prints in the silt — or what reads as boot prints, except the toe is too wide and the weight distribution is wrong for anything Dry. At least two different sets. The left-branch disturbance is heavier.

> [!read-aloud]
> The left branch has been used more than the right — the silt is disturbed from here to the next junction. When you look closer, the impressions are wrong: the weight is off-centre, the toe too wide for anything Dry.

**The smell:** Whatever the party couldn't name at the ladder. Wet vegetation, something mineral, something organic. Not canal smell. Not rat smell. Jean-Claude places it immediately if he makes no check at all: it is Grung. Ambient, faint, a day or two old. Not one individual — the smell of a space that has had Grung in it repeatedly.

**The markings:** Small incisions on the limestone, low on the wall, easy to miss. At the Y-junction, three marks on the left branch. At the Bridge connector, two marks near the far hatch. They are not maintenance notation — Calveno's canal commission uses chalk and paint, not cuts. They are too precise and too consistent in placement.

> [!read-aloud]
> Low on the wall, knee-height. Three cuts into the limestone — small, clean, exactly the same depth. Not chalk marks. Not paint. Whoever made these had time, had a tool, and did it deliberately.

> [!dm]
> Jean-Claude recognises the marks as Grung in origin — the spacing, the depth, the placement logic. That is all he can say with confidence. What they mean is opaque to him. Grung trail notation varies by caste and context; without knowing the specific system, the marks read as *intentional* and *recent* and *Grung,* full stop. That is already more than anyone else in Calveno knows.

**What the party does not find:** Whoever made these marks. No active presence. No encounter. The tunnels are empty. Whatever was here worked at night and left before dawn. The absence is its own information — this was disciplined, not wandering.

## Reporting to Nona

The party comes back with: confirmed prints, confirmed smell (Jean-Claude), confirmed markings in Grung notation, no active presence, no explanation.

Nona listens without interrupting. Then she is quiet for a moment.

> *"Grung. In my tunnels. During the Beffa."*

She does not say what she makes of this. She asks one question:

> *"Did they see you?"*

If no: she nods. If yes or unknown: she nods differently, and sends Enzo somewhere immediately after the party leaves.

> [!dm]
> Nona suspects something is building. She does not know what. This is accurate — she is not withholding from the party; she is working with the same incomplete information. The investigation confirms the reports are real and raises a question none of them can yet answer. That is the correct exit state for a first hint.

## Jean-Claude — The Unease

Jean-Claude can confirm the Grung presence. He cannot explain it. That gap — knowing what was here but not why — is the thing that sits with him after the tunnels.

Grung do not wander this far north. Grung expansion is deliberate and directed. Whatever sent scouts this far into a Central Strait city during a festival had a reason. Jean-Claude knows enough to know that, and not enough to know what the reason is.

> [!dm]
> Do not push this as a revelation scene. If the player goes somewhere with it, follow. If they do not, the unease is in his pocket until the Beffa makes it legible.

## Deep Investigation — The Blackpowder Layer

The initial investigation ([[#What the Party Finds|above]]) reveals Grung presence. This section covers what the party finds if they push deeper — past the Bridge connector, into the main collector system under the Mercatura and Le Paludi.

> [!dm]
> This layer is gated by risk. The deeper the party goes, the closer they get to the guarded blackpowder positions. Do not volunteer this content — the party has to choose to keep going past the point where the initial signs have already answered Nona's question.

---

### The Blackpowder Barrels

Past the Bridge connector, the sewer network opens into the main collector system — larger tunnels, 8 ft high, running water, stone vaulting above. At certain junctions, the party finds something new.

> [!read-aloud]
> The tunnel widens. The air changes — dry, chemical, wrong for a sewer. Ahead, against the left wall, dark shapes. Barrels. Six of them, stacked two high and three across, lashed to the wall with rope and wedged with timber. The wood is fresh — pale, unstained, recently cut. The barrels are sealed with tar.

> [!check] Investigation — Identify the Barrels
> DC 10 (the barrels are not hidden, only guarded).
> Fail: sealed cargo, no identification.
> Success: blackpowder. The tar seal, the careful stacking away from water, the timber wedging to prevent shifting — this is magazine storage, not smuggling.
> Crit success: the barrels are positioned at a structural weak point. The vaulting above this section is thinner than the surrounding tunnel — someone chose this spot because the ceiling here is load-bearing for the surface above.

**What this means (JC reads automatically):** This is not a supply cache. Blackpowder stored at structural weak points in a city's sewer system during a festival has exactly one purpose.

---

### The Guarded Positions

Each blackpowder magazine has a sentry team — two green-caste labourers and one blue-caste handler. Their standing orders: hide at the sound of movement, let intruders pass, report after. They do not engage unless the barrels are touched.

> [!mechanic]
> **Sentry Patrol (secondary sites):** 2 Grung + 1 Grung Elite Warrior. The Grung hide (Stealth +4, advantage in dim light/water). They break cover only if the party interacts with the barrels. If discovered, they attempt to flee and report. Killing them silently prevents a report to the handler network.

> [!dm]
> If the party finds one magazine, they can find others. Each magazine is at a different junction beneath the festival districts. Finding and disabling a magazine removes one of the five strike points from the Day 5 detonation. The party does not know there are five unless they capture a handler or find the primary site.

> [!read-aloud]
> The tunnel opens into something larger. The ceiling vaults high overhead — pale stone, old, the kind of masonry that holds up a plaza. Every crack, join, and crevice in that ceiling is packed with blackpowder, held in place by crude scaffolding — timber frames lashed together and wedged between the walls, each shelf loaded with powder wrapped in oiled cloth. The amount is staggering. The air tastes of sulphur and charcoal.
>
> In the centre of the chamber floor, cut into the stone, a circle. Symbols scored deep. Fresh. The cuts are precise and deliberate — someone spent hours on this. The water flowing through the channels parts around it, guided by shallow trenches that keep the circle dry.

> [!dm]
> The party is now in the most dangerous position in the sewer network. The Grung guarding this chamber operate under a different standing order: **shoot on sight, remain hidden, do not let anyone who sees it live.** They are not the hide-and-report sentries at the secondary sites. They are killers.

> [!mechanic]
> **Primary Site Guard:** 4 Grung Elite Warriors + 1 Red-Caste Operative (use Grung Wildling stat block, MM p.149, CR 1). All have hand crossbows with Grung Poison bolts. They attack from concealment (surprise round likely — DC 16 Perception to detect). The red-caste operative prioritizes the summoning circle's integrity and will fight to the death to prevent its disruption.

> [!check] Arcana — The Summoning Circle
> DC 14.
> Fail: magical, purpose unknown.
> Success: a summoning circle for an extraplanar entity — something from the outer planes, not a fiend or celestial. The design is not Grung in origin; someone with formal arcane training built this.
> Crit success: **Slaad.** The circle is configured to summon and release a Slaad — no binding, no control. Whatever comes through this circle will be uncontrolled and hostile to everything around it. The circle is keyed to a detonation trigger: when the blackpowder above ignites, the circle activates. The summoning and the explosion are one event.

**If the party destroys the circle:** no Slaad. The primary detonation can still fire, but the boss-tier distraction is removed. The raid loses its single most effective response-fixer.

**If the party removes the blackpowder:** the primary detonation fails. The Mercatura plaza does not collapse. The Slaad circle has no trigger. Four secondary sites may still fire, but the operation loses its centrepiece.

**If the party is discovered and escapes:** the primary site guard reports up. Simone's handlers know the operation is compromised at the primary site. She has options: accelerate the timeline (detonate early, lose synchronization), abandon the primary site (four secondary strikes only, reduced scale), or hunt the party.

## Optional Encounters

Drop either of these if the party is moving through the tunnels and the scene needs teeth. Neither reveals anything about the Grung presence — they are sewer hazards, not plot.

### Canal Crocodiles

Calveno's outer canal water has always had crocodiles working the tidal margins. Two have pushed up through the Bridge connector's flood overflow into the collector tunnels and settled in the standing water near the Y-junction.

> [!mechanic]
> **2 Crocodiles.** AC 12, HP 19 each. Bite: +4 to hit, 4d6+2 piercing; grappled target (DC 12 Strength to escape). In a 5-ft tunnel, a grappled creature cannot be pulled clear without the rescuer also making a DC 10 Athletics check. The crocodile has advantage on Stealth in ankle-deep water. Passive Perception 10 — they detect movement by vibration, not sight.

> [!dm]
> The crocodiles are not related to the Grung presence. To push past quietly: DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth), with disadvantage for anyone in armour heavier than leather. They do not pursue past the Y-junction.

---

### A Grung Who Hasn't Left

The handlers work at night and are gone before dawn. If the party enters at an awkward hour — or pushes deep and fast — one is still in the Bridge connector, finishing a route check.

> [!read-aloud]
> Movement in the connector ahead — away from you, fast. A shape in the dark already moving toward the far hatch. It heard you before you saw it.

> [!mechanic]
> **1 Grung Elite Warrior.** AC 13, HP 49. Multiattack (2 strikes): +4 to hit, 1d6+2 piercing + 2d4 poison. **Grung Poison:** DC 12 Constitution save or poisoned until end of next turn. **Standing Leap:** jump up to 25 ft without running start. **Amphibious.** Carries hand crossbow (20 bolts).

> [!dm]
> Her objective is the far hatch, not the fight. On her first turn she moves toward the exit; she only attacks if the party blocks or grabs her. She will not speak. If Jean-Claude addresses her in Grung she stops for one beat — not because she will answer, but because she is recalibrating. Then she continues toward the exit. Do not have her reveal anything about the operation: she runs, she escapes, or she dies. No names, no purpose, no information beyond the fact that she was very clearly there to do a job.

Grung do not wander this far north. Grung expansion is deliberate and directed. Whatever sent scouts this far into a Central Strait city during a festival had a reason. Jean-Claude knows enough to know that, and not enough to know what the reason is.

DM Note

Do not push this as a revelation scene. If the player goes somewhere with it, follow. If they do not, the unease is in his pocket until the Beffa makes it legible.

Deep Investigation — The Blackpowder Layer

The initial investigation (above) reveals Grung presence. This section covers what the party finds if they push deeper — past the Bridge connector, into the main collector system under the Mercatura and Le Paludi.

DM Note

This layer is gated by risk. The deeper the party goes, the closer they get to the guarded blackpowder positions. Do not volunteer this content — the party has to choose to keep going past the point where the initial signs have already answered Nona’s question.

The Blackpowder Barrels

Past the Bridge connector, the sewer network opens into the main collector system — larger tunnels, 8 ft high, running water, stone vaulting above. At certain junctions, the party finds something new.

Read Aloud

The tunnel widens. The air changes — dry, chemical, wrong for a sewer. Ahead, against the left wall, dark shapes. Barrels. Six of them, stacked two high and three across, lashed to the wall with rope and wedged with timber. The wood is fresh — pale, unstained, recently cut. The barrels are sealed with tar.

Investigation — Identify the Barrels

DC 10 (the barrels are not hidden, only guarded). Fail: sealed cargo, no identification. Success: blackpowder. The tar seal, the careful stacking away from water, the timber wedging to prevent shifting — this is magazine storage, not smuggling. Crit success: the barrels are positioned at a structural weak point. The vaulting above this section is thinner than the surrounding tunnel — someone chose this spot because the ceiling here is load-bearing for the surface above.

What this means (JC reads automatically): This is not a supply cache. Blackpowder stored at structural weak points in a city’s sewer system during a festival has exactly one purpose.

The Guarded Positions

Each blackpowder magazine has a sentry team — two green-caste labourers and one blue-caste handler. Their standing orders: hide at the sound of movement, let intruders pass, report after. They do not engage unless the barrels are touched.

Mechanic

Sentry Patrol (secondary sites): 2 Grung + 1 Grung Elite Warrior. The Grung hide (Stealth +4, advantage in dim light/water). They break cover only if the party interacts with the barrels. If discovered, they attempt to flee and report. Killing them silently prevents a report to the handler network.

DM Note

If the party finds one magazine, they can find others. Each magazine is at a different junction beneath the festival districts. Finding and disabling a magazine removes one of the five strike points from the Day 5 detonation. The party does not know there are five unless they capture a handler or find the primary site.

The Primary Site — Shoot on Sight

The primary detonation chamber is a large collector nexus beneath the Mercatura — a vaulted stone room 40 ft across, 15 ft high, where four drainage channels converge. This is the smoking gun.

Read Aloud

The tunnel opens into something larger. The ceiling vaults high overhead — pale stone, old, the kind of masonry that holds up a plaza. Every crack, join, and crevice in that ceiling is packed with blackpowder, held in place by crude scaffolding — timber frames lashed together and wedged between the walls, each shelf loaded with powder wrapped in oiled cloth. The amount is staggering. The air tastes of sulphur and charcoal.

In the centre of the chamber floor, cut into the stone, a circle. Symbols scored deep. Fresh. The cuts are precise and deliberate — someone spent hours on this. The water flowing through the channels parts around it, guided by shallow trenches that keep the circle dry.

DM Note

The party is now in the most dangerous position in the sewer network. The Grung guarding this chamber operate under a different standing order:

shoot on sight, remain hidden, do not let anyone who sees it live. They are not the hide-and-report sentries at the secondary sites. They are killers.

Mechanic

Primary Site Guard: 4 Grung Elite Warriors + 1 Red-Caste Operative (use Grung Wildling stat block, MM p.149, CR 1). All have hand crossbows with Grung Poison bolts. They attack from concealment (surprise round likely — DC 16 Perception to detect). The red-caste operative prioritizes the summoning circle’s integrity and will fight to the death to prevent its disruption.

Arcana — The Summoning Circle

DC 14. Fail: magical, purpose unknown. Success: a summoning circle for an extraplanar entity — something from the outer planes, not a fiend or celestial. The design is not Grung in origin; someone with formal arcane training built this. Crit success:

Slaad. The circle is configured to summon and release a Slaad — no binding, no control. Whatever comes through this circle will be uncontrolled and hostile to everything around it. The circle is keyed to a detonation trigger: when the blackpowder above ignites, the circle activates. The summoning and the explosion are one event.

If the party destroys the circle: no Slaad. The primary detonation can still fire, but the boss-tier distraction is removed. The raid loses its single most effective response-fixer.

If the party removes the blackpowder: the primary detonation fails. The Mercatura plaza does not collapse. The Slaad circle has no trigger. Four secondary sites may still fire, but the operation loses its centrepiece.

If the party is discovered and escapes: the primary site guard reports up. Simone’s handlers know the operation is compromised at the primary site. She has options: accelerate the timeline (detonate early, lose synchronization), abandon the primary site (four secondary strikes only, reduced scale), or hunt the party.

Optional Encounters

Drop either of these if the party is moving through the tunnels and the scene needs teeth. Neither reveals anything about the Grung presence — they are sewer hazards, not plot.

Canal Crocodiles

Calveno’s outer canal water has always had crocodiles working the tidal margins. Two have pushed up through the Bridge connector’s flood overflow into the collector tunnels and settled in the standing water near the Y-junction.

Mechanic

2 Crocodiles. AC 12, HP 19 each. Bite: +4 to hit, 4d6+2 piercing; grappled target (DC 12 Strength to escape). In a 5-ft tunnel, a grappled creature cannot be pulled clear without the rescuer also making a DC 10 Athletics check. The crocodile has advantage on Stealth in ankle-deep water. Passive Perception 10 — they detect movement by vibration, not sight.

DM Note

The crocodiles are not related to the Grung presence. To push past quietly: DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth), with disadvantage for anyone in armour heavier than leather. They do not pursue past the Y-junction.

A Grung Who Hasn’t Left

The handlers work at night and are gone before dawn. If the party enters at an awkward hour — or pushes deep and fast — one is still in the Bridge connector, finishing a route check.

Read Aloud

Movement in the connector ahead — away from you, fast. A shape in the dark already moving toward the far hatch. It heard you before you saw it.

Mechanic

1 Grung Elite Warrior. AC 13, HP 49. Multiattack (2 strikes): +4 to hit, 1d6+2 piercing + 2d4 poison. Grung Poison: DC 12 Constitution save or poisoned until end of next turn. Standing Leap: jump up to 25 ft without running start. Amphibious. Carries hand crossbow (20 bolts).

DM Note

Her objective is the far hatch, not the fight. On her first turn she moves toward the exit; she only attacks if the party blocks or grabs her. She will not speak. If Jean-Claude addresses her in Grung she stops for one beat — not because she will answer, but because she is recalibrating. Then she continues toward the exit. Do not have her reveal anything about the operation: she runs, she escapes, or she dies. No names, no purpose, no information beyond the fact that she was very clearly there to do a job.

Rewards and Costs

  • Rewards: Tangle trust; confirmed intelligence that the reports are real; Jean-Claude’s Grung knowledge earns immediate Passage goodwill
  • Costs: An unanswered question now sits on the table, and none of them know what it is counting down to

Exit States

  • Investigation complete, reported to Nona: The reports are confirmed real. Nona has Grung boot prints, Grung smell, and Grung notation under her city during the Beffa. She does not know what it means. The party does not know what it means.
  • Investigation incomplete: Nona gets partial confirmation. She treats it as real anyway.
  • Party investigates and says nothing: Nona finds out they were in the tunnels. She asks what they found. The credit does not appear until they answer honestly.

# Warren — Marrow's Crate

## Island Premise

Dren, a Dry runner who handled cargo for the Warren's broker network, delivered a crate to Marrow's three weeks ago and never returned. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] can surface this lead after the reunion scene when the consignment window comes up. His body was found near the Harbourmaster's Office ten days ago, ruled accidental drowning. The crate is still on Marrow's shelf, its consignment window expiring. The crate contains a letter that implicates House Vretek and Commendant Alessi Brol in feeding Passage cargo timing to Tessarine merchants. The person who killed Dren is still watching the canal approaches.

---

## Strong Start

> [!read-aloud]
> Marrow is already watching when you step down into the alcove. He weighs something on his brass scale, sets it aside, and folds his hands. "Three weeks on the shelf," he says. "Policy is three weeks. I'll pay fifty gold for the intended recipient or for the person who can tell me what's in it." He does not say what happens at the end of the week.

Ask the party what they do first. Marrow will answer direct questions with direct answers — he does not know what is in the crate, he does not know who sent it or who it was for, and he did not ask. He knows Dren, he knows Dren is dead, and he knows the crate has to move.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Uncovers. Pulling on the crate unravels a surveillance operation and a House-level corruption thread. |
| Unstable Condition | Serin Haut has been watching the canal approaches for ten days. Any move toward the crate may be observed. |
| Consequence | The letter surfaces or it doesn't. Haut disappears or she doesn't. Both matter to the Tangle differently. |
| Link of Relevance | House Vretek and Brol are names the party may hear again; the Tangle's operational security is directly at stake. |

---

## The Investigation

The party has three starting threads. They do not need to use all three.

**Canal inquiry.** Dren was a known runner in Le Paludi. DC 12 — dock workers, ferryman, or tavern regulars can place Dren on the canal that night. On a success: a canal worker saw Dren arguing with a woman in a green coat near the Harbourmaster's Office, thirty minutes before the drowning was estimated.

**Watch records.** DC 15 — official records from the district watch office confirm drowning verdict and list one witness: a canal hand who "heard a splash." The witness cannot be located. On a success or a 5 gp bribe (reduces DC to 12): the watch log notes a "foreign-trade enquiry woman" who identified the body and then left without signing the record book.

**Employers.** DC 13 — tracking Dren's other regular clients in the canal district turns up two legitimate deliveries that week and one unusual job: a pickup from a boat tied at the outer basin, unusual time, unusual route. The employer for that pickup is not a name anyone knows.

**The woman in the green coat.** Once the party has this detail from any source, a second inquiry in Le Paludi (DC 12) identifies her as a regular at a specific canal-side coffeehouse — a Tessarine trade arbitration consultant who has been in Calveno four months.

---

## Serin Haut

Haut is a Dravosi intelligence attaché operating under Tessarine trade-assessor cover. She has been watching the canal approaches for ten days, monitoring for anyone who shows interest in the crate or Dren's death. She is patient and experienced. She is not watching from one fixed position.

> [!mechanic]
> **Serin Haut:** Spy (MM p.349), +1 Deception, concealed shortsword, 3 doses basic poison (ingestion, DC 11 Con save, 2d6 poison damage on fail).

> [!dm]
> Haut will not engage in the Warren — she does not know where it is. She engages in Le Paludi if she believes the party has the crate or can identify her. If the party makes two or more canal inquiries in the same day, she begins following the last person to ask questions. Passive Perception DC 14 to notice the tail. If noticed, she makes no hostile move — she stops following and changes her route. She reports the development and waits.

**Her room:** if the party locates her lodgings (Persuasion DC 13 with a Le Paludi contact, or Dren's employer thread leads there): a locked strongbox holds a codebook worth 500 gp to the Tangle or to Tessarine rivals, 420 gp operational coin, a list of three non-Passage informants in Calveno's canal district, and Ferrin Locke's signed cooperation agreement (see [[warren-ferrin-locke|Warren — Ferrin Locke]]).

---

## The Crate

Sealed with Dren's wax and courier notation. Inside:

- A sealed letter implicating House Vretek and Commendant Alessi Brol in selling Passage cargo timing windows to Tessarine factor [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]]'s advance agents.
- 280 gp in Tessarine silver.
- A secondary House Vretek signet ring worth 120 gp as jewelry or considerably more as evidence.

The letter is addressed to no one. It was meant to be collected by a Tangle intermediary who has since gone quiet.

---

## Outcome Options

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Give letter to the Tangle | 400 gp, major trust; Passage handles Brol/Vretek quietly; names disappear from the network within a month |
| Sell to Vretek rivals | 600–750 gp; Vretek enmity is lasting and institutional |
| Blackmail Brol | Up to 800 gp; attempted murder on the blackmailer within two weeks |
| Destroy the letter | House Vretek eventually owes an unnamed favour to whoever made this go away |
| Give Haut to the Tangle | Major Tangle goodwill; the canal district gets quieter; Haut disappears non-lethally |
| Take Haut's room and codebook | 500 gp + 420 gp + informant list; Haut notices within a week; the Passage asks questions eventually |

---

## Loaded Guns

- Ferrin Locke's cooperation agreement is in Haut's strongbox. The party may find it before they find Ferrin, which makes [[warren-ferrin-locke|Warren — Ferrin Locke]] faster to start.
- The Vretek signet ring is portable and recognizable. Anyone who handles it in the wrong company will be asked where it came from.
- Iacopo Fieschi — Tessarine envoy in Calveno — is connected to this operation. The letter names his advance agents. He is also a Beffa mark and a sitting Council factor. These facts are separate. They can be connected.

---

## Clocks

> [!mechanic]
> **Marrow's consignment window:** expires at end of week; Marrow solves it himself after that in a way the party will not be able to trace.
> **Haut's patience:** if the party moves loudly in Le Paludi, she escalates from watching to active interference within 48 hours.

---

## Player Choices

- Claim the crate and deal with Haut (direct; the exposure risk is immediate)
- Identify Haut before approaching the crate (safer; requires the investigation path)
- Let the crate expire and tail whoever Marrow hands it to (possible; Marrow will not confirm or deny)
- Open the letter and use the contents directly (political; multiple outcome branches)

---

## Exit States

- **Resolved:** crate handled, Haut neutralised or driven off, letter delivered or burned. The Tangle knows the outcome.
- **Complicated:** letter surfaces but Haut escapes; or letter is held and not used; Vretek enmity or Brol paranoia activates later.
- **Ignored:** Marrow moves the crate himself at week's end. The Tangle loses the letter and does not know who has it. Haut concludes no one is coming and departs Calveno.

---

- [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] — Tessarine factor in Calveno; indirectly named via advance agents

# Warren — Nona's Table

## Island Premise

Nona has been searching for Perrin for weeks. She knows he is in Calveno before he knows she knows. The food is already on the table when he walks in. The conversation that follows is the shape of their entire relationship: she feeds him, names the thing he hoped food would delay, and then tells him what she needs from him next. The Vestra is the apex. She has not been told yet, and Perrin is the one who tells her.

---

## Strong Start

> [!read-aloud]
> The Tangle Chambers smell the same as they always have: old stone, lamp oil, and whatever Nona is cooking. Enzo is holding the inner door — he has already seen you. He does not speak. He steps back and gestures, one hand, toward the table.
> The table is set. Bread. A pot. Two portions already.

Then stop. Ask Perrin what he does first — sits, speaks, looks around. Nona is at the counter and will not turn until she hears a chair move.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Settles. Nona converts weeks of silence and the Vestra's loss into the terms of what Perrin owes and what she will give. |
| Unstable Condition | Nona does not know the *Vestra* is gone. Perrin does. Everything else in the scene waits behind that. |
| Consequence | How Perrin handles the Vestra reveal determines whether the Tangle treats the party as trusted assets or expensive liabilities. |
| Link of Relevance | Perrin's family credit; Tangle access for ship disguise; the Below; three active Warren problems. |

## Scene Spine

| Beat | Scene | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The food | Nona feeds Perrin before she says anything. Enzo and Ruk are present. Silence is allowed. |
| 2 | What she has noticed | Nona names what she already knows — his route, his ship, his crew. She asks about Jean-Claude specifically. |
| 3 | The Jean-Claude pivot | The moment Perrin confirms a Grung is with him, Nona sets down her spoon. First ask lands here. |
| 4 | The Vestra | Perrin tells her. She hears it. See DM Notes below. |
| 5 | The Tangle leads | She names what she needs from him — Bela, Marrow, Ferrin — pick one before the table clears. |
| 6 | The held-back thing | *"There is one other thing. Not tonight."* The Aruhe commission. She tells Perrin alone, later. |

---

## Running the Scene

**The food comes first.** Nona will not begin the conversation until Perrin has eaten. Ruk may offer more stew. This is not a tactic — it is how she operates. The players will feel the weight of whatever they are about to say under the cover of soup.

**She already knows more than Perrin expects.** The Passage has ears. She knows he arrived in La Vasca, she knows who is with him, she has a fragmentary read on the *Surety*. She will not say how much she knows until she has heard what Perrin volunteers. Note what he omits.

**She asks about Jean-Claude by description, not by name.** She has a Passage report: *"one of your crew is not Dry and not Rattkin."* She wants to know what that means. When Perrin tells her — that Jean-Claude is a Grung, or Grung-connected, or that there is a Grung traveling with them — she sets down whatever is in her hands.

> [!read-aloud]
> Nona sets down her spoon. She folds her hands on the table. "How well does he know their kind?"

If the answer is well, or if Jean-Claude is actually present at the table: she pivots immediately. The sewer problem has been sitting on her for two weeks. She offers it before the Tangle leads, before the Vestra, almost before pleasantries are done. This is the first ask.

> *"Before the other things. I need to know what is in the tunnels under my city."*

Full job brief: [[warren-grung-sewers|Warren — Grung in the Sewers]].

**The Vestra reveal.** Nona will not ask about the ship by name. She will ask about Vincenzo's chair at the table — whether Perrin has been sitting in it. The conversation will arrive at the *Vestra* through what Perrin says or fails to say.

> [!read-aloud]
> Nona looks at the far end of the table. Then she looks at Perrin. "Vincenzo's chair. Have you been sitting in it?"

When she hears it, she will:

1. Stop moving.
2. Set down whatever is in her hands carefully.
3. Be quiet for several seconds.
4. Ask only: *"How?"*

She does not cry at the table. She has too much practice with this. What Perrin sees is the moment she decides to carry it alone, and he knows that look.

After a breath: *"Tell me what you need."*

**The Tangle's offer.** Nona will route the *Surety* disguise work through the Tangle, provide Passage broker access for false papers, and let the party use Warren channels for city movement. The cost is named plainly:

> *"I need three things looked at. You don't have to do all of them. But you'll take one before you leave this table."*

She does not explain what the three things are until Perrin agrees to look. Then she gives him the leads — Bela, Marrow's crate, the leak — in the order she thinks he can stomach them. Bela first; it has a clock.

**The thing she holds back.** If Perrin's standing is good by the end of the meal, she does not bring up Aruhe at the table. She says: *"There is one other thing. Not tonight."* She tells Perrin about it later, privately. The Aruhe commission is a different kind of ask — not a Tangle favour, not a debt. She has not decided yet whether to frame it as one. Full details: [[nona-midchain-commission|Nona's Midchain Commission]].

## Loaded Guns

## DM Notes

**Nona's voice.** She is not performing warmth and she is not performing menace. She is tired and capable and specific. Her sentences are short. She asks questions that assume you will answer honestly because she will know if you don't.

Voice cues:

> *"I'm not going to ask you to grieve faster than you're ready to. But I need you working."*

Public player primer for the Shattered Sea campaign — setting overview, major factions, homebrew peoples, ship rules, and character creation guidance.

# Player Primer

![[The-Shattered-Sea.webp|Aerial view of the Shattered Sea island chain with turquoise reefs and scattered green islands]]

The **[[shattered-sea|Shattered Sea]]**, 1495 DR: sixty thousand square miles of reef, deep channel, cliff port, free harbour, lost ruin, colonial ledger, old god, hungry storm, and ships with too many secrets in the hold. Magic here is part of the infrastructure — enchanted instruments, divine tribute systems, ruins still running on power no one has claimed, and magic treated the same way everything else is treated out here: as leverage.

This is a sandbox campaign about sailing past the edges of the map. You will bargain with captains who smile while counting your exits, dodge patrol officers who treat extortion as paperwork, hear prayers muttered into saltwater before every voyage, and learn which islands welcome strangers only because they have not decided what to charge yet.

The sea is beautiful. The sea is expensive. The sea remembers.

---

## What Kind of Story Is This?

TLDR: Seen Archer? That but Age of Sail High Magic DnD with some Renaissance punk vibes

[[shattered-sea|The Shattered Sea]] is swashbuckling, dangerous, and a little rotten under the polish. Warships fly lacquered pennants over holds full of stolen cargo. Merchant princes speak softly because they already own the room. Priests of [[umberlee-and-waveservants|Umberlee]] bless ships with one hand and count tribute with the other. Pirates, smugglers, clerks, monks, hunters, spies, and deserters all use the same docks because out here everyone needs passage eventually.

Expect:

- **Nautical exploration** across islands, reefs, storms, trenches, and contested ports.
- **High magic in practical hands**: enchanted instruments, divine tribute, old ruins, ship upgrades, strange species, and magic treated as part of the economy.
- **Colonial pressure** without a clean map of good and evil. Institutions want taxes, leverage, obedience, labour, souls, or silence. Individuals inside them may want something smaller and messier.
- **Ancient mysteries** visible at the edges: impossible stone, wrong currents, missing ships, old records, and sailors who refuse to say what they saw east of the charts.
- **Player-driven trouble.** There is no single correct route. Your alliances, grudges, bargains, and mistakes are the plot.

---

## The Sea Itself

Two hard boundaries define the Scatter. To the west, the [[galewall|Galewall]]. To the east, the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]]. Between them, everything else.

![[Shattered-Sea-Map.webp|Illustrated map of the Shattered Sea showing its island chains, currents, and surrounding regions]]

The air changes before land appears: warm, salt-heavy, green with rainforest carried over the water. Then the islands rise in pieces: pale limestone, black basalt, dark jungle, reef water bright enough to hurt your eyes, and deep channels where the colour drops away all at once.

The main island chain is the **[[verdant-scatter|Verdant Scatter]]**, running between the [[galewall|Galewall]] and the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] in two arcs: the larger, more administered **[[crown-islands|Crown Islands]]** to the north and the denser, harder-to-govern **[[midchain|Midchain]]** to the south. Between them runs the **[[central-strait|Central Strait]]**, the main trade route of the region.

### [[galewall|The Galewall]]

![[Ashwall-Islands.webp|Dark volcanic islands rising from rough gray water beneath a stormy sky]]

To the west stands the [[galewall|Galewall]], a permanent tropical storm belt between the Scatter and the colonial homelands. It appears first as a dark line across the horizon, then as stacked grey weather systems with cold water underneath and wind that builds in stages.

Crossing it takes about three weeks with an experienced pilot. Everyone knows a ship that did not make it. For most sailors, the [[galewall|Galewall]] is not a route. It is a dare with a fee attached.

### [[crown-islands|The Crown Islands]]

![[Crown-Islands.webp|Mountainous green Crown Islands ringed by bright reefs under clearing storm clouds]]

The northern arc is made of five broad, mountainous islands with forested highlands, deep natural harbours, reef systems, and Dravosi flags at every major anchorage. The islands are rich enough to feed cities and steep enough to fortify, which is why the colonial powers have never stopped caring about them.

Publicly, the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] mean administration: ratings, inspections, port fees, naval patrols, trade houses, and harbours where authority has a uniform. They are safer than the [[midchain|Midchain]] in the way a locked room is safer than an open road.

### [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]]

![[Port-Tidefall.webp|Fortified cliffside port city built in tiers above a busy harbor]]

[[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] is the Dravosi fortress-port at the western mouth of the [[central-strait|Central Strait]], carved directly into the cliff face of [[calders-tooth|Calder's Tooth]]. The city rises in tiers: Dockfront at the waterline, the Shelf mid-cliff, and [[fort-crestwall|Fort Crestwall]] above with cannon looking seaward.

This is where the Crown's authority is loudest and most negotiable. Every ship entering the Strait is expected to submit to inspection. The [[harbourmasters-office|Harbourmaster's Office]] sells charts and ratings; the [[waveservants|Waveservants]] keep a shrine near the waterline; and the gallows at the harbour gate make sure nobody mistakes bureaucracy for softness.

### [[calveno|Calveno]]

![[Calveno.webp|Sunlit canal city of pale stone buildings and boats moving through turquoise water]]

[[calveno|Calveno]] is the oldest commercial centre in the Scatter: a canal city of pale stone facades, flat-bottomed boats, public negotiations, and private debts. There are no docks in the ordinary sense. Boats thread through channels cut between buildings, and the sound of the city is a thousand conversations happening at once in the open.

Everything here is visible. That is the point. Deals are witnessed, alliances are performed, and the right association seen by the right people can matter as much as the cargo itself. [[tessarine-concordat|The Tessarine Concordat]] has deep roots here, as does the Rattkin [[the-passage|Passage]].

### [[central-strait|The Central Strait]]

![[Central-Strait.webp|Wide blue-green shipping strait cutting between low islands and reef shallows]]

[[central-strait|The Central Strait]] is the broad corridor of pale blue-green water between the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] and the [[midchain|Midchain]]. It runs forty to eighty miles wide depending on where you cross, deep enough for the largest vessels in the region and sheltered enough that smaller ships use it constantly.

This is the Scatter's main east-west highway. The current pushes east whether you want it to or not, spinner dolphins work the shipping lanes, and Dravosi inspection at the western mouth makes the Strait profitable before a single cargo changes hands.

### [[midchain|The Midchain]]

![[The-Midchain.webp|Cluster of lush Midchain islands surrounded by bright reef water and deep channels]]

The southern arc is dozens of small and medium islands packed close together: limestone, coral, jungle, reef, hidden channels, and local arrangements that do not survive contact with paperwork. Most islands are a half-day's sail from the next. Fresh water, shelter, and trouble are always nearby.

[[midchain|The Midchain]] is difficult to govern from outside. Colonial powers hold strategic points and send patrols through the channels, but most of the region belongs to island groups, free ports, smugglers, pilots, family networks, and whoever knows the reef better than the person chasing them. [[kalowe|Kalowe]] as well as the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] both call the midchain home.

### [[kalowe|Kalowe]]

![[Kalowe.webp|Harbor settlement on a low tropical island at sunset, with cranes and boats along the shore]]

[[kalowe|Kalowe]] is the primary [[midchain|Midchain]] free port, built across three reef islands over a natural lagoon. The reef breaks the swells, the harbour water lies mirror-flat, and the dry dock cranes are the first thing visible above the treeline on approach.

If [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]] is where papers become chains, [[kalowe|Kalowe]] is where papers become optional. It is the standard port for unregistered vessels, black-market cargo, crew-for-hire, ship repairs, and people who need to become harder to find. It has no colonial authority, which is not the same thing as having no politics.

### [[verdant-teeth|The Verdant Teeth]]

![[Sorn.webp|Forested island with a pale beach and dense jungle rising inland]]

Two days south-west of [[kalowe|Kalowe]] sit the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]], five closely grouped islands held by [[grung-clans|Grung clans]]. From the water they read as dense rainforest, low reef-fringed coasts, and elevated limestone ridges hidden under canopy. Charts mark the interiors with some version of "do not approach."

Outsiders trade at designated beaches and stay at the waterline. The [[grung-clans|Grung]] touch is poisonous, their caste protocols are strict, and the coastal settlements of the [[midchain|Midchain]] know that raid activity has worsened. Everyone has heard enough to avoid the interior. Some merchants still go to the beach for the lucrative trade opportunities.

### [[tail|The Tail]]

![[The-Tail.webp|Storm-dark island chain with steep green ridges and white surf breaking through channels]]

[[tail|The Tail]] is where both arcs of the Scatter narrow toward the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]]. The islands grow fewer, taller, colder, and more wind-exposed. High cliffs drop straight to deep water, morning fog burns off by midday, and the sea takes on a harder colour near the shelf edge.

This is Maw-adjacent country: longline grounds, serious pilots, salvage staging, cliff communities, and people who have lived close enough to the trench to stop treating unease as useful information. From here, the east stops feeling like direction and starts feeling like depth.

### [[the-drowned-maw|The Drowned Maw]]

![[The-Drowned-Maw.webp|Vast dark blue ocean sinkhole spiraling into deep water]]

To the east lies the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]], a vast deep-sea trench where compasses drift, sound carries strangely, and the water turns dark long before the horizon changes. Sailors cross it regularly. Most have no trouble. The ones who do have trouble tend to become warnings rather than sources.

The Maw is not forbidden. Nothing so simple. Ships go there for salvage, pilgrimage, research, desperation, and profit. The [[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|Sentinels of the Eyrie]] watch it from the [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]]. [[waveservants|The Waveservants]] do not like questions about it. Every chart grows less confident near the edge.

### [[outer-reach|The Outer Reach]] and [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]]

![[Sunken-Crown.webp|Circular reef atoll surrounding a dark central lagoon in open water]]

East of the Maw, the charts thin out into open ocean. The [[outer-reach|Outer Reach]] has no colonial presence, no reliable resupply, and few landmarks a western pilot would trust. Getting there means crossing the Maw and then committing to days of open water.

The best-known region beyond is the [[sunken-crown|Sunken Crown]]: five low islands around a deep blue hole, black stone and pale reef around water that drops too cleanly to be comfortable. It is associated with old [[umberlee-and-waveservants|Umberlee]] worship, isolated [[tabaxi|Tabaxi]] communities, and local navigation that outsiders routinely underestimate.

---

## Powers on the Water

- **[[dravosi-crown|The Dravosi Crown]]** controls much of the [[crown-islands|Crown Islands]] through naval force, fortress ports, and a bureaucracy that treats paperwork like divine law. Resistance becomes "administrative non-compliance," and administrative non-compliance can become cannon fire once properly filed.

- **[[tessarine-concordat|The Tessarine Concordat]]** prefers leverage to conquest. Its factors dress plainly, speak warmly, and always know the current price of what you are carrying. They do not need to seize a city if they can own it.

- **[[the-passage|The Passage]]** is the [[rattkin|Rattkin]] network beneath and between the ports: runs, holds, courier routes, hidden caches, and spoken in skitter-cant, a completely silent language of nose and whisker movement.

- **[[grung-clans|The Grung Clans]]** hold the rainforest interiors of the [[verdant-teeth|Verdant Teeth]] in the [[midchain|Midchain]]. Coastal islanders trade at designated beaches and do not go inland. Everyone knows Grung touch is poisonous. Everyone knows the slave raids have been getting worse.

- **[[umberlee-and-waveservants|Umberlee]] and the [[waveservants|Waveservants]]** are the religious fact of life at sea. [[umberlee-and-waveservants|Umberlee]], often called the Bitch Queen of the Sea, is the goddess of storms, shipwrecks, and the sea's destructive appetite. Her [[waveservants|Waveservants]] keep shrines at port entries, their robes smell of tallow and brine, and their blessings are transactional by design. They collect tribute from everyone. Sailors who do not pay do not sail, or at least do not sail confidently.

- **[[sentinels-of-the-eyrie|The Sentinels of the Eyrie]]** are an [[aarakocra|Aarakocra]] monastic order watching the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] from high basalt stone. They are not a navy, not a church, and not a government. They observe, record, and keep recording when everyone else starts arguing about what the records mean. **[[high-eyrie|The High Eyrie]]** is their basalt sea-stack monastery near the northeastern Crown coast. Visitors are rare, the practical approach is aerial, and its ledgers are understood to be the most complete Maw observation record in the Scatter.

---

## Peoples of the Shattered Sea

Most species from the 2024 sourcebooks have a place in the Scatter. The following homebrew options are native to the setting:

- **[[grung|Grung]]**: amphibious, poisonous, caste-shaped survivors of a harsh society. A Grung PC should be ready to define what they believe about the order they came from.
- **[[rattkin|Rattkin]]**: small, flexible, hard to catch, and native to the hidden infrastructure of port life. Rattkin make excellent smugglers, scouts, couriers, spies, sailors, and people who were definitely not in that locked room.
- **[[tabaxi|Tabaxi]]**: feline humanoids with ancient roots in the [[shattered-sea|Shattered Sea]], especially among the isolated island tribes of the Sunken Crown.
- **[[aarakocra|Aarakocra]]**: winged people whose relationship to height, distance, and danger is fundamentally different from ground-bound folk.

If you want to play something stranger, ask. [[shattered-sea|The Shattered Sea]] has room for oddities, but the character still needs a reason to stay with the crew.

---

## Ships, Home, and Upgrades

Your vessel is not just transportation. It is shelter, leverage, reputation, storage, escape route, and eventually home.

Once the ship is yours, it operates as a combined **[[ship-bastion|Ship Bastion]]**: the 2024 [[ship-bastion|Bastion]] rules adapted for a mobile vessel.

- Facility slots are pooled across the party.
- Weekly Bastion Turns handle upkeep, crew wages, facility orders, repairs, trade, visitors, and maritime events.
- Ship size matters. A sloop cannot hold the same life, guns, cargo, and magical infrastructure as a frigate. See **[[ship-stats|Ship Stats]]** for the tier system.

Early on, expect to think like sailors even before you own the deck under your feet. Crew, cargo, water, repairs, charts, port fees, bribes, and grudges all matter.

---

## The Starting Situation

You begin at **Level 3** aboard the *[[saltwright|Saltwright]]*.

![[Saltwright.webp|The Saltwright, a dark-sailed wooden ship crossing rough seas at dusk|730|892x502]]

A hard-used two-masted merchant brig captained by **[[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]]**, who offered you passage to [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]]

![[portraits/Beaumont-Sel.webp|Beaumont Sel, a weathered sailor gripping a ship's wheel by lantern light]]

You might be a paying passenger, a working hand, a shipwrecked survivor, a stowaway, a fugitive, a pilgrim, a hired blade, a scholar with bad funding, etc. Whatever brought you aboard, the *[[saltwright|Saltwright]]* is where your stories collide.

---

## Character Creation

- Use **D&D 2024 rules by default**. 2014 material is allowed if adapted cleanly to 2024.
- Start at **Level 3**.
- Roll stats with **4d6 drop lowest**. You may roll three arrays; if you hate all three, use point buy.
- Take standard starting equipment plus **one uncommon magic item** from your previous adventures.
- Official sourcebook content is static. Homebrew or adjusted content may be tuned during play if balance gets weird.
- Powerful, strange, optimized, comedic, or highly specific builds are welcome. The one hard requirement: make a character with some reason to work with the party.
- Character death is possible. The DM will not aim to kill you, but the sea, the dice, and your decisions will not be padded. Death will be treated with narrative weight, and resurrection or a new same-level character are both on the table.

### Optional: [[mortis|The Mortis System]]

A Mortis is a Session Zero option that pairs a permanent mechanical drawback with a targeted mechanical benefit. It is not a curse and not a punishment. It is a fact about your character expressed through mechanics: the same truth that limits them also makes them exceptional.

Mortises require DM approval and lock in at Session Zero.
