# Beat 5: Perrin

*Below the waterline, the [[saltwright|Saltwright]] is quiet.*

*Six feet of headroom, and two lanterns turned so far down they give off more warmth than light, a faint amber glow that turns the shadows amber too. Salt barrels along the starboard side, fish crates stacked to the port bulkhead, grain sacks loosely lashed in the back. The smell is brine and old wood and time, the deep-layered damp of a hull that has spent a decade below the waterline, and underneath all of it, the particular cold mineral smell of deep water very close, held back by nothing but two inches of planking.*

*It is close down here. Dark. Private.*

[Address Perrin directly.]

*You are one of the [[rattkin|Rattkin]]. [[the-passage|The Passage]] runs through every port in the Scatter on routes no colonial chart has captured. The [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi Crown]] keeps standing bounties on your kind — rarely enforced, always present.*

*The [[vestra|Vestra]] was your grandfather's ship. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw's]] husband built her, ran her, and left her to the family when he died. You inherited the route and everything that came with it. Three days ago something came up from the deep water over the Maw and took her apart. Something large and deliberate. You went into the water with nothing but your grandfather's cloak on your back. You woke up on the beach of [[keth-naar|Keth-Naar]] — a voice still echoing somewhere distant, and a blade in your hand you don't remember picking up.*

*The Saltwright was in the harbour. You found the hold before anyone found you. The captain doesn't know you're here. On your way down, you helped yourself to a couple of loose gems from a crate near the gangway.*

*Could you show us — who's hiding in this hold, and where?*

[Let the player go.]

[The hold is not silent — the deck above is audible through the planking. Boots, rope work, the occasional voice. A fishing competition. If Perrin explores: the false panel in the aft wall is latched shut and well-made. Whatever Beaumont keeps behind it, it isn't loose. The gems from the gangway crate are the only find. If they ask about a better hiding spot: this is the only one. Let them settle. Then:]

*Then, against the hull, something lands.*

*Not a wave. Not the vessel settling. A weight, deliberate and controlled, pressing against the outside of the planking at waterline level, and then going perfectly still.*

> [!check] Perception
>
> This roll is flavour only — something is out there regardless of the result.
>
> - **DC 12**: Large, warm-blooded, and clinging to the hull. It came from the water. It is not struggling.

> - **DC 20**: There is a smell drifting through the gap in the planking above it. Amphibious, but not fish. Not salt. Something different that clears your sinuses.

# Beat 6: Jean-Claude

*You stand on white sand, and you can smell them before you can hear them.*

*You came out of the Verdant Teeth. Five islands two days south of [[kalowe|Kalowe]], dense rainforest canopy, Grung territory as far back as anyone has records. Your people run on caste and colour — blue ranks below purple ranks below gold — and the system holds because everyone inside it believes it is the only way. You believed it too, once.*

*A month ago you ran. A gnome is dead. A sister named Simone made a choice, and you left in the dark with people screaming behind you. You have been moving through the [[midchain|Midchain]] since, one island ahead of the hunter unit Simone assembled. They know your methods. She taught them.*

*Dense scrub at your back, close enough to scratch. Mangroves to your left, their roots threading down into dark water, the whole tangle breathing salt and wet green and mud in the heat. The air clings to you.*

*Could you show us who's standing on that beach right now?*

[Let them finish. If they ask about the hunters: half a mile out, dogs in front, they have a scent and they know it. If they ask about the channel: wide and dark and warm — JC reads water the way Stripes reads fish, and this channel is swimmable, but 200 feet of open dark water with dogs on the bank is not a plan. The ship is the only option that doesn't make things worse.]

*A month without being seen. Almost.*

*They are getting closer. Half a mile in the trees, maybe less. Several of them, moving with the confidence of people who have a trail and know it. In front of them, rampaging through the underbrush, dogs.*

# Beat 7: The Hold

*(On deck. Address Delmar, Crissdalynn, and Stripes.)*

*[[beaumont-sel|Beaumont]]'s voice drops a register when he speaks again. The ease is still there. So is something beneath it.*

**Beaumont**: *"Passenger, go below."* He tilts his head toward the hatch. *"Port hatch. You and the bird both."*

*"Patrol boat. Won't take long."*

[If they push back or ask if it's dangerous:]

**Beaumont**: *"Mais, I run this route eleven years. They know [[saltwright|the Saltwright]]. They know me."* A pause. *"Go below and let me handle it, cher. Ol' Rook is a pussycat."*

*Delmar, you go first. The ladder is steep and the hold swallows you whole. The smell hits before your eyes adjust: brine, old fish, the amber lantern light barely reaching the far corners.*

*Stripes — Beaumont's look finds you too. A tilt of the old head toward the hatch. Down you go.*

> [!dm]
> Three hiding zones: salt barrels along starboard, fish crates stacked against the port bulkhead, grain sacks loosely lashed at the aft wall. Crates are the best cover — deepest shadow, tightest lanes. Anyone declaring stealth does it now, before Crissdalynn comes down.

*Crissdalynn, you come down behind him. Six feet of headroom. You fit, but only just.*

> [!dm]
> Jean-Claude is afraid of birds — instinctive, not chosen. The moment Crissdalynn descends the ladder, play it: Jean-Claude presses flat against the farthest bulkhead, hand on whatever weapon is closest. Crissdalynn doesn't know why. Delmar sees it first. Give that a beat — let Jean-Claude's player decide how they handle the six-foot Aarakocra now sharing their hiding spot in the dark. If the group is being stealthy, ask Jean-Claude for a Stealth check with disadvantage. Whatever the result, the real point is the held breath — two strangers in a dark hold, one of them barely keeping it together, all of them listening to boots cross the deck overhead. Five people in this hold. Nobody planned it. Give it one beat before the ship moves.

*Then the ship moves.*

*A groan from outside the hull, low and structural, the sound of timber under pressure. Another vessel coming alongside in the dark. The [[saltwright|Saltwright]] adjusts to the new weight in a slow, unwilling shift, a change in the rhythm underfoot. Iron on rail. Rope going taut somewhere above you. The sound of it travels through the planking like a hand pressed flat against the wood.*

*Boots on the deck. Several sets, moving without hurry. Then a voice: clipped, bored.*

> [!dm]
> This is [[barnaby-rook|Rook]]. He's above the hatch, not yet visible. Play him flat and practiced — a man who runs this shakedown on every route and has stopped finding it interesting. The boredom is the threat.

*"Manifest. Mr Sel."*

*Beaumont's voice comes down through the planking, unhurried:* **"Right here, cher. Salt, dried fish, cloth out of [[kalowe|Kalowe]]. Eleven years on this route, ya'll should remember? Where's Norrington?"**

*A beat.*

*"Officer Kingsly has retired."*

*Beaumont goes quiet for just a moment.*

**Beaumont**: *"Mm."*

*Hushed orders. Footsteps spreading out across the deck above your heads.*

*"Where's your strongbox?"*

**Beaumont**: *"Non. No strongbox. I keep what I need on me."*

*"Merchant Naval Code c147b. Merchant vessels must securely lock all valuables and contain a working strongbox. You're deficient."* A small pause — the sound of a man who has memorised this line and finds it very useful. *"It's a safety issue."*

*Beaumont's voice does not change.* **"I don't know anything about that, cher. I run the same route I always run."**

*"New policy."* The footsteps shift. Slow. Moving toward the wheel. Toward Beaumont. *"Forty gold clears it tonight. Or we hold the cargo at [[calveno|Calveno]] while the paperwork sorts itself out. Could be a while."*

*Long enough that you hear the water against the hull. Long enough that you hear [[bisou|Bisou]] make one small sound above you.*

**Beaumont**: *"Don't play now, cher."*

*"Then we'll take a look below. See what else you're carrying."*

*Above you, Beaumont goes quiet. The footsteps move toward the hatch.*

*What do you do?*

> [!dm]
> Party options: fight before the crew reaches the bottom of the ladder, let themselves be found and see what Rook actually wants, or signal Beaumont and let him buy more time. All three are viable. The hatch opens in one round. See Session 01 for the boarding encounter.

# The Saltwright Boarding

*This encounter begins the moment the party commits at the end of Scene 07 — The Hold. Initiative starts on the first hostile action.*

## Setup

[[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] has left the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] and boarded the [[saltwright|Saltwright]], shaking down [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] under the pretense of an inspection. The party is below deck. When they're found, the best Rook offers is forty gold Beaumont doesn't have.

## Balance Overview

**XP Thresholds — 5 PCs, Level 3**

| Tier | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Easy | 375 XP |
| Medium | 750 XP |
| Hard | 1,125 XP |
| Deadly | 2,000 XP |

**Phase Budget Summary**

| Phase | Enemies | Adjusted XP | Rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — The Hold | 2× Deckhand, 1× Enforcer (crossbow) | 225 | Easy |
| 2 — Above Deck | 2× Enforcer, 2× Deckhand | 375 | Medium* |
| 3 — The Gangplank | Rook (CR 3), 1× Enforcer, 1× Alchemist | 1,500 | Hard** |

\*\* The gangplank bottleneck cuts effective party DPR ~40%, pushing into Hard-to-Deadly in practice.

Between-phase breathing room exists. Not a short rest, but enough for a healing potion or tactical reset. Spell slots and ki points don't come back.

### Phase 1 — The Hold

*Party has every advantage. The Enforcer makes it a real fight.*

Three of Rook's crew descend: two deckhands up front, an Enforcer behind them with a heavy crossbow. Standard inspection. They expect shrimp and provisions, not five armed strangers.

Beaumont's emergency stash: 3× potions of healing (2d4+2 each) behind a false panel in the hold's aft wall — visible to any PC who looks aft.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Combatants** | 2× Dravosi Deckhands, 1× Dravosi Enforcer (heavy crossbow — effectively melee in here) |
| **Terrain** | Cramped cargo hold. Maximum engagement range ~20 ft; most lanes 5 ft wide. |
| **Lighting** | Dark. The Enforcer has no darkvision — fighting blind unless he reaches a lantern cone. |
| **Loot** | Beaumont's potion stash: 3× Potion of Healing behind a false panel aft wall. |
| **Surprise** | Party has it. |
| **Pressure** | If any crewman gets off an audible shout, Phase 2 loses surprise. |
| **Win condition** | All three crewmen silenced before they can signal above. |

**PC Spotlights — Phase 1**

- **JC:** Umbral Sight active. Invisible to darkvision creatures, advantage on attacks. Priority target: the Enforcer before he closes to melee.
- **Crissdalynn:** No darkvision. Best position near the hatch to intercept anyone breaking for the ladder.
- **Delmar:** Cramped lanes isolate targets. Rakish Audacity fires freely. Burn SA on the Enforcer first, not low-HP deckhands.
- **Perrin:** Vicious Mockery costs no attack roll and doesn't need line of sight beyond 60 ft. Good opener to shave the Enforcer's first attack.
- **Stripes:** The hold aisle is a single chokepoint he can own. Trip Attack keeps the Enforcer prone; he can't stand without eating an opportunity attack. Action Surge ends him in one round.

| Direction | Lever | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Easier | Remove the Enforcer — only two deckhands descend | Drops to ~75 XP (Trivial) |
| Easier | Alert Call requires crewman's action, not a reaction | Gives party a full round |
| Harder | Enforcer has a lit hooded lantern on his belt | Collapses JC's Umbral Sight in the same zone |
| Harder | One deckhand was already below, watching quietly | No full surprise; he shouts immediately on Round 1 |

### Phase 2 — Above Deck

*Pirates have position; party has momentum.*

The party emerges through the hatch. If Phase 1 was clean, topside crew is watching, not expecting resistance.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Combatants** | 2× Dravosi Enforcers at the hatch, 2× Dravosi Deckhands at the rail |
| **Terrain** | Open deck, night. [[beaumont-sel\|Beaumont]] is at the wheel. |
| **Lighting** | Dim — full night, only the Saltwright's lanterns. |
| **Pressure** | Deckhands at the rail can signal the gangplank to pull before Phase 3 is possible. |
| **Win condition** | Deck crew defeated or driven back before the gangplank is pulled. |

**PC Spotlights — Phase 2**

- **Crissdalynn:** Send airborne toward the rail deckhands immediately — she can intercept before they reach the gangplank.
- **JC:** Umbral Sight still operational in patches near the hull and rigging. Position matters.
- **Delmar:** Enforcers at the hatch are clustered — needs one ally adjacent or isolatable target for Sneak Attack.
- **Perrin:** Clear sight lines to rail deckhands = Eldritch Blast lanes. Priority: whoever is closer to the gangplank.
- **Stripes:** Feline Agility closes instantly. Disarming Strike breaks one Enforcer's Pack Tactics and hands Delmar a clean Sneak Attack angle.

| Direction | Lever | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Easier | Split the Enforcers — one at hatch, one at rail | Breaks Pack Tactics; reduces to single +4 attacks |
| Easier | Deckhands break for the gangplank on their first turn | Converts to chase objective rather than combatants |
| Harder | Both Enforcers focus the first PC out of the hatch with Pack Tactics | ~75% hit chance; avg 18 damage in one round — enough to drop Perrin or Crissdalynn |
| Harder | Alchemist throws an Incendiary Flask through the open hatch as party emerges | DC 13 Dex save, 2d6 fire + burning; raises Phase 2 XP to ~575 |

## What Happened (Played)

### Summary

The party cleared all three phases of the boarding encounter. Phase 1 went fast — the party had the drop on the Dravosi crew in the hold. Cap'n Gorgeous (the Dravosi Enforcer) walked into the ambush and was killed instantly before he could call a shout. The two deckhands followed. Phase 1 complete without alerting the topside crew.

Phase 2: Delmar boosted [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] through the hatchway; she burst out and knocked two deck Dravosi prone. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] and [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] came up through a gap in the decking and flanked. Both Dravosi Enforcers dispatched; one deckhand named [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] surrendered when he saw his allies fall. Delmar picked up Geoffrey's sword after he dropped it and gave it back to him — Geoffrey joined the party as the first member of their crew.

Phase 3: The party used Jean-Claude's [[flask-of-endless-water|Decanter of Endless Water]] to blast [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] off the gangplank, separating him from the Enforcer and Alchemist. They quickly finished the Enforcer and wounded the Alchemist severely. The Alchemist threw a gas canister; only Jean-Claude and Perrin were caught in the cloud and both resisted. Jean-Claude identified the batch — standard Grung hunting stock, specifically Simone's hand. The Alchemist was then dispatched. Rook hauled himself back aboard and fired his flintlock at Beaumont; the round bounced off Beaumont's shell. Beaumont entered the fight. Session wrapped here.

### Key Events

- **Phase 1 — The Hold:** Party ambushed the boarding crew in the dark. [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]] (Dravosi Enforcer, nicknamed for his appearance) was killed in a single round before he could alert topside. Both deckhands dispatched. Phase 1 complete with surprise intact for Phase 2.
- **Phase 2 — Above Deck:** Crissdalynn launched through the hatch with Delmar's assist, knocking two Dravosi prone. Perrin and Jean-Claude breached from a gap in the decking and flanked. Dravosi Enforcers and one deckhand killed. Geoffrey Draves surrendered. Delmar returned his sword and recruited him; Geoffrey became the party's first crew member.
- **Geoffrey Draves recruited:** Dropped his sword when he saw the fight turn. Delmar convinced him, returned the blade, and he fought on the party's side. First crew acquisition despite the party having no ship yet.
- **Phase 3 — The Gangplank:** Rook separated from his men by a Decanter blast. Party killed the Enforcer and wounded the Alchemist. Canister thrown; Jean-Claude and Perrin both resisted.
- **The Canister Reveal:** Jean-Claude passed the save and placed the gas. Cheap Grung hunting stock — specifically [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]]'s batch. His sister is supplying the Dravosi Crown. He said nothing. Phase 3 continued.
- **Beaumont enters the fight:** Rook fired his flintlock at Beaumont from the gangplank; the round deflected off his shell. Beaumont joined combat: *"Boy, I shit out harder things than you every mornin'."* Session ended here.
- **Current state at session close:** Barnaby Rook — unharmed, alone, all minions dead. Party — full resources largely intact. Encounter still in progress.

Beaumont’s emergency stash: 3× potions of healing (2d4+2 each) behind a false panel in the hold’s aft wall — visible to any PC who looks aft.

What Happened (Played)

Summary

The party cleared all three phases of the boarding encounter. Phase 1 went fast — the party had the drop on the Dravosi crew in the hold. Cap’n Gorgeous (the Dravosi Enforcer) walked into the ambush and was killed instantly before he could call a shout. The two deckhands followed. Phase 1 complete without alerting the topside crew.

Phase 2: Delmar boosted Crissdalynn through the hatchway; she burst out and knocked two deck Dravosi prone. Perrin and Jean-Claude came up through a gap in the decking and flanked. Both Dravosi Enforcers dispatched; one deckhand named Geoffrey Draves surrendered when he saw his allies fall. Delmar picked up Geoffrey’s sword after he dropped it and gave it back to him — Geoffrey joined the party as the first member of their crew.

Phase 3: The party used Jean-Claude’s Decanter of Endless Water to blast Barnaby Rook off the gangplank, separating him from the Enforcer and Alchemist. They quickly finished the Enforcer and wounded the Alchemist severely. The Alchemist threw a gas canister; only Jean-Claude and Perrin were caught in the cloud and both resisted. Jean-Claude identified the batch — standard Grung hunting stock, specifically Simone’s hand. The Alchemist was then dispatched. Rook hauled himself back aboard and fired his flintlock at Beaumont; the round bounced off Beaumont’s shell. Beaumont entered the fight. Session wrapped here.

  • Phase 2 — Above Deck: Crissdalynn launched through the hatch with Delmar’s assist, knocking two Dravosi prone. Perrin and Jean-Claude breached from a gap in the decking and flanked. Dravosi Enforcers and one deckhand killed. Geoffrey Draves surrendered. Delmar returned his sword and recruited him; Geoffrey became the party’s first crew member.

Player recap of Session 02 — the taking of the HCS Surety, the galley below, and the moral weight of a caged Moucheron. Canon events as they happened.

# 02 — Conflict is a Surety

---

[[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] had been in the water once. The [[flask-of-endless-water|Flask of Endless Water]] hadn't been enough. He hauled himself back over the rail, cold and furious, crew dead or defected. The ship's bell rang. Gun ports ground open.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-01-rook-final.webp|Barnaby Rook knocked from the HCS Surety rigging into dark water]]

[[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]]'s wind bent him toward the rail, then away. He fired his flintlock at close range. She caught it on her bracers.

[[beaumont-sel|Beaumont]] solved the cannon problem by throwing [[bisou|Bisou]] through a gun port. She pissed in the powder. [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] fired through the second port and hit [[ensign-wouters|Ensign Wouters]] in the dark below. The guns stayed quiet.

Rook went back up the rigging. Delmar picked up a chair, called for the wind, threw it. Rook went into the water a second time. Something long and eel-like moved through it.

[[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] fished out his admiral hat with a boat hook. [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont]] said it belonged to the captain.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-02-beaumont-reckoning.webp|Beaumont Sel settles accounts with the party on the captured HCS Surety]]

Beaumont settled accounts.

To [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]]: a Friend of the [[the-passage|Passage]], any Kin in need could ask. Quietly: [[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] was looking for her lost grandson, and believed [[anzolo|Anzolo]] had already been sent.

Beaumont slid a [[truth-stone|Truth Stone]] across the decking to [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]. He told the truth: former kinsmen had hunted him, he stowed away to survive, nobody sent him.

[[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] led them below, leading with the cook.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-03-grigori-galley.webp|Shepherd Grigori hosts the party in the HCS Surety galley]]

The galley smelled wrong for a ship — bread, herbs, something on a low heat. [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] waited at the head of the table: dark wild hair, a [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine]] shirt, a [[dravosi-crown|Dravosi]] naval coat rolled to the sleeves. He asked what kind of pirates they were. No trafficking, no cannibalism, Robin Hood — near enough. He told them about Cap'n Gorgeous, and [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]], who will send ships. His condition: anyone who wants off at the next port walks free. Then he mentioned they'd forgotten to feed Ket. Every sailor found something to look at on the ceiling.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-04-ket-cage.webp|Ket watches from his brass cage in the HCS Surety hold]]

[[ket|Ket]] was a [[moucheron|Moucheron]] — pigeon-sized, sentient, a starving humanoid mosquito from [[murrat|Murrat]]. Rook had taken him as a specimen, curious about the mercenaries out of [[kalowe|Kalowe]] — the [[five-blades|Five Blades]].

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] filled a wine glass with his own blood. Ket drank. His abdomen went red. Calmer. Not safe.

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] drew his longsword and moved for the cage. [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] got there first, deflected the blade, put herself between Perrin and the bars — and stepped past the safe distance. Ket fed from her arm. She pulled back. Perrin cast Tasha's Hideous Laughter. Ket went down giggling in mosquito honks.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-05-ket-release.webp|Ket feeds from Ensign Wouters' body and leaves the opened cage]]

They used Wouters' body as a lure. Perrin sprung the cage with Mage Hand from across the room. Ket fed for a minute, lifted off, and flew toward home. Grigori said he was glad.

Crew assembled: [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]], [[sem-holst|Sem Holst]] the shipwright, [[alys-kuiper|Alys Kuiper]] the surgeon, [[old-faas|Old Faas]] for the rigging, [[thunk|Thunk]] (the good kind of explosion), young [[noor|Noor]]. Wouters was shot in the groin during boarding. Grigori was leaving at [[calveno|Calveno]] for Il Gioco delle Beffe.

Perrin told the crew who he was: a Black-Jaw. The [[the-passage|Passage]] code alongside captain's law.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-06-beaumont-departure.webp|The party watches the Saltwright depart from the captured HCS Surety]]

Rook's cabin: 45 gp, letters of marque, a blunderbuss. Under the floor: 110 gp, two garnets. The cargo held a pendant engraved *For Mira, from the sea*, and a crate — flintlocks, [[miras-blade|Mira's Blade]], twenty vials of Grung poison tincture, the same preparation Jean-Claude had recognised on the Alchemist's bandolier. Mira's Blade went to Perrin.

Morning. Beaumont warned the weather toward [[calveno|Calveno]], said he could be found in [[kalowe|Kalowe]] when off route. Delmar told him he had a friend in Admiral Fisk. [[bisou|Bisou]] had spent the morning removing 15 gp of shinies from the Surety; Beaumont called it fair business. The [[saltwright|Saltwright]] pulled away.

The [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] set heading for Calveno: still Crown-marked, still needing a name.

![[sessions/session-art/session-02-07-storm.webp|The HCS Surety holds anchor in a storm as something strikes the hull|355x200]]

Two hours out, a tropical storm hit from the east — roaring winds, rain horizontal, the sea steep and grey. Canvas down, anchors out. Jean-Claude was seasick.

Three hours in, a gap opened to the northwest: a Crown Isle on the route toward Calveno, probably [[aldenmere|Aldenmere]]. It closed.

Then the hull took an impact. A second. A third — the Surety lurched hard to port.

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] reached for his spyglass.

Shepherd Grigori waited at the head of the table: dark wild hair, a Tessarine shirt, a Dravosi naval coat rolled to the sleeves. He asked what kind of pirates they were. No trafficking, no cannibalism, Robin Hood — near enough. He told them about Cap’n Gorgeous, and Rupert Knighton, who will send ships. His condition: anyone who wants off at the next port walks free. Then he mentioned they’d forgotten to feed Ket. Every sailor found something to look at on the ceiling.

Ket was a Moucheron — pigeon-sized, sentient, a starving humanoid mosquito from Murrat. Rook had taken him as a specimen, curious about the mercenaries out of Kalowe — the Five Blades.

Jean-Claude filled a wine glass with his own blood. Ket drank. His abdomen went red. Calmer. Not safe.

Perrin drew his longsword and moved for the cage. Crissdalynn got there first, deflected the blade, put herself between Perrin and the bars — and stepped past the safe distance. Ket fed from her arm. She pulled back. Perrin cast Tasha’s Hideous Laughter. Ket went down giggling in mosquito honks.

They used Wouters’ body as a lure. Perrin sprung the cage with Mage Hand from across the room. Ket fed for a minute, lifted off, and flew toward home. Grigori said he was glad.

Crew assembled: Geoffrey Draves, Sem Holst the shipwright, Alys Kuiper the surgeon, Old Faas for the rigging, Thunk (the good kind of explosion), young Noor. Wouters was shot in the groin during boarding. Grigori was leaving at Calveno for Il Gioco delle Beffe.

Perrin told the crew who he was: a Black-Jaw. The Passage code alongside captain’s law.

Rook’s cabin: 45 gp, letters of marque, a blunderbuss. Under the floor: 110 gp, two garnets. The cargo held a pendant engraved For Mira, from the sea, and a crate — flintlocks, Mira’s Blade, twenty vials of Grung poison tincture, the same preparation Jean-Claude had recognised on the Alchemist’s bandolier. Mira’s Blade went to Perrin.

Morning. Beaumont warned the weather toward Calveno, said he could be found in Kalowe when off route. Delmar told him he had a friend in Admiral Fisk. Bisou had spent the morning removing 15 gp of shinies from the Surety; Beaumont called it fair business. The Saltwright pulled away.

The HCS Surety set heading for Calveno: still Crown-marked, still needing a name.

Two hours out, a tropical storm hit from the east — roaring winds, rain horizontal, the sea steep and grey. Canvas down, anchors out. Jean-Claude was seasick.

Three hours in, a gap opened to the northwest: a Crown Isle on the route toward Calveno, probably Aldenmere. It closed.

Then the hull took an impact. A second. A third — the Surety lurched hard to port.

Jean-Claude reached for his spyglass.

  • The hull — three impacts in the storm, the third deliberate. Something is out there.
  • The Knighton pursuit — Rupert Knighton will not forgive the death of Cap’n Gorgeous gently.
  • Simone’s supply line — Jean-Claude has the evidence. Twenty vials of Simone‘s tincture reached a Dravosi privateer. The party doesn’t have the full picture yet.
  • Nona and Anzolo — Nona Black-Jaw is looking. Anzolo may already be at sea. Perrin has named himself to the crew and is still moving.

# The Rook Resolution

*Opens mid-combat. [[barnaby-rook|Barnaby Rook]] hauled himself back aboard the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] after being blasted off the gangplank. He fired his flintlock at [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] — round deflected off the shell. Beaumont entered the fight. The [[dravosi-alchemist|Alchemist]] and [[capn-gorgeous|Enforcer]] are dead. [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]] is on the party's side.*

**Resolution:** See [[the-rook-resolution|the Rook Resolution page]] — Rook went into the water a second time in Session 02 and did not come back. Presumed dead, taken by something eel-like.

## State at Open

| Entity | Status |
|---|---|
| [[barnaby-rook\|Barnaby Rook]] | Unharmed. Alone. **120 HP. AC 17.** (4-PC: 110 HP.) Pistols fired. Cornered Wolf active. |
| [[capn-gorgeous\|Cap'n Gorgeous]] (Enforcer) | Dead |
| [[dravosi-alchemist\|Dravosi Alchemist]] | Dead. Gas canister resolved. |
| [[geoffrey-draves\|Geoffrey Draves]] | Defected; fighting with the party. Rook knows his name. |
| [[beaumont-sel\|Beaumont Sel]] | In the fight. CR 2, 44 HP, AC 19. Multiattack: Uppercut (+6, 1d8+4) and Jab (+6, 1d4+4). Kalowe Maneuver: [[bisou\|Bisou]] delivers a potion of healing (3 available) to any downed or bloodied ally within 30 ft. Speed 15 ft. |

**Active traits:** Cornered Wolf (no allies within 30 ft.) — Parry reduces 1d10+6, applies to ranged attacks, advantage on saves. Naval Footwork — Disengage as bonus action every round.

## Before He Falls — Checklist

> [!dm]
> This fight has a shape. Don't let it end before the shape is complete. If party damage is outpacing the checklist, use Parry on every triggering hit.

- [ ] All three lair actions fired in sequence: Arm the Guns → Fire the Guns → Call to Arms.
- [ ] Call to Arms fired and was refused. Grigori's voice came up from below. Rook knows he is alone.
- [ ] At least one PC downed or shoved into the water.
- [ ] At least 3 full rounds of initiative elapsed.

## The Fight

Rook spent two phases watching from the cutter deck. He knows who's hurt, who's dangerous, who the weak link is.

### Round 1 — The Opening

**Free action:** *"Uncover the lanterns."* He kicks the hood off the nearest hooded lantern. Bright light floods his end of the deck. [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]'s Umbral Sight collapses anywhere within the lantern's 20-ft. radius.

**Naval Footwork:** He Disengages as a bonus action, moves to a position where at most two PCs can reach him.

### Round 2+ — The Fight

Two Cutlass attacks per turn, shove option whenever a PC is near the gangplank edge or rail. He Disengages after attacking. Uses rigging and cargo nets as cover, corners where only one PC can engage at a time.

**Targeting priority:**

1. Whoever looks most injured
2. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] — softest target, ranged threat
3. Whoever is closest to the gangplank edge — shove them in

### Legendary Actions

3 per round, regained at start of his turn.

| Action | Cost | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Reposition** | 1 | Move up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Stay ahead of the party's positioning — not to escape. |
| **Cutlass Strike** | 2 | One Cutlass attack with shove option on a hit. Use between PC turns to threaten anyone who thinks the gap is safe. |
| **Pistol Reload** | 2 | Reload one expended flintlock; does not fire. Worth using if the party is playing ranged. |

---

## Lair Actions — Round Arc

On initiative count 20 each round (losing ties). Cannot repeat same lair action two rounds in a row. Run in this sequence.

### Round 1 — Arm the Guns

Rook bellows the order below. Gun port hatches scrape open. Two amidship cannon ports are uncovered. No immediate effect — guns primed for next round.

> [!dm]
> No save, no damage — setup only. **Beaumont's response:** On his turn, Beaumont tosses [[bisou\|Bisou]] to the nearest exposed gun port. She soaks the powder in the chamber. One gun disabled for the rest of the fight. Beaumont loses his action; party loses one cone of fire in Round 2. This is automatic.

### Round 2 — Fire the Guns

One cannon discharges (the one Bisou didn't reach). 30-ft. cone from its gun port along the weather deck.

> [!mechanic]
> Every creature in the cone: DC 14 Dexterity save. **Fail:** 4d10 bludgeoning. **Success:** half.

> [!dm]
> Average 22 on a fail drops most PCs at this level. Anyone chasing Rook toward amidships is in the kill zone. Use Cutlass Strike as a legendary action this round.

### Round 3 — Call to Arms

Rook grabs the bell line and hauls. Three times. The iron note rings out sharp and clean over dark water.

He waits.

No boots on the ladder. No voice called up.

Then, muffled through the hatch, flat and final: *"No."*

His jaw tightens. He draws his pistol and puts a round through the door frame.

*"You shot me?! Fuck you, Brataby!"*

Footsteps move away. A long pause. They return.

*"The crew says they quit. I can't blame them. Hostile work environment."*

Nobody comes up. The lair action fails.

> [!dm]
> The voice is [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]]. The round hit the door frame — he's CR 19, the splinter barely registered. *"You shot me?!"* is genuine irritation. *"The crew says they quit"* lands in his usual register: warm, deliberate, unruffled. This is the moment the table should feel Rook's situation — his crew hates him enough not to fight for him even now. Rook continues fighting. Something shifts in his posture. He stops calling orders. He just swings. **HP threshold:** If Rook is above 55 HP when Round 3 arrives, delay Call to Arms — use Reposition instead and run it once he crosses the threshold.

---

## Geoffrey Crisis

Once, on any turn Rook chooses — free action, no cost:

*"Draves. You swore an oath. Look at what you're standing next to."*

> [!mechanic]
> [[geoffrey-draves\|Geoffrey]] makes a DC 12 Wisdom save (roll openly). **Fail:** spends next action doing nothing — standing, hand on sword, unable to commit. Recovers the following turn. Use when action economy feels lopsided. Not as the first thing Rook does.

---

## Roleplay Off-Ramp

Rook is pragmatic, not suicidal. He will not offer terms first.

**Threshold:** ≤40 HP remaining.

**What opens him:** DC 14 Persuasion with something real — leverage, face-saving offer, proof killing him makes things worse.

**What he'll give:** Manifest goes dark, Saltwright goes free, Surety pulls away. He keeps his ship.

**What he won't give:** Names from other inspections. Crown internal business.

---

## Dial

**Rook going down too fast:**

- Parry everything — no per-round limit. Average reduction 11.5 (1d10+6).
- Delay Call to Arms — use Reposition until he crosses 55 HP.
- Geoffrey hesitates one round early.
- Rook climbs the rigging (DC 10 Athletics, costs his action) — positioning problem worth one round.

**Rook surviving too long:**

- Beaumont heals via Kalowe Maneuver (3 potions; 2d4+2 each). Use freely.
- Rook drops a shove this round.
- Geoffrey flanks with a PC, granting advantage on their attack.
- Drop negotiation threshold to 55 HP.

# Below Deck

*Fires immediately after [[session-02-scene-01-rook-final|Scene 01 — Rook Final]] resolves with the party controlling the Surety. Trigger on the first character who goes below.*

The smell reaches you at the ladder. Something slow-cooked, heavy with aromatics, filling a dank space that has no business smelling this good. The stove ticks with heat, its iron side beaded with moisture from whatever has been simmering on it for the last hour. Someone has been down here making something out of a Crown patrol galley's stores.

The galley is lit. One man is at the table, and his presence fills the low-ceilinged space the way a fire fills a room. Dark hair loose to his shoulders, a thick wiry beard to match. A coat of deep red and gold, salt-stiff at the cuffs but unmistakably the coat of a senior Dravosi Naval Officer, the sleeves rolled up against protocol. A bottle of fine old wine sits in front of him, already well begun. Several places have been set at the table, as if he was expecting company.

He is tying off a bandage on his forearm, one-handed, without slowing the meal. He looks up when you enter, and his eyes find you in the lamplight. Dark. Very still. Entirely unsurprised. His face cracks into a warm smile.

*"So the ship is under new management?"*

He asks it the way you ask if the kitchen is still serving. He gestures to the places he has set at the table.

*"You must be starving. Sit. The crew has some questions."*

## Shepherd Grigori

> [!dm]
> [[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] is a CR 19 undead Hierarch sorcerer. Warm, deliberate, completely unfrightened. The ease is not an act. Nothing in this room threatens him. He is here because Rook was transit, not purpose. He is mildly irritated about the arm ("Brataby" came out with genuine feeling) but has moved past it, visibly. He is heading to Calveno where a young heir the Crown physicians gave up on is waiting. The party is an inconvenience that has become slightly more interesting. No plans to hurt anyone unless they make it necessary.

> [!dm]
> **The faith is real.** Modelled on the Khlystý — a mystic sect that treats excess as devotion, pleasure as prayer, and the body as the instrument through which the divine is reached. The meal is not an affectation; he made something real out of the galley's stores because he takes pleasure seriously. Play this straight. The warmth is genuine. The healing is genuine. The horror is that he also considers the binding genuine: he healed them, they are part of him now, and he sees this as a fair and natural exchange. He is not wrong about the healing. He is wrong about everything that follows from it.

> [!dm]
> The crew stayed behind the door because they were afraid. Grigori stayed at the table because he wasn't. When the crew asked who should talk to the pirates, everyone looked at him and he said *"Fine"* and refilled his glass. He considers this mildly inconvenient and entirely beneath him. He does not show it.

**Who he is, if asked:** *"A shepherd. I go where people have problems that cannot be fixed. And I fix them."* Pressed: stories of courts, grateful families, a young heir in Calveno whose physicians had given up. Warm. Specific. Verifiable, if anyone cared to check.

**About the wound:** *"A misunderstanding. Nothing worth discussing."* He does not elaborate.

**About the fight:** *"I heard. These things happen at sea."*

**About the bell / the hatch:** *"He rang for All Hands. I declined on behalf of the crew."* A pause. *"He was not pleased."* He refills his wine.

**About Rook:** Nothing positive. Nothing angry. The absence of feeling is more specific than dislike.

## Crew Beat — Murrat

*Fires naturally once the crew is at the table. Can be triggered by any Rook question, or let it come up organically between courses.*

Old Faas puts it plainly, without being asked:

*"He took us to Murrat."*

He says it the way you report a weather event you survived.

*"Wanted a live one. A specimen, he called it. Went ashore with six crew. Four came back needing the surgeon."*

Alys doesn't look up from whatever she's doing with her hands.

*"Severe puncture wounds. Blood loss. Two of them I genuinely wasn't sure about."*

She pauses.

*"Shepherd Grigori sat with them through the night. I did what I could, but."* She sets her hands flat on the table. *"They pulled through because of him. I'll say that plainly."*

Grigori does not respond. He refills his wine.

> [!dm]
> Don't push the Grigori angle here. Let it sit. The crew believes he saved those sailors — because he did — and the warmth they have for him is genuine and slightly uncomfortable given what he is. Alys is not wrong to credit him. She doesn't know what the credit means.

## The Question

Once the party confirms they're in charge, Grigori sets down his fork.

*"Then I have a question. If you will indulge me."*

He refills his wine without asking if anyone wants some.

*"In my travels I have met three kinds of pirates. The first kind. Strange ones. Their plans make no sense. They take things you would not think to value. Unpredictable. They almost never hurt people by accident, but only because hurting people is the goal."*

He rotates the glass once.

*"The second kind are businessmen. Hostages, cargo, passage fees. Pure mathematics. They prefer you alive because you are worth more. Very clean thinking. I can respect it."*

*"And then there are the robin hood ones."* A slight pause. *"These have a code. They keep their word when it costs them something. They are embarrassed by their crew's bad behavior, which I find charming, actually. Not a common trait in the profession."*

He says, quieter, almost to the wine: *"I am always glad to meet the third kind. There are fewer of them than there should be."*

He looks at the party. Genuinely curious.

*"I ask because the answer tells me what kind of cook I should be."*

> [!dm]
> Intelligence gathering in a dinner party coat. He wants to know how dangerous they are. Any real answer works. Silence or deflection is the only wrong move. Let the table argue about which type they are. That argument is the scene. If they ask which type he is: *"I am a guest. The question does not apply."*

---

## His Condition

Before any deal is done, he raises it without pressure — an expectation that reasonable people share:

*"One thing only. The crew. Anyone who wants to leave at the next port, you let them leave. They have had a very particular kind of week."*

He does not negotiate it. He does not threaten if refused. He notes it the way you note something obvious and moves on.

**If the party refuses:** The warmth doesn't leave all at once. It thins. *"That's unfortunate."* He waits. He does not raise his voice. If they press: he stands up slowly. The coat settles differently. The room gets very quiet. He still does not speak first.

> [!dm]
> He can kill everyone at this table without moving from where he stands. He is choosing not to because it would be inconvenient and he finds the dinner pleasant. That calculus changes only if they insist.

## The Pretty One

Before the Calveno question, something occurs to him.

*"The tall one. Long hair. Looked like a statue."*

He waits.

*"Is he still alive?"*

When the answer is no:

He sets his glass down.

*"Mm."* A pause. *"That is a shame."*

He taps the rim once with one finger.

*"House Knighton. Very old family. Well connected in the Navy. His father will hear his son died on this patrol, and the vessel is now missing. Commodore Knighton does not solve his problems alone. He sends his own fleet."* A beat. *"The Knights. Those ships do not weigh themselves down with brigs."*

He picks up his glass again.

*"So. [[kalowe|Kalowe]]. No Crown presence, no Knighton contacts I am aware of. Five days for the work, perhaps. [[calveno|Calveno]] has better facilities. Two days, maybe less. If you're going to Calveno that would be good for me, I have business there."*

He does not say which he would choose.

> [!dm]
> Grigori does not know [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]]'s real name — he recognized the Knighton house crest on the coat, not the man. The Knighton who commands the pursuit fleet is [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]]: Commodore, the Knight Squadron, Dravosi Crown Navy. He is also Geoffrey Draves's uncle. The party does not know this. If the party is committed to Tidefall regardless: *"Your ship. Your risk."*

## Threat Threshold

Grigori is not a threat in this scene unless the party creates the conditions. He becomes a problem if they:

1. Refuse to answer the question and won't be moved
2. Threaten him directly, or threaten the crew in front of him
3. Refuse to let any crew off at the next port

In any of those cases: the warmth leaves the room. He does not threaten. He does not move. He says *"That's unfortunate"* and waits.

> [!dm]
> If combat somehow starts: CR 19, 263 HP, AC 17, CHA 21, Mad Monk's Resilience (CON save to drop to 1 HP vs non-radiant non-crit). He does not die. He thanks them for the meal and walks off the ship.

Once the party has answered the question and the condition is acknowledged, Grigori glances toward the locked door. Small gesture, barely a nod. The lock turns from the inside and the crew files out — wary, tired, relieved in that specific way of people who had a plan for dying that they no longer need.

# The Ship

*Fires after [[session-02-scene-03-grigori|Scene 03 — Grigori]] settles. The party has a Crown patrol cutter, a small crew, and no captain. Someone is going to want to look around.*

Full deck-by-deck layout, dimensions, and tactical notes: **[[hcs-surety-layout|HCS Surety Layout]]**. This scene covers what's worth slowing down for.

**[[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey Draves]]** is the right guide for this. He was the ship's carpenter — he knows every creaking plank, where the copper is lifting, which strakes need recaulking. He also has opinions, delivered quietly, about what he finds. He's committed to the party but he worked on this ship and some of that is still in him.

---

## Ship Roles

Geoffrey does not launch straight into a tour. He stops them at the wheel first, with the manner of someone who has been thinking about this since the fight ended.

*"Before I show you around — you should know what this ship needs to run."*

He ticks it off. Not lecturing. Just practical.

**The Surety runs on ten. Minimum four.** Those four cover:

- Someone at the wheel who makes decisions when things go wrong — **Captain**
- Someone who can read a chart and plot a course without putting them on a reef — **Navigator**
- Someone managing the rigging and the deck crew — **Bosun**
- Someone who knows which planks need caulking before they become a flooding problem — **Carpenter** (he does not gesture at himself, but the pause is its own gesture)

Beyond minimum:

- A **Gunner** to maintain the 6-pounders and not misfire them into the hull
- A **Cook** for any voyage over three days — *"I understand our guest below is useful in a galley,"* he says, without audible irony
- A **Surgeon** — the cabinet is stocked, but Alys has been handling things on her own
- **Marines** for boarding actions, armed watch, anything requiring a blade and a reason to hold ground

Then ordinary sailors. Enough bodies to work the lines and keep the watches. *"You need eight to ten to run her properly. You have five of the old crew and me — if everyone stays."*

He says *if everyone stays* without emphasis. It is still emphasis.

| **Navigator**        | Ensign Wouters  | (Killed during boarding — post not filled)                                       |
| **Bosun**            | Old Faas        | Defaults to leaving; no strong opinion either way                                |
| **Carpenter**        | Geoffrey Draves | Committed to the party                                                           |
| **Carpenter's Mate** | Sem Holst       | Defaults to leaving; stays if someone asks about the ship with genuine interest  |
| **Surgeon**          | Alys Kuiper     | Defaults to leaving; stays if the Surgeon's Berth is acknowledged as a real post |

> [[thunk|Thunk]], the ship's gunner, is present during this conversation and has not been introduced. Geoffrey knows he exists. He did not think to mention it. If a PC looks around and asks who handles the guns, Geoffrey says *"Thunk does"* as if this is obvious and waits for the next question. Thunk waves. He is approximately six foot five and appears very pleased to be acknowledged.
>

He'll answer questions freely, give honest assessments of the surviving crew if asked. But when the party sets course, he crosses back to the [[saltwright|Saltwright]] and continues his own route. The party has to put someone at this wheel themselves.
>
> If nobody steps forward, Geoffrey eventually says, flat: *"Someone has to steer."* He looks at each PC in turn. It is more pressure than he intends.

## Weather Deck

The party has already spent a session fighting here. Two things worth a beat:

**The lanterns.** Rook kicked them on in Round 1 to collapse Jean-Claude's Umbral Sight. Still burning. Someone has to put them out, or they burn through the night.

**The guns.** Two 6-pounders, bow and stern swivels. All operational. Geoffrey, if asked: *"Crown-issue. Both functional. Powder's below. I'd recommend not firing them without the charge tables — first round might be educational."* He says it like a man who has watched someone skip the charge tables.

**The net trap**, if it was never triggered, is still rigged to the port rail. Geoffrey points it out unprompted: *"That was set for boarding defense. He rigged it himself, the day before we ran into you."* He does not say who the target was. He does not have to.

## Gun Deck

The ship's interior. Where the crew lived.

**Boarding locker** — 8 cutlasses, 4 boarding axes, 6 grappling hooks, 4 loaded flintlocks in a case, rope, 3 smoke signals. Geoffrey: *"Don't ask me why there are more weapons than crew."* The party can arm themselves properly here.

> [!DM]
> **The Bastion.** The Surety is already a functional Tier 1 bastion. The Boarding Locker is the party's **Weapons Locker** — it doesn't need construction, just formal designation. Geoffrey doesn't use that terminology; he just knows where everything is stocked and in what condition. The Chart Table (next room) is the **Chart Archive** — same principle. Two facilities installed, two slots open: Crew Quarters (natural fit: **Crew Berths**) and Galley (natural fit: **Provisions Store**). The medic's cabinet is pre-positioned as a **Surgeon's Berth** the moment someone with the right training fills the Surgeon role. Let this emerge through the tour rather than as a rules announcement — the party should feel like they're discovering what they already have. Full slot mapping: [[hcs-surety-layout|HCS Surety Layout]]. Facility mechanics: [[ship-bastion|Ship Bastion]].

**Chart table** — Crown Islands survey charts covering the eastern waypoints and Central Strait approaches. A compass, dividers, and a 3-month captain's log bolted to the surface. The log is methodical, professional, and increasingly terse. [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]] appears in three entries — the first is two paragraphs, the second is one, the third is four words: *"Sel. Again. Noted."*

> [!DM]
> The log also has the inspection manifests from the last three months. Anyone reading carefully will notice a pattern: ships with Fisk's Fleet registry get flagged more often than average. It's not written down as policy. It's just the numbers.

**Medic's cabinet** — 2 healer's kits, 1 potion of healing, 1 potion of greater healing (2d4+2), surgical instruments in a sealed roll. The surgeon's berth is pre-built but needs a surgeon. Alys Kuiper has been handling things. She will continue to handle things, with declining enthusiasm, if no one hires a proper surgeon.

- *Weapons rack:* spare cutlass, one loaded blunderbuss (4d6, 15-ft cone, one shot). Geoffrey: *"I didn't know about the blunderbuss."* He sounds like he means it.
- *Locked chest* (DC 15 Thieves' Tools, or Rook's key): 45 gp, Crown commission papers, sealed letter from the Tidefall Harbormaster regarding [[beaumont-sel|Beaumont Sel]]'s manifest, 1 potion of greater healing (2d4+2), 1 [[potion-of-water-breathing|potion of water breathing]].

## Hold

Low overhead (5'8"), six inches of bilge water at the lowest point. Bring a light.

**Inspection storage** — six months of boarding manifests, a fee ledger, and three blank Crown writs in a sealed folder. The writs are forgeable Crown authority. Ensign Wouters, if he is with the party, looks at the blank writs and then very deliberately looks at something else.

**Seized crates (×2, unlabeled)** — The fee ledger in inspection storage lists them as "confiscated goods, pending Crown review." They have never been opened for Crown review, because Rook never intended to send them for Crown review. The padlocks are simple (DC 10 Thieves' Tools or a crowbar).

*Crate 1:* Two silver candelabras (25 gp each), a locked jewelry box (DC 12; inside — a small pendant worth 15 gp, a name engraved on the back: *"For Mira, from the sea"*), a cask of fine brandy (12 gp, ostensibly seized for unpaid duties), a bolt of Calveno silk (20 gp). None of this is formally receipted as Crown property. It is simply here. **Subtotal: ~97 gp.**

*Crate 2:* Two flintlock pistols in good condition (loaded, 15 gp each), [[miras-blade|Mira's Blade]] — a +1 shortsword with a distinctive notched pommel, the kind of blade that belongs to a specific person rather than a ship's locker — and a sealed package labeled in Rook's hand: *"Contraband — R.B."* Inside: twenty vials of Grung poison tincture, sealed in wax, worth ~5 gp each to the right buyer (100 gp total as black-market contraband). Geoffrey stares at these for a moment and says nothing.

**Locked cargo crate** (DC 14 Thieves' Tools) — 150 gp in mixed coin and a folded map. The map shows an anchorage marked *"Galewall"* with a bearing and a rough depth sounding. No name. No context. The sounding suggests shallow water over something large.

## The Crew

By the time the hold tour finishes, the old Surety crew has had an hour to take stock of their situation. They're not hiding. They're not hostile. They're waiting to see what kind of management this is.

Each of them defaults to leaving at the next port. Not out of anger. It's simply what sailors do when a ship changes hands under fraught circumstances. The party can change this, one conversation at a time.

---

**[[sem-holst|Sem Holst]]** is already cataloguing damage Geoffrey didn't mention. He'll tell you exactly what's wrong with this hull and exactly how long it will take to fix, and he will not soften either number. He wants to know if the party is actually serious about maintaining the vessel — not what it can do, but the ship itself. If a PC demonstrates they know the difference between a caulked seam and a packed one, or asks a question about the hull that isn't about how fast it can go, he reconsiders. *"Not many privateers bother learning that."* He says it the way you'd admit something surprised you.

---

**Ensign Wouters** was at the chart table before anyone asked him to be — per prep notes. In play, Wouters was killed during the boarding. The Navigator post is open.

---

**[[alys-kuiper|Alys Kuiper]]** is in the medic's cabinet doing inventory. She finds this calming. She will announce, without particular inflection, that healer's kit supply is adequate for two more field engagements and that the surgical instruments are well-maintained except for one probe that needs replacing. She is not asking to stay. She is not asking to leave. She is performing the inventory because someone has to and she is the most qualified, and she would like that fact to be acknowledged. If the party formally names the post — Surgeon, ship's medical officer, something that constitutes an actual role — she stays. If they mention they intend to keep the Surgeon's Berth staffed and stocked, she looks at the cabinet the way Holst looked at the hull: assessing what it could be.

---

**[[old-faas|Old Faas]]** is up in the rigging. He went up right after Grigori gave the nod and he hasn't come down. He is not hiding. He just prefers to be useful in ways that keep him off the deck and out of conversations. He'll come down when needed. The argument to stay is simple: ask for his assessment of the rigging, and listen to the full answer. He will give a detailed, quietly passionate, twelve-minute account of every line, block, and splice and what each needs. Anyone who doesn't walk away partway through gets an evaluating look. *"Most people leave before the fore-topgallant."*

---

**[[noor|Noor]]** is near the galley, failing to be invisible due to enthusiasm. They have a sailing manual open and are reading it while standing up. They are the easiest to recruit — they haven't decided where they're going and they want, more than anything, to be on a ship that goes somewhere interesting. Any destination the party names that isn't immediately familiar prompts them to check the manual. If it's not in the manual, they look thoughtful. This is apparently a point in the destination's favor.

---

**[[thunk|Thunk]]** came through the locked door last, unhurried, and has since drifted toward the gun deck with the easy gravity of a man returning to something he was interrupted from. He is the Surety's gunner. He does not mention this. If the party skips the hold tour, they may reach their first destination never knowing he was there.

He is enormous. The Surety's interior doorframes did not anticipate him. He smells of old iron and powder and something faintly sweet, which turns out to be the tallow he packs around the shot pouches. He left blacksmithing because the sea called him, and when pressed on what that means he says *"very loud, actually — I cannot sleep sometimes, so I come here instead"* with complete sincerity.

He will answer any question with full, earnest detail. Ask about the guns. Ask about the charge tables. Ask about his hands. He has good answers to all of these and he would genuinely like to share them, in the direct, slightly formal cadence of someone translating from a language he learned before Common. The warmth is real. The enthusiasm for things that explode is also real.

His condition to stay is simply that someone asked. Not a formal role. Not a title. One conversation where the other person wanted the answer.

> [!DM]
> **Thunk is the best hire in this scene and he will not tell them that.**
>
> Mechanically: when Thunk mans a cannon, he counts as two crew for the purpose of determining how many guns can be manned. If the party ever installs a **Carpenter's Shop** (Smithy facility) on the Surety, he can run it without additional staff. He left blacksmithing for the sea but the forge is still in him.
>
> The accent is Arnold Schwarzenegger. Not a joke — play it straight, with the short declarative sentences and the earnest odd emphases. Sample lines: *"Ja, I like this gun. She has good — temperament."* / *"The charge ratio, I already calculate. You want to hear?"* / *"Do not worry. I am very careful. Mostly."* / *"I was a blacksmith. But the sea, she is louder."*
>
> The roleplay reward is inverted: he does not need to be persuaded or noticed or given a reason to feel useful. He just needs someone to ask the right question. The right question is anything about the guns, the powder, or the work.

---

> [!DM]
> These conversations don't need to be formal scenes. They happen naturally as the party moves through the ship. Reward any PC who engages: Perception to notice what Holst is cataloguing, Insight to read what Alys is actually asking for, Investigation to give Wouters something useful to work with at the chart table. None of these are hard sells — they just need a reason, and the reason can be small.
>
> Track who commits before the party sets course. All five are functional crew. Losing any of them creates a real gap in the role table established at the start of this scene.

## The Ship, as a Thing

After the tour, there's a moment where it settles. This is their ship. It needs a crew of ten to run properly and they have five survivors, one carpenter, and whatever the party brings. It has two functioning cannons and a registry plate that says it belongs to the Dravosi Crown. It has a chart table with the Strait fully mapped. It has 6 tons of usable cargo space and a boarding locker stocked for a crew that no longer exists.

Geoffrey, if no one says anything: *"She's sound. Needs work, but she's sound. I know where the problems are."* He pauses. *"What do you want to do with her?"*

That's the question. Move to [[session-02-scene-05-central-strait|Scene 05 — Central Strait]] once the party sets a course.

Ship Roles

Geoffrey does not launch straight into a tour. He stops them at the wheel first, with the manner of someone who has been thinking about this since the fight ended.

“Before I show you around — you should know what this ship needs to run.”

He ticks it off. Not lecturing. Just practical.

The Surety runs on ten. Minimum four. Those four cover:

  • Someone at the wheel who makes decisions when things go wrong — Captain
  • Someone who can read a chart and plot a course without putting them on a reef — Navigator
  • Someone managing the rigging and the deck crew — Bosun
  • Someone who knows which planks need caulking before they become a flooding problem — Carpenter (he does not gesture at himself, but the pause is its own gesture)

Beyond minimum:

  • A Gunner to maintain the 6-pounders and not misfire them into the hull
  • A Cook for any voyage over three days — “I understand our guest below is useful in a galley,” he says, without audible irony
  • A Surgeon — the cabinet is stocked, but Alys has been handling things on her own
  • Marines for boarding actions, armed watch, anything requiring a blade and a reason to hold ground

Then ordinary sailors. Enough bodies to work the lines and keep the watches. “You need eight to ten to run her properly. You have five of the old crew and me — if everyone stays.”

He says if everyone stays without emphasis. It is still emphasis.

She is not asking to stay. She is not asking to leave. She is performing the inventory because someone has to and she is the most qualified, and she would like that fact to be acknowledged. If the party formally names the post — Surgeon, ship’s medical officer, something that constitutes an actual role — she stays. If they mention they intend to keep the Surgeon’s Berth staffed and stocked, she looks at the cabinet the way Holst looked at the hull: assessing what it could be.

Old Faas is up in the rigging. He went up right after Grigori gave the nod and he hasn’t come down. He is not hiding. He just prefers to be useful in ways that keep him off the deck and out of conversations. He’ll come down when needed. The argument to stay is simple: ask for his assessment of the rigging, and listen to the full answer. He will give a detailed, quietly passionate, twelve-minute account of every line, block, and splice and what each needs. Anyone who doesn’t walk away partway through gets an evaluating look. “Most people leave before the fore-topgallant.”

Noor is near the galley, failing to be invisible due to enthusiasm. They have a sailing manual open and are reading it while standing up. They are the easiest to recruit — they haven’t decided where they’re going and they want, more than anything, to be on a ship that goes somewhere interesting. Any destination the party names that isn’t immediately familiar prompts them to check the manual. If it’s not in the manual, they look thoughtful. This is apparently a point in the destination’s favor.

Thunk came through the locked door last, unhurried, and has since drifted toward the gun deck with the easy gravity of a man returning to something he was interrupted from. He is the Surety’s gunner. He does not mention this. If the party skips the hold tour, they may reach their first destination never knowing he was there.

He is enormous. The Surety’s interior doorframes did not anticipate him. He smells of old iron and powder and something faintly sweet, which turns out to be the tallow he packs around the shot pouches. He left blacksmithing because the sea called him, and when pressed on what that means he says “very loud, actually — I cannot sleep sometimes, so I come here instead” with complete sincerity.

He will answer any question with full, earnest detail. Ask about the guns. Ask about the charge tables. Ask about his hands. He has good answers to all of these and he would genuinely like to share them, in the direct, slightly formal cadence of someone translating from a language he learned before Common. The warmth is real. The enthusiasm for things that explode is also real.

His condition to stay is simply that someone asked. Not a formal role. Not a title. One conversation where the other person wanted the answer.

DM Note

Thunk is the best hire in this scene and he will not tell them that.

Mechanically: when Thunk mans a cannon, he counts as two crew for the purpose of determining how many guns can be manned. If the party ever installs a Carpenter’s Shop (Smithy facility) on the Surety, he can run it without additional staff. He left blacksmithing for the sea but the forge is still in him.

The accent is Arnold Schwarzenegger. Not a joke — play it straight, with the short declarative sentences and the earnest odd emphases. Sample lines: “Ja, I like this gun. She has good — temperament.” / “The charge ratio, I already calculate. You want to hear?” / “Do not worry. I am very careful. Mostly.” / “I was a blacksmith. But the sea, she is louder.”

The roleplay reward is inverted: he does not need to be persuaded or noticed or given a reason to feel useful. He just needs someone to ask the right question. The right question is anything about the guns, the powder, or the work.

DM Note

These conversations don’t need to be formal scenes. They happen naturally as the party moves through the ship. Reward any PC who engages: Perception to notice what Holst is cataloguing, Insight to read what Alys is actually asking for, Investigation to give Wouters something useful to work with at the chart table. None of these are hard sells — they just need a reason, and the reason can be small.

Track who commits before the party sets course. All five are functional crew. Losing any of them creates a real gap in the role table established at the start of this scene.

The Ship, as a Thing

After the tour, there’s a moment where it settles. This is their ship. It needs a crew of ten to run properly and they have five survivors, one carpenter, and whatever the party brings. It has two functioning cannons and a registry plate that says it belongs to the Dravosi Crown. It has a chart table with the Strait fully mapped. It has 6 tons of usable cargo space and a boarding locker stocked for a crew that no longer exists.

Geoffrey, if no one says anything: “She’s sound. Needs work, but she’s sound. I know where the problems are.” He pauses. “What do you want to do with her?”

That’s the question. Move to Scene 05 — Central Strait once the party sets a course.

# Central Strait Events

*These fire during any transit through the [[central-strait|Central Strait]], regardless of destination. Use them to fill travel time, establish the world, and pull on PC threads. Fire 2–3 per leg.*

---

## Generic Strait — Roll or Choose

### The Dolphins

A pod of spinner dolphins finds the bow wake somewhere in the mid-Strait and rides it, leaping for no reason other than that they can. They stay for an hour. Then, in unison, they sound. Every one of them, gone.

Thirty minutes later: the squall. It comes up fast, no warning, over in twenty minutes. Anyone who watched the dolphins had the only warning available.

> This one is free. No roll needed. Just atmosphere, and the lesson that the strait talks if you know how to listen.

---

### The Becalmed Merchant

A wide-hulled brig sitting dead still in flat calm, crew lounging on the rail. As the [[uncertainty|Surety]] passes, her captain hails across. Friendly enough.

*"Did you hear about the Crown cutter gone missing off the eastern waypoints? Ours was due for inspection last week and I can't find anyone to process the papers."*

He is genuinely worried — not about the missing ship, about the paperwork delay. He has a cargo of pressed salt fish and a delivery window and the bureaucracy has failed him.

> [!dm]
> He is looking at the Surety. He does not know it is the missing Crown cutter. If anyone waves a Crown manifest at him, he will be absurdly grateful and ask if they can stamp his papers right now, from the deck, across the water.

---

### Night Watch

Second night out. The watch hears something moving alongside in the dark. Not breaking surface. Parallel course, maybe half a mile to port, for thirty minutes — then nothing. No splash. Just displacement in the water and the sound of something heavy and unhurried.

[[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]], when told in the morning: *"Probably nothing."* He does not sound like he believes this.

> [!dm]
> It is not a [[sawek|Sawek]] — not this far west, probably. It is a very large shark working a current edge. But "probably" is doing a lot of work, and the party doesn't know the difference. Leave it unresolved.

---

### The Bad Receipt

A schooner on a converging course, no flag flying. When it sees the Surety, it changes course. Hard, clean, fast. If the Crown pennant is still flying, it peels south immediately. If the pennant is down, it closes to hailing distance first.

From fifty yards, the crew looks at the Surety. Then at each other. Then the schooner peels away anyway, running south hard.

Whatever they decided, they decided in about four seconds.

> [!dm]
> That's the [[the-bad-receipt|Bad Receipt]] — a Kalowe-refit schooner that works the Tidefall Gate approaches. They saw the hull name, ran the numbers on a stolen Crown cutter, and decided today was not the day. If the party gives chase: she's faster in a straight line, but the Surety has the wind angle. It becomes a choice, not a given. The Bad Receipt is not a threat — it's the first glimpse of the world the party is about to enter.

---

### Convoy Ahead

Three merchant hulls running east in loose formation, Crown escort frigate at the rear. The escort makes the Surety immediately — hails across, professional, clipped.

*"Identify and state your destination."*

A formality. Mostly. The escort captain is young and has not yet developed the habit of looking at things less carefully than they deserve.

> Drama suite: DC 10 / 15 / 20 Deception. Each tier determines how long the escort keeps pace alongside before accepting the answer and returning to the convoy.

---

## Party-Specific Hooks

*Each fires once, on the appropriate watch or quiet moment. Don't stack them. One per day of travel.*

---

### Delmar — Fleet Signal

Halfway through the Strait, a ship on the northern horizon. Running east, no acknowledgment of the Surety. Distance makes the hull name unreadable.

The pennant is [[fisks-fleet|Fisk's Fleet]].

[[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] watches [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] watching it for a while, then goes back to work without saying anything.

> Play this straight. No confrontation, no revelation — just the pennant at distance. Whatever it costs Delmar to watch it pass, that's the scene.

---

### Jean-Claude — The Collar

Something bobs past the hull on the port side, late afternoon. Small. White. [[noor|Noor]] fishes it out with a boathook, not sure what it is.

It's a Grung slave collar. Iron ring, locking pin, a Crown registry mark stamped into the metal. Cracked down the middle, snapped off someone's neck by force or the sea.

No context. No body. Just the collar and the registration number, which [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] can read if he gets close enough, and which he will recognize as a clan identification code.

> Don't editorialize. Hand Jean-Claude the collar and let the player decide what it costs him. He can say nothing, as he did in the hold. That's the thread.

---

### Perrin — The Hull Name

A passing merchant running west — Midchain registry, Kalowe home port. Routine. But one of the deck crew leans over the rail as she passes and stares.

Not at the ship. At [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]]. He says something to the man beside him. The merchant doesn't stop.

Perrin might catch the hull name on the stern — *The Clement Sorrow*. He might recognize it. A Kalowe salvage operator, one of the sister ships to the [[vestra|Vestra]], bought at auction after the disaster and repurposed. That deckhand's face rings a bell that shouldn't ring anymore.

> The thread is: someone from before the Vestra is alive, and they've seen Perrin, and they're heading to Kalowe. What happens next depends entirely on whether Perrin tells anyone.

---

### Crissdalynn — The Compass

The ship's compass nudges northeast for two hours in the mid-Strait. No cause. The current is steady, the heading is held, but the needle disagrees. Then it corrects, clean, like it never happened.

[[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] remembers what [[master-kyzil|Kyzil]] told her about the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] — that it distorts instruments in the eastern passages, bends compass needles toward itself as a ship approaches. The Narrows. The Tail. Far east.

This is not the eastern passage.

> Don't explain it. One look at the compass, one beat where Crissdalynn knows what it means, and move on. The Maw is reaching west. That's all.

---

# Session 03 — Getting in on the Joke

## Durable Changes

- **Ship renamed.** HCS Surety is now the *Uncertainty* (private vessel, HCS prefix dropped). Docked at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]], Black-Jaw dry dock, Calveno. 5-day repair estimate. Password: *garden*.
- **Party levelled to 4.**
- **Shepherd Grigori departed.** Left at Calveno docks. Cold handshake. Said his business would take a week or two. No incantation magic — unidentified by Perrin at Arcana 18.
- **Nona Black-Jaw met.** Attacks on Perrin called off (she thought he was captured). Vestra crew consolation ordered to Enzo. Perrin promised a favor without hearing terms. Sent Perrin away with a sending stone.
- **Master Kyzil reunited with Crissdalynn.** Dove from sun. Had been searching Kalowe and Tidefall for her after the ship went down.
- **Delmar's coat locked in captain's chest.** Did not come ashore in Dravosi red.
- **Delmar's water moment.** Stepping off the gangplank, water reached up toward him; thought he heard his name. Then gone.

## Scene Log

1. **Perrin's abyss vision.** On watch in storm — black water held still one breath, then he was somewhere else. Worked stone floor, channels, bioluminescent drifting shapes. Something turned its attention toward him: curious, not hunting. Then he inhabited a 60-ft creature's body — barbed tail, ancestral hunting instincts. Saw something far larger below (longer than two ships). Dove, drove the barb into a whale, was taken down with it. Back at the floor, watched something rise and strike the hull from below. The vision cost whatever sent it: one word burned into his mind — *"Grow."* One second had passed.
2. **Whip shark combat.** Perrin fell from rigging (rolled a 1), JC arrested none of it, Crissdalynn caught both from crow's nest. First impact hit ship from below. Perrin gave bardic inspiration to all three, started drumming. Delmar hit with two swivels + broadside simultaneously. Shark dove, came back angrier. JC arrowed from rigging; shark tail-swiped JC, opened his chest (held on). Round 3: Crissdalynn flew out, seized sixty feet of shark, lifted it from the sea. Shark rolled nat 1 on contested strength. JC shot arrow through its anus; exited mouth. Fight over.
3. **Grigori heals JC.** Red viscous light, wordless, no components. Perrin: Arcana 18, couldn't place it. Grigori said nothing and went back below.
4. **Whip shark salvage.** Barb (4-ft bone spike, serrated; Delmar's), scales (hull patching), teeth, meat. JC recovered 3 fertilized eggs from the body.
5. **Five days at sea.** Old Faas taught Perrin the ropes; told stories about running cargo with Rook; built like a brick shithouse, faster up rigging than anyone. JC and Sem Holst worked hull — JC cast Mending, Sem quietly fixed what JC missed. Crissdalynn found Rook's chart archive: he broke Imperial rules about the Drowned Maw twice, kept no record of what he found. Delmar ran ship admin in "Admiral Fisk form" too long — hair wrong, cadence shifted, called Crissdalynn "Crystalline." Snapped out after drinking from her flask.
6. **Bioluminescent whale.** Day 2 at sea: glowing outline moving on parallel heading. Perrin recognized it from the vision. Watched it for a long time.
7. **Approach to Calveno.** Very busy port, flying Crown colours up the main approach would draw eyes. Perrin knew an alternate approach. Ship renamed *Uncertainty* on the approach channel.
8. **La Vasca arrival.** Covered dry dock, Black-Jaw colors. Cobb (rattkin, Perrin's old contact) at water's edge. Perrin shook his hand and bolted immediately.
9. **Grigori departs dockside.** Cold handshake to Delmar. A week or two in the city. May paths cross again.
10. **Delmar's water moment.** Stepping off gangplank: water reached up, thought he heard his name. Then land. Gone.
11. **Jean-Claude in Calveno.** Changed color green (disguise during festival prep). Less attention. Found Casa Lupo first; shopkeeper directed him to Studio Orsini for the egg. Told Marta Orsini he fertilized the egg himself.
12. **Umberlee servant encounter.** Older woman, blue-gray robes, white hair, slight limp, small leather book. Found Delmar specifically. Had a message from the Bitch Queen. Waiting at Waveservant Shrine; not sleeping until he came. Delmar: Deception 19 — told her Umberlee herself had required this errand first. She believed it and left. Delmar told Geoffrey: they're not going to a second location alone.
13. **Crissdalynn scouts Calveno.** Tried from above. Too many people. Gave up. Found Delmar instead.
14. **Nona meeting (Le Paludi).** Nona at stove, back to door. Enzo and Ruk present. Rattkin mother just finishing — crying about a son who hadn't come home. Nona and Perrin wait for her to leave. Nona asks what it means when a rat king misses check-in. Perrin tells her about the Vestra. Nona cracks her wooden spoon. Consolation for Vestra crew ordered to Enzo. Nona realizes she'd thought Perrin captured by the [[tarahs|Tarahs]] — Cobb had reported one of their ships coming in. Calls off the attacks before Enzo leaves. Asks Perrin a favor (unstated). He says yes. Gives him a sending stone.
15. **Kyzil reunion (Le Paludi streets).** Dove from sun in silence, knocked Criss back 20 ft. Recognized her by smell before she could see. Had been searching Kalowe and Tidefall. "Priscilla, you're alive." Straightened up, looked at the others. "Hi, I'm Master Kyzil." Crissdalynn broke down. Perrin had been in a barrel; emerged slowly; finger-shake introduction.
