Session 03 — Getting in on the Joke
Player recap of Session 03 — Perrin's vision from the abyss, the whip shark, five days at sea, and the first day in Calveno. Canon events as they happened.

# 03 — Getting in on the Joke

---

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] was on watch. The storm had thinned to hard sideways rain and the water below the rail gave nothing back. For one breath the black surface held still. His knees buckled. He went somewhere else.

The pressure arrived first — fathoms of it, cold and absolute. Beneath his feet: worked stone, worn smooth, channels cut in long deliberate lines toward the dark. Around him: pale bioluminescent things drifting in loose constellations, completely unbothered. He breathed. His chest didn't move. Something in the space turned its attention toward him. Not hunting. Curious.

Then his body wasn't his. Sixty feet of muscle. A barbed tail, ancient. His skin read the water in frequencies he couldn't name. Above, through dark fathoms: a hull, and the smell of blood. Below: something longer than two ships end to end, moving in an unhurried arc. His instincts were sharpened over generations to hunt exactly this. He dove. He drove the barb in and pulled. The whale sounded into the dark and took him with it.

He was back at the bottom. Back to his own size. He watched from below as the shape rose — fast, the lower lobe streaming — and the hull above him exploded inward. Then, at enormous cost, one word burned into his mind:

*"Grow."*

His knees finished buckling. One second had passed.

---

[[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]] was thirty feet up the rigging. He rolled a one.

[[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]] was within ten feet. He lashed out with his tongue, braced himself, and arrested approximately none of it. He came down with Perrin, both tangled together in a fall they hadn't finished taking.

[[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] came off the crow's nest and caught both of them before they hit the deck.

**Crissdalynn:** *(setting Perrin down carefully)* It's okay. I only eat rats.

The first impact struck the ship from below.

The shark was over sixty feet long. Longer than the ship itself. Perrin climbed three rungs of rigging and raised his voice above the rain.

**Perrin:** Listen to me, everybody. This here's a whip shark. Big long fucker. I know everything about it. Get back.

He gave bardic inspiration to all three of them and started to drum.

[[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] put all the guns on it simultaneously — two swivels and the broadside in one coordinated shot. Red mist burst from the water. The shark dove and came up angrier. *"You're not even food,"* Delmar told it, leveling the blunderbuss. *"You're the food that my food eats."*

Jean-Claude put an arrow in it from the rigging. The shark studied him from the waterline, then swept its tail across the deck and opened his chest. He held on by one roll. Perrin's song in the rigging reminded him what happened if he didn't, and he held on.

Round three. Crissdalynn flew out over the water, seized sixty feet of shark, and lifted it clean out of the sea. Contested strength. The shark rolled a natural one.

She held it there, the creature thrashing, its entire underside exposed.

Jean-Claude watched from the deck. Bowstring drawn.

*"She's holding it by the tail. The anus is basically a bullseye. If I fire directly into it, the arrow could conceivably come out its mouth."*

He released. It went in the back door and came out the other end.

The thrashing stopped. The fight was over.

*"Turns out,"* Jean-Claude said, *"the only way to kill a shark is to shoot it in the butt. That's all it takes."*

Delmar's voice carried up from the gun deck:

*"We have learned much today."*

[[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] came up from below carrying tins of pale healing liquid for the crew. He found Jean-Claude and extended his hand. A red, viscous light flowed from his wrist and settled into the wound. Flesh knit together, perfectly, silently. No components. No words. No incantation. He said nothing else and went back below.

Perrin rolled an 18 on arcana and still couldn't place it.

Delmar dove in manta ray form and retrieved the shark's barb. A four-foot spike of bone and cartilage, serrated on every edge but the base. The party also cut loose scales for hull patching, pocketed the teeth, and someone took the meat. Jean-Claude recovered three fertilized eggs from the body.

**Jean-Claude:** We're going to a port. We have fertilized whip shark eggs. Do you know what that means?

---

Four days. Long gray swells. [[old-faas|Old Faas]] showed Perrin the ropes and told stories about the old days running cargo with [[barnaby-rook|Rook]]. It turned out the old man was built like a brick shithouse, faster up the rigging than any rat. Jean-Claude and [[sem-holst|Sem Holst]] worked the hull in companionable silence: Jean-Claude casting Mending, Sem quietly fixing what he missed without mentioning it. [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn]] dug through Rook's chart archive and found, among other things, that he had broken Imperial rules about the [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] twice and kept no record of what he found there.

Delmar ran ship's administration in his Admiral Fisk form. Long enough that his hair sat wrong and his cadence shifted and he called Crissdalynn *Crystalline.* She handed him her flask. He drank. The brown faded back toward red.

**Delmar:** *Thank you, Miss Khinriss. You're right. I was acting a little strange, wasn't I?*

He went back to training [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]], calling him Mr. James.

Day two, Crissdalynn spotted it first from the crow's nest: a glowing outline in the water, moving slowly on a parallel heading. Perrin climbed to the rigging. He recognized it. He watched it for a long time.

---

*"Land ho."*

[[calveno|Calveno]] was a very, very busy port. Flying Crown colours up the main approach in a stolen government ship would draw eyes. Perrin knew the other way in.

The name question came up on the approach.

**Crissdalynn:** I vote *Uncertainty.*

**Jean-Claude:** Drop the prefix. Just *Uncertainty*, private vessel. HCS would be a target.

**Crissdalynn:** I like the idea it comes out naturally — they ask the name, someone says we're uncertain, and it just gets written down.

They agreed. The [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] became the *Uncertainty* somewhere in the approach channel.

[[la-vasca|La Vasca]] — a covered dry dock, Black-Jaw colors — had a ship's cradle already waiting. [[cobb|Cobb]], a stocky brown rat Perrin had known for years, was at the water's edge. Perrin shook his hand, said it was all sorted, and bolted for the door without finishing the sentence. One look back at the group:

*"You guys fucking handle the ship. I'm going."*

As Delmar stepped from the gangplank onto shore, the water reached up toward him for a moment, and he thought he heard his name on the wind. Then he was on land and it was gone.

[[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] came down after. He shook Delmar's hand. The cold hit first. Deep cold, nothing to do with the dock or the season. He thanked the crew and said his business in the city would take a week or two. Perhaps their paths would cross again. He left.

---

Jean-Claude changed one thing before heading into the city: he was green instead of blue. Festival preparations were already underway; people were half in costume. He drew far less attention than usual. He found his way to [[casa-lupo|Casa Lupo]] and inquired about a shortbow. The shopkeeper pointed him toward [[studio-orsini|Studio Orsini]] for the egg.

**Jean-Claude:** *(producing the egg)* I fertilized it myself. The infant will have multiple extra muscles.

Delmar and Crissdalynn were stopped in the [[le-paludi|Mercatura district]] by an older woman in blue-gray robes: white hair, slight limp, a small leather book. She had found Delmar specifically. Umberlee's Bitch Queen had a message, and she would be at the [[waveservant-shrine|Waveservant Shrine]] all day, and she was not sleeping until he came. Delmar rolled a 19 on deception and told her that Umberlee herself had required this errand first. She believed him and left. Once she was gone, he told [[geoffrey-draves|Geoffrey]] they were not going to a second location alone.

Crissdalynn had attempted to scout the city from above, found more people than she had ever seen in one place, and given up. She found Delmar instead.

---

[[le-paludi|Le Paludi]]. [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]]'s kitchen was warm. She was at the stove on her stool, back to the door, holding an enormous spatula. [[enzo|Enzo]] leaned against the far wall; [[ruk|Ruk]] stood near the door. A rattkin mother was just finishing at the table. She was crying. Asking Nona what to do about a son who hadn't come home. *Ruk: "Don't worry. Nona will take care of it."* Nona: *"Yes. Yes."*

She looked up. She saw Perrin.

She waited until the other family had gone.

**Nona:** *Peron. What does it mean when a rat king doesn't meet their check-in?*

Perrin told her about the Vestra. Nona's hand tightened on the wooden spoon until it cracked. She discarded the piece and kept stirring.

**Nona:** *I don't care about the Vestra, Peron. I do not care about Vincenzo's boat. I miss him dearly, but we lost so much money on that stupid talking boat. I am glad it is at the bottom of the ocean. Now you, though — how many men must we kill to put its head on my wall?*

He tried to explain the Leviathan to her. The water boiling, the lightning, and then nothing. He did not say plainly that there were no other survivors. She understood it anyway. She told [[enzo|Enzo]] to make sure the Vestra's crew had consolation.

Then she understood what she'd assumed when he stopped checking in. What she'd already set in motion.

**Nona:** *Enzo — before you go. Call off the attacks. I thought you were captured.*

Delmar had locked his Dravosi red coat in the captain's chest before coming ashore.

Nona had a favor to ask. She hadn't said what it was.

**Perrin:** For you, Nona? Absolutely.

She gave him a sending stone.

---

Later that afternoon, Crissdalynn and Delmar and Jean-Claude were back on the streets of Le Paludi. The wind went quiet. The afternoon sun was high and behind them.

Something had the sun behind it. It dove in silence. Crissdalynn was knocked back twenty feet, two arms around her from the front, the wind out of her chest.

She recognized the smell before she could see.

**Kyzil:** *Oh my God, Priscilla, you're alive. Thank God.*

He straightened himself. Looked at the others.

**Kyzil:** *Hi, I'm — I'm [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]]. Nice to meet you. What happened?*

Crissdalynn broke down.

**Kyzil:** *I'm so glad you survived. I heard the ship was down. A foul wind came from the south. I looked through [[kalowe|Kalowe]] for you. I looked in [[tidefall|Tidefall]]. I can't believe you ended up here.*

Perrin had arrived at some point and seen a large owl-like figure dive-bomb Crissdalynn. He was currently in a barrel. He emerged very slowly.

**Perrin:** Perrin's the name. That's all you need to know. Nice to meet ya.

Kyzil slowly knelt and extended one finger.

**Kyzil:** *It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, Master Perrin.*

Perrin touched the finger.

**Perrin:** Yeah.

He straightened himself. Looked at the others.

Kyzil: Hi, I’m — I’m Master Kyzil. Nice to meet you. What happened?

Crissdalynn broke down.

Kyzil: I’m so glad you survived. I heard the ship was down. A foul wind came from the south. I looked through Kalowe for you. I looked in Tidefall. I can’t believe you ended up here.

Perrin had arrived at some point and seen a large owl-like figure dive-bomb Crissdalynn. He was currently in a barrel. He emerged very slowly.

Perrin: Perrin’s the name. That’s all you need to know. Nice to meet ya.

Kyzil slowly knelt and extended one finger.

Kyzil: It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, Master Perrin.

Perrin touched the finger.

Perrin: Yeah.

> [!read-aloud]

# Session 03 — Before the First Impact

> [!dm]
> Perrin-only contact. One second in-world — no other PC experiences or notices it. If someone was already watching closely: a blink, one hand tightening on wet wood. Cut immediately to the first hull impact.

---

## Beat 1 — Contact

> [!read-aloud]
> No sensation of falling — you are simply somewhere else.
>
> The cold arrives first. Then the pressure — everywhere at once, the weight of countless fathoms pressing down onto your chest. There is something solid beneath your feet. Your lungs scream for air.
>
> You open your mouth. Nothing comes.

*[Let the player react.]*

> [!read-aloud]
> You breathe. Somehow you breathe.

---

## Beat 2 — The Space

> [!read-aloud]
> A shape moves at the edges of the dark. Pale things, lit from within, pulsing in long slow rhythms like breath. Dozens. Hundreds. Moving in loose constellations through the water around you, unbothered by your presence. The floor beneath you is worked stone, worn perfectly smooth. Channels run through it in long deliberate lines toward the darkness. There are no walls. There is no ceiling.
>
> The space orients. Something turns its attention toward you — not from a direction you can find, not through anything you can see.

> [!dm]
> [[auralis|Auralis]] is not a figure. His attention gives the space its orientation; he attends to Perrin the way a system attends to an anomaly. The contact is a fraction of his total focus — the rest is occupied with the fissure.

> [!check] Insight — What is this attention?
> **DC 12.**
> Crit fail: reads as malicious — Perrin may react defensively, possibly breaking contact.
> Fail: nothing readable; the space feels empty.
> Near miss: something is attending, but indistinct.
> Success: monitoring, not predatory. This presence is not threatening him. It is not *for* him.
> Crit success: the attending fraction is near-infinitesimal. The rest of Auralis is occupied with something else entirely.

*[Ask Perrin: What does he do? Does he try to speak? Move? Look for an exit?]*

---

## Beat 3 — The Hunt

> [!read-aloud]
> The bioluminescent things scatter. The darkness closes in — total, moving, cold against every surface at once. There is only the water, everywhere.
>
> The breath arrives before you find it. Cold seawater moving through you in a long slow draw, through something you have no word for. Your chest is enormous. Your body is enormous. It extends behind you in the dark — longer than the Surety, longer than anything you have ever been — and the tail comes last, far back, the long lower lobe trailing through the current, the hook at its end dense and yellowed and scarred white at the joint.
>
> Your skin reads the water in frequencies you cannot name. Above: blood, diluted, days old, mixing with storm churn. The hunger registers it as a direction.

> [!dm]
> The blood above is from the Surety: Rook fight, Wouters overboard, days at anchor in chummed water. The shark has been circling since before the storm. Auralis isn't hiding it — Perrin can smell it. He is pulling attention downward. Ask: *"What does Perrin smell?"*

> [!read-aloud]
> Something else is below. Longer than two ships laid end to end, wider across the back than a warehouse floor, moving in slow unhurried arcs. Its breath comes in long cycles. The body already knows the angle. The body surges.
>
> The impact is a sound you feel in your cartilage. The hook seats. The whale decides to run. The drag is enormous. It dives. Pitches. Sounds into the dark.
>
> And then awareness narrows — contracts down through the whole length of you to one point: the joint. The base of the tail lobe. White-scarred and flexing under load. You feel it flex. Hold. Flex again.

> [!check] Nature — What is this point?
> **DC 10;** advantage with ship or rigging experience.
> Crit fail: reads as reinforced — misses the vulnerability.
> Fail: a junction, no particular significance.
> Near miss: seam under repeated tension.
> Success: structural seam where two different tissues meet under load. This seam can fail.
> Crit success (DC 14+): slashing damage, perpendicular to the grain — can sever the lobe and free the ship.

> [!dm]
> Auralis is showing Perrin the structural weak point. Don't name it. If asked, ask back: *"What does it feel like?"*

> [!read-aloud]
> The hunt does not finish. The ocean leaves.
>
> The bioluminescent things drift back to the edges of the stone. The floor is beneath your feet. You are the size you have always been.

---

## Beat 4 — The Vision

> [!read-aloud]
> The stone beneath your feet goes transparent.
>
> You are looking up through black water at the underside of a ship. From below, from the dark, something rises — fast, faster than anything that size should move. The hook catches the bioluminescent light for just a moment before the hull above you explodes inward. The hook is through. The creature drives its weight sideways and the ship lurches, then pulls. Every person grabbing at the barb is driving it deeper.

> [!dm]
> One of many attacks Auralis has watched over centuries. The sequence is accurate: Hooking Drive hooks the hull; until freed, the ship cannot move; pulling on the barb makes it worse.

> [!read-aloud]
> One more vision. Someone falling from the stricken ship into the water. You see them from below, entering the surface from underneath, bubbles and limbs and the white of a face looking down.
>
> The creature turns toward them before they are fully in the water.

> [!dm]
> Blood Frenzy (advantage on bloodied targets) + Surge reaction (30-ft move + bite when anything enters the water within 30 ft). After the Rook fight, anyone overboard is dead before the crew responds. Don't say it. Show it.

---

## Beat 5 — The Withdrawal

> [!read-aloud]
> The orientation of the room shifts. Something below — far below the transparent floor — pulls the attention of the space away. Not entirely. A fraction remains.
>
> One word arrives. The last one. It costs something — you can feel the cost without knowing what currency is being spent.
>
> **GROW.**

*[Stop. Ask Perrin: does he say it aloud? Does it mean anything to him yet?]*

> [!read-aloud]
> Then nothing. The space is still here. But the orientation is gone. You are alone at the bottom of the world.

> [!dm]
> Auralis is returning his attention to the fissure — this contact cost focus he could not spare. GROW is not an explanation or a goodbye. It is the one thing he wanted Perrin to carry.

> [!read-aloud]
> The stone goes.
>
> The sea comes back — the smell of it, the spray, the hull groaning under anchor strain in the storm. You catch the rail. One hand. One knee on the deck.
>
> The water below the ship is dark.

Session 03, Scene 02 — Whip shark encounter: three phases (probing, hook-seated, blood interruption), crew defaults, fast solution map, and ship narration reference.

# The Shark

*→ Run guide opener ends at "the lanterns swing hard to port and stay there." Continue here.*

**Starting state:** The shark is circling and probing. The barb has not yet seated. Players can act before the hook lands.

**Target time:** 60–75 minutes. If it runs long, compress aftermath and move to Calveno.

---

## Shark Stat Snapshot

**HP:** 114 | **AC:** 15 | **Attack bonus:** +9 | **Speed:** swim 60 ft.

| Attack | Hit | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Bite | 22 (3d10+6) piercing | Grappled, escape DC 17 |
| Barbed Tail | 17 (2d10+6) slashing | DC 17 Str save or pulled 20 ft; off-vessel means overboard |
| Hooking Drive | Activated on hook seat | Ship cannot move until tail is freed; pull/drown cycle begins |

**Blood Frenzy:** advantage against any creature below max HP.

**Surge:** when a creature enters water within 30 ft., shark moves up to 30 ft. and bites if in range. Not an action. State it clearly once when first relevant.

---

## Combat Setup

| Element | State |
|---|---|
| Shark | Circling port; dorsal fin breaks surface briefly during probing |
| Tail | Below the waterline at all times; hook and joint never visible from deck |
| Ship | Listing 5–10 degrees port once hook seats; rail close to water |
| Visibility | Pre-dawn after storm; dim light; nothing visible below the waterline |
| Overboard | Death pressure; Surge fires immediately |

---

## Crew Defaults

| Crew | Default If Undirected | If Directed |
|---|---|---|
| [[sem-holst\|Sem Holst]] | Bracing breach, shouting hull state | Cannot fight; confirms if an action worsens or helps the breach |
| [[geoffrey-draves\|Geoffrey]] | Frozen at rail, waiting for orders | Relay orders, fetch tools, direct Thunk, hold a line |
| [[thunk\|Thunk]] | Trying to bring a swivel gun to bear | Fire swivel gun for 2d6, hold a line, restrain gear |
| [[old-faas\|Old Faas]] | Cuts anchor chain on Round 2 unless stopped | Stop cutting, handle rigging, hack at lobe if directed into hold |
| [[alys-kuiper\|Alys]] | Below with wounded | Stabilize a downed PC if called |
| [[noor\|Noor]] | Hiding in hold | Screams if flooding reaches him; use as flooding alarm |

> [!dm]
> **Round 2 warning:** "Old Faas has a hatchet out at the anchor chain." Give the party a beat to stop or redirect him.

---

## Run Loop

Each round:

1. **Name the phase.** Probing, pulling, drowning, or repositioning.
2. **State the ship consequence.** List, hull sound, water, crew movement.
3. **Ask for PC actions.**
4. **Use one crew default** if no PC redirects that crew member.
5. **Advance the shark.** Probe strike, hook attempt, pull, or drown.
6. **Remind the table what changed.** Hull worse, breach wider, shark hurt, window open or closed.

Do not track ship HP. Sem is the hull narrator.

---

## Phase Structure

### Phase 0 — Probing (Rounds 1–2)

The shark tests the hull with glancing tail strikes. A deep underwater percussion from below the port hull, then the hull shaking. The dorsal fin may break the surface — long, pale, moving too slowly for its size.

Players can act here. Meaningful intervention (significant damage, deterrent, distraction) can delay or prevent the hook seating. Default: if the party does nothing, the hook seats at the end of Round 2.

| Pre-Hook Option | Result |
|---|---|
| Deal 20+ damage during probing | Shark recoils; no hook attempt this round |
| Chum, bright light, or loud percussion | DC 13 Wis; success delays probe 1 round. Three successes → shark disengages entirely |
| Thunk's swivel gun | 2d6; on 8+, shark skips hook attempt this round |

### Phase 1 — Hook Seats

> [!read-aloud]
> The next impact is different. Not a strike — a catch. The hull groans and doesn't stop groaning. The list doesn't correct. From below, Sem starts screaming.

The barb is through the hull, below the waterline, into the hold. The pull begins immediately.

### Phase 2 — The Pull

The shark turns and drags. The bow swings hard to port — 30 degrees in a few seconds.

> [!read-aloud]
> The bow lurches to port like something enormous grabbed it and yanked. The rigging shrieks. Anyone not holding something goes down.

> [!mechanic]
> All PCs and crew on deck: DC 12 Athletics or Acrobatics or fall prone and slide 10 ft. toward port rail. The shark then reverses direction mid-pull — the bow starts to come back, but the hook angle changes, driving the barb deeper.

### Phase 3 — The Drown

> [!read-aloud]
> The port rail goes under. The bow tilts hard. Water comes over the side in sheets. Then the ship fights back — she's too light, too full of air. The shark cannot hold her under. The ship hits the waterline like a dropped plank. The hull rings. Something below breaks.

**Hull condition (Sem narrates — not HP):**

1. *"She can take another one, but not five more."*
2. *"The frames are cracking — she's breathing water now."*
3. *"One more of those and I can't keep her up."*

After stage 3: the ship breaks apart if unresolved.

### Cycle Reset

After the drown, the shark repositions and begins again: probe → hook attempt → pull → drown → repeat. Each full cycle advances Sem's hull narration by one stage.

### Blood Interruption

If blood enters the water (PC overboard, crew blood washing out through the breach, shark wound) — the shark abandons the pull, moves to the blood source, and spends one round investigating. Hook tension releases temporarily.

> [!read-aloud]
> The tension releases. The ship groans back toward level. Somewhere in the dark water, something is moving toward the blood.

> [!dm]
> One round. After it, the shark repositions and re-hooks. This is the player opportunity window.

---

## The Joint

The joint — the scarred seam where the lower lobe begins — is **below the waterline**, outside the hull. Never visible from the weather deck.

**What they can discover:**

- From the hold: the lobe enters through the breached planking below water level; they can touch it, feel it flexing — but the joint is further out, outside the hull, underwater
- From above deck: the tail disappears into dark water; no visible indication of joint location
- Perrin's dream: he knows the joint is roughly 10 ft. along the lobe from the hull, and how deep

**Attacking the joint:**

- Over the rail: DC 12 Acrobatics first or fall overboard. Attack at disadvantage from unstable deck. 20+ slashing severs the lobe.
- Overboard: full access, no disadvantage, but Surge fires immediately. Death pressure.
- Perrin's knowledge removes disadvantage on the over-the-rail attack and lets him direct another PC precisely.

**Cutting the lobe from inside the hold:**

- Needs 3 successful hits (any damage) or 1 hit dealing 15+
- Severs the lobe stub from the shark; barb remains wedged in hull but shark is freed
- Breach widens; Sem screams; shark disengages

> [!dm]
> The designed solution is the joint (easiest sever mechanic), but cutting the lobe from the hold is a real option with a harder threshold. Any physical plan that makes sense gets a roll and a consequence.

## Fast Solution Map

**Pre-hook (during probing):**

| Player Approach | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Deal 20+ damage | Shark recoils; no hook attempt this round |
| Chum / salt pork / noise | DC 13 Wis; success delays one round. Three successes → shark disengages |
| Bright light at waterline | Shark Perception at disadvantage for this encounter |
| Thunk's swivel gun (directed) | 2d6; on 8+, shark skips hook attempt this round |

**Post-hook:**

| Player Approach | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Target joint (over rail) | DC 12 Acrobatics or fall overboard. Disadvantage on attack (or none with Perrin). 20+ slashing severs lobe. |
| Cut lobe from hold | 3 hits any damage or 1 hit 15+. Severs lobe; barb stays; shark disengages. Breach widens. |
| Pull the barb | First try: no roll; ship grinds toward shark, Sem screams. Persist: DC 18 Athletics while shark not pulling. Widens breach on success. |
| Cut anchor / outrun | Needs Old Faas + PC rigging + PC at helm. DC 14 helm check. Barb tears free when speed reaches 4+ knots but widens breach. |
| Main cannon | DC 15 to angle downward. 4d10 on hit; on d6 roll 1–2, also hits hull for 2d10. Sem is furious. |
| Oil / fire | 2d6 fire per round; DC 14 Wis or shark loses next action. Fire spreads to rail on Round 3 unless managed. |
| Eye shot | Reach weapon, rail position. DC 16 attack; 1d8+mod and shark loses blindsight for encounter. |
| Ask Grigori | He can calm water within 30 ft. as a ritual — flattens waves, reduces drown impact severity by one stage. Does it silently, no explanation. |

## Ship Narration

**Probing:**

- A low percussion from below the port hull. Not a wave. Regular.
- The ship rocks to port and doesn't fully settle before the next one comes.
- From below: something moving along the hull, slow and heavy.

**Hooked / pull:**

- The list deepens hard as the shark drives weight into the hull, then partially corrects.
- Salt water comes over the port rail in a sheet.
- Barrels in the hold roll to port and hit the bulkhead together.

**Drown:**

- The port rail goes under. It comes back. Everything not lashed is wet.
- The ship hits the surface hard — not a roll, a strike.
- From below: a sound like a frame cracking, then Sem's voice.

**When the joint severs:**

> [!read-aloud]
> The sound is a cannon shot. Not a crack — a percussion, something under enormous tension releasing all at once. The shark recoils hard to port. The tail stub wrenches free from the hull with a grinding tear. Water hits the breach fast for three seconds before Sem gets his brace in. The ship rolls back toward level. The port side goes quiet.

---

## Behavioral Arc

| Shark State | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 114–58 HP | Committed; pressing probing hits; hooking and cycling aggressively |
| 57–29 HP | Testing escape angles; circling wider; more responsive to deterrents |
| 28 HP or lower | Looking for a reason to disengage; chum, light, pain, or noise can end it |
| 0 HP | Hard and fast. No body. No confirmation. It may be dead; no one knows. |

---

## After It Ends

The fight ends when the shark disengages, is driven off, or dies.

- Tail stub or barb remains wedged in hull unless the resolution removed it.
- Sem can keep the ship afloat in calm water, not another storm.
- The Uncertainty needs dry dock before rough sailing.
- Move to [[session-03-scene-03-aftermath|Scene 03 — Aftermath]] quickly.

The port rail goes under. The bow tilts hard. Water comes over the side in sheets. Then the ship fights back — she’s too light, too full of air. The shark cannot hold her under. The ship hits the waterline like a dropped plank. The hull rings. Something below breaks.

Hull condition (Sem narrates — not HP):

  1. “She can take another one, but not five more.”
  2. “The frames are cracking — she’s breathing water now.”
  3. “One more of those and I can’t keep her up.”

After stage 3: the ship breaks apart if unresolved.

Cycle Reset

After the drown, the shark repositions and begins again: probe → hook attempt → pull → drown → repeat. Each full cycle advances Sem’s hull narration by one stage.

Blood Interruption

If blood enters the water (PC overboard, crew blood washing out through the breach, shark wound) — the shark abandons the pull, moves to the blood source, and spends one round investigating. Hook tension releases temporarily.

Read Aloud

The tension releases. The ship groans back toward level. Somewhere in the dark water, something is moving toward the blood.

DM Note

One round. After it, the shark repositions and re-hooks. This is the player opportunity window.

The Joint

The joint — the scarred seam where the lower lobe begins — is below the waterline, outside the hull. Never visible from the weather deck.

What they can discover:

  • From the hold: the lobe enters through the breached planking below water level; they can touch it, feel it flexing — but the joint is further out, outside the hull, underwater
  • From above deck: the tail disappears into dark water; no visible indication of joint location
  • Perrin’s dream: he knows the joint is roughly 10 ft. along the lobe from the hull, and how deep

Attacking the joint:

  • Over the rail: DC 12 Acrobatics first or fall overboard. Attack at disadvantage from unstable deck. 20+ slashing severs the lobe.
  • Overboard: full access, no disadvantage, but Surge fires immediately. Death pressure.
  • Perrin’s knowledge removes disadvantage on the over-the-rail attack and lets him direct another PC precisely.

Cutting the lobe from inside the hold:

  • Needs 3 successful hits (any damage) or 1 hit dealing 15+
  • Severs the lobe stub from the shark; barb remains wedged in hull but shark is freed
  • Breach widens; Sem screams; shark disengages
DM Note

The designed solution is the joint (easiest sever mechanic), but cutting the lobe from the hold is a real option with a harder threshold. Any physical plan that makes sense gets a roll and a consequence.

Ship Narration

Probing:

  • A low percussion from below the port hull. Not a wave. Regular.
  • The ship rocks to port and doesn’t fully settle before the next one comes.
  • From below: something moving along the hull, slow and heavy.

Hooked / pull:

  • The list deepens hard as the shark drives weight into the hull, then partially corrects.
  • Salt water comes over the port rail in a sheet.
  • Barrels in the hold roll to port and hit the bulkhead together.

Drown:

  • The port rail goes under. It comes back. Everything not lashed is wet.
  • The ship hits the surface hard — not a roll, a strike.
  • From below: a sound like a frame cracking, then Sem’s voice.

When the joint severs:

Read Aloud

The sound is a cannon shot. Not a crack — a percussion, something under enormous tension releasing all at once. The shark recoils hard to port. The tail stub wrenches free from the hull with a grinding tear. Water hits the breach fast for three seconds before Sem gets his brace in. The ship rolls back toward level. The port side goes quiet.

Behavioral Arc

Shark StateBehavior
114–58 HPCommitted; pressing probing hits; hooking and cycling aggressively
57–29 HPTesting escape angles; circling wider; more responsive to deterrents
28 HP or lowerLooking for a reason to disengage; chum, light, pain, or noise can end it
0 HPHard and fast. No body. No confirmation. It may be dead; no one knows.

After It Ends

The fight ends when the shark disengages, is driven off, or dies.

  • Tail stub or barb remains wedged in hull unless the resolution removed it.
  • Sem can keep the ship afloat in calm water, not another storm.
  • The Uncertainty needs dry dock before rough sailing.

# Session 03 — Aftermath

> [!dm]
> Keep this short. Three beats: damage, Grigori, depart. Don't let it breathe into a logistics scene.

---

## Beat 1 — The Damage

[[sem-holst|Sem]]'s report, delivered at the breach:

- Tail stub wedged in the hull; he and Geoffrey need two hours to work it free.
- The breach itself is manageable — packed timber and pitch holds for calm water. Not for another storm.
- They need a dry dock.
- ETA to [[calveno|Calveno]] at current pace: five days, weather holding.

> [!dm]
> One exchange with Sem, one clear message: *dry dock or she sinks in the next bad weather.* Move on.

---

## Beat 2 — Grigori

![[session-03-03-grigori-healing.png|Grigori heals a wounded crewman too quickly on the wet dawn deck while the breach work continues behind him]]

First light. [[shepherd-grigori|Grigori]] comes up the companionway with a tin mug in each hand. Looks at the rail, the breach work, the state of the crew. Not alarmed.

He offers the mugs to whoever is nearest. Checks on the crew by name. If anyone is hurt, he crouches and asks if he can look — not a command. If yes, he puts a hand on the injury and murmurs. It heals faster than it should.

> [!check] Medicine — The healing
> **DC 13** casual observation / **DC 17** close examination.
> Crit fail: reads as normal magical healing — faster maybe, nothing unexpected.
> Fail: faster than expected, but maybe he's just skilled.
> Success: tissue knitting at a rate unrelated to what Grigori put into it. Injury site is too warm after.
> Crit success (DC 17+): the warmth in his hands doesn't come from body heat and doesn't withdraw when he lifts his hand.

Nobody has seen him sleep. If a player asks: he smiles and says the sea keeps him company.

> [!check] Insight — Reading Grigori
> **DC 14** surface read / **DC 18** sustained attention.
> Crit fail: reads as tense beneath the calm — misread entirely.
> Fail: unreadable; warm and professional, nothing leaks through.
> Success: genuinely unbothered. No alarm behind the calm.
> Crit success (DC 18+): whatever he is, fatigue isn't part of it. His eyes haven't changed since last night.

> [!dm]
> Don't explain the healing or name it. Move on before anyone asks a follow-up — Sem needs the stub, Noor needs something, Geoffrey drops a tool. Grigori stands, picks up his mug, watches the horizon.

---

## Beat 3 — Depart

The stub comes free. Sem patches the breach. Sails up in early morning light. The storm left the water flat and grey.

> [!read-aloud]
> The Surety moves. For the first time since the anchor dropped, the hull answers the wind the way it's supposed to — straight, clean, no drag. Old [[old-faas|Faas]] ties off the last line and looks back at the water behind them. The bioluminescent wake is long gone. The sea gives nothing back.

Set heading: [[calveno|Calveno]]. Five days.

# Calveno Day One

*Two beats: the water noticing Delmar, and Branca finding him. They don't need to happen simultaneously — let the party breathe and explore first.*

---

## Beat 1 — The Gangplank

![[sessions/session-art/session-03-06-gangplank-water.png|The basin water rises toward Delmar's boot as he steps from the Surety onto La Vasca's stone quay]]

The party is crossing from ship to dock at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]]. Grigori has already walked off into the city without looking back. Sem is at the breach. Cobb is hovering.

When [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] steps off the gangplank onto Calveno's stone quay, the water in the covered basin shifts. Not a wake from the hull. A slow deliberate rise along the stone edge, close to where his foot lands — like something in the channel below recognized the weight of him. It reaches toward his foot and then it doesn't. Gone in a breath. The basin settles.

> [!dm]
> Don't narrate this unprompted. Ask Delmar's player what the water looks like if they're watching; otherwise move on. It happened regardless. It will happen again.
>
> Nobody else sees it unless they were already looking at the water at his feet. Don't make it a group event.

---

## Beat 2 — Branca Finds Delmar

She has been at the Calveno Waveservant Shrine for three weeks — the goddess told her where the party was heading before they knew it themselves. When word came up through the port this morning (a Rattkin canal crew, a word to a chandler, the chandler to the shrine), she left and started asking.

She is good at asking. She has been doing this a long time.

She finds [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] in the streets — wherever he's drifted, Mercatura or the canalside or near a tavern. She comes around a corner or steps out of a shop doorway, already consulting the booklet when she looks up.

> [!read-aloud]
> A woman in her mid-forties, salt-white hair pulled back hard, Waveservant blue-grey robes. A slight limp — the kind that has been ignored so long it's become posture. She produces a small leather booklet from her sleeve, consults it without urgency, and looks up at Fisk with the specific warmth of someone who has delivered very bad news many times and decided the kindest thing is to make it easy. *"You're a difficult man to find,"* she says, pleasantly. *"We have an appointment."*

> [!check] Insight — "We have an appointment"
> DC 12 surface read, DC 16 mechanism clear.
>
> - Crit fail: reads her as cold or threatening — misread; she's warm, not menacing.
> - Fail: professional veneer; can't read through it.
> - Near miss: she means exactly what she said. Not rhetorical.
> - Success: not metaphor. A name is in the booklet — probably his. Not improvising and not lying.
> - Crit success (DC 16+): the goddess told her to be here. Branca treats that as operationally equivalent to a calendar entry. She has done this many times.

---

## While Branca Finds Delmar

The other three PCs are in open Calveno sandbox. Entry hooks available on Day One:

- **Perrin** — Nona's pressure is already live; Cobb has delivered his warning. The [[warren|Warren]] route is the pull.
- **Jean-Claude** — if he is anywhere in the city, offer the handler recognition beat. See [[calveno-jean-claude-beats|Calveno — Jean-Claude Beats]] for the full beat and the Handler Cell ride.
- **Crissdalynn** — if she's with Delmar at the shrine, the booklet arrives there. If she's elsewhere, Branca finds her separately before end of day.

Route any PC intent through [[calveno-sandbox-run-guide|Calveno Sandbox Run Guide]].

---

## The Invitation

![[sessions/session-art/session-03-06-shrine-communion.png|Branca stands knee-deep in the Waveservant Shrine basin while Delmar watches the canal water listen]]

[[branca|Branca]] wants him to accompany her to the Waveservant Shrine — Calveno for her communion with Umberlee. Today, if possible. She checks the booklet: *"I've gone ahead and blocked the third tide — does that work, or should I find something that fits your schedule a little better?"*

She does not explain what the communion entails. Not because she's withholding — because she assumes he knows.

> [!dm]
> **If Delmar asks what the communion is:** she says it's routine — the goddess has questions and she conveys them. *"You don't need to say anything unless you want to."* She believes this is accurate and reassuring.
> **If Delmar refuses:** Branca smiles, notes the refusal in the booklet, says she'll find another slot. She's in Calveno until further notice.

### At the Shrine

The basin is fed directly from the canal. She steps into it up to her knees, tilts her head back, and speaks low in Aquan. Whatever passes between her and the goddess happens in silence.

> [!check] Perception (Delmar) — The basin water
> DC 10, or passive Perception 10.
>
> - Fail: misses it; only Branca knows it happened.
> - Near miss: the water near his foot rises slightly and settles — brief, gone.
> - Success: the water rises toward him when he approaches the basin, the same slow deliberate reach as the gangplank. Nobody else triggers it.
> - Crit success: the reach is directional and controlled — not responding to current or his movement. Responding to him.

She looks at Delmar: *"She sees you."* A pause. *"That's all she wanted. For now."* She steps out of the water, dries her robes without comment, and notes the appointment as complete.

> [!check] Religion — What does "She sees you" mean?
> DC 14 surface read, DC 18 full implications.
>
> - Crit fail: thinks being seen is being claimed — incorrect; confuses observation with a pact.
> - Fail: sounds significant but meaning is opaque.
> - Near miss: gods of this type maintain awareness through open water; different from prayer.
> - Success: being seen means Delmar's actions near the sea are potentially visible to Umberlee. Not passive.
> - Crit success (DC 18+): being seen is not being claimed. It is being *filed*. The beginning of a kind of attention.

> [!dm]
> **If Delmar brings the party:** the shrine is public. Any PC present sees Branca step into the basin, go still, and come back with that professional energy intact. The goddess said nothing to them. That is its own information.
>
> **If Crissdalynn is present:** Branca produces a tide-table booklet after the communion ends and hands it to Crissdalynn without ceremony. Umberlee told her to keep it until someone came in from the direction of the Maw. Don't explain what it means — this is Crissdalynn's entry hook.

# Session 04 — The Frog, the Owl, and the Bomb

## Durable Changes

- **Delmar confessed.** Told the party he was a real admiral — five-ship privateer fleet sponsored by the [[chain-council|Chain Council]]. They stole the [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] from a shrine in [[sunken-crown|Vafnar]]; the Maw destroyed the fleet hours later. Crissdalynn pulled him free. The Pearl fell into the Maw with the wreckage.
- **Umberlee spoke through Branca.** At the [[waveservant-shrine|Calveno harbor shrine]], Umberlee possessed [[branca|Branca]], demanded the Pearl's return, killed and resurrected Branca as a demonstration, then negotiated: bring the Pearl, keep your life, souls stay with Umberlee. Delmar counter-offered to deliver those who commissioned the theft. Umberlee read his mind freely and deferred: "Bring me the pearl. We will talk then."
- **Boots of flying → Delmar.** Jean-Claude bought boots of flying from [[casa-lupo|Casa Lupo]] (125gp). Perrin won the roll but doesn't wear shoes — Rattkin go barefoot. Delmar received them.
- **Jean-Claude's silent shortbow.** +1 shortbow from Casa Lupo (50gp): completely silent, does not reveal position when firing from hidden, no attunement.
- **Jean-Claude sold whip shark eggs.** 3 fertilized eggs for 300gp (30 platinum) to a Le Paludi market merchant. He has 250gp remaining after shopping.
- **Kyzil sparring match.** Non-lethal four-on-one on the Ponte Bassa rooftop, 3 rounds. Kyzil's stat block (CR 14) confirmed: 4 attacks, returning daggers (piercing + force), DC 19 open palm, Downburst legendary action, Empty Wing Parry reaction (+5 AC). Party held well — Crissdalynn grappled him (nat 1 contested), Delmar landed a sneak attack through bardic inspiration, Perrin's drum drew Kyzil's tactical concern.
- **Grung bombing plot exposed.** Party investigated [[nona-black-jaw|Nona]]'s Grung sightings in the sewers. Found directional markers, traps, and a catamaran loaded with 8 barrels of black powder. Jean-Claude ambushed two patrol Grung; Crissdalynn kingfishered a fleeing purple Grung. Jean-Claude executed the purple captive after it refused to talk and confirmed Simone's involvement.
- **Felix Aho captured.** Green Grung laborer, hired (not ideological). Revealed: coordinated bombing from 4 underground attack points, scaffolding holding black powder against sewer ceilings, 2-day deadline timed to festival, purple garrisons and red leaders at each point, 6 ships total ferrying powder. Offered full cooperation for 1 month of protection.
- **Grung defectors exist.** Felix revealed that Grung who leave Simone's faction are kill-on-sight. Jean-Claude is considered a defector. He did not know defectors existed as a recognized category.
- **Nona's favor executed.** Sending stone call: investigate Grung in the sewers. Nona provided Hero's Feast through cooking. Party completed the investigation and returned with Felix and full intel.
- **Delmar abstaining from alcohol.** Drank from his flask before the waitress arrived — not liquor. Unusual for him.
- **Kyzil staying through the festival.** Confirmed present in Calveno at least through Il Gioco delle Beffe.
- **Ponte Bassa established as party base.** Cheap tavern near La Vasca, Passage front. Two rooms rented.

## Scene Log

1. **Le Paludi Market** — Jean-Claude sold 3 whip shark eggs (300gp as 30pt). Merchant noted fertilization reduces value (culinary delicacy, not breeding stock).
2. **Casa Lupo** — Jean-Claude bought +1 silent shortbow (50gp) and boots of flying (125gp, intended for a party member).
3. **Le Paludi streets** — Jean-Claude met Kyzil. Kyzil: "Your kind isn't from here. Why are you here?" Dismissed him as no threat. Crissdalynn vouched. Delmar bear-hugged Kyzil.
4. **Ponte Bassa** — Party established tavern as base. Kyzil discussed Crissdalynn's pilgrimage: gave her the hardest in Eyrie history because he knew she could do it. Maw has been unruly since the wreck. Kyzil senses something foul from the south.
5. **Ponte Bassa rooftop** — Boots gifted; Perrin → Delmar (retcon: Rattkin don't wear shoes). Kyzil challenged spar.
6. **Kyzil spar (Rounds 1–3)** — Crissdalynn grappled Kyzil R1 (nat 1 contest). Delmar joined with Tavern Brawler chair throw. Kyzil's Downburst broke grapple R2 (Crissdalynn saved first via bardic inspiration, failed second). R3: Kyzil rescued Crissdalynn from falling off roof, then attacked all four — pinned Jean-Claude's shirt as dominance display. Delmar hit through Empty Wing Parry via bardic inspiration (17 damage). 3 rounds, stat block held as designed.
7. **Walking to harbor** — Delmar confessed: real admiral, five ships, Chain Council privateers, Pearl of Souls theft, Maw destroyed fleet. Water tracks him when he steps off land.
8. **Calveno harbor shrine** — Umberlee possessed Branca. Demanded Pearl + Delmar's death. Delmar lied; Umberlee saw through it, killed and resurrected Branca. Revised deal: Pearl for Delmar's life. Delmar counter-offered: Pearl + the commissioners. Umberlee deferred.
9. **Ponte Bassa morning** — Crissdalynn leg-swept Delmar for meeting Umberlee without her. Nona's sending stone: "Bring your friends, especially the blue one." Festival registration opened; party signed up.
10. **Nona's safe house** — Nona briefed: 6 Grung sightings in Warren tunnels/sewers. Blue, green, one purple. Unprecedented — no Grung has crossed the Central Strait. Rattkin witness described purple Grung in market district. Hero's Feast from Nona's cooking.
11. **Calveno sewers** — Jean-Claude on ceiling (Gloom Stalker), Perrin invisible, Delmar traps, Crissdalynn rear. Found Grung directional markers ("500m →"), triggered crossbow trap (miss). Black powder scent increasing. Exited at Le Paludi coast.
12. **Le Paludi coast** — Perrin scouted boat: 3 Grung, 8 barrels of black powder. Jean-Claude ambushed 2 patrol Grung from ceiling (24 damage instant kill via Dread Strike). Ship exploded (fire arrow to powder). Crissdalynn kingfishered the purple Grung at 45ft fly speed. Jean-Claude executed it after it called him a traitor.
13. **Sewer exit interrogation** — Felix Aho (green Grung laborer) revealed the full operation: 4 attack points, scaffolding against ceilings, 2-day deadline, purple garrisons + red leaders, 6 ships total. Defectors exist — kill on sight. Felix wants 1 month protection.
14. **Nona's safe house** — Felix delivered; Ruck guards him. Festival cover made transport easy. Nona: "I knew I chose the right people."

## Rules and Rulings

- **Silent shortbow:** +1 to hit/damage, no sound on draw or fire, does not reveal position from hidden. No attunement. DM confirmed.
- **Boots of flying:** uncommon, attunement, 4hr flight, regains 2hr per 12hr not in use.
- **Grappled condition:** zero movement, no disadvantage on attacks. Grappler feat gives advantage on grappled target.
- **Deflect attacks (Crissdalynn):** reduce damage; if reduced to 0, spend 1 focus point to redirect — DC 13 Dex or 2d6+4 damage.
- **Tavern Brawler:** proficiency with improvised weapons, 1d4 + Str.
- **Bardic inspiration retroactive:** DM allowed as reaction during spar.
- **Gloom Stalker:** invisible in complete darkness to darkvision-reliant creatures. Confirmed.
- **Hero's Feast (Nona's cooking):** cured diseases/poison, immune to poison and frightened, Wis saves advantage, +2d10 max HP for 24 hours.
- **Umberlee's divine insight:** trumps Deception regardless of roll.

Delmar counter-offered to deliver those who commissioned the theft. Umberlee read his mind freely and deferred: “Bring me the pearl. We will talk then.”
  • Boots of flying → Delmar. Jean-Claude bought boots of flying from Casa Lupo (125gp). Perrin won the roll but doesn’t wear shoes — Rattkin go barefoot. Delmar received them.
  • Jean-Claude’s silent shortbow. +1 shortbow from Casa Lupo (50gp): completely silent, does not reveal position when firing from hidden, no attunement.
  • Jean-Claude sold whip shark eggs. 3 fertilized eggs for 300gp (30 platinum) to a Le Paludi market merchant. He has 250gp remaining after shopping.
  • Kyzil sparring match. Non-lethal four-on-one on the Ponte Bassa rooftop, 3 rounds. Kyzil’s stat block (CR 14) confirmed: 4 attacks, returning daggers (piercing + force), DC 19 open palm, Downburst legendary action, Empty Wing Parry reaction (+5 AC). Party held well — Crissdalynn grappled him (nat 1 contested), Delmar landed a sneak attack through bardic inspiration, Perrin’s drum drew Kyzil’s tactical concern.
  • Grung bombing plot exposed. Party investigated Nona‘s Grung sightings in the sewers. Found directional markers, traps, and a catamaran loaded with 8 barrels of black powder. Jean-Claude ambushed two patrol Grung; Crissdalynn kingfishered a fleeing purple Grung. Jean-Claude executed the purple captive after it refused to talk and confirmed Simone’s involvement.
  • Felix Aho captured. Green Grung laborer, hired (not ideological). Revealed: coordinated bombing from 4 underground attack points, scaffolding holding black powder against sewer ceilings, 2-day deadline timed to festival, purple garrisons and red leaders at each point, 6 ships total ferrying powder. Offered full cooperation for 1 month of protection.
  • Grung defectors exist. Felix revealed that Grung who leave Simone’s faction are kill-on-sight. Jean-Claude is considered a defector. He did not know defectors existed as a recognized category.
  • Nona’s favor executed. Sending stone call: investigate Grung in the sewers. Nona provided Hero’s Feast through cooking. Party completed the investigation and returned with Felix and full intel.
  • Delmar abstaining from alcohol. Drank from his flask before the waitress arrived — not liquor. Unusual for him.
  • Kyzil staying through the festival. Confirmed present in Calveno at least through Il Gioco delle Beffe.
  • Ponte Bassa established as party base. Cheap tavern near La Vasca, Passage front. Two rooms rented.

Scene Log

  1. Le Paludi Market — Jean-Claude sold 3 whip shark eggs (300gp as 30pt). Merchant noted fertilization reduces value (culinary delicacy, not breeding stock).

  3. Le Paludi streets — Jean-Claude met Kyzil. Kyzil: “Your kind isn’t from here. Why are you here?” Dismissed him as no threat. Crissdalynn vouched. Delmar bear-hugged Kyzil.
  4. Ponte Bassa — Party established tavern as base. Kyzil discussed Crissdalynn’s pilgrimage: gave her the hardest in Eyrie history because he knew she could do it. Maw has been unruly since the wreck. Kyzil senses something foul from the south.
  5. Ponte Bassa rooftop — Boots gifted; Perrin → Delmar (retcon: Rattkin don’t wear shoes). Kyzil challenged spar.
  6. Kyzil spar (Rounds 1–3) — Crissdalynn grappled Kyzil R1 (nat 1 contest). Delmar joined with Tavern Brawler chair throw. Kyzil’s Downburst broke grapple R2 (Crissdalynn saved first via bardic inspiration, failed second). R3: Kyzil rescued Crissdalynn from falling off roof, then attacked all four — pinned Jean-Claude’s shirt as dominance display. Delmar hit through Empty Wing Parry via bardic inspiration (17 damage). 3 rounds, stat block held as designed.

# Session 04 — Day 1: Arrival Evening

*Pick up in the street the instant Kyzil lands — late afternoon, Le Paludi. This plays out the reunion Session 03 ended on. Give Crissdalynn the floor.*

---

## Strong Start — Kyzil Reunion

> [!read-aloud]
> The wind goes quiet. The sun is high and behind you — and then something with the sun behind it drops out of the sky in dead silence and hits Crissdalynn square in the chest, two arms around her before the wind is even back. The smell lands before the sight does: feathers, incense, home. "Oh my God, Priscilla. You're alive." [[master-kyzil\|Master Kyzil]] holds her at arm's length, then looks at the rest of you, remembering himself. "Hi. I'm — Master Kyzil. What happened?"

Let the reunion breathe. Then the evening presses in: the ship in its cradle, a city dressing for festival, and — for Delmar — a woman in a shrine across the district who has not moved since she found him an hour ago.

> [!dm]
> This is Day 1 evening; the open city day is tomorrow (registration at dawn). If the party wants to bed down, fine — but Branca does not wait *politely*, she waits *absolutely* (see below). Handle Delmar's awareness of her before he rests easy.

---

## Kyzil — Roleplay Notes

**NPC — Master Kyzil** ([[master-kyzil\|page]]): Owl Obi-Wan — relief held under monastic discipline. He grabs Crissdalynn like she's been dead for a year; then recovers formality with visible effort. Speaks softly. First question to anyone near her is always "Who." Not hostile — categorizing.

**What he knows:** He searched east of Midchain. Corrected course when word reached him that Crissdalynn was alive and heading toward the Central Strait. He knows her original ship went down to *"a foul wind from the south"* — he will not volunteer this tonight. Grief sits under discipline; he shares facts when he judges her ready, not when the party asks.

**What he offers (tonight):**

- Asks about Crissdalynn's pilgrimage progress — how many of the four trials has she completed?
- Offers to teach **Read the Current** (a monk technique) in a future sparring session.
- Warns that Maw weather has made the High Eyrie approach route dangerous.
- Will challenge the party to a four-on-one nonlethal spar if anyone wants to test him (playful, not threatening; he wins easily and enjoys himself).

> [!dm]
> Don't dump Kyzil's full lore. He is protective. Tonight he wants to feed Crissdalynn, assess the people around her, and sleep in the same building. Deeper threads — the foul wind, the Maw, the Red Lady traces — arrive on Days 2–3 through play, not exposition.

---

## Branca's Vigil

**[[branca\|Branca]] will not leave the [[waveservant-shrine\|Waveservant Shrine]].** She found Delmar an hour ago, he put her off, she walked to the shrine and sat down. She has not moved since. She will not — overnight, all of tomorrow, however long it takes. She is that much of a zealot, and waiting costs her nothing.

There is no skipping this scene; there is only *when* Delmar walks into it. The Pearl Summons runs in full on [[session-04-day-2\|Day 2]]. Tonight establishes the pressure.

> [!dm]
> If Delmar tries to long rest without going to the shrine, give it about ten seconds, then: he can't quite settle — and when he looks toward the Mercatura he *knows*, the way you know a held breath, that she's still in there in the dark, awake, hands folded, waiting. She'll outlast him. Don't force the visit tonight. Let the dread sit.

**If Delmar goes to the shrine tonight:** run the [[session-04-day-2#the-shrine--pearl-summons|Pearl Summons]] from Day 2 immediately. It works at any hour — the shrine is always open; the font is always breathing.

---

## Cobb's Check-In

[[cobb\|Cobb]] finds Perrin before the evening is done — at the tavern, the dock, or wherever Perrin settles. He knows Perrin already went to see Nona.

**NPC — Cobb** ([[cobb\|page]]): Young Warren Rattkin, dockworker's coat, speaks quietly, glances at exits out of habit. Drops onto a bench without asking permission. Loyal to Nona but likes Perrin — won't hide him from the family, won't volunteer more than he knows. Emotional default: cautious warmth. What cracks it: being asked to choose between Nona's instructions and Perrin's safety.

> [!read-aloud]
> A young Rattkin in a dockworker's coat drops onto the bench beside Perrin without asking. "She was glad you came. She won't say it twice, so I'm saying it." He glances at the sending stone if it's visible. "That thing's not decorative. When she uses it, she means now, not when you get around to it."

**If Perrin asks about the stone or the favor:** "I don't know what she's planning. I know she's been waiting for a reason to use it, and you showing up gave her one. That's all I've got." He's telling the truth — Nona keeps her plans close.

**If Perrin asks about the Warren:** "It's still there. She's still there. The Rattle still works. Come see for yourself — she'd like that." (Genuine; not a summons.)

> [!dm]
> Cobb is bridging. Perrin already met Nona, apologized, and left with the sending stone and an unconditional favor he hasn't heard yet. Cobb's role tonight is to reinforce that the stone is live and the favor is coming — not to arrange a first meeting.

> [!dm]
> **Spotlight.** Crissdalynn owns the opening beat (Kyzil). Once that breathes, make sure Delmar feels Branca's weight before the party sleeps. JC and Perrin get city texture tonight — their threads activate when the city opens.

## The Shrine — Pearl Summons

*Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn (was there when Branca first found him). Revelation / horror set-piece.*

This is a **fixed dramatic beat**, not a negotiation. The offer is unacceptable by design; the refusal is expected; the point is the demonstration. Run it as scripted and let the silence between boxes work.

### Arrival

> [!read-aloud]
> The [[waveservant-shrine\|Waveservant Shrine]] is a low, tide-stained vault off a Mercatura canal. The font behind the bench holds a hand's depth of seawater that will not lie flat — it rises and falls, slow, like something breathing under it. [[branca\|Branca]] is exactly where she sat down: upright, awake, salt-white hair pulled back hard, the little leather tide-table booklet open on her knee. "So," she says, bright and clipped, the warmth of someone rescheduling a missed meeting. "You came. Good. We have an appointment."

**NPC — Branca:** corporate cult executive assistant — bubbly, efficient, too much eye contact; opens "So!", closes "Does that work for you?", checks the booklet mid-sentence as if it settles every objection. She believes making divine horror *pleasant* is a kindness. She is the soft instrument; what comes through her is not.

### The Possession

Branca stops mid-sentence. Her eyes roll back to white. The voice is not hers.

> [!read-aloud]
> Branca's eyes roll white. When she speaks it is not her voice — it is the sea given a throat, cold and enormous and patient. "FISK. You carry what is Mine. Go down to the wreck. Bring Me the Pearl. Return it to My shrine — and I will grant you the one mercy you have earned: a swift death, and the souls you stole brought home to Me. This is My grace. Accept it."

**The demand (plainly):** retrieve the [[pearl-of-souls\|Pearl of Souls]] from the [[red-lady\|Red Lady]] wreck at the [[the-drowned-maw\|Drowned Maw]] and return it to a shrine of Umberlee. The "reward" is Delmar's *own death* and the surrender of the souls he carries. A death sentence dressed as salvation. He will refuse — by design.

> [!dm]
> This brushes Delmar's secret. The party hears that he **carries souls Umberlee claims** and that there's a Pearl to retrieve. They need not learn the five captains / Vel Orn story — keep Her words to "what is Mine" and "the souls you stole." Only Delmar's player knows he carries voices.

### The Wrath

The instant Delmar refuses:

> [!read-aloud]
> The refusal is barely out of your mouth before the light goes wrong. Thunder walks across a sky that was clear a breath ago; the canal shivers in its channel. The thing wearing Branca *roars* — and then, almost offhand, it takes her head in her own two hands and snaps her neck. The body folds. The shrine goes silent. Branca lies on the wet stone, not breathing.

Hold the silence. Then —

### The Return

> [!read-aloud]
> Mist gathers off the canal — too fast, too deliberate — and curls in around the fallen woman like a tide coming home. Branca's chest heaves. She drags in one enormous, gasping breath, sits up, blinks the white from her eyes, finds the booklet, smooths her robe, and looks up with that same bright warmth, as if nothing happened. "I hope," she says, "you understand my lady Umberlee's power. And her grace."

> [!check] Insight — After the Revival
> DC 12 (no advantage from prior knowledge; this is emotional, not logical).
> Fail: reads as shock; the depth doesn't register.
> Success: Branca means it completely — she experienced her own murder as a privilege and is not performing. *That* is the horror.
> Crit success: Branca has been through this before. Not once. Her faith is forged, not learned — and the thing that spoke through her left a trace of salt on the air that is not fading.

**The bind:** the only way to satisfy the goddess is to die for her, so Delmar has to find a third answer — and the Pearl she wants is inside the [[red-lady\|Red Lady]] — exactly what the salvage commission is racing for. Demand and money pull at the same wreck from opposite directions.

## Batta Zusto — The Salvage Commission

*Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn. Social / investigation.*

Today the Red Lady thread has a name and a face. **[[batta-zusto\|Batta Zusto]]** operates from the upper tier of the Bridge exchange — mid-tier broker, stocky, late fifties, dressed a touch too formally for the weather. Clean information, priced, no embellishment. Not hostile, not protective of clients.

**NPC — Batta Zusto** ([[batta-zusto\|page]]): Information broker, not a fixer. Sits with his back to the crowd — not paranoia, confidence. States facts and states prices. Silences are deliberate and longer than normal; he lets the buyer fill them. Never qualifies a claim. The cup in front of him is a prop — he doesn't drink during business. Verbal style: short declarative sentences, no hedging. "The commission exists. It's funded. The gear is rented, not purchased. That's three things. Forty gold or equivalent."

### Entry

Two paths in:

- **The party asks after Maw salvage** anywhere in Calveno — a chandler, a dock regular, or Savia names "Zusto" once.
- **Delmar makes himself visible** as a Maw expert — Zusto (or his runner) finds *him*.

> [!read-aloud]
> The Bridge's upper tier runs narrow — stone counters, sealed ledgers, men who do not speak first. Batta Zusto sits at a counter with his back to the crowd, a cup of something cold he has not drunk, watching nothing. He does not look up when you approach. He waits until you sit, then: "I know what you're asking. The question is whether you can afford the answer or only the rumour."

### What Zusto Sells

**Price:** 40 gp, or a piece of Maw navigation intelligence worth ~80 gp, or the confirmed wreck name.

| Intel | Detail |
|---|---|
| Commission shape | Deep-access Maw cargo recovery. Not a survey — someone knows what they're looking for. |
| Three supply chains | Hired diving apparatus (not bought — rental, returned after). Premium sealed chart package. Crew contacts in two ports. |
| Money origin | Came through a **Port Tidefall factor** Zusto has worked with before. Good for the credit. Not previously interested in salvage. |

Batta Zusto — The Salvage Commission

Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn. Social / investigation.

Today the Red Lady thread has a name and a face. Batta Zusto operates from the upper tier of the Bridge exchange — mid-tier broker, stocky, late fifties, dressed a touch too formally for the weather. Clean information, priced, no embellishment. Not hostile, not protective of clients.

NPC — Batta Zusto (page): Information broker, not a fixer. Sits with his back to the crowd — not paranoia, confidence. States facts and states prices. Silences are deliberate and longer than normal; he lets the buyer fill them. Never qualifies a claim. The cup in front of him is a prop — he doesn’t drink during business. Verbal style: short declarative sentences, no hedging. “The commission exists. It’s funded. The gear is rented, not purchased. That’s three things. Forty gold or equivalent.”

Read Aloud

The Bridge’s upper tier runs narrow — stone counters, sealed ledgers, men who do not speak first. Batta Zusto sits at a counter with his back to the crowd, a cup of something cold he has not drunk, watching nothing. He does not look up when you approach. It will jump into and out of the crater if pressed.

[[nona-black-jaw|Nona Black-Jaw]] emerges from her safehouses within the hour. Both bodyguards at her sides — [[enzo|Enzo]] in his tailored suit, jaw set, claws out; [[ruk|Ruk]] carrying a cauldron of stew on one shoulder and a cleaver on the other.

Nona does not come to fight. She comes to feed.

> [!read-aloud]
> A very small, very old Rattkin woman walks into the dust of the Mercatura with a ladle in one hand and a loaf of bread in the other. She is flanked by a jaguar in a suit and a lizardfolk carrying a pot large enough to bathe in. She does not look at the crater. She looks at the people sitting on the ground beside it.
>
> She starts handing out bread. She does not ask names. She does not ask what happened. She sits down next to a woman who is still calling her husband's name and puts a piece of bread in her hand and holds it there until the woman takes a bite.

Nona works the crowd for an hour. She talks to the victims. She listens. She learns.

What she hears: names. Missing names. Husbands, sons, fathers, dock workers, boatmen — gone. Taken underground. Families standing where someone stood ten minutes ago and finding nothing but dropped tools and trampled festival cloth.

And she recognizes the pain. She has heard it before. Countless Rattkin have simply disappeared and their loved ones never learned why. The Crown took them, or the sea took them, or the world took them, and nobody came to explain and nobody came to bring them back. The grief in the Mercatura is the grief of the Warren. Nona has carried it for forty years.

### The Speech

> [!dm]
> Nona does not climb on a box. She does not raise her voice. She stands in the middle of a crowd of people who have just had their world broken and she speaks the way she always speaks — flat, clear, specific, the voice of a woman who has been at war for longer than most of these people have been alive and has never once pretended it was easy.

> [!read-aloud]
> "I know what this is." She says it to no one in particular and everyone at once. "I know what it is to look for someone who was here a minute ago and find nothing. I have done it more times than I can count. My people have been disappearing for decades — taken, sold, worked until they break, and the ones left behind never get told where or why or whether there's a body to mourn."
>
> She pauses. Looks at the faces. Continues.
>
> "Today it happened to you. And you are going to feel a thing I have felt my whole life — that the world took someone you love and nobody who was supposed to stop it even tried. I am not going to stand here and tell you it gets easier. It does not."
>
> The bread is gone. She sets down the ladle.
>
> "The Passage stands with the citizens of Calveno. I am too old to swing a sword, and my knees are not what they were. But I know how to find people who have been taken. I have been doing it since before this city built its first canal. I will assemble a crew. We will make chase. And we will bring your brothers and your sons and your fathers back. I am making you that promise in front of your neighbours and in front of my God and in front of the two extremely large gentlemen behind me who will remind me of it if I try to go to bed instead."

> [!dm]
> Enzo does not smile. Ruk nods once.
>
> Nona's vow is real. She will assemble a pursuit force from Warren volunteers, Passage contacts, and anyone in Calveno willing to crew a fast ship. The pursuit is the next beat of the raid situation — whether the party joins it, leads it, or watches it leave without them.
>
> **What this changes:** Nona has publicly declared the Passage's allegiance to Calveno's citizens. This is unprecedented. The Passage has operated in the shadows for generations — Rattkin help Rattkin, and the Dry take care of themselves. Nona just broke that wall. She did it because the grief is the same grief, and because she is old enough to be done pretending otherwise.

Last day of La Finestra. Crowd peak. The ground opens. This is the session’s crescendo if the table reaches it — if not, hold for Session 05. Run the raid situation file alongside this page.

DM Note

The Detonation

Timing: mid-morning, maximum crowd density in the festival districts.

Five detonations fire within seconds of each other. The primary charge is the largest — the Mercatura plaza. Four secondary charges hit the Bridge, two points in Le Paludi’s working yards, and the harbour approach.

Tactical Map — Raid Overview

The Primary — Mercatura Plaza

Read Aloud

The sound comes from below. Not thunder — thunder has a sky. This has stone. The Mercatura plaza shudders once, a ripple running through the cobblestones like a wave through water. Then the centre drops. Twenty feet of plaza collapses inward — stone, earth, festival cloth, registration desks, people — falling into a cloud of dust and noise that swallows everything. The crowd does not scream. They are waiting for the punchline.

Then something hauls itself out of the hole.

Hold for one breath. Then —

Read Aloud

It is red. It is enormous. It pulls itself up through rubble and dust on arms too long for its body, a mouth that opens wider than a mouth should, and eyes that are not looking at the crowd the way a person looks at a crowd. It is looking at the crowd the way a fire looks at a building. The Slaad shakes the dust from its back, opens that impossible mouth, and roars.

The screaming starts.

DM Note

The crowd’s first instinct is to freeze — three days of false alarms have conditioned them to wait before reacting. That hesitation buys the Grung three to five seconds. By the time the crowd breaks and runs, the secondary detonations have fired, and the festival’s trained response (“wait for the joke”) has become the city’s worst liability.

The Secondary Sites — Simultaneous

At the four secondary strike points, smaller charges open holes in the ground. No collapse — a breach. Dust, debris, a gap wide enough for Grung to pour through.

Read Aloud

The ground buckles — not a collapse, not here, but the cobblestones crack and a section of yard floor drops two feet. Dust fountains up. From below, shapes — small, fast, disciplined — emerge through the gap and fan out into the crowd. They are not panicking. They know exactly where they are going.

DM Note

At each secondary site: purple-caste raid teams emerge from a spent

Globe of Invulnerability into the chaos. They push the crowd — specifically able-bodied workers, sailors, dockhands — toward a catching force positioned at the perimeter. The catching force binds targets and moves them underground through the breach within two minutes. The operation is fast, silent where it can be, and brutally efficient. Each secondary site runs independently; losing one does not stop the others.

The Slaad — Boss Encounter

The session’s climactic fight if the party reaches Day 5. The Slaad is at the primary breach point in the Mercatura.

Tactical Map — Mercatura Crater

Mechanic

Custom stat block: Otar the Foul. CR 8. AC 15, HP 150 (16d10+64). Speed 40 ft., climb 20 ft. Legendary Resistance (1/Day). Multiattack: Bite (+8, 2d8+5 piercing + DC 15 Con Slaad egg), Claw (+8, 2d6+5 slashing, 10-ft reach), Tongue Lash (+8, 1d8+5, 30-ft reach, DC 16 Str or pulled 25 ft and grappled). Foul Miasma: 10-ft radius, lightly obscured, 1d6 poison to creatures starting turn in it. Entropic Regeneration: 10 HP/round. Suppressed by fire or acid damage. Chaos Pulse (Recharge 5-6): 20-ft radius, DC 15 Dex, 4d10 force + prone. Area becomes difficult terrain. Unstable Form (≤75 HP): Melee attacks deal +1d6 acid; melee attackers within 5 ft take 1d10 acid. Legendary Actions (2/round): Lash (Tongue Lash attack), Thrash (5-ft DC 16 Str or pushed 10 ft + prone), Bile Spray (2 actions, 15-ft cone, DC 15 Con, 3d6 acid). Rubble Surge (reaction): Hurls rubble at a creature moving 15+ ft within 30 ft — DC 15 Dex, 2d10 bludgeoning + speed 0. Hits flyers. Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves vs. spells/magical effects. Resistances: cold, lightning, thunder. Immunities: frightened.

Environment: Collapsed plaza. 20-ft-diameter crater, 10 ft deep. Rubble in 40-ft radius. Festival cloth, broken desks, dust (dim light 2-3 rounds). 2d6 civilians trapped in rubble — Slaad targets them if no PC in reach.

Tactics: The Slaad is not intelligent. It attacks the nearest creature. It does not pursue strategically — it is chaos, not tactics. It uses Tongue Lash to yank ranged attackers (Jean-Claude) into melee. Chaos Pulse punishes clustering. Rubble Surge punishes repositioning and flight (Crissdalynn). It will jump into and out of the crater if pressed.

The tactical key: fire or acid suppresses the 15 HP/round regeneration. The party does not have reliable fire damage by default. Without fire, the fight is a war of attrition they will lose.

DM Note

Fire sourcing. The party needs to find fire or acid. Here’s what’s available in the environment:

  • Festival torch racks at the Mercatura — scattered in the collapse. DC 12 Investigation finds one still burning in the rubble.
  • Giacomo’s oil stock — if Moretti & Sons is near the Mercatura, a crate of chandler’s lamp oil spilled in the blast. DC 14 Investigation to locate, then throw or pour.
  • Overturned vendor cart — a festival alchemist’s cart tipped in the collapse. DC 14 Investigation finds two flasks of alchemist’s fire (2d6 fire, splash) in the wreckage.
  • Ruk — arrives after round 5 if the party is struggling (see scaling below). Carries a lit festival torch and a cleaver. He brings fire; the party doesn’t need to ask.

Reward creative improvisation — canal oil, broken lanterns, cooking fires from a nearby food stall. If the idea is plausible and the player is specific, give it a DC and let it work.

DM Note

The choice the Slaad creates: every round the party fights the Slaad is a round the extraction runs at the secondary sites. After round 3: DC 12 Perception hears screams from the Bridge. After round 5: smoke visible from Le Paludi. The party must decide — stay and kill, or split and save. This is not a punishment — it is a design decision that makes the raid feel like a coordinated operation.

Scaling: this is a Deadly encounter for four Level 4 PCs. The regeneration is the primary threat. If struggling: Ruk arrives after round 5 with a festival torch and a cleaver (2d6+4 slashing + 1d6 fire). He does not speak. He hits the thing. If dominating: the Slaad targets trapped civilians in the rubble, forcing repositioning. Tongue Lash pulls a PC into the crater for a bad position. If the party splits early: the Slaad pursues the nearest target for 2 rounds, then loses interest and attacks civilians.
