# Il Palio delle Voci — DM Notes

Player-facing overview: [[il-palio-delle-voci|Il Palio delle Voci]]

The Palio is a multi-phase skill challenge spanning three in-game nights. The party can enter as performers, but stage crew and crowd work are full contributors — no bard required. The goal is to have the most crowd at midnight on the final night. Rival bands actively disrupt.

## Party Roles

**Performer** *(CHA-primary)*

- Performance (DC varies by phase) — core contribution each phase
- Persuasion — working the crowd between sets; pulling undecided audience
- Bardic Inspiration, Vicious Mockery, Enthrall, etc. — full magical support valid

**Stage Crew** *(DEX/STR/WIS)*

- DEX Acrobatics — rigging dramatic entrances, aerial work, dangerous stage business
- STR Athletics — hauling props, managing pyrotechnics physically, building crowd-visible spectacle
- WIS Perception DC 13 — timing a cue at the exact right moment (advantage to Performer check that phase if successful)
- INT (Arcana or tools) — operating alchemical or mechanical effects; failed check = chaos table roll

**Crowd Work** *(WIS/CHA/INT)*

- Insight DC 12 — read what the crowd wants (success gives Performer +2 to next check)
- Persuasion or Deception — redirect wandering audience
- Deception DC 14 — spread a rumour about a rival band (rival loses 1 success from running total; detectable with Investigation DC 16)

Each party member contributes one role per phase. Non-party recruits contribute a flat +2 to one role's result.

## Phase 1 — La Prova (DC 12)

*First night. Short sets. First impressions.*

**Need:** 2 successes from available roles.

- **Pass:** Establish a crowd base. Rival bands take note.
- **Fail:** Crowd is polite but unconvinced. Party loses the opening Insight bonus (they don't know what this crowd wants yet).

**Rival action:** La Canzone Nera sends a representative to "offer advice" — actually fishing for the party's weakest link. WIS Insight DC 13 to recognise this. If the party shares information, La Canzone Nera counters their Phase 2 approach directly.

## Phase 2 — La Sfida (DC 14)

*Second night. Full sets. Sabotage welcome.*

**Need:** 3 successes from available roles.

Rival disruptions (party can counter one per phase; others land):

- **La Canzone Nera** — bribes the Mercatura stage platform crew. On a failed Stage Crew check, a prop fails or lighting cuts out. DC 15 Investigation to discover who arranged it.
- **Il Vento di Seta** — poaches the best viewing spot on the Velo Quarter bridge, blocking sightlines. Crowd Work DC 14 to counter (redirect via Le Paludi waterfront instead).
- **Le Ossa del Toro** — starts a crowd surge. Cluster of audience rushes toward the waterfront. If unaddressed, party loses 1 success worth of audience automatically. Crowd Work DC 13 to intercept; STR DC 14 to physically redirect the surge.

- **Pass:** +2 to all Phase 3 checks. One rival band is visibly struggling.
- **Fail:** Entering the finale as underdogs. Recoverable — Performer gets one "all-in" option in Phase 3.

## Phase 3 — Il Grande Finale (DC 16)

*Final night. Three hours. Simultaneous.*

**Need:** 3 successes out of 4 possible role checks.

**All-In mechanic:** Once per finale, any party member may declare All-In. They gain advantage, but on a failure suffer a Complication. Can only be used once as a group.

| d6 | Complication |
|---|---|
| 1 | Pyrotechnic misfires — coloured smoke covers the stage; next Performance check at disadvantage |
| 2 | String breaks / instrument goes out of tune — automatic -1 failure this phase |
| 3 | A crowd member climbs on stage and won't leave — managed as bonus action or performer checks at -2 |
| 4 | Rival fan starts a chant drowning out the set — Persuasion DC 15 to shut it down or lose this phase's Crowd Work result |
| 5 | It starts raining — Stage Crew DC 14 or lighting rig fails |
| 6 | Nothing bad happens. The crowd thinks it was intentional. +1 success this phase. |

**Rival band performance (rough tracking):**

- La Canzone Nera: 2 automatic successes per phase (flawless but boring — crowds erode)
- Il Vento di Seta: 2 per phase (consistent)
- Le Ossa del Toro: 1 per phase + bonus 2 in Phase 3 from sheer volume

## Outcome Tiers

| Total Successes | Result | Reward |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 | Respectable showing | Crowd remembers them warmly; no prize; halfling at Ponte Bassa asks if they want to try next year |
| 4–6 | Second place | 100 gp split; a Tessarine scout approaches about a booking (Concordat circuit connection) |
| 7–8 | Third (close) | Crowd respect; Le Ossa del Toro want to buy them a drink |
| 9+ / Win | Palio banner + 300 gp | [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] mentions the party to [[cosimo-verantio|Cosimo Verantio]] as "people worth knowing"; Morsani appears at their stage just before midnight; the crowd knows their name |

## Recruitable NPCs

**Tomasso the Halfling** *(Ponte Bassa most evenings)*
A halfling fiddle player who hustles dockworkers for pocket money. Will join for a 10 gp cut of any prize. Contributes +2 to Performer checks. Has an annoying habit of improvising when he thinks the tempo is wrong — DC 12 Performance from the lead performer each phase to keep him on the arrangement or he goes off-script (which sometimes works: DC 14 Performance or +1 bonus success).

**The Rattkin from the Warren**
Ask Essa Two-Tooth. She will know someone. A young Rattkin plays an instrument nobody in the party can identify — six strings, played horizontally, sounds like two instruments arguing. Contributes +2 to Stage Crew checks (the visual is extremely strange and extremely good). Will not perform on the Mercatura stage due to unspecified prior incident; Velo Quarter or waterfront only.

**Prospero Morsani's Cabinet**
[[prospero-morsani|Morsani]] will not perform. He will, for the right question, lend a single prop from the locked wardrobe cabinet. The prop produces a spectacular visual effect usable once during the Grande Finale — treat as an automatic success on one Stage Crew check. He will not explain what it is beforehand. It will be appropriate. It will be strange.

## Key Facts

- Registration closes three days before La Prova. Committee office is on the Mercatura.
- La Canzone Nera has won three of the last five years. The committee families are bored of them.
- The Velo Quarter crowd is the swing vote; whoever owns that stage going into the Finale has a significant advantage.
- Morsani appearing at a stage just before midnight has predicted the winner correctly for eleven consecutive years. Nobody knows how.

## DM Notes

The Palio works best if the party enters with at least one non-performer. A party with no bard is not at a disadvantage — Stage Crew and Crowd Work contributions are mathematically significant. Tomasso exists specifically to give parties without a charisma class an option.

If the party wins: give them the banner. Put it on their ship eventually. Let NPCs recognise it.

If the party loses honourably: Il Vento di Seta's Tessarine booking agent approaches anyway. "Not a win, but the crowd noticed you." This opens the same Concordat connection at half value.

Le Ossa del Toro will invite the party to play a joint set if they lose. No stakes, no crowd, just because they liked watching them fight for it.

# Calveno — Warren, Salvage, and Ship Disguise

## Situation

[[calveno|Calveno]] is useful because Perrin can reach the [[warren|Warren]] here and the party can disguise the [[hcs-surety|HCS Surety]] without using a public dry dock. It is dangerous because the same city is under Tessarine debt pressure, watched by commercial ledgers, and quietly assembling a salvage commission aimed at Delmar's *Red Lady*.

---

## Current State

The Seven Houses are locked four-to-three over Tessarine terms. [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] holds debt leverage over six Houses, making the holdout faction more interesting than the formal majority. Separately, unusual money is moving through the broker network toward the Maw; the Warren has noticed enough to know a *Red Lady* salvage commission is forming, but not who is behind it.

For the *Surety*, Calveno has no usable public dry dock. The Arsenal queue is fourteen months and paperwork-heavy. The practical option is a Warren-routed job through [[savia-brentino|Savia Brentino]] at the [[carpenters-slip|Carpenters' Slip]], with compounds from [[studio-orsini|Studio Orsini]] and an outer anchorage that avoids Canal Commission records.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Records. Calveno turns every favour, debt, arrival, and cargo movement into leverage. |
| Unstable Condition | The party needs Warren help while the Warren is already tracking suspicious salvage money and Passage exposure. |
| Consequence | The *Surety* can be de-marked, but Perrin incurs Tangle debt and Delmar may walk into the salvage operation targeting his own wreck. |
| Link of Relevance | Perrin's family credit opens the route; Delmar's ship is the target; Tessarine ledgers make even quiet work observable later. |

---

## The Work

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Location | Southwest approach anchorage, outside Arsenal fortified canal |
| Access | Warren introduction through Perrin; cold approach to Savia fails |
| Timeline | 1 day assessment + 4 days work |
| Cost | ~180 gp labour + 40 gp Studio Orsini compounds |
| Paper trail | No Canal Commission filing; Tangle keeps its own record |

Changes: hull coating, nameboards, pennant removal. Does not change: cutter silhouette. Savia says once: *"She'll still read as a cutter to anyone who knows cutters. That's not a paint problem."*

### Savia's Line

Savia does not do cosmetic work. The correct frame is maintenance: hull recoating, damaged nameboards, bow fittings assessment. She understands the real purpose and will do the job if the Warren routes it, but she will not call it disguise work and neither should the party.

She refuses the bow registry plate: *"Not structural."* The party removes it themselves.

### False Papers

The Calveno Passage broker network can produce a false home port, vessel name, and owner-of-record in two days for 60 gp, routed through the Warren. The papers are clean. The Tangle keeps a copy.

---

## Key Facts

- Savia Brentino will not take a cold illegal-looking job; a Warren introduction changes the shape of the request.
- Savia frames the work as maintenance, not cosmetic disguise, and refuses to touch the bow registry plate.
- The Tangle does not charge coin for this kind of routing. It records a favour.
- Tessarine factors do not need to care about the *Surety* specifically to notice a cutter-class vessel changing appearance outside the Arsenal.

---

## Involved Parties

- [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] — can access the Warren; spends family/network credit
- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — tied to the *Red Lady* salvage target
- [[warren|The Warren]] / the Tangle — routes the job and keeps a copy of any papers
- [[savia-brentino|Savia Brentino]] — Carpenters' Slip operator; structural work only, no official filings on quick jobs
- [[marta-orsini|Marta Orsini]] — supplies paint stripper and pigment compounds from Studio Orsini
- [[batta-zusto|Batta Zusto]] — Bridge intermediary for the hidden salvage money
- [[iacopo-fieschi|Iacopo Fieschi]] — Tessarine envoy with House debt leverage

---

## Timeline

- This month: three ships ask Savia about discreet work; she refuses and remembers.
- Day 1: Perrin contacts the Warren; Tangle decides whether to route the job.
- Day 2: Studio Orsini compounds are picked up; stripper begins working on naval grey.
- Days 3–6: Savia and two workers recoat hull, replace nameboards, and assess fittings.
- Later: the Tangle calls in the favour on its own timing.

---

## Triggers

- Perrin asks the Warren for help disguising the *Surety*
- Delmar investigates the *Red Lady* salvage money or appears near the wrong broker
- The party cold-approaches Savia and becomes the fourth suspicious vessel inquiry
- [[estratto|Estratto]] (Tessarine auditor) notes the cutter-class vessel at the outer anchorage and begins identity verification

---

## Consequences

- **Clean Warren route:** *Surety* leaves de-marked, with Tangle debt and possible false papers
- **Cold approach:** Savia refuses and remembers the party; the list of suspicious vessels grows
- **Tessarine notice:** the work becomes a ledger detail that may surface later
- **Salvage thread engaged:** [[red-lady-salvage-money|Red Lady — Salvage Money]] connects the party to the *Red Lady* commission before they are ready

---

## Open Questions

- Who is ultimately funding the *Red Lady* salvage commission?
- What job will the Tangle route back through Perrin as payment?
- What false vessel name and home port can survive inspection?

## Situation

Formal debrief received. Surviving counts. The pilgrimage is not formally complete. The missing Sentinels have not yet been asked about.

---

## Key Actors

- [[crissdalynn-khinriss|Crissdalynn Khinriss]] — sole survivor of the *Red Lady* alongside Fisk; pilgrimage task incomplete; wants back in
- [[master-kyzil|Master Kyzil]] — gray-ash feathers; senior master; assigned the pilgrimage; found Crissdalynn in Calveno; has news about two missing Sentinels he has not yet shared
- [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]] — holds 200 years of Maw observation records; non-interference doctrine; currently in an anomaly period with no historical precedent; two Sentinels missing

---

## Current State

Kyzil found Crissdalynn in Calveno. He arrived from the east, spotted her from height, and made contact. Formal account received — he heard the account of the Maw and the storm. He confirmed that surviving the Maw interior counts. He delivered the High Eyrie weather warning. He stopped himself before asking about the missing Sentinels — wants the anomaly records alongside her account before he asks that question. The pilgrimage is not formally complete. He asked to meet again tomorrow.

The two missing Sentinels have not returned. The current anomaly period exceeds the 200-year observation record.

---

## High Eyrie Weather Warning (Delivered)

> *Storms forming without pressure lines. Abnormal wreck patterns. Wind shear breaking Maw-side approach. Turbulence pushing into the Central Strait. Returning to the Eyrie from either the Maw side or the Central Strait is now difficult and dangerous.*

---

## What Advances It

- Crissdalynn meeting with Kyzil again — what he tells her about the missing Sentinels changes the scope of the pilgrimage
- The party learning what happened to the two missing Sentinels
- Crissdalynn sharing what she observed during the sinking — her account of the Maw, the storm, and what she heard
- Any High Eyrie observation record that correlates with known Maw events (Leviathan arrival, fissure widening)
- The party bringing firsthand Maw experience that unlocks the 6-day fissure cycle in the Eyrie data

## What Blocks It

- The pilgrimage is incomplete by the High Eyrie's standard — "I survived the sinking" is not the same as "I mapped the Maw from inside a storm"
- The non-interference doctrine creates tension with what the party is doing — the Eyrie observes; it does not act
- Two Sentinels missing implies a threat the Eyrie is not handling publicly

---

## Master Kyzil — DM Notes

**Active problem:** Not sure Crissdalynn will consider this pilgrimage — which nearly took her life — complete. Has confirmed surviving counts, but hasn't asked the question directly yet.

**Goal:** Hear the full account of the Maw, test her skills, share what he knows about the missing Sentinels in the right order.

**Voice:** Owl Obi-Wan trying to recover dignity after an uncharacteristic relief hug. Questions first, answers second. Wind and tide metaphors. Minimal, precise movement; often unsettlingly quiet.

**Key lines:** *"Who told you surviving does not count?"* / *"Who were you when you entered the storm, and who came back?"*

**Context:** Masters dispersed Sentinels away from the Eyrie peak as Maw conditions worsened. Kyzil was away when the *Red Lady* went down; tracked Crissdalynn by current and weather patterns.

**Calveno entry (already happened):** Kyzil spotted Crissdalynn from high above the city and dived in on silent barn owl wings, using the sun as cover. He hit her with a hug hard enough to scrape talons on stone, then straightened into formal master-mode. Formal account received. Challenge to a nonlethal four-on-one spar still possible.

**Read the Current (optional lesson):** Kyzil can teach Crissdalynn this Kensei technique — spends existing ki/focus on a hit to learn combat-readable information about a target.

---

Info earned through attention, not access. A visitor expects answers; receives a ledger. The training terrace turns conversation into a balance test. Masters ask what the character recorded, not what they think. The record contains the key pattern only if the party brings the right context — their own firsthand Maw experience unlocks a 6-day fissure cycle in the data.

# Governor's Seat — Voss and the Sealed Orders

## Situation

Governor Aldric Voss, 7 years in post at [[port-tidefall|Port Tidefall]], is boxed out of his own fort. Six weeks ago two extra companies arrived under sealed Admiralty orders he was not given. He sent three requests for clarification to the Admiralty — none answered. He is willing to trade access and information for Admiralty-level leverage: specifically, someone who can explain what is being staged from his port.

---

## Current State

The sealed orders remain in [[fort-crestwall|Fort Crestwall]] under the Commandant's lock. The supply manifest includes reef-diving equipment and underwater charges — destination: [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]]. The orders are routed through the Maw Surveillance Directorate, a body with no official charter Voss can find.

**Delmar Fisk's Admiral name is still in the guard rotation** — gate officer Crowe never updated it. The door opens on his name alone.

---

## What Voss Can Provide

In exchange for Admiralty-level leverage or intelligence:

- Name of the officer who delivered the sealed orders
- Supply manifest addendum (reef-diving equipment, underwater charges — destination: Drowned Maw)
- A letter of introduction that functions as a [[fort-crestwall|Fort Crestwall]] pass

---

## DC Gates

- DC 13 Persuasion: get the manifest addendum without full quid pro quo
- DC 16 Deception: bluff past guards without using Fisk's name

---

## DM Notes

Voss is not hostile — he is frustrated and outmaneuvered. He represents the institutional Crown that bureaucracy has left behind. A party that treats him as a trade partner rather than an obstacle will find him cooperative.

The Maw Surveillance Directorate is the lead worth pulling on. It has no official charter Voss can find — which means it is either very new, very classified, or operating under a different authority structure than the Admiralty he knows.

---

# Jean-Claude — Grung Expansion

## Situation

[[simone-tabarnack|Simone Tabarnack]] is actively looking for Jean-Claude as part of a broader Grung expansion she is architecting. Jean-Claude knows the Grung slave system from the handler side, ran from it, and does not yet understand how far Simone's reach has extended.

---

## Current State

Blue-caste scouts have reached outer Midchain waters under trade cover, farther than the Grung have operated in years. One raid hit a small coastal settlement; a second overextended and failed. Rumour of unusually distant Grung raids is moving through fishing communities.

Simone does not know Jean-Claude's location. She knows he is alive and outside the Verdant Teeth. Rook was her buyer for Grung hunting toxin into the Central Strait; with Rook gone silent, her operative asked the wrong questions in Tidefall and **exposed the supply channel at one end.** [[verity-hollowell|Verity Hollowell]] is positioned to hear the wrong-shaped inquiry.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Hunts. Simone expands territory and searches for the deserter who understands the system's failure points. |
| Unstable Condition | The slave-soldier program is tactically useful but breaking down faster than Karath can replace captives. The Calveno raid is the operation that fills the gap — and proves Simone can reach anywhere. |
| Consequence | Grung raids push closer, Tidefall suspicion rises, and Jean-Claude's past becomes an active operational liability. After Calveno, it becomes a personal indictment: he understands everything that was done, and he was in the city when it happened. |
| Link of Relevance | Jean-Claude's terminal node is Sorn: Simone, Pell, the Botukuri household, and the slave system concentrate there. Calveno is the moment the distance between him and that node collapses. |

---

## Narrative Devices

- **Loaded Gun:** Simone's Rook toxin channel is burned at Tidefall; Verity Hollowell is positioned to hear the wrong-shaped inquiry.
- **Foreshadowing:** Sideways looks at Felix Aho's stall, distant raid rumours, blue-caste scouts under trade cover.
- **Clock:** Each world tick can move the scout circuit closer or force Simone to accelerate because the slave-soldier math is failing.
- **Reversal Potential:** The Vaka know Gold-caste divisions; the Grung order is less unified than it looks from below.

---

## Key Facts

- Simone is gold-marked and commands as expansion warlord under pure-gold leadership.
- She is looking for Jean-Claude as an operational loose end, not family sentiment.
- Karath has six confirmed *vethka* hulls on the expanded raid circuit, each carrying fourteen crew and four tons of captive cargo.
- Slave soldiers are breaking down and sometimes turning on handlers mid-raid.
- Jean-Claude understands the program's failure point because he ran slave-handling operations on Sorn before deserting.
- The Calveno raid uses Dravosi patrol gaps, sewer extraction routes, and summoned Slaad as a distraction. This is what Simone built the western supply chain to fund.

A nervous fisherman at the Flat Water knows where the Bad Receipt stashed nine crates of prize cargo on a nameless rock 3 miles east — and the Bad Receipt's captain is on the causeways today, asking the same question.

# Kalowe — The Bad Receipt's Cache

## Situation

Two seasons ago, [[the-bad-receipt|the Bad Receipt]] took a prize in the Central Strait and offloaded nine crates on a nameless limestone shelf 3 miles east-southeast of the Kalowe gap while the heat died down. The pilot who led them there died four months later of fever in Veth. Captain Orina Fale has been operating without being able to collect the cache for eight months — nobody else aboard knew the exact rock.

A fisherman named Damu saw them anchor there.

He has been nursing an ale at [[the-flat-water|The Flat Water]] for three days, working up to selling the location. [[reweti-kahurangi|Reweti Kahurangi]] has noticed but says nothing.

The Bad Receipt sailed into Kalowe this morning. Fale is on the second causeway with two crew, quietly asking harbour workers about the dead pilot's last job.

## Current State

**Damu** is at The Flat Water, second table from the terrace, visibly nervous. If the party looks capable and unaffiliated with any crew Reweti has reason to distrust, she will catch their eye and nod toward him. He will sell the rock's precise location — including a traced copy of his chart — for 50 gp. He wants coin, not a cut.

**Orina Fale** is not offering money yet. She will.

## The Tidal Clock

- **Move that day:** 12-hour head start on the Bad Receipt; easy pickup
- **Wait until morning:** Fale has narrowed it to the eastern approaches; she arrives 4 hours after the party
- **Wait two days:** Fale finds the rock herself; cache is gone

## The Rock

Flat limestone shelf, 60 ft wide, barely above waterline at mean tide. Single wind-bent palm; notch on eastern face where the Bad Receipt tied off. The nine crates are on the eastern face behind a natural rock shelf — covered with salvaged canvas and weighted stones. No guardians, no traps. Anyone who lands and looks will find them in 5 minutes.

## Cargo

| Crates | Contents | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Spice (pepper, nutmeg, clove) | 300 gp wholesale |
| 3 | Undyed trade cloth | 200 gp wholesale |
| 3 (sealed) | Silver plate tableware, Dravosi merchant mark | 300–350 gp |
| **Gross** | | **800 gp** |

*One of the sealed silver plate crates contains an engraved service with a noble house seal — worth 200 gp to the right buyer, or trouble if the wrong people recognise it.*

**Selling options:**

- [[taufa-fifita-and-sons|Taufa Fifita & Sons]]: 720 gp (10% cut, no questions, 2-day wait)
- Harbour direct: 680 gp (faster, fewer buyers)
- Silver plate sold elsewhere: 350 gp for those 3 crates at any non-Dravosi port

## If the Bad Receipt Arrives During Loading

Fale carries 8 crew + a swivel gun (1d10 bludgeoning, 1/round). She will not fire — she wants the cargo undamaged. She will hail and demand answers. She is a businesswoman, not a murderer; violence is expensive. If the party is armed and already has most of the cargo, she will negotiate.

*Negotiated split:* She trades the spice and cloth for the silver plate + 100 gp. Party nets ~500 gp + she respects them.
*Party refuses:* She leaves, makes a note, remembers.
*Party fights at sea:* Eight crew + swivel gun vs. the party on an open rock with no cover.

## Orina Fale

Captain of the Bad Receipt. Midchain mixed heritage, forties, sharp-featured, always dressed well for a pirate. Runs on business logic. Respects people who make sensible decisions under pressure.

## Consequences

| Outcome | Result |
|---|---|
| Party moves fast | 670 gp net; no confrontation; Damu is fine |
| Fale arrives during loading | Negotiated split; ~500 gp; Fale respects them |
| Party waits two days | Cache gone; Damu got paid for nothing |
| Party sells Damu's info to Fale | Fale pays 80 gp; Damu learns within a week and doesn't forget |

## Triggers

- Party asks Reweti about work, news, or local opportunities
- Party is at The Flat Water long enough for Reweti to read them as capable → she nods toward Damu
- Party notices the Bad Receipt in the harbour and asks who she belongs to

## Open Questions

- Does the party want a working relationship with Orina Fale? She is a useful Midchain contact.
- Does anyone investigate the noble house seal on the engraved service?

A dying privateer at Grimaldi's Dispensary has half a treasure chart tattooed on her forearm — the other half burned. The cache is on Orak: 800gp in old Imperial coin and matched silver, buried in a tidal sea cave with a 3-hour window and a constrictor snake.

# Kalowe — The Captain's Map

## Situation

[[sera-maddock|Sera Maddock]], 71, three days from dead by [[ilaria-grimaldi|Ilaria Grimaldi]]'s estimate, is in the dispensary's back room on a charitable arrangement neither discusses out loud. She was a privateer on Dravosi-licensed runs forty years ago. Her crew buried a cache on [[orak|Orak]] and she is the last survivor who knows where.

Half the chart is tattooed on her left forearm — eastern face of Orak, compass bearing 087° from the southeastern rock stack, cache depth in fathoms. She burned the other half when the man she was going to share it with tried to sell her to the Crown.

**Her deal:** 200 gp and passage out of Kalowe (not to Tidefall — she wants a healer city). The tattoo half is enough to find it.

## Current State

Sera has been in the dispensary four days. Grimaldi mentioned the tattoo to the party unprompted (unusual forearm tattoo, patient in the back). She will arrange an introduction only if she thinks the party will honour the deal.

**Sera's clock:** lung sickness — treatable in Tidefall, not here. She is not in pain but is slow and short of breath and aware she is on a clock.

## What Sera Will Tell

- Cache is at bearing 087° from the rock stack at Orak's southeastern tip — eastern face, sea cave entrance
- Entrance is at waterline at mid-tide; walkable at low tide; 8 feet under at high tide
- Cache is 6 feet under a flat stone, 40 feet into the cave interior
- There is "some kind of animal" in the cave — she hasn't been there in 40 years

## What Sera Won't Say

- Full cache: 800 gp old Imperial coin (collector value 1,000 gp to [[algernon-reginald-clyde|Algernon Clyde]]) + matched silver earrings and bracelet, 180 gp
- The cave floods to the ceiling at full high tide — 3-hour window around low tide
- The cave animal was, 40 years ago, a giant constrictor snake; she assumes it's dead

## Orak: The Cave

- 2-hour sail east-southeast of Kalowe; small, low, overgrown; paired with [[dreth|Dreth]] across a narrow channel
- Entrance: 60 ft deep, 20 ft wide, narrows to 10 ft inside
- High tide floods the cave to the ceiling — water rises 1 foot every 10 minutes; at 2 hours the entrance is waist-deep; at 3 hours, neck-deep
- The dig: 20 minutes with tools, 40 without; flat stone 40 ft in, 2×3 ft, flush, unmarked

### Encounter 1: Giant Crabs ×4 (CR 1/8)

Tidal zone colonists. Scatter from torchlight but will attack if the party blocks the exit. HP 13, AC 15, Claw +3 / 1d6+1 bludgeoning. Nuisance, not threat.

### Encounter 2: Giant Constrictor Snake ×1 (CR 2)

Interior past the 30 ft mark. Not aggressive unless cornered or the party makes noise near its nest. HP 60, AC 12, Bite +5 / 2d6+4 piercing + grapple, Constrict +5 / 2d8+4 bludgeoning + restrained (escape DC 16).

*Torch behaviour:* DC 11 Animal Handling to keep it at bay while backing away; on failure it strikes.

## Cache Loot

| Item | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Old Imperial coin | 800–1,000 gp | Face: 800 gp; collector's value to Algernon Clyde: 1,000 gp |
| Matched silver earrings + bracelet | 180 gp | Pre-Imperial, distinctive maker's mark |
| Sera's fee | −200 gp | Passage + coin |
| **Net (standard sale)** | **780 gp** | Up to 980 gp selling coin to Clyde |

## Consequences

- **Honour the deal:** 780–980 gp net; Sera gets passage and treatment; Grimaldi satisfied; Clyde delighted if in port
- **Betray Sera (take info, abandon her):** Grimaldi will not deal with them again; harbour bosses hear within a day
- **Go to Orak without Sera's bearing:** Seven cave entrances on the eastern face — no bearing, no cache

## Triggers

- Party buys supplies from Grimaldi and she mentions the patient with the tattoo (already done)
- Party follows up on the patient; Grimaldi arranges introduction if she trusts them
- Party asks around Kalowe about old privateers or eastern reef islands

## Open Questions

- Does the party take Sera anywhere, or pay her and leave her?
- Does Algernon Clyde buy the coin? He'll be excited about the provenance.
- The party is currently in Calveno (5-day dry dock). Sera has three days. Does the window close before they return?

# Kalowe — The Drifting Hulk

## Situation

The *Pale Covenant*, a two-masted trading schooner, has been drifting 4 miles north-northeast of the Kalowe gap for two nights. No lights. No answer to hails. Under Midchain free-port custom, the first boarding party to establish presence and bring cargo to port holds salvage rights — the harbour bosses will record the claim and take 10%.

The *Pale Covenant*'s captain, Orlen Vass, died still owing eighteen months of unpaid [[umberlee|Umberlee]] tithe — a deliberate public snub. The entire crew of nine went down with him. Their shadows and his specter now inhabit the ship and will not leave it.

## Current State

Word reached the causeway by the morning market. Two other crews in Kalowe are aware of it and considering whether to try. The party has a narrow window — probably until the next morning.

**What [[suryo-wibowo|Suryo Wibowo]] knows:** The salt merchant who spotted her came through for provisions yesterday. Green stripe, ochre hull, open hatch amidships. Smelled strange even from a distance — old copper and wet stone. He did not board.

**What the [[kalowe-waveservant-shrine|Waveservant shrine]] knows:** Brother Tamoa recognises the *Pale Covenant* from the ledger — Orlen Vass, tithe balance outstanding. He will tell the party the tithe status if they describe the colours. He can also perform a consecration ritual (10gp incense + saltwater into the basin) that suppresses the specters for 1 hour from boarding — enough to load the hold.

**What the party doesn't know:**

- The crew were killed by specters and their own undead shadows within hours of Vass dying
- The captain's specter is anchored to the wheel and cannot move from the helm deck
- Permanent resolution: pay the tithe posthumously, or destroy the wheel (AC 15, 20hp; the specter fights to prevent this)

## Key Facts

- Cargo: mixed spice, undyed cloth, 3 sealed crates of silver plate tableware — ~1,000gp total
- After 10% harbour fee + 10% [[taufa-fifita-and-sons|Taufa Fifita & Sons]] cut: ~810gp net
- Ship herself is intact and seaworthy — 60-ton trading schooner, prize value ~4,000gp; fast-sale in Kalowe: ~2,400gp
- The tithe shortcut: 54gp covers the outstanding 18 months; any Waveservant can receive a posthumous payment

## DM Notes

**Aboard the *Pale Covenant*:**

- Below decks: **4 Shadows (CR 1/2)** — haunt the cargo hold and crew quarters; emerge on any light source entering the hold. HP 16, AC 12, Strength Drain (hit + DC 13 Con save or -1d4 Str; 0 Str = new shadow). Resist most damage; immune to exhaustion/frightened/grappled; vulnerable to radiant. In dim light they attack with advantage — *the hold is dim.*
- Helm deck: **1 Specter (CR 1)** (Captain Orlen Vass) — anchored to the wheel, cannot be driven off, only destroyed or appeased. HP 22, AC 12, Life Drain +4 / 3d6 necrotic (DC 13 Con or max HP reduced until long rest). Says nothing except *"Pay what you owe"* on repeat, directed at nobody visible.

*If the party brought torches:* the hold becomes bright; shadows lose advantage and attack immediately rather than lurking.

**The tithe shortcut:** 54gp, handed to Tamoa at the shrine. Once paid, all specters dissolve without a fight; shadows dissipate 1d6 rounds later, one at a time. Cleanest resolution. Tamoa remembers the favour — future shrine services at half price.

**The consecration shortcut:** 10gp ritual from Tamoa before boarding. Suppresses undead for 1 hour. Tight for loading cargo but doable.

**Captain's cabin (unlocked):** logbook showing the tithe dispute, silver compass worth 120gp (engraved *OV*), letter from a factor in Tidefall expecting the silver plate delivery.

## Loot

| Item | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Spice (cargo) | 400 gp | Fifita takes 10% |
| Undyed cloth, bales | 300 gp | Same |
| Silver plate tableware, 3 crates | 300 gp | Factor in Tidefall is expecting this |
| Captain's silver compass | 120 gp | Non-magical; beautiful; engraved *OV* |
| **Net (sell all via Taufa)** | **~810 gp** | After harbour fee + Fifita cut |
| *Pale Covenant* (prize) | 2,400–4,000 gp | 2,400 fast-sale; 4,000 at Tidefall; needs crew of 6 |

## Triggers

- Party asks [[suryo-wibowo|Suryo]] about news, provisioning runs, or work
- Party notices causeway talk about the abandoned ship and asks a harbour worker

## Consequences

- **Party boards and clears it:** 810gp cargo + possible prize ship; known at Kalowe as effective operators
- **Party uses the tithe shortcut:** costs 54gp, saves the fight; Brother Tamoa remembers the favour
- **Another crew gets there first:** cargo is gone; if they didn't know about the tithe, they come back short two sailors and badly shaken

## Open Questions

- Does the party take the cargo or the whole ship?
- Do they report the tithe situation to Tamoa, or just loot and leave?

A sunken merchant ship 2 miles off the Kalowe reef holds a sealed strongbox; the only survivor wants the party to dive for it, and a merrow has already moved in.

# Kalowe — The Merrow's Prize

## Situation

The *Cormorant*, a small merchant sloop, went down three months ago on the reef shelf southwest of the Kalowe gap after her pilot misjudged the channel at night. The captain's strongbox — 600gp in mixed coin and a pair of matched rubies — sank with her. Her first mate, [[davu-kamu|Davu Kamu]], survived and has been drinking at [[the-flat-water|The Flat Water]] ever since, trying to find anyone willing to dive for it. The wreck is 30 feet down. A [[sawek|merrow]] has since claimed the hull as a den and dragged the strongbox into the grotto it made under the collapsed stern.

## Current State

Davu is two months past his savings and offering 30% of whatever is recovered — which he cannot actually guarantee, since the money isn't his to split; the captain's widow in Tidefall has a claim. He has not mentioned this. He knows the dive location within 200 yards, has the strongbox key, and knows there was something large living in the wreck the last time a hired diver got close and came back empty-handed.

**What the party knows (if they talk to Davu):**

- Sunken sloop, 2 miles southwest, reef shelf, ~30ft
- 600gp in a locked iron strongbox (he has the key)
- 30% cut (180gp + rubies, which he'll value at 60gp — they're worth 90gp each)
- "Something in the wreck" — big, pale, wrong-shaped

**What the party doesn't know:**

- The merrow has reinforced the grotto with salvaged chain and hull planking
- Two [[hunter-shark|hunter sharks]] patrol the outer reef — not in the grotto, but will investigate noise and blood
- The rubies are worth 180gp total, not 60gp; Davu is underselling in case he can buy them back later

## Key Facts

- The *Cormorant* sank 3 months ago; 30ft down on a sandy reef shelf, listing badly to starboard
- Merrow lair under the collapsed stern — tight quarters, 10ft ceiling, poor visibility
- Hunter sharks patrol the reef approach; can be avoided with quiet movement (Stealth DC 12 underwater, disadvantage without Swim speed)
- Davu's key opens the strongbox; lock can also be picked (DC 14 Thieves' Tools, underwater disadvantage applies)

## DM Notes

**[[davu-kamu|Davu Kamu]]** — Midchain mixed heritage, late thirties, former first mate. Drinks steadily rather than heavily; talks in the careful way of someone who knows he is leaving things out. If the party agrees to the job, he insists on coming along in a boat to navigate but will not enter the water. If they discover the rubies' real value and confront him, he admits it without much shame: *"I needed someone to say yes."*

**The wreck approach:**

- Small boat or swimming — Davu can borrow a dinghy from the Fifita family quay for 2sp
- Visibility underwater: 30 feet in open water; 10 feet near the wreck (silt disturbed by the merrow's movement)
- Athletics DC 12 to swim to depth without a Swim speed; failure costs a turn, not drowning (yet)

**The merrow:**
It has built a proper den. Bones of previous prey are stacked at the grotto entrance — hard to miss. It attacks the moment anything enters the grotto. HP 45, AC 13, Spear +6 to hit / 2d6+4 piercing, Claws +6 / 2d6+4 slashing, 40ft swim speed.

*If the party kills the merrow outside the grotto* (baiting with blood or noise), they can enter freely.

**The hunter sharks:**
They become interested when blood enters the water. Roll a d6 at the start of each round after blood appears: on a 4+, one shark investigates. Two sharks total; circle and attack anyone wounded. This is a pressure mechanic, not a second encounter — driven off by DC 13 Animal Handling or by leaving the water quickly.

## Loot

| Item | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mixed coin (strongbox) | 600 gp | Davu's 70% cut is 420gp; party's 30% is 180gp |
| Matched rubies (pair) | 180 gp total | Davu claims 60gp; real value 90gp each |
| *Cormorant*'s spyglass | 50 gp | Still functional; waterlogged leather case |
| Bolt of indigo silk | 80 gp | Salvage from the hold; heavy, awkward to carry |

If party negotiates a better cut (DC 14 Persuasion with leverage about the sharks/merrow): Davu goes to 40% (240gp + rubies).

## Triggers

- Party talks to [[reweti-kahurangi|Reweti Kahurangi]] about new work, or sits near Davu long enough for him to make his pitch
- Party asks anyone in port about local salvage opportunities

## Consequences

- **Party succeeds:** 180–600gp depending on cut negotiated, the spyglass, possibly the silk. Davu buys them a round and disappears within two days.
- **Party ignores it:** The merrow expands its territory; kills a diver from another crew within the month. The wreck becomes a local hazard warning.
- **Party kills the merrow but leaves the box:** The strongbox is openly salvageable — another crew gets it within a week.

## Open Questions

- Does the party tell Davu about the rubies' real value?
- Does anyone contact the captain's widow in Tidefall about the legal claim?

# Kalowe — The Sawek Bounty

## Situation

A [[sawek|Sawek]] has settled into the blue hole at the base of the channel between Kalowe's second and third limestone islands — the same passage inter-island skiffs use at night. Three fishing boats have been hit in the last two weeks. One man is dead. The harbour bosses are offering 300gp for proof of kill: the distinctive bony ridge-plate from the creature's forehead.

## Current State

The Sawek is well-fed and territorial. It attacked the first boat that passed over its hole and now treats the channel as its hunting ground. Fishermen have stopped using it; dry-dock workers are adding an hour to every material run between the second and third islands.

**[[kettil-ormsson|Kettil Ormsson]] at [[ormssons-fittings|Ormsson's Fittings]]** has a cracked keel plank from one of the damaged boats propped outside — repairing it as a favour. Will mention the Sawek without drama if asked about local trouble.

**[[ilaria-grimaldi|Ilaria Grimaldi]] at [[grimaldis-dispensary|Grimaldi's Dispensary]]** treated the survivor from the fatal attack. She can describe the attack pattern: the Sawek came up from directly below, seized the hull with its tentacles, pulled the boat partially under, then lost interest when it broke apart. The man who died went into the water.

**The harbour bosses** pay on sight of the ridge-plate. No witnesses required.

## Key Facts

- The blue hole is 20 feet deep at the base; the channel above is 40 feet wide, 15 feet deep at high water
- The Sawek patrols the channel 2–3 hours after dark, returns to the hole after 1–2 hours
- Its lair has accumulated debris: coin, gear, and one specific piece of cargo it has been sitting on
- Ridge-plate: wedge of dense bone, cream-coloured, about 18 inches across — harvested by removing the top of the skull post-mortem (10 minutes, cutting tool)

## DM Notes

**[[sawek|The Sawek (CR 5)]]:** HP 95, AC 14 (natural), swim 40ft, land 5ft. Tentacle attacks grapple on hit (escape DC 14). Ink cloud reaction (20ft heavily obscured, recharge on surfacing). Sunlight sensitivity — disadvantage on attacks and Perception in direct sunlight.

*Don't fight it underwater.* In its hole: 40ft swim speed, cover from channel walls, ink cloud makes retreat lethal. The party should surface the fight.

**The bait approach (recommended):** [[wibowos-provisions|Wibowo's Provisions]] sells offal — 1sp creates a blood trail. The Sawek investigates in 1d6+2 rounds. Fight at the waterline: half its body above water, half below. It can still grab the boat (grapple on hit, DC 14 Str/round to break free; failure = pulled 10ft toward the hole).

**The trap approach:** The channel narrows to 20 feet 60 yards north of the blue hole. Chain across at depth (available from Ormsson's Fittings, 5sp/ft) fouled against both walls — Sawek makes DC 13 Dex save or tentacles restrained (no tentacle attacks; uses action to attempt DC 16 Str, 2 tries/round). Removes its grapple attack.

**The lair (post-kill):** Visibility nil without light. Floor holds:

- 6 weeks of accumulated debris from passing boats
- A sealed iron box it sank two weeks before settling here — contains dry-stored pilot charts for the eastern reef channels (60gp standard; 90gp to [[algernon-reginald-clyde|Algernon Reginald Clyde]] if he's in port)
- 185gp in mixed coin, gritty with silt
- A gold chain with a Midchain trading house seal pendant — belongs to a merchant missing since last season; his family in Veth would pay 50gp reward (nobody in Kalowe knows whose it is without investigation)

## Loot

| Item | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Harbour bounty (ridge-plate) | 300 gp | Paid by harbour bosses; immediate |
| Mixed coin (lair floor) | 185 gp | Takes 30 min to sift |
| Pilot charts, eastern reefs | 60–90 gp | 90gp from Clyde; 60gp from any chart buyer |
| Gold chain with seal pendant | 150 gp | 50gp reward from Veth family OR 100gp melt value |
| **Total (sell everything)** | **~735 gp** | Before costs (chain, bait, etc.) |

## Triggers

- Party asks Kettil about what happened to the boat outside his shop
- Party asks Grimaldi about recent injuries
- Party asks at harbour offices about local hazards or open contracts

## Consequences

- **Party kills it:** 735gp total, harbour bosses grateful, inter-island channel reopens — dry-dock crew will remember this
- **Party avoids it:** The Sawek kills again within two weeks; harbour bosses quietly double the bounty to 500gp
- **Party dragged under:** Drowning rules apply; the Sawek drags grappled creatures to the blue hole floor (20ft/round while failing to escape)

## Open Questions

- Does the party return the merchant's gold chain to Veth for the reward, or sell it?
- Does anyone want the remaining body parts? (Teeth, ink sacs, tentacle segments: 40gp to an alchemist)

Removes its grapple attack.

  • A sealed iron box it sank two weeks before settling here — contains dry-stored pilot charts for the eastern reef channels (60gp standard; 90gp to Algernon Reginald Clyde if he’s in port)
  • 185gp in mixed coin, gritty with silt
  • A gold chain with a Midchain trading house seal pendant — belongs to a merchant missing since last season; his family in Veth would pay 50gp reward (nobody in Kalowe knows whose it is without investigation)

# Kalowe — Takowan and Ship Disguise

## Situation

The *Takowan*, a Dravosi intelligence vessel, has overstayed Kalowe's primary dry dock for eleven days on a three-day repair claim. It is not being repaired — its shore parties are mapping Passage contact names on the causeways. Kalowe is also the best Midchain option for disguising the stolen *[[uncertainty|Uncertainty]]*, but the only safe work route runs through Perrin's Passage node while the *Takowan* is watching.

---

## Current State

The *Takowan* is about two-thirds through its survey. If it finishes, Kalowe's unregistered traffic becomes legible to the Crown and courtesy stops begin within the season. **[[noa-fifita|Noa Fifita]]** can repaint and de-identify the *Uncertainty* in a back-channel slip between the second and third limestone islands, but he will not work while the *Takowan* is in port.

The party's practical choice: burn risk into Perrin's contact network now, delay until the *Takowan* leaves, force the ship to depart, or use Calveno's Warren-routed option instead.

*(Note: the Calveno refit at [[la-vasca|La Vasca]] may have already addressed some of this — check current ship identity status before running this situation.)*

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Watches. Everything through the reef gap gets noted by someone. |
| Unstable Condition | The *Takowan* is mapping Passage contacts faster than Kalowe can pretend nothing is happening. |
| Consequence | If the survey completes, Kalowe stops being a safe harbour for Passage traffic and anyone outside Crown paperwork. |
| Link of Relevance | Perrin's Passage node opens the door; Delmar and the *Uncertainty* make the visit dangerous; Jean-Claude loses one of his safest ports if Kalowe burns. |

---

## Key Facts

- The *Takowan* is an intelligence ship, not a damaged vessel.
- Noa Fifita can change the *Uncertainty*'s affiliation markers, not its cutter silhouette.
- Perrin's Passage contact at Kalowe is currently unidentified; using it while the *Takowan* is mapping risks burning it within a day.
- Delmar Fisk walking the causeways is the highest-value sighting the *Takowan*'s captain has had in years.

---

## Noa Fifita

Short, still, salt-bleached canvas trousers. Does not greet customers, does not negotiate, looks at the hull instead of the speaker. If the party explains, he lets them finish and prices the job as if they said nothing.

Sample lines:

- *"Two hundred. Three days, maybe five."*
- *"She's a cutter. Paint her any colour you want. She's still a cutter."*
- *"The plate comes off. What you do with it after — not my business."*

First meeting:

1. Perrin makes contact through the second-causeway Passage stall
2. Noa names the back of the second-island chandlery after dark
3. First price: 200 gp; 3 days, maybe 5
4. Papers not his work; can point toward brokers for 50 gp and 1 extra day

If the party has a credible plan to move the *Takowan*, Noa's price drops to 150 gp. He does not offer this; he responds to it.

**The work:** hull colour, bow registry plate, nameboards, pennant. Does not change: patrol-cutter silhouette, age, worn caulking. False papers: 50 gp, 1 additional day, through Passage broker network.

---

## Strong Start: Night Approach

> [!read-aloud]
> The reef breaks the swell before you hear it — a low white roar in the dark that softens as you come through the gap into still water. The lagoon smells of salt and something warmer: woodsmoke, the sharp wet smell of caulking iron still cooling somewhere on the second island. Three limestone islands ahead, connected by stone causeways. The dry-dock cranes are dark shapes above the treeline. At the primary berth, below those cranes, a vessel is lit — lanterns at the rail, a Crown pennant hanging motionless in air you cannot feel moving. Her crew is awake. Someone on that deck is watching the gap you just came through.

Night reef approach is navigable but narrow. Hunter sharks work the current; no encounter unless someone enters the water. If the party passes the bell rope too fast, it rings — the *Takowan*'s watch notices.

---

## Blocks

- Wait until the *Takowan* leaves, accepting contact-network damage while it remains
- Force or lure the *Takowan* away before using the Passage node
- Approach at night through the reef gap and avoid the main lagoon
- Choose Calveno's Warren-routed option instead

## Consequences

- **Fast and careful:** Noa works the hidden slip; the *Uncertainty* leaves de-marked but still cutter-shaped
- **Use the node under watch:** contact likely burns; the Tangle notices the cost
- **Delay too long:** Kalowe's Passage infrastructure becomes mapped enough for Crown pressure
- **Botch public exposure:** the *Takowan* identifies Delmar, the *Uncertainty*, or both

---

- [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] — holds the Kalowe Passage node

# The Knighton Pursuit

[[shepherd-grigori|Shepherd Grigori]] warned the party: [[rupert-knighton|Rupert Knighton]] will not let [[capn-gorgeous|Cap'n Gorgeous]]'s death go unanswered. Ships will be sent.

## Known Facts

- Knighton knows (or will learn) the circumstances of Cap'n Gorgeous's death.
- He has the authority and resources to dispatch ships.
- No timeline established.
- Grigori knew enough about Knighton to warn the party — suggests Knighton's reputation for follow-through is well known.

## Pressures

- The party is operating on a Crown-marked vessel (HCS Surety, still unflagged) — this will make interception easier.
- The Saltwright departed with Beaumont. If Knighton traces the boarding, he traces both ships.
- The letters of marque in Rook's cabin may be relevant to how quickly the Crown traces Rook's loss.

### World Update — Session 03

**Roll:** 8 — Partial
The Knight deployed in the Central Strait followed a merchant report matching Beaumont's wrong description westward. Investigated a different vessel — wasted time, but diverted closer to Calveno's waters in the process. Still searching on the wrong description. No actionable intelligence. See [[surety-missing|Surety Missing]] for the full search state.

### World Update — Session 04

**Roll:** 9 — Partial
The Knight picked up a fragmented report from a port contact — "a cutter that looked Crown-built" heading west into the Calven Roads, crew composition and markings unconfirmed. ## Clock

Unknown timeline. Depends on how fast Knighton learns of the boarding and how close his nearest ships are to the party's route. One Knight is now in the western Central Strait — closer to Calveno than before, but looking for the wrong ship.

The Pearl of Souls is broadcasting across the Maw fissure, turning a geological planar leak into a directed attractor that Auralis is containing and Umberlee needs Fisk to retrieve. Delmar carries the five captains' souls and the secret of why the fleet sank.

# Maw Pearl Crisis

## Situation

The [[pearl-of-souls|Pearl of Souls]] is intact inside the *[[red-lady|Red Lady]]* wreck at the Shelfworks eastern edge, below [[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s domain boundary. It broadcasts a soul-collection signal across the planar fissure, drawing entities from the Elemental Plane of Water into the mortal sea. Removing it does not close the fissure, but it removes the attractor.

---

## Current State

The fissure is geological and widening slowly. Under normal conditions it would leak elemental water and occasional passive drift. The Pearl changed the behaviour: the [[leviathan|Leviathan]] followed the signal, a Ridgeback followed the signal, and the next incursion will do the same unless the Pearl is moved or silenced.

[[auralis|Auralis]] has shifted from passive watch to active containment. His old wards are failing under the Pearl's beacon and the elemental surge. Umberlee cannot retrieve the Pearl because the wreck sits below her jurisdiction, so she is keeping [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] alive and pressured as her proxy.

---

## Delmar's Secret

[[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] stole the Pearl from [[umberlee|Umberlee]]'s Blue Shrine at [[vel-orn|Vel Orn]] before the campaign began. When the fleet sank, Umberlee pressed five captains' souls into him — the five who stayed loyal. The five he could have saved.

**The secret Delmar carries:** The crime that triggered the sinking was his. He made the call. He didn't intend the outcome, but five people paid with their souls and he knows it.

**What Delmar wants:** Resurrect the five captains. If resurrection is impossible, release them so they can find their afterlives. Full resurrection is where his guardrails come off.

**If the party learns the secret:** The question is not whether they forgive him — the question is whether the five captains do.

> [!dm]
> Players do not know the full shape of this. Delmar knows he carries voices. The party does not know about the five captains or what Delmar did.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verb | Calls. The Pearl turns the Maw from hazard into beacon. |
| Unstable Condition | The signal keeps crossing the boundary while salvage damage strips pressure-management architecture from the Shelfworks. |
| Consequence | More entities follow the beacon; lower Shelfworks access collapses; Umberlee escalates pressure on Fisk. |
| Link of Relevance | Delmar stole the Pearl and carries the captains; Perrin is bound to Auralis; the party's Maw choices decide whether the region stays navigable. |

---

## Narrative Devices

- **Loaded Gun:** The Fleet Intelligence Room aboard the *Red Lady* may reveal who arranged the Pearl theft and why the wreck ended up beyond Umberlee's reach.
- **Foreshadowing:** Warm water, dead-fish smell, colour-shifted light below 80 ft, missing Sentinels, and salvage crews abandoning lower tiers.
- **Clock:** Each world tick can bring another entity through or push the Leviathan higher into salvage zones.
- **Reversal Potential:** Returning the Pearl to Umberlee may solve the attractor while empowering a hostile goddess; keeping it may save leverage while sustaining the crisis.

---

## Key Facts

- The Pearl is the active attractor; the fissure is the underlying geology.
- The Leviathan and Ridgeback are confirmed directed incursions, not random sea monsters.
- The *Red Lady* wreck and Pearl sit below Umberlee's domain boundary.
- [[auralis|Auralis]] predates Umberlee's claim and guards the deeper machine around the fissure.
- Salvagers are dismantling upper exhaust/pressure architecture — not harmless ruins.
- Recovering the Pearl is the most consequential Season 1 action currently available.

---

## Involved Parties

- [[delmar-fisk|Delmar Fisk]] — stole the Pearl unknowingly as far as the party knows; five captains pressed into him; Umberlee's necessary proxy.
- [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin Black-Jaw]] — saved by Auralis after the *Vestra* sank; bound as warlock; Leviathan is his quarry.
- [[umberlee|Umberlee]] — wants her artifact back; cannot access the boundary zone; uses [[branca|Branca]] and the Dead Lady as pressure.
- [[auralis|Auralis]] — last Antheri guardian; containing the fissure from below; responds more than he initiates.
- [[branca|Branca]] — senior Waveservant; civil scheduler and pressure valve for Umberlee.
- [[leviathan|Leviathan]] — first confirmed incursion; hunting near the wreck.
- [[high-eyrie|High Eyrie]] — has anomaly records and missing Sentinels but lacks the Pearl explanation.

---

## Locations

- [[the-drowned-maw|Drowned Maw]] — fissure region and domain-boundary problem.
- [[shelfworks|Shelfworks]] — visible newest layer of Antheri pressure/exhaust architecture.
- [[antheri-ruins|Antheri Ruins]] — bottom-up containment machine built around the fissure.
- [[red-lady|Red Lady]] — wreck containing the Pearl and Fleet Intelligence Room.
- [[vel-orn|Vel Orn]] — original theft site; shrine now without its anchor artifact.

---

## Timeline

- Pre-campaign: Fisk's fleet steals the Pearl from Umberlee's shrine at Vel Orn.
- Fleet sinking: Umberlee sinks the fleet expecting recovery, then discovers the Pearl has fallen beyond her reach.
- Vestra sinking: Leviathan destroys the *Vestra*; Auralis finds Perrin afterward.
- 2026-05-16 world tick: Ridgeback follows the signal through; High Eyrie instruments register an anomaly.
- 2026-05-16 world tick: Leviathan ranges into lower Shelfworks; heat event at 80 ft closes lower-tier salvage in practice.

---

## Triggers

- Party reaches the Shelfworks or *Red Lady* wreck.
- Fisk accepts, refuses, or stalls Umberlee's retrieval demand.
- Perrin asks Auralis direct questions.
- The party learns the Pearl is causing directed incursions.
- Another fissure event fires during a world tick.

## Blocks

- Boundary-zone depth: instruments fail and conditions degrade.
- Leviathan patrols within retrieval range.
- Auralis does not volunteer the whole truth.
- Umberlee and the party may want incompatible outcomes once the Pearl is recovered.

## Consequences

- **Pearl recovered and removed:** directed incursions stop; fissure remains a passive geological hazard.
- **Pearl returned to Umberlee:** crisis quiets, but Umberlee regains a major soul artifact.
- **Pearl kept from Umberlee:** party gains leverage and danger; Umberlee escalates.
- **Pearl left in place:** more entities follow the signal; lower Shelfworks and Red Lady access deteriorate.
- **Auralis line fails:** upper tiers flood, the gold rush collapses, and the Antheri machine is tested openly.

---

## DM Notes

### Auralis and the Antheri Machine

Auralis is a manufactured demigod — the last Antheri consciousness fused into an immortal framework engineered to survive the trench bottom. The visible Shelfworks are the newest layer of a bottom-up machine: vents, pressure bleeds, and safety architecture. Salvagers are pulling valves off a pressurized planar system.

Checks at the Shelfworks:

- Perception DC 12: temperature drops and light changes colour below 80 ft.
- Arcana/History DC 14: lower channels are too regular for habitation and too large for plumbing.
- Investigation DC 15: salvage damage concentrates on flow/pressure-regulation structures.
- Nature DC 13 + Sentinel records: identify safer approach windows to the *Red Lady*.

Party level 4–5 should work around or time the danger, not fight the Leviathan.

### Umberlee Pressure

[[branca|Branca]] stays polite until Fisk stalls too long. The Dead Lady exists to remind him what is at stake, not to kill him. Umberlee needs Fisk functional — killing him risks losing the five captains and the Pearl permanently.

Waveservants will not discuss the theological problem: Umberlee does not own the deepest water in the known world.

### The Five Captains

Maren, Rael Corven, and three others are pressed into Delmar. Each has a thread that can surface via the mortis mechanic:

- [[maren|Maren]] — knows Halythion exists; personal lead from a sea elf friend.
- [[rael-corven|Rael Corven]] — his Cloak of Useful Things went down with the Red Lady; potentially recoverable.

---

## Open Questions

- What third option exists besides returning the Pearl or leaving it?
- Who commissioned the theft, and did they intend the Pearl to sink beyond Umberlee's reach?
- What exactly did the Antheri build the containment machine to prevent?
- Why has the Leviathan not claimed the Pearl?

---

Auralis and the Antheri Machine

Auralis is a manufactured demigod — the last Antheri consciousness fused into an immortal framework engineered to survive the trench bottom. The visible Shelfworks are the newest layer of a bottom-up machine: vents, pressure bleeds, and safety architecture. Salvagers are pulling valves off a pressurized planar system.

Checks at the Shelfworks:

  • Perception DC 12: temperature drops and light changes colour below 80 ft.
  • Arcana/History DC 14: lower channels are too regular for habitation and too large for plumbing.
  • Investigation DC 15: salvage damage concentrates on flow/pressure-regulation structures.
  • Nature DC 13 + Sentinel records: identify safer approach windows to the Red Lady.

Party level 4–5 should work around or time the danger, not fight the Leviathan.

Umberlee Pressure

Branca stays polite until Fisk stalls too long. The Dead Lady exists to remind him what is at stake, not to kill him. Umberlee needs Fisk functional — killing him risks losing the five captains and the Pearl permanently.

Waveservants will not discuss the theological problem: Umberlee does not own the deepest water in the known world.

Maren, Rael Corven, and three others are pressed into Delmar. Each has a thread that can surface via the mortis mechanic:

Nona has located Aruhe — a deserted cliff island near the Verdant Teeth — from old Passage route notes and wants Perrin to survey it as a clandestine Rattkin shipyard site. She is aware the Grung avoid it; she does not know why. The Blight is already inside.

# Nona's Midchain Commission — Aruhe Survey

## The Ask

This is the second thing Nona offers Perrin, not the first. The sewer investigation ([[warren-grung-sewers|Warren — Grung in the Sewers]]) is the immediate ask at the table. Aruhe comes later, privately, once the meal is done and the Tangle leads have been distributed. She does not mention it to anyone else at the table.

Nona found a reference to Aruhe in forty-year-old Passage route notes — a waypoint entry: *good water, good stone, one approach, don't stay past dark.* No explanation of that last line. She cross-checked the chart against three other old sources. Every one describes the same thing: high cliffsides, a single navigable harbour entrance, a deep-water anchorage inside. The island sits east of Karath, inside the reef shadow of the Verdant Teeth, and has been deserted for as long as anyone currently alive can remember.

She chose it specifically because the Grung avoid it. An island Grung patrols will not land on is an island no Crown vessel will find evidence of Grung near. She has worked out that the avoidance creates a blind spot. She has not worked out why the Grung avoid it.

Her exact words to Perrin, paraphrased: *the Passage needs a fixed place in the Midchain, not just routes. The Below is an exit; she wants a door that opens both ways. Aruhe might be it. She wants to know if it can be held. She wants Perrin to tell her that, not a report.*

She will contact the *Uncertainty* via signal lantern each evening at dusk. Perrin answers. She asks three questions. He answers in twenty-five words or fewer.

---

## What Nona Does Not Know

> [!dm]
> The Grung call Aruhe *"the island that is already eaten."* They patrol the surrounding reefs but have not landed on it in living memory. The coastal strip is abnormally crowded — too many giant frogs, scorpions, snakes, and spiders packed against the shoreline, pressed there as if something worse holds the interior.
>
> Something does. The Blight has established a Memorial in the abandoned interior. The Death Bloom is at the island's centre. The corruption has pushed through every flooded ditch and terrace structure outward from the Death Bloom. What is left in the interior is not wilderness — it is a dungeon.
>
> None of this is visible from the sea.

---

## Toy Fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Verb** | Scouts. Nona sends Perrin ahead of the decision, not after it. What he finds sets the terms — and what he finds is not what she sent him to find. |
| **Unstable Condition** | Nona believes the island is empty. The Blight believes the same thing about the island. One of them is about to learn otherwise. |
| **Consequence** | Positive survey report opens the Tangle's first real Midchain anchor — if the Blight can be cleared. Honest report gives Nona what she needs to make the real decision. |
| **Link of Relevance** | This is what Nona held back from the table conversation — the work she mentioned to Perrin by name, not to the party. It is the first thing she has given him that is not a favour, a debt, or a test. |

---

## Commission Objectives

Nona wants answers to five questions. She does not need them all at once.

| # | Question | What It Determines |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Is the harbour deep enough for a Tier 2 vessel at high tide? | Can the *Saltmarsh Trader* use it as a base |
| 2 | Is there freshwater on the island? | Settlement viability without resupply infrastructure |
| 3 | Is the entrance defensible by a small crew? | Whether five fighters can hold access during construction |
| 4 | Is there sign of current occupation or frequent visitation? | Whether anything has found the island in the years since the charts were drawn |
| 5 | What is the Grung patrol frequency and closest approach? | Whether the location can remain clandestine for the 18–24 months a shipyard takes |

Question 4 is the one that answers itself the moment the party lands.

---

## Daily Check-In — Signal Lantern Protocol

The *Uncertainty* carries paired signal lanterns: one rail-mounted aft, partner kept below. Range 30 miles, 25-word message limit.

Nona's format each evening: *[Condition check] — [Objective update] — [One question]*

The condition check is always first: she wants to know the party is alive before she asks about the island. If there is no reply by two hours past dusk, she waits one more evening.

**What Perrin sends back:** short, factual, in order. Nona is reading these in the dark. She is not looking for reassurance.

> [!dm]
> If the lantern is destroyed or lost, Nona will not know what happened. The party is operating without a net.

---

## Running the Survey

Three-phase sequence with escalating danger. The party can complete phases 1–2 without triggering the Blight. Phase 3 is the dungeon.

### Phase 1 — Approach and Harbour (Safe)

The harbour entrance is technical but navigable. Correct bearing (east-northeast on the old chart) is required; the gap is only visible on direct approach.

| Task | Check | DC | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Navigate reef entrance, first pass | Dexterity (Water Vehicles) | 10 / 14 | With/without bearing note. Failure: grounded on outer reef, 2d6 hull HP damage. |
| Assess harbour depth | Intelligence (Navigation) | 13 | Success: reliable depth estimate (~40 ft at centre). |
| Read the shoreline fauna behaviour | Wisdom (Perception) | 12 | Success: something is pressing the animals outward from the interior. Displacement, not natural crowding. |

Inside the harbour: deep water (~40 ft at centre), limestone cliffs on three sides, a narrow shingle beach at the back. The cliffs are 150–200 ft. One stone staircase cut into the cliff face above the beach leads to the plateau.

### Phase 2 — Clifftop Survey (Dangerous, Not Blight)

The plateau above the harbour is overgrown. Old stonework — terrace walls and collapsed structures — is visible under the growth. The stonework has been dissolving at the base: acid drainage from the interior has reached the terrace footings.

| Task | Check | DC | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assess clifftop defensibility | Intelligence (any military background) | 10 | Clear yes — sight lines cover the approach, high ground holds the entrance. |
| Identify acid drainage source | Intelligence (Investigation) | 12 | Traces toward the interior. PC knows it is coming from inside the island. |
| Investigate terrace stonework | Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Nature) | 13 | The terraces dissolved from below, not from neglect. Something in the interior is producing this. |
| Survey freshwater source | Wisdom (Survival) | 11 | A freshwater spring feeds the drainage channel. It runs year-round. |

> [!dm]
> The *don't stay past dark* warning. The original Passage runner who wrote this note landed in the harbour, climbed to the plateau, noted the freshwater and the cliff approach, and then heard the interior at dusk. He left. He never elaborated. He also never went back. If the party is on the plateau at dusk and makes a DC 10 Perception check, they hear it too: sound that should be wind moving through the old terrace walls, except the air is still.

### Phase 3 — Interior (Blight)

The interior is the dungeon. The Death Bloom is at the centre. The corruption has spread through every flooded ditch and terrace structure. A party that moves inland triggers Blight encounter content.

> [!dm]
> Do not require the party to clear the interior to complete the survey. Phases 1–2 are enough for Nona's five questions. The interior is a choice — and a loaded one, because the site cannot be used as a settlement while the Blight holds the interior. Perrin will know this when he sees it.

---

## Grung Proximity

Aruhe's surrounding reefs are part of the Verdant Teeth patrol circuit. The Grung turn back at Aruhe's beach line — they do not land.

- Patrol boats: flat-bottomed, 2–3 crew, darts and boarding hooks
- Circuit frequency: every 36–48 hours past the eastern reef
- A ship anchored inside the harbour is not visible from the patrol route
- A ship anchored outside on the approach is visible within 48 hours
- Any light or fire on the island at night is visible from the Karath side

> [!dm]
> The Grung response to a ship at Aruhe is not a territorial challenge. It is retreat followed by a larger force. They do not want to know what is there. They want whatever is there to stay there.

---

## What Nona Will Do With an Honest Report

She will be quiet for a moment. Then she will ask how bad. Then she will ask if Perrin thinks it can be cleared. She is not asking the party to do it immediately. She is asking if it is possible. The Below gives the Tangle time; this site gives them permanence. She will wait for permanence.

She will not punish an honest assessment. She will punish a report that she later discovers was incomplete.

---

## Outcomes

| Outcome | Result |
|---|---|
| Survey completed, Blight reported honestly | Nona takes the full picture to the Tangle. The commission becomes a longer-arc project: clear the island, then build. |
| Survey completed, Blight omitted | Nona proceeds. The Tangle sends a construction team. They find out. Nona finds out Perrin knew. |
| Interior cleared as part of the survey | The site is viable immediately. Nona's standing in the Tangle shifts significantly. Perrin's standing with Nona shifts more. |
| Party driven off by Blight or Grung | Partial information. Nona gets enough to know the site is complicated. She asks Perrin to go back. |
| Grung discover the operation | Verdant Teeth knows someone was at Aruhe. Their response is unusual — not territorial but alarmed. The site is now a political problem, not just a logistical one. |

---

## Triggers

- Perrin agrees to the commission at Nona's table
- Nona mentions "the work" she referenced earlier and Perrin follows up
- The party is departing Calveno and Perrin asks what Nona needs

# Shepherd Grigori — The Cold Handshake

## What the Party Knows

[[shepherd-grigori|Grigori]] traveled aboard the *[[uncertainty|Uncertainty]]* as a cooperative guest. He healed [[jean-claude-tabarnack|Jean-Claude]]'s wounds with red, viscous, gaseous light that flowed from his wrist — no verbal, no somatic, no material components. [[perrin-black-jaw|Perrin]]'s Arcana check (18) could not identify the magic. It just flowed.

At [[la-vasca|La Vasca]], he shook [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]]'s hand goodbye. It was icy cold — like touching a dead body.

He said he had business in [[calveno|Calveno]]. He mentioned "Impuni" — someone he needs to reach in time. He expects to be done in one to two weeks. He walked into the city alone.

## What the Party Does Not Know

Grigori is an undead sorcerer-lich and shepherd of the [[khlysty|Khlysty]] — a secret sect that threads through Dravosi and Tessarine noble courts. When he heals someone, he binds a thread of his phylactery into their life. As long as they live, he cannot be permanently destroyed. The cure is real. The patient genuinely recovers. They never know they have been bound.

His Calveno business: a hemophiliac [[tessarine-concordat|Tessarine]] heir whose physicians gave up. The cure is now complete. The heir is recovering. Grigori has departed without asking for anything. The network expanded by one.

He considers himself a benefactor. He is not performing warmth — CHA 21 is real.

## Clues the Party Can Find

The trail exists only if the party looks. Nothing forces discovery.

**Servant rumours.** Within a day of Grigori's departure, Tessarine household servants talk: a man came after dark, was with the patient for twenty minutes, left without asking for anything. He smelled like wine and something else. Someone says he was singing under his breath the whole time. The family is not publicizing this.

**The cold handshake.** Delmar felt it. Medicine or Nature DC 15 confirms: that was not living body temperature. No illness produces cold like that.

**The unidentifiable magic.** Red viscous light, no components. Arcana DC 22 (higher than the party's failed 18) to recognize it as necrotic energy reflavoured through a sorcerous origin — the caster's body is the focus. Below DC 22, the magic remains unclassifiable.

> [!check] Arcana — Identify Grigori's healing magic
> DC 18 already failed (Session 03). DC 22 with new evidence or context (seeing a second Khlysty healing, finding a text describing the method).
> Fail: the magic has no school signature the caster recognizes. Genuinely unclassifiable.
> Success: necrotic energy channelled through the caster's own body as a living (or unliving) focus. The red light is blood-aspected. No known divine or arcane tradition does this.
> Crit success: the caster is the component. Whatever Grigori is, his body is the spell focus — which means his body is not normal.

> [!check] Medicine/Nature — The cold handshake
> DC 15. Delmar experienced it directly; advantage if he is the one rolling.
> Fail: cold hands. Could be anything.
> Success: that was not living body temperature. No circulation-based illness produces uniform cold like that. The hand felt like preserved tissue.
> Crit success: Delmar recalls exactly — not clammy, not feverish-cold. Dry, even, and the same temperature throughout. Like meat that has been sitting in a cellar.

## Pressures

- **Grigori's timeline.** He said one to two weeks. If the party is still in Calveno when that window closes, he may reappear — or he may already be gone. The party does not control this.
- **The Tessarine connection.** The healed heir's family is grateful and powerful. If the party investigates the rumours, they will find a family that considers Grigori a saint. Contradicting that assessment will not be welcome.
- **Pattern recognition (future).** Grigori has done this across multiple courts. Other healed-noble NPCs exist in the world. The Calveno heir is the nearest data point, but not the only one.

## If the Party Ignores This

Nothing bad happens to them in the short term. Grigori liked the party. He is not hostile. He moves on.

The [[khlysty|Khlysty]] network expands. Each new heir makes Grigori harder to permanently kill. If the party encounters him again in 5, 10, or 20 sessions, the network is larger and the moral problem is worse — more living children whose continued health depends on the phylactery bond remaining intact.

The thread goes dormant. It resurfaces naturally when the party meets a noble heir who survived something unsurvivable, when someone mentions a wandering healer matching Grigori's description, or when Grigori contacts them because he needs something.

> [!dm]
> Let this thread sleep. Do not force it. The horror compounds with time — a Grigori reveal at level 10 hits harder than at level 4 because more healed children are in play and the party has met some of them. Seed miraculous recoveries into noble courts the party visits. Never label them as Khlysty until the party connects the pattern themselves.

## Running This at the Table

> [!dm]
> Play Grigori's absence as unremarkable. He said he had business. He left. If no one asks about him, the session moves on. Do not prompt the party to investigate — if they care, they will ask.

> [!dm]
> If the party investigates: the Tessarine household is findable. The servants talk. The family does not. The heir is recovering and is not available for visitors. Grigori left no forwarding address. The trail ends at the household door unless the party pushes hard.

> [!mechanic]
> Grigori is CR 19. The party is level 4. If they track him down and start a fight, he will try to leave. If cornered, this is a death scenario. He does not want to kill them — he liked them. He will use dominate person and mass suggestion to end the encounter without casualties. If forced to kill, he considers it a waste.

- **Delmar** — felt the cold handshake. The physical evidence lives with him.
- **Perrin** — failed the Arcana check. Knows the magic was wrong but not how.
- **Jean-Claude** — was healed by Grigori's magic. The red light touched him. If the phylactery binding applies to anyone Grigori heals: Jean-Claude may be a thread. (DM decision — this has not been established in canon.)

> [!dm]
> The Jean-Claude binding question is yours to answer. If yes, it creates a ticking personal stake. If no, the mystery stays external. Decide before the party asks, not after.
